- **Use when:** A hero or social loop that must show several features at once, or a launch whose first second has to prove breadth.
- **Avoid when:** The story needs one idea at a time, a single-message sting, or a 9:16 frame where the cells would shrink below about 540 px wide.

### Macro number scramble, one-frame snap-out

`oh-macro-scramble-snap-out` · signature · energy high · launch, sting, feature, vertical

Huge digits fill and overflow the frame, re-rolling every frame. On one frame the view cuts back to the whole figure, which rolls into the final metric and holds: the number is the hook before any brand appears.

- **Build:** Lay out the final figure once with typeStyle('display') (tabular figures, fixed group separator) at a size where the whole string spans about 0.9 W, and draw each digit column as a Roll-style strip whose mask stays 1.6 lines tall during the macro phase, so outgoing digits stack and overflow vertically. Macro phase: scale the wrapper to 1.22 about the frame centre and, on every whole frame (fd), give 1-2 columns a new digit from rand(`${seed}:${fd(frame)}`). Snap: on a single frame decided with fd (so the motion-blur sub-samples agree), cut the scale to 1.0 with no tween, clip the masks to one line and lock the columns left to right 3 f apart until the final string is forced; then hold on breath (scale +0.065%/f) with no glints or sparkles, and keep the brand out until the end lockup. Sound: five dry glitch ticks inside the first 0.6 s, then the bed drops at least 30 dB within one frame on the lock frame and stays silent through the hold; reuse the identical tick cluster under the closing sting as a bookend.
- **Timing:** Macro 29 f; snap 1 f at f29; settle 12 f; final string forced from f41 (0.68 s); hold 72 f with only the scale drift. Ticks at about 0.17, 0.23, 0.31, 0.36 and 0.40 s.
- **Use when:** The strongest proof is one metric (users, hours saved, uptime) and the film earns attention with the outcome before the brand.
- **Avoid when:** There is no credible or impressive number, or the tone is calm and premium.

### Oversize line flies through, restarts small

`oh-oversize-fly-then-small` · signature · energy high · launch, feature, vertical

A huge fragment of the headline, about a quarter of frame height, brakes in from the right with its letters fading on as it slows, then dissolves; three frames later the same line restarts small and centred so it can be read.

- **Build:** Start the big line's clock 6 f before the film's first frame (t = f + 6), so frame 0 already shows its first letters fading on as it brakes. Layer 1: the line at about 270 px, weight 500, colour rgba(255,255,255,0.65) on C.ink (or over a single-hue wash), with x = startX + inertia(t, 0, -70, 0.89).x (601 px of travel from 70 px/f). Per-character opacity is 0.65 * prog(t, 6 + 1.5i, 12 + 1.5i, E.smooth), so letters only resolve once the speed drops below about 20 px/f, and the whole layer fades 1 -> 0 over its last 7 f on E.smooth while it is still sliding. Start layer 2 on the next frame, with no empty frames between: a dissolve to an empty frame and a fresh start reads as the film restarting. Layer 2: the same line at reading size with its final centred layout precomputed, per-character opacity prog(t, 1.3i, 1.3i + 5, E.smooth), and container x = inertia(t, 0, -10.8, 0.88).x: an 84 px drift that lands exactly centred and never passes 12 px/f. Keep the opening type translucent and make the end card solid white, so the film reads as a question becoming an answer.
- **Timing:** Big line visible from f0 (its clock t = f + 6) to f35: slide 39 f, about 35 px/f at t = 6 and 17 px/f at t = 12; letters 6 f each, 1.5 f stagger; fade over the last 7 f. No gap; small line from f36, 13 characters in 17 f, drift settled in about 40 f.
- **Use when:** The headline has a thesis word worth previewing big, in a dark, energetic launch.
- **Avoid when:** Light stages where 65% white loses contrast, or headlines longer than about 5 words whose big fragment will not read. Also avoid it when the big fragment would sit still and cropped at both edges at any point: viewers read an oversized, cropped line that vanishes and then restarts small as a false start, not a preview. It has to travel every frame it is on screen.

## Transitions

A transition is a designed handoff, not a cut between unrelated pictures. Something always crosses the seam: a velocity, a shape held within ±20-30 px of the same screen point, a dot, a line or a stage colour. The default that carries most edits is the velocity handoff. The outgoing move speeds up about ×1.13-1.2 per frame over its last 16-24 f, the cut lands on its fastest frame at 25-40 px/f, and the incoming shot opens at that speed or faster and slows about ×0.92-0.94 per frame to rest in 45-90 f. A scale jump of 1.3-2.5x (8-9x for a frame-filling macro of a related mark) is invisible when the scale velocity matches in log space, about −8% per frame on both sides of the cut. One-take seams (morphs, irises, portals, carets) run 20-90 f and keep every element edge under about 80 px/f, and only flat mask edges may move faster. Polarity flips, where mean luma jumps by 150 or more of 255, are the loudest punctuation: put them on downbeats, once or twice per film. Blending appears only as 1-2 ghost frames at a motion peak, never as a crossfade seam.

### Anchored overlay, background swap

`tr-anchor-overlay-cut` · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature, walkthrough, loop, vertical

A foreground element (a pin, a status pill, a modal, a big word) keeps its exact screen position while the world behind it hard-cuts, so a total change of scene reads as a change of zoom or context.

- **Build:** Render the overlay from one absolute-frame function drawn by every act it crosses (deviceAt in references/transitions.md §4.1). Use the identical transform string on both sides of each cut, so its last frame in one act and its first in the next are consecutive samples of one curve. Each background change is an act boundary; a montage is 2-3 background acts in a row behind the same overlay. The overlay keeps its own clock through the cut (a running scale tween, a 0.5-1 px/f drift or a breath() push), so it is never static for more than 48 f. After the last swap the overlay acts on the new world: it travels into its slot on E.glide over 40 f (moves up to 350 px), or FLIPs into an input.
- **Timing:** Background holds of 10-22 f each in a montage (2-3 swaps), or a single swap. Overlay offset across the cut: 0 px ideally, 30 px at most. Overlay drift 0.5-1 px/f. Follow-up move 40 f on E.glide. Cuts on beats or 16ths.
- **Use when:** Showing that one thing persists across contexts: a location going from 3D city to map, a request going from an empty void to the full app, a claim held over a run of photos.
- **Avoid when:** The overlay is text that must be reread after each swap, or the backgrounds are busy and bright enough to swallow it. Keep backgrounds near 5% mean luma under light overlays.

### Angle change on a shared drift

`tr-drift-matched-angle-cut` · workhorse · energy calm · launch, feature, loop

A hard cut jumps to a new angle or the next state of the same object (front to top-down, open to closed) while the slow zoom or pan carries on at exactly the same rate, so a calm shot changes viewpoint with no jolt and no speed ramp.

- **Build:** Write the drift once as a function of the absolute frame and multiply it into both acts' anchor-camera k (src/lib/camera.ts): d(abs) = lmix(1.10, 1, prog(abs, a, a + 96, E.outSoft)) for a settling pull (lmix(1, 1.10, ...) for a push), plus any pan as sx += v · (abs − a). zoomSpeed(kA, cut − 1) then equals zoomSpeed(kB, cut) by construction. Shot A frames the subject from one angle. Shot B frames the same subject at least 30 deg away (yaw ±35-50 deg on a tilted UI plane, or a top-down pitch on an object built with depth) or in its next state (lid open to closed, card face to back). Its on-screen centre stays within ±40 px of A's and its apparent size within ±15%. Cut on an act boundary 8-16 f into the drift, on a beat, while the frame still changes about 0.3% per frame. When the subject itself acts (a lid closes, a device turns), drive that action from one absolute progress too and cut at 35-55% of it, so it finishes in the new angle. Keep the stage colour and light identical, and add no ghost frame.
- **Timing:** Drift 96 f on E.outSoft from 1.10x (or a 2-4 px/f pan). Cut 8-16 f in, at −0.26 to −0.36% scale per frame (about 3 px/f at the frame edge); the drift settles 40-80 f after the cut. Angle change at least 30 deg, centre offset at most 40 px, size change at most 15%. Optional subject action 36-60 f on E.smooth, cut at 35-55% of it. Cut in 0 f.
- **Use when:** Calm films and product beauty shots where a velocity ramp would be too loud: showing an object's second side or its next state within one continuous gesture.
- **Avoid when:** The two angles look alike (under about 30 deg it reads as a jump cut), the subject's size or position jumps, or one side is static. For a lift in energy, use a velocity handoff instead.

### Conveyor line swap

`tr-conveyor-line-swap` · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature, vertical, loop

The current line floats up and fades, the stage is empty for an instant, and the next line rises from below into the same spot, so a run of statements reads as one upward feed.

- **Build:** Outgoing line: translateY 0 → −135 px through depart(q), with q = prog(f, 0, 30, E.in); opacity 1 → 0 over its last 8 f, plus blurOut(q, 8). Leave 2 empty frames. Incoming line: translateY +188 → 0 through arrive(p), with p = prog(f, 0, 30, E.out). Its opacity goes 0 → 1 over the first 10 f, so it flies faded while faster than 20 px/f, and its colour goes C.mute → C.ink over 16 f with mixColor. For a word-by-word version, use Words.tsx with stagger 3-4 and out/outDur 16, so each old word rises away as its replacement rises in. Keep one direction (up) for the whole run.
- **Timing:** Exit: 30 f on E.in (last frame about 26 px/f, while fading). Gap 2 f. Entry: 30 f on E.out (first frame about 37 px/f, while faded); colour over 16 f. Per-word stagger 3-4 f. One line per bar or half bar.
- **Use when:** Sequences of short claims, lists of capabilities, a subject that changes while the predicate stays.
- **Avoid when:** Lines of very different length or alignment (the eye loses the slot), or more than 4-5 lines in a row without another seam type.

### Motion-masked swap

`tr-motion-masked-swap` · workhorse · energy medium · feature, loop, launch

Content changes on exactly the frame something else moves fastest (background rings whipping past, a card kicking into a tilt), so the change hides inside the motion and two states chain in one space with no visible cut.

- **Build:** Drive a large secondary motion with a curve whose peak falls on the swap frame s. Either run a background sweep on E.smooth over 20-24 f, from s − 11 to s + 11, so its peak speed lands on s. Or kick a card with rotateY = 12 deg × hitPulse(f − s + 2, 2, 3) and skewY 2 deg on the same envelope, in a perspective(900px) container. Decide the content with fd(frame) >= s, so every motion-blur sub-sample agrees, and give the new content its own arrival (a slam or a word reveal) from s. Give kicked cards a soft shadow (0 18px 40px rgba(0,0,0,.18)) so the tilt reads.
- **Timing:** Sweep: 20-24 f on E.smooth, centred on the swap. Kick: attack 2 f, decay tau 3 f, settled in about 8 f. Repeat no faster than every 48-54 f.
- **Use when:** Changing copy inside a continuous environment; cycling examples (photos, prompts, results) in a loop.
- **Avoid when:** The masking motion is weak (under about 20 px/f at its peak), so the swap shows; or the content is a counter (roll the digits instead).

### Path relay

`tr-path-relay` · workhorse · energy calm · launch, feature, walkthrough, loop

A line and its lead dot carry the eye from one place to the next. The connector bends around a rounded corner with the camera following, or continues across a cut and enters the next shot from the same edge at the same angle.

- **Build:** Draw the connector as an SVG path (stroke ≥ 1.5 px, C.white on ink or C.ink on paper) with pathLength 1, revealed by stroke-dashoffset; corners are arcs of r = 40 px. Place the lead dot with getPointAtLength (from @remotion/paths, or an analytic line-plus-arc), where the arc length grows with prog(f, a, b, E.linear) at 8-16 px/f. The camera follows with a lag: the anchor-camera Shot frames the dot's position at f − 10. Across a cut, start shot B's path at the frame edge where A's path left, at the same angle and speed, so the dot reaches its target 18 f after the cut. Off-frame variant: the dot or cursor speeds out of frame on E.contact over 24 f and stays hidden 12 f while the camera relocates. It then re-enters at ≤ 60 px/f, slowing ×0.92 per frame to rest in about 36 f.
- **Timing:** Dot at a constant 8-16 px/f. Corner radius 40 px. Camera lag 8-12 f. One run lasts 60-72 f. After a cut the dot lands 18 f later. Off-frame gap 12 f; re-entry at ≤ 60 px/f, slowing ×0.92 per frame.
- **Use when:** Money, data or messages travelling (send, route, sync), flowcharts and timelines, and films whose UI already uses lines and nodes.
- **Avoid when:** The film has no line language, or the path would cross readable text. A path that loops back reads as indecision.

### Product surface cover wipe

`tr-cover-wipe` · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature, walkthrough, vertical

A product surface (a UI panel, a window, a device) moves in front of the old shot and either passes straight through it with the scene changed behind it, or lands and becomes the new shot.

- **Build:** Pass-through: a panel 1.15x the frame height, showing the product's real UI, moves at a constant 64-72 px/f (prog with E.linear) from fully above the frame to fully below. The scene beneath switches on the first frame the panel covers the frame completely, decided with fd(frame); the motion-blur pass streaks the panel. Land: the product window rises about 940 px from below the frame to its rest pose over 44 f on E.glide, above the title layer, while the title fades 1 → 0 over 36 f, starting 16 f before the window moves. Occluder variant: during a fast camera push, time one foreground object to cross the lens on the push's peak frame, covering at least 60% of the frame for 2-4 f, and change the world behind it then. In every version the surface sits above the old shot in z-order, and its own content does not need to be readable until it rests.
- **Timing:** Pass-through: about 2600 px at 64-72 px/f, or 36-40 f; the scene switches on the full-cover frame. Land: 940 px over 44 f on E.glide (peak about 64 px/f at 31% of the move); the title fades over 36 f, starting 16 f before. Occluder: covers for 2-4 f at the push's peak.
- **Use when:** Promise to product: the UI pushes the headline off. Scene changes that should show the product itself rather than a graphic.
- **Avoid when:** The surface is a plain coloured slab (then it is a preset wipe), or the pass-through would need more than 80 px/f; shorten the distance with a cut instead.

### Reveal by subtraction

`tr-subtract-reveal` · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature, walkthrough, sting, loop

The clutter in front of the hero flies off toward the frame edges or shrinks away, uncovering a hero that was already sitting at its final size behind it.

- **Build:** Layer order: the hero at the bottom, static, already at its final size and position; the clutter above it. Each clutter item moves along the vector from the hero's centre through its own centre, its distance scaled by (1 + index × 0.1), on E.contact over 30 f. Set its travel to twice its distance to clear the frame, which keeps it under about 75 px/f until it is gone; keep that clearing distance ≤ 750 px by starting big cards near the edges. Window variant: the current window shrinks into the corner where the cursor sits, with transform-origin on that corner and k = lmix(1, 0.05, prog(f, 0, 40, E.contact)). Its opacity goes to 0 over the last 6 f, and the next panel's entrance starts 4 f after it vanishes. Staccato variant: remove one item every 5-7 f on hard steps (fd), re-centring the survivors instantly, until one remains, held 17 f.
- **Timing:** Scatter: 30 f on E.contact; items clear the frame by about frame 24; stagger 0-2 f; the hero stays static throughout. Window minimize: 40 f on E.contact in log scale (far corner ≤ 75 px/f), fading over the last 6 f; next entrance 4 f later. Staccato: one removal every 5-7 f, final hold 17 f.
- **Use when:** Ending a busy montage on the one stat, card or word. Walkthroughs that change app areas through the product's own window behaviour.
- **Avoid when:** The hero is not ready behind the clutter (it must never pop in), or the clutter is readable content the viewer has not finished.

### Shape match cut

`tr-shape-match-cut` · workhorse · energy medium · any

The hero shape leaves one shot at a known point and size, and the next shot opens on a matching shape (the mark, the flat UI, the real object) on the same point, so the object's identity carries across a change of world.

- **Build:** Record the outgoing shape's centre and size on its last frame (toScreen from src/lib/camera.ts, or inkBox from src/lib/measure.ts for type). Open the incoming act with the matching shape centred there within ±20 px, at 0.57-1.3x that size. Keep motion on both sides. The outgoing shape shrinks 2-4% over its last 4 f on E.in (or a coin turns face-on, rotateY 90 → 10 deg over 22 f on E.out). The incoming shape keeps going, for example k = lmix(0.57, 1, prog(f, 0, 18, E.out)), with no overshoot. Match colour, corner radius and stroke weight so only the medium changes (device screen to flat UI, coin emblem to logotype, circle to app icon), and hold the result 12-30 f before it moves on.
- **Timing:** Cut in 0 f. Centre offset ≤ 20 px. Scale ratio 0.57-1.3x. Incoming settle 18 f on E.out, with half the change done in about 2 f. Outgoing pre-cut shrink 4 f on E.in. Hold 12-30 f.
- **Use when:** Turning a problem shape into the answer, a device mockup into the bare UI, or a physical object into the mark.
- **Avoid when:** The silhouettes differ (round against tall), so the match cannot be seen. Use a dot relay or a container morph instead.

### Tip-back exit

`tr-tip-back-exit` · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature, walkthrough

The outgoing scene tips away from camera like a sheet laid onto a table, or flips up into a line, speeding up and fading into the next stage colour, and the next element lands on the clean field.

- **Build:** Wrap the outgoing scene in a 3D container (transform-origin 50% 100%, perspective 1200 px) and tip it: rotateX 0 → 40 deg and translateY 0 → +10% over 30 f on E.smooth. Lay a floor of the stage colour over it, opaque across the bottom 25% and transparent from 55% up, so the scene sinks into the stage, and dim it toward the next act's stage colour (overlay 0 → 0.9) over the last 12 f. Fast version: rotateX 0 → 88 deg with translateY 0 → −400 px over 20 f on E.contact (last frame about 70 px/f), so the scene flattens into a line at the top edge and uncovers what sits beneath. Flat version: a clip-path inset from the bottom grows on E.contact over 24 f, and the cut lands on its fastest frame. The next element starts on the frame the exit clears, or 1 f before.
- **Timing:** Tip-back: 30 f on E.smooth (rotateX 40 deg). Flip to a line: 20 f on E.contact. Crop collapse: 24 f on E.contact. Dim overlay 0 → 0.9 over the last 12 f. The next element starts 0-1 f after the exit clears.
- **Use when:** Ending a UI section to hand over to a statement or an alert, when the next beat needs an empty stage for big type.
- **Avoid when:** The next act opens on the same pose (use a relay instead), or the dim would go to black and back up (a dip) instead of into the next stage colour.

### Velocity handoff cut

`tr-velocity-handoff-cut` · workhorse · energy any · any

The outgoing shot speeds up in one direction and is cut on its fastest frame. The next shot opens already moving the same way and brakes to rest, so momentum runs straight through the edit.

- **Build:** Make the cut an act boundary in timeline.ts so motion-blur samples never straddle it, and place it on a beat with b(). In the outgoing act, drive the camera (src/lib/camera.ts) or the hero's translate on E.exit (E.contact, or E.in for a harder snap) over its last 16-24 f, so it ends at peak speed on the final frame; for a zoom, apply the same ramp to k through lmix. In the incoming act, start the key element moving on frame 0 in the same screen direction at 1.0-1.5x that speed and slow it on E.out over 45-90 f. Size the two sides with exitSpeed(D, T, ease) and entryDistance(v, T) from references/transitions.md; for a flicked list, use y = v0·(1 − k^f)/(1 − k) with k = 0.92-0.943 and no overshoot. Give each act one dominant screen vector (+x in one act, −x in the next) and start every incoming element on the side it would enter from.
- **Timing:** Exit: last 16-24 f on E.exit (speed grows about ×1.1-1.2 per frame), ending at 25-40 px/f (never above 60) or −6 to −8% scale per frame. Entry: 30-55 px/f on frame 0, slowing about ×0.92-0.94 per frame (E.out over 45-90 f; entryDistance(40, 60) is about 400 px). A 1-3 px/f drift may run under the hold before the ramp. Text inside a moving shot must be under 20 px/f by the time it has to be read.
- **Use when:** Most cuts between moving shots: feature-to-feature edits, montages, chapter changes, and any film that must never stop. Velocity-matched cuts are exempt from the two-uses-per-type limit.
- **Avoid when:** One side has to be still (a held statement or a designed freeze), or the two shots would move in opposite directions. Carry a shape or an anchor across instead.

### Band wipe

`tr-band-wipe` · accent · energy medium · feature, launch, walkthrough, loop

A band crosses a region (snapping up, lingering, then whipping off, or sweeping across a chart) and the content changes along its edge: the old state is erased under it and the new state draws in its wake.

- **Build:** Clip both states to the region and drive one band position b(f). The old state stays clipped to the side the band has not reached (clip-path: inset(0 0 0 b px)), and the new state draws in behind it (a line chart's stroke-dashoffset follows b). In the full look the band is a luminous light core falling off through a warm hue, screen-blended over the content. Sweep profile: a 368 px band crosses a chart at a constant 60-70 px/f (prog with E.linear, about 27 f for a 1400 px chart plus the band), starting 2 f after the control that caused it (a tab) lands, never easing out, until the chart edge cuts it off. Hang-time profile, for a full-frame band behind giant type: the bottom edge goes from 81% to 66% of frame height over 6 f on E.out, 66% to 53% over 20 f at constant speed, and 53% to 0 over 16 f on E.contact. In the hang-time profile the band's edges are flat mask edges, so they may pass 80 px/f; nothing textured rides on them.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Fill the band with the one accent (or ink on a paper stage) at full strength. Its trailing side falls off by opacity of that same colour over 30-40% of its width, with no light core, no screen blend and no second hue. The full look relies on glow, gradient, beige, orange; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** Sweep: 368 px band at a constant 60-70 px/f (about 27 f across a 1400 px chart), starting 2 f after the cause. Hang-time: 6 f (E.out) + 20 f (constant speed) + 16 f (E.contact) = 42 f. The new state draws in within 6-10 f after the band passes.
- **Use when:** Swapping a data series, a filter result or a big-type card in place, when a control's tap should visibly cause the change.
- **Avoid when:** Applied to whole scenes again and again (it becomes a preset wipe), or when the band would cross text the viewer has not finished reading.

### Defocus cut

`tr-defocus-cut` · accent · energy medium · launch, feature, walkthrough

The outgoing shot throws itself out of focus in a few frames, the film cuts to a shot that is still fully defocused with its content already moving, and the lens snaps sharp as that content settles.

- **Build:** In the outgoing act's last 6 f, wrap the scene in RackFocus with t = prog(f, T − 6, T, E.in) and blur 16 px, fading it toward the next stage colour (opacity 1 → 0.2). Hard cut on the act boundary. The incoming act opens in RackFocus at blur 24 px and t = 1, held for 6-12 f while its content already moves in (cards on a diagonal, E.out over 20 f). Then t goes 1 → 0.1 over 8 f on E.in (the snap) and 0.1 → 0 over 12-20 f on E.outSoft with mid = true. Text in the incoming shot uses Words.tsx or blurIn so it lands sharp, and readable text is never blurred for more than 6 f.
- **Timing:** Out: 6 f on E.in to 16 px. Cut. Defocused hold 6-12 f at 24 px. Snap 8 f (E.in) to t = 0.1. Settle 12-20 f (E.outSoft). Incoming card move 20 f on E.out. About 30-45 f in all.
- **Use when:** Joining two shots with nothing in common (no shared shape, direction or colour), or a deliberate 'look again' beat.
- **Avoid when:** As the default seam (it turns into a soft crossfade), on shots dominated by small text, or more than twice per film.

### Envelope-matched type cut

`tr-envelope-match-type-cut` · accent · energy medium · launch, feature, sting, vertical

A big line hard-cuts to a much smaller, longer line whose words start spread apart so it spans exactly the old line's width, then the gaps close while the sideways drift carries on, so the outer edges of the type survive the cut.

- **Build:** On the cut frame, measure line A's on-screen width W_A and its centre or left edge (measureTracked from src/lib/measure.ts times A's current scale). Lay line B out at rest (cap height 2-3x smaller, more words) and read its natural width W_B, which must be smaller than W_A, and its word positions from measureTracked prefixes. Spread B with an extra gap per word space, g(f) = g0 · (1 − prog(f, 0, 36, E.outSoft)) with g0 = (W_A − W_B)/(n − 1), applied as translateX g · (j − (n − 1)/2) on word j of a centred line (g · j with the left edge pinned for a left-aligned one). Each word keeps its own tracking, so it stays readable while the gaps close. Cut on the act boundary, optionally with one ghost frame of B at 0.65 opacity over A. Both lines carry the same horizontal drift through the cut (A's creep, for example −3.5 px/f), which decays in B over 60 f on E.outSoft, and B may ink in from C.mute to C.ink over 16 f with mixColor.
- **Timing:** Cut in 0 f, or 1 ghost frame at 0.6-0.7 incoming. The gaps close over 36 f on E.outSoft, half done by frame 5. The outermost words travel (W_A − W_B)/2: keep that at or under 160 px so their first frame stays under 20 px/f, or fly them at 0.6 opacity for the first 6 f. Shared drift 3-4 px/f, decaying in B over 60 f. Hold B at least 60 f.
- **Use when:** A big two- or three-word claim hands over to its full sentence or call to action; any big-to-small type change where both lines share a centre or a left edge and the type already drifts sideways.
- **Avoid when:** B is naturally wider than A (use a blur-swap rescale instead), either line is a single word (there are no gaps, so collapse one word's tracking instead), or the alignment changes across the cut.

### Horizon rise

`tr-horizon-rise` · accent · energy medium · launch, sting

A huge disc rises from the bottom edge like a planet horizon, its rim washing over the frame, until its dark core swallows the screen and becomes the stage for the next line.

- **Build:** One full-frame layer holds a circle of radius R = 1.1 × frame width (2112 px at 1080p), centred horizontally: a dark core in the next act's stage colour out to 55% of R, then bands of rim colour out to 85%, softened by a 30 px blur. In the full look the rim is several hues with a bloom. Bake the disc as a dithered PNG with scripts/dither-gradient.py so the soft falloff does not band. Move its centre from y = H + R (the disc's top just touching the bottom edge) to y = 0.58 H over 56 f on E.dolly, with the previous scene disappearing behind it; at rest the core covers all four corners. Start the next text at about frame 46, inside the core. Lighter version: a rim band 40% of the frame height rises from the bottom edge over 16 f on E.in, and the cut lands mid-rise on the beat.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Keep one hue: the dark core, then a rim of the accent at full strength falling off by opacity of that same accent (no second hue, no bloom), baked dithered. Or use a hard-edged ink disc with a 1.5 px accent edge rising over a paper stage. The full look relies on gradient, glow; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** Rise: 56 f on E.dolly, about 2570 px of centre travel at 1080p (the rim's leading edge peaks near 70 px/f mid-move). Next text from about frame 46. Band version: 16 f on E.in. The core fills the frame on a downbeat.
- **Use when:** A single colour event that divides the film into acts (UI section to brand moment), or a calm lift from a statement into the next card.
- **Avoid when:** More than once per film, or on a light film where the dark core would be the only dark frame.

### Iris from a glyph

`tr-iris-from-glyph` · accent · energy high · launch, feature, sting

A small dot appears on a word or icon in the current shot and balloons exponentially to swallow the frame, showing the next scene inside it, so the reveal starts from content rather than from nowhere.

- **Build:** Render the incoming scene above the outgoing one, clipped with clip-path: circle(r at cx cy). The 14 px seed dot (in the next scene's stage colour) appears on the glyph, scale 0 → 1 over 6 f on E.out, and holds 6-10 f. Then r = lmix(14, R, prog(f, 0, 20, E.linear)), where R is the distance to the farthest frame corner: a constant ratio of about ×1.25-1.29 per frame. Over the same 20 f, (cx, cy) moves from the glyph to the frame centre on E.smooth. Optional residue: when the disc reaches r ≈ 900 px, step its fill through three tones of one hue over 6 f, and leave a 90 px ring one tone darker at that radius as set dressing for the new shot. For an app icon, use a funnel instead of a circle: a clip polygon anchored at the icon's base whose top width and height grow ×1.18 per frame over 24 f.
- **Timing:** Seed in over 6 f, hold 6-10 f. Iris 20 f at a constant ratio (about ×1.25-1.29 per frame, radius in log space). Centre drift 20 f on E.smooth. Optional tonal ramp: 3 steps over 6 f. Funnel variant: 24 f at ×1.18 per frame. The disc fills the frame on the downbeat.
- **Use when:** A word in the copy names what the next scene shows (a benchmark, a feature, a place); dark-to-light or light-to-dark act changes.
- **Avoid when:** A linear radius (it crawls, then snaps); the same iris more than twice per film; a seed glyph the viewer has not had 6 f to find.

### Polarity flip cut

`tr-polarity-flip-cut` · accent · energy high · launch, sting, feature

A hard cut flips the stage between near-black and near-white on a downbeat, often with the same icon or pill held on the same spot in inverted colours, so the luminance jump itself is the accent.

- **Build:** Plan adjacent acts with opposite stage luminance (mean luma differing by at least 150 of 255) and cut on their act boundary on a downbeat, after a dropout or silence, with one impact in the sound. Carry the flip; never cut from a static frame. Either cut on the outgoing motion peak (a zoom-through or an accelerating exit), or end on a shape centred at P and open on the same shape at P ±20 px, at 1-2.5x the size, with fill and ground swapped. An ink icon on paper becomes a paper icon on ink; an accent pill on paper becomes a paper pill on an accent field. The incoming shape is already drifting, translateY −36 px over 30 f on E.out. For a softer edge, draw two ghost frames with the incoming shot at 0.12 and then 0.94 opacity over the fully opaque outgoing frame. Declare the cut for scripts/forensics.py, and use no flash frame and no dip through black.
- **Timing:** Cut in 0 f, or 2 ghost frames at 0.12 and 0.94. Anchor scale jump 1.0-2.5x. Post-cut drift 30 f on E.out. After a flip to dark, wait 12-20 f before any small type. At most one flip per bar and two flip cuts per film.
- **Use when:** Act breaks: problem to answer, public to private, demo to claim. The strongest punctuation on a drop.
- **Avoid when:** A third time in one film; a flip from a static frame with nothing carried; or when the accent field would be the film's second full-frame accent flood.

### Select and retype swap

`tr-select-retype-swap` · accent · energy calm · launch, feature, walkthrough, vertical

A finished headline is selected like text in an editor, the highlight holds for a beat, and on one frame the selection is replaced by a caret that types the next line in the same place.

- **Build:** Set both lines left-aligned in the same font, size and baseline, with line A rendered as per-character spans. The selection is a highlight rect 1.15 em tall from the ascender line: C.ink on paper with the covered glyphs switched to C.paper, or C.white with C.ink glyphs on an ink stage. Its left edge jumps one word leftward every 2-3 f, from the last word to the first, decided with fd and placed from measureTracked prefix widths; for a select-all it covers the line in one frame. The caret sits solid at its left edge. Hold the selection 10-12 f. Then, on one fd frame, remove line A and the highlight together, leave the caret at the line start and put one tick on that frame. Type line B with TypeOn from the same frame (2 f per character on E.type, head fade 4 f, caret blinking once idle). For a centred line, offset it by (full width − typed width)/2, using typeOn().followX through a 6-10 f lag. If the new line's last word is the beat that lands, give it the accent and relax it to ink over 12 f through charStyle.
- **Timing:** Selection 2-3 f per word (or a 1 f select-all), hold 10-12 f, replace on 1 f. Line B types at 2 f per character on E.type (a 20-character line in 40 f), and the caret blinks 30 f on, 30 f off once idle. About 60-75 f in all for a five-word, 20-character pair.
- **Use when:** Products where text is the medium (editors, prompts, writing and AI tools); correcting a claim, where the assumption is selected and overwritten by the answer; two or three headline swaps that should feel authored.
- **Avoid when:** The product has nothing to do with text, lines run past about 40 characters (the typing outlasts the read), or the swap repeats more than three times in a row and turns into a typing demo.

### Stepped column fill

`tr-stepped-column-fill` · accent · energy medium · sting, launch, loop

Columns rise from the bottom edge in a stepped pyramid centred under the hero, spreading outward until they close into one solid field that becomes the next stage behind it.

- **Build:** Split the frame into N equal columns with no gutters, layered below the hero: 12-16 at 1920 px, or the hero's own grid unit so they line up with the bars or pixels of a mark. Column i starts d_i = |i − c| · 2 f after the first, where c is the column under the hero's centre. It rises from the bottom edge with height = H · prog(f, s + d_i, s + d_i + 40, E.smooth), so the tops form a stepped pyramid that widens outward. Fill each column with the next act's stage colour; in its full look every column carries a multi-hue vertical ramp. The columns are flat mask edges on a flat fill with nothing textured on them, so their tops may peak near 76 px/f. The hero keeps a living-hold creep throughout. Where the field rises behind it, draw a second copy of the hero in the opposite tone clipped to the union of the column rects (built by the same geometry function), so the hero flips tone exactly where a column stands behind it, with no fade. On the frame the outermost column fills, swap the column layer for one plate of that colour and land that frame on a downbeat. The hero answers it with scale 1 + 0.02 · hitPulse(f − close, 2, 5), or with its next build step.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Fill every column with one flat colour: the next stage colour, or the accent if this is the film's one accent flood. Or alternate two adjacent lightness steps of one hue from column to column and let them merge into a single tone as the field closes. Never put a ramp inside a column. The full look relies on gradient, orange, purple; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** Each column rises over 40 f on E.smooth (tops peak at about 76 px/f at 1080p). Stagger 2 f per column outward from the centre (7 steps for 14-15 columns), about 54 f in all. The field closes on a downbeat and swaps to one flat plate on the same frame. Hero pulse: attack 2 f, tau 5 f.
- **Use when:** Marks built from bars, steps or pixels; data and analytics products, where the columns read as a chart; stings and loop intros that change the stage colour behind a held hero.
- **Avoid when:** As a general scene change between unrelated shots (it reads as a preset blinds wipe), behind small readable type, or more than once per film.

### Collapse to a dot relay

`tr-dot-relay` · signature · energy medium · launch, feature, sting

The hero collapses into one small dot, or the whole world shrinks into it. The dot, the only thing that survives, opens into the next object: a check ring, an avatar, the mark.

- **Build:** Collapse the hero (a card, a prompt box, or the detached dot of an i) to a 24-52 px dot: width and height go to the dot size and border-radius to 50%, over 4 f on E.in when it feeds a cut, or 16 f on E.out when it snaps and holds. To take the world with it, start 15 f later and scale the world group with k = lmix(1, 0.03, prog(f, s, s + 24, E.contact)) about the dot centre, over the next stage colour. Its corner radius grows to 50% and its mask edge is feathered 40 px; unmount it once it is smaller than the dot. The dot stays at full opacity through the seam (one absolute-frame function, or a hard cut that holds it on the same screen point). Then it opens into the next object: a check ring (stroke-dashoffset 1 → 0 and scale 0.6 → 1 over 8 f on E.out, its label 4 f later), an avatar disc (fill ramps paper → ink linearly over 12 f, icon fading in over the last 4 f), or the mark.
- **Timing:** Collapse: 4 f (E.in, into a cut) or 16 f (E.out, snap and hold). World shrink: 24 f on E.contact for a dot near centre (edges ≤ 66 px/f), or 40 f for a dot near a corner, starting 15 f after the collapse. Reopen over 8-12 f. Any device rotation that follows settles over 28 f on E.out.
- **Use when:** Submit, send, process, receive: actions that mean 'this went in and came out as that'. Also the film's signature device when the mark contains a dot.
- **Avoid when:** The dot would blink out or change size or colour at the seam, or the film already has an implosion seam.

### Giant word punch-out

`tr-giant-word-punch-out` · signature · energy high · launch, sting, vertical, feature

A hard cut lands on an extreme close-up of an oversized word sliding fast and braking, its letters resolving one by one. A second cut jumps out to the whole word at reading size, arriving with wide tracking that slams together.

- **Build:** Close-up act: set the word at 2-2.5x its final size, cropped by the frame, with x = x_end + (x_start − x_end)·0.92^f, starting at no more than 70 px/f. Each letter animates blur 12 → 0 px and colour C.mute → C.ink over 12 f on a 2 f stagger starting at frame 4, so the first letter lands sharp at frame 16, when the pan is down to about 18 px/f. Cut on the act boundary while the word still moves at 13-20 px/f. Wide act: show the whole word, with p = prog(f, 0, 30, E.out) driving scale lmix(1.38, 1, p) and letter-spacing from 0.8 em to its resting track. Add a horizontal-only blur (SVG feGaussianBlur stdDeviation '18 0') set by blurIn(p, 18), opacity 0.5 → 1 over the first 8 f, and colour mixColor(C.accent, C.ink, t) with t going 0.6 → 1 over 17 f. Hold 30-60 f, then exit on E.in over 6-12 f.
- **Timing:** Close-up 18-22 f: starts at ≤ 70 px/f and slows ×0.92 per frame (about 18 px/f by frame 16); letters resolve over 12 f with a 2 f stagger from frame 4. Cut at 13-20 px/f residual speed. Wide entry 30 f on E.out: scale 1.38 → 1, tracking 0.8 em → rest, horizontal blur of 18 px gone by 60% of the move, outer letters ≤ 60 px/f. Colour settles in 17 f. Hold 30-60 f. Exit 6-12 f on E.in.
- **Use when:** A one-word claim or product name that deserves two beats: read it, then see it whole. Vertical cut-downs where one huge word fills the frame.
- **Avoid when:** Lines of more than two words, or words over about 10 letters (the close-up loses the word); or when the next shot needs the word small within a second.

### Portal zoom with aspect morph

`tr-portal-aspect-zoom` · signature · energy high · launch, feature

A window opens in the middle of a solid tile. Tile and window grow faster and faster while the square stretches to 16:9, until the window's interior is the next scene and the tile's border has flown off the edges.

- **Build:** Draw an outer rect in the accent and an inner rect inset by 30% of the outer width and height on each side. The next scene renders inside the inner rect's clip (insetClip) from frame 0, at its final transform. Outer width w = lmix(204, 4800, prog(f, 0, 39, E.linear)), a pure exponential of about ×1.084 per frame, with aspect = mix(1, 16/9, prog(f, 0, 30, E.smooth)) and height = w / aspect. The accent border's outer edges leave the frame near frame 30, and the inner window covers the frame at frame 39, when the clip is dropped. Optional lead-in: the words on either side speed inward under the tile (translateX by their distance over 22 f on E.in, with blurOut). Then the tile turns 90 deg like a cube to bring a plain accent face to the front (CSS 3D box, front = the mark, side = accent at brightness 0.85, over 12 f on E.inOut), and holds that blank face 6 f before the window opens. Keep text out until the window has filled; the next scene's labels rise in as the border clears.
- **Timing:** Lead-in: converge 22 f, cube turn 12 f, blank hold 6 f. Portal: 39 f at ×1.084 per frame (border gone by about frame 30, inner window edges ≤ 78 px/f). Aspect 1 → 1.78 over the first 30 f. Next-scene labels start from about frame 30 on a 4-6 f stagger.
- **Use when:** The film's energy peak and act break, going inside the product, when the mark or app icon is a tile.
- **Avoid when:** The accent has already flooded the frame once (the tile border is a brief accent flood), or another zoom-through sits in the same act.

### Scale-through cut

`tr-scale-through-cut` · signature · energy high · launch, sting, feature, loop

An object shrinks faster and faster toward a fixed point, the film cuts, and a matching object appears much larger on the same point and keeps shrinking as it brakes, so one pull-back runs through two different worlds. The mirror version swells into the cut and opens on an undersized object that grows.

- **Build:** Choose an anchor screen point and keep both objects centred on it within ±30 px (fixed sx, sy in an anchor-camera Shot, or transform-origin on the anchor). Outgoing: k = lmix(1, 0.75, prog(f, T − 20, T, E.in)), so the last frame shrinks about 7.8%; cut on an act boundary. Incoming: the same subject in a new medium (3D render to flat map, device to flat UI, brand card to product world) with k = lmix(1.8, 1, prog(f, 0, 40, E.out)). Its first frame shrinks about 8.4%, so scale velocity is continuous in log space. For a related mark shown as a frame-filling macro, use k = 1 + (S0 − 1)·0.84^f from S0 = 8-9 and snap to 1 once |1 − k| < 0.01. Push version: the hero swells 1 → 1.22 on E.in over the last 16-24 f while the rest of the frame dims (brightness 1 → 0.6 on a dark stage), and the next shot opens at 0.8 and grows to 1 over 30 f on E.out.
- **Timing:** Exit: 16-24 f on E.in to 0.70-0.80 (last frame −7 to −9% per frame). Cut on a downbeat. Entry: 1.7-2.0x → 1 over 30-40 f on E.out (first frame −8 to −9%), or an 8-9x macro shrinking toward rest ×0.84 per frame and settled by about 30 f. Anchor drift ≤ 30 px. Push variant: +20-25% over 16-24 f, then 0.8 → 1 over 30 f.
- **Use when:** Changing medium or world while keeping the subject: 3D to flat, device to UI, brand card to product, a mark coming back as a macro. Also hero pull-backs at act changes.
- **Avoid when:** The two objects cannot share a centre point, or both sides are calm; a scale jump without matched scale velocity reads as a jump cut. Use it at most twice per film.

## Camera

The camera is one transform on one world container (src/lib/camera.ts). A shot frames a world point at a screen point at scale k, and lc() blends shots with k in log space, so a zoom keeps an even perceived speed and the subject travels a straight line. What makes camera work feel expensive is the speed profile more than the path. Moves arrive fast and brake (E.out, E.cam), cruise at 3 px/f or less under readable copy, and leave by accelerating over the last 18-24 f into a cut on the fastest frame, ending at 13-47 px/f, and the incoming shot is already moving when it opens. Hero moves are 2-3x pushes over 60-67 f on E.smooth, peaking around 4-5% scale per frame, with the caption starting in the last 25% of the move so the text and the settle land together. No hold is ever dead: a 0.04-0.07%/f creep or a 0.3-1.5 px/f drift runs under every read longer than about 30 f. Keep camera speed under 60-80 px/f at the frame edge, render anything above 12 px/f with the motion-blur pass (--blur), keep roll under 11 deg and give each act one rotation axis.

### Breathing zoom between interactions

`cam-breathing-zoom` · workhorse · energy calm · launch, feature, walkthrough

After a reveal the camera slowly pulls back, coasts through a stop and turns smoothly into a slow push that lands on the next interaction, so the frame breathes across a whole act.

- **Build:** Drive only k, from a keyframed zoom rate rather than from poses: rate(i) = interpolate(i, [s0, s0 + 72, s0 + 108, s0 + 168], [-0.0025, 0, 0.0014, 0.0011], {extrapolateLeft: 'clamp', extrapolateRight: 'clamp'}) with linear interpolation, and k = k0 * Math.exp(sum of rate(i) for i = s0..f), computed in a pure loop every frame with no state kept between renders. Put ax, ay on the element the next interaction touches, so the zoom pivots on it and it holds its screen position. Keyframe the rate so it crosses zero rather than resting there: |rate| may stay under 0.0002 for no more than 12 f. Close the act with a short exhale under the final hold: k x lmix(1, 0.94, prog(f, T, T + 60, E.out)).
- **Timing:** Pull after a reveal: -0.25%/f falling to 0 over 72 f (about -9% total). Push into the next interaction: 0 rising to +0.14%/f over 36 f, about +6% within 60 f of the zero crossing; table and list acts run +0.03 to +0.17%/f (about +6.6% total). Rate keyframes 36-90 f apart, linear. Exhale x0.94 over 60 f on E.out.
- **Use when:** Dashboard, analytics or table acts of 4-10 s with several interactions in one framing, where cutting would cost orientation.
- **Avoid when:** Shots shorter than about 90 f, acts that already move pose to pose with big pushes, or a scrolling feed (a zoom on a moving list reads as wobble).

### Detail first, then pull back

`cam-detail-first-pullback` · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature, walkthrough

A shot opens tight on the one thing that matters (giant prompt words, a chart counting up, a status pill) with no chrome, then the camera pulls back to show it sitting in the full window.

- **Build:** Anchor on the hero element (ax, ay at its centre, or at the caret for typed words) and hold k = 1.6-1.7 while its value animates; for giant type, pan sx after the caret at 2-4 px/f. Then pull with cam = lc(TIGHT, CONTEXT, prog(f, a, a + 52, E.cam)), so the hero barely moves on screen while the frame widens around it, and fade out any partly cropped edge tiles over the 16 f before the pull so they don't pop at the frame edge. Bring the context in during the pull: window chrome and neighbouring panels fade 0 -> 1 over 30 f from 20% of the move, optionally behind <RackFocus t={1 - prog(f, a, a + 30, E.smooth)} blur={10}>. The hero card can tip pitch 0 -> 6 -> 0 deg and yaw 0 -> -4 -> 0 deg as it docks into its slot. For an end-of-film re-establish, open the tight frame soft (RackFocus t = 1, blur 6) and resolve it over the pull.
- **Timing:** Tight hold 24-52 f while the value animates. Pull k 1.6-1.7 -> 1.0 over 52 f on E.cam (peak about 4%/f at 27%), or a settle back over 56-80 f on E.out (half done by f10-12). Edge tiles out over 16 f before the pull, context in over 30 f, 3D tip peaking mid-move. Re-establish k 2.2 -> 1.0 with focus over 60 f on E.cam (peak about 5.6%/f).
- **Use when:** Result reveals, analytics, prompts and input moments where the value should land before the load of the full UI; breaking up a repeated card formula; re-establishing the whole product after a run of close details.
- **Avoid when:** The product hasn't been seen yet and the tight frame stays unrecognisable for long (keep the tight hold under 52 f), or the wider frame adds nothing new.

### Fit-to-content follow

`cam-fit-bounds-follow` · workhorse · energy calm · feature, walkthrough, launch, vertical

As a route, graph or plan builds, the camera widens just enough to keep every piece that matters in frame, so the shot opens close on the first node and ends on the whole structure.

- **Build:** Each frame, collect the world boxes that must stay visible: the origin, every item revealed so far (with its half-size) and the travelling head if there is one, its box stretched ahead along its direction of travel by 18% of the frame converted to world px at the current k. Turn their bounding box plus a 12% frame margin into a target shot: ax, ay at the box centre, sx, sy at frame centre (or shifted off the caption band), and k = min((W - 2 x SAFE.x) / boxW, (H - 2 x SAFE.y) / boxH), clamped between the opening k and a floor that keeps the smallest label at TYPE.ui size (24 px) on screen; when the floor binds, let the oldest items leave the frame rather than shrinking type. Smooth it as a pure function of the frame: loop i from the shot's first frame to f, keep lnT = min(lnT, ln kTarget(i)) so the zoom never pumps back in while the set grows, and step c += (target - c) x 0.07 for ax, ay and ln k, clamping each step to 1.2% of zoom and 12 px of screen travel, then feed exp(c.lnk) to the anchor camera so the widening keeps an even pace in log space. When the structure is complete, either hold the full fit as the payoff under a cam-living-hold pull or punch in on the destination with lc(FOLLOW, DEST, prog(f, e, e + 54, E.cam)).
- **Timing:** Follow coefficient 0.06-0.08 per frame (time constant 12-16 f); zoom at most 1.2%/f, centre at most 12 px/f on screen (--blur if the corners ever pass 12 px/f). Margin 12% of the frame, 18% lead on the head's side. Nodes 20-40 f apart give a steady widening rather than steps. Closing punch-in 48-60 f on E.cam, or a hold with a -0.08%/f pull.
- **Use when:** Pipelines, agent plans, org charts, dependency or network graphs and routes that build piece by piece, where the first node needs close-up legibility and the payoff is the whole shape.
- **Avoid when:** The finished structure already fits one comfortable framing, a single moving lead is the whole story (cam-lead-follow), or the full structure cannot fit with 24 px labels (split it into chapters with cuts instead).

### Follow the lead dot

`cam-lead-follow` · workhorse · energy medium · walkthrough, feature, vertical, launch

A small lead (a progress dot, a travelling packet, a drawing line's head) moves through the layout and the camera follows it with a soft lag, never quite stopping, so the viewer always knows where to look.

- **Build:** Make the follow a pure function of the frame: loop i from the shot's first frame to f, updating c += (lead(i) - target - c) * 0.08 (target is the lead's desired screen position, for example 40% of the frame height), plus a constant 2 px/f drift in the direction of travel; never keep state between renders. Feed c into the anchor camera (ax, ay on the lead's world point) and draw the lead as a flat dot in the one accent colour with no halo. Reveal each step row as the lead passes it: opacity prog(f, tPass, tPass + 12, E.smooth) with a 12 px rise through arrive(). At a corner, let the lead turn first and the camera's lag carry the turn; at the destination, punch in (cam-punch-in-insert) or ease to rest on E.rest.
- **Timing:** Lag coefficient 0.08 per frame (time constant about 12 f). Peak 12.5 px/f, residual drift 2-2.5 px/f, never 0. Step rows reveal over 12 f as the lead passes. Bumps between steps about 40 f.
- **Use when:** Agent progress, pipelines, timelines and journeys across a map: any story told by one thing moving through a layout.
- **Avoid when:** The lead moves faster than about 20 px/f for long stretches (the lag lets it escape the frame), or the whole layout fits in one framing.

### Isolating push into one item

`cam-isolating-push` · workhorse · energy medium · feature, walkthrough, launch

The camera pushes into one row, card or column while everything around it fades, dims or slides off the edges, picking a single thread out of a busy layout.

- **Build:** Anchor the push on the chosen item and pick a preset. Dive: k x lmix(1, 4, prog(f, a, a + 80, E.smooth)) while sibling rows fade from 1 to 0 opacity over 20 f from a; as the push ends, the item's icon dims to 0.3 and the next state swaps in on a whole frame (fd), a zoom-through without a cut. Accelerate-through: k x lmix(1, 1.25, prog(f, a, a + 60, E.in)) while the surroundings fade to the background colour over 16 f, then cut or swap on the peak frame. Eject: k x lmix(1, 1.48, prog(f, a, a + 30, E.smooth)) and then +4% over 60 f on E.linear, the flanking words taking blurOut text blur up to 6 px once they pass 80% of the half-width on their way off frame. Gentle focus: wrap the side columns in RackFocus (t 0 -> 1, blur 8) and dim them to 0.6 opacity while the parent pushes x1.06 over 18 f on E.smooth.
- **Timing:** Dive 80 f, x4 on E.smooth (peak about 5%/f), sibling fades 20 f, swap on the last frame. Accelerate-through 60 f, x1.25 on E.in, surround fade 16 f. Eject 30 f, x1.48 on E.smooth, then +4% over 60 f. Focus pull 18 f, x1.06, blur 8 px, opacity 0.6, running straight into the next move.
- **Use when:** Choosing one result from a list of parallel processes, moving from a typographic act into a UI close-up without a cut, or steering the eye to where the next action will happen.
- **Avoid when:** The item is still too small to read at 4x, or the surrounding layout carries information the viewer still needs.

### Layered parallax truck

`cam-parallax-truck` · workhorse · energy calm · launch, feature, walkthrough

The camera trucks sideways across a scene split into two or three depth planes: the background barely moves, the subject moves with the camera and a near element slides past faster, so a flat layout reads as space.

- **Build:** Split the world into at most three layers in one AbsoluteFill (background, subject and an optional foreground), each with its own transform, and drive a single camera translation x = D * prog(f, a, a + N, E.cam), or a constant 1-3 px/f drift for a hold. Apply it at 0.3x to the background, 1.0x to the subject and 1.6x to the foreground, and scale the background to 1.08 so its slower travel never reveals an edge. Keep the subject's readable text under 20 px/f and let the text-free foreground carry the fast motion, which the blur pass smears above 12 px/f.
- **Timing:** Truck 200-400 px over 90-120 f on E.cam (subject peak about 12 px/f for 300 px over 105 f), or a 1-3 px/f drift. Plane factors 0.3 / 1.0 / 1.6. Background overscan 5-8%.
- **Use when:** Hero product shots and feature cards that need depth without 3D, and slow establishing moves.
- **Avoid when:** Dense UI walkthroughs where the eye has to track one control, or any scene with more than three planes (it starts to look like a parallax demo).

### Living hold creep

`cam-living-hold` · workhorse · energy calm · any

Under every hold the frame keeps a barely visible push, pull or sideways drift, so no shot sits dead while the viewer reads.

- **Build:** Set the anchor camera's ax, ay on the focal element so the creep pivots there. Multiply k by breath(prog(f, holdStart, holdEnd, E.linear) * (1 - nextMove), amount), where amount = 0.0005 x the hold length in frames and nextMove is the next move's 0..1 progress, so the next move releases the creep with no velocity step. Push on proof and result shots, pull (negative amount) on busy or chaotic boards, and use a tiny creep on the end card. For type or a single card, drift sideways instead: with g = f - holdStart, sx = sx0 - v * (g - 20 * (1 - Math.exp(-g / 20))), which leaves the seam at zero velocity and reaches v after about 60 f. Keep every layer the camera carries static inside the one transform, so nothing stair-steps on the pixel grid during the creep.
- **Timing:** Scale creep 0.04-0.07%/f (+2.4 to +4.2%/s), at most 0.1%/f in a 40-60 f tail after a big push. Pulls about -0.08%/f. End card 0.0125%/f. Lateral drift 0.3-0.5 px/f for UI and cards, 1.5-3 px/f for big display type. E.linear once at speed, with a 20 f exponential ease-in from a seam. Released over the next move's own ease.
- **Use when:** Any hold longer than about 30 f: reading a caption, watching a counter, a UI state sitting after an action, the end card.
- **Avoid when:** A designed freeze of at most 15 f on a silence, or a shot where a big camera move or a travelling cursor already supplies the life. Never stack a creep on top of a punch-in drift on the same axis.

### Pull-back that lands an event

`cam-pull-lands-event` · workhorse · energy calm · walkthrough, feature, launch

A long, gentle pull-back runs from a close-up to the full view, and as it decelerates the next UI event (a modal, labels, a caption) starts, so it lands together with the camera's settle.

- **Build:** Pull with lc(CLOSE, WIDE, prog(f, a, a + 108, E.smooth)), where WIDE.k is about 0.56 x CLOSE.k. Start the event at a + round(0.72 x 108) = a + 78. A modal arrives on SPR.firm from 0.92 to 1 scale, opacity up over 8 f, landing within 4 f of a + 108. Captions start no earlier than a + 81 (the last 25% of the move) and no later than a + 114, while labels and values can type in through the whole pull. After the settle, hand over to a breath creep instead of a dead lock.
- **Timing:** 108 f on E.smooth, zoom x0.56, peak about 1.5%/f (about 24 px/f) mid-move. Event starts at 72% of the move; the SPR.firm modal settles within 4 f of the camera. Captions start in the last 25% of the move or up to 6 f after it.
- **Use when:** Walkthroughs and single-take films that move pose to pose, and any long move whose ending would otherwise be a dead beat.
- **Avoid when:** Short or fast moves under 50 f, where an event in the tail just competes with the motion, and the finale, where the lockup needs a clean frame.

### Punch-in insert on the same render

`cam-punch-in-insert` · workhorse · energy medium · feature, walkthrough, launch, vertical

A hard cut jumps from the wide view to a 2-2.5x on-axis close-up, or to a 3-4.5x macro of the exact control being used, while every animation keeps running, then cuts back out.

- **Build:** Lay the product out once and define two Shots on it: WIDE, and INSERT with ax, ay on the control's centre (or the cursor tip), sx, sy at frame centre or on a third, and k = 2.0-2.5 for an on-axis punch or 3-4.5 for a macro insert. Switch on a whole frame, cam = fd(f) >= CUT ? INSERT : WIDE, and keep the cursor path, hover lift, typing and counters on their own clocks so they carry on mid-motion across the cut; place the cursor with toScreen() of the active shot. Never hold the insert still: give it a 1-2 px/f linear drift along the action's direction, or open it with a decaying offset (+8% of frame width, decayed on E.out over 96 f). Build the UI as live layout at its final size, never as an upscaled bitmap, so text stays sharp at k = 4.5, and cut back out on the next action or at the peak of an exit move.
- **Timing:** Wide holds 20-64 f before an on-axis punch (90-220 f when it establishes the scene). On-axis close-up about 60 f. Macro insert 46-74 f, up to 76-154 f when it carries an action. Scale 2.0-2.5 on-axis, 3-4.5 macro. Drift inside the insert 1-2 px/f linear (3-5 px/f for a 2.5x component slide). Cut on the click, keystroke or beat, with no transition frames. Chain 2-3 punches on consecutive beats for a staccato build.
- **Use when:** Small UI actions that need hero weight (send, picking a date, a chip), long walkthroughs that need their visual scale reset, and a wide/close rhythm that keeps both context and legibility.
- **Avoid when:** The UI doesn't hold up at 3-4.5x, or the close-up isn't obviously the same place (keep the cut on-axis or anchored to the cursor, or it reads as a jump).

### Reactive reframe

`cam-reframe-to-subject` · workhorse · energy calm · walkthrough, feature, launch

When something new appears (a popover, a result, the hero icon), the camera glides a few hundred pixels and pushes in slightly until it sits where the eye wants it.

- **Build:** On the event cue c, blend from the current camera into a reframed Shot: cam = lc(CURRENT, REFRAMED, prog(f, c + 4, c + 4 + N, E.glide)). REFRAMED puts ax, ay on the new element's centre and sx, sy at frame centre (or offset to leave room for its caption), with k = CURRENT.k x 1.05-1.23. Starting 4 f after the element begins to appear lets the content lead and the camera follow. The element arrives on its own curve; a popover, for example, scales 0.05 -> 1 from the click point over 10 f on E.out, its opacity rising over the first 4 f. To centre a hero after a punch-in, use the same blend over 22 f with position and k on one curve, so the subject arrives on a long tail.
- **Timing:** Popover reframe: starts 4 f after the pop, settles in 20-40 f on E.glide, k x1.05. Hero centring: 22 f on E.glide, 150-350 px of travel, peak about 22 px/f at 31% of the move, k 1.0 -> 1.23.
- **Use when:** After any UI event that changes what matters on screen, or after a punch-in that left the hero off-centre.
- **Avoid when:** Every small UI change (keep it for the ones that matter), or an element that already appears near frame centre (a move under 40 px reads as a twitch).

### Seamless loop drift

`cam-seamless-loop-orbit` · workhorse · energy calm · loop, vertical

In a looping clip the camera drifts along a slow, closed figure-eight (a little sideways, a little up, breathing in and out) and returns exactly to its first frame, so the loop has no seam.

- **Build:** With L the loop length in frames and u = 2 * Math.PI * f / L, set sx = sx0 + 32 * Math.sin(u), sy = sy0 + 12 * Math.sin(2 * u) and k = k0 * Math.exp(0.03 * Math.sin(u + 1.2)) on the anchor camera, plus yaw = 3 * Math.sin(u) deg for a 3D product. Every term completes a whole number of cycles in L, so frame L equals frame 0 exactly and the motion never stops (the speed peaks around 0.6 px/f at L = 360). Time the content's own loop to L or a divisor of it.
- **Timing:** Loop L = 240-480 f. Amplitudes 24-40 px sideways and 10-16 px vertically (at twice the frequency), zoom +-3%, yaw +-3 deg. Peak speed about 0.5-0.8 px/f.
- **Use when:** Feature loops, background clips and vertical loops that replay endlessly.
- **Avoid when:** Linear films with cuts (use a living hold instead), or loops shorter than about 4 s, where the drift turns into a visible wobble.

### Zoom-out hop between areas

`cam-zoom-out-hop` · workhorse · energy medium · walkthrough, feature, launch

To travel between two distant parts of one product, the camera eases back as it sets off, crosses at a wider framing that shows where it is going, and pushes back in as it arrives.

- **Build:** Keyframe Shots A and B at the same k on the two areas, blend cam = lc(A, B, prog(f, a, a + N, E.smooth)), then multiply cam.k by dip(prog(f, a, a + N, E.linear), depth) from src/lib/camera.ts. Driving the dip on linear time instead of on the pan's eased progress is the point: the pull-back starts before the pan gathers speed and the push-in finishes after it slows, so the widest framing coincides with the fastest travel and the frame edge peaks 28-40% lower than the same pan without the hop. Set depth = clamp(1 - 0.7 x W / (A.k x D), 0.15, 0.45), where D is the world distance between the anchors, so both areas share the frame at mid-move, and size N = A.k x D / 34 frames at depth 0.45 (A.k x D / 25 for a shallow 0.15-0.25 hop, interpolated between) to keep the edge under about 60 px/f. Start B's caption in the last 25% of the move and render with --blur.
- **Timing:** Pan on E.smooth over N = A.k x D / 34 f at depth 0.45, or A.k x D / 25 at 0.15-0.25: about 76 f for 2,600 px at k = 1, 106 f for 1,800 px at k = 2, 72 f for 1,800 px at k = 1. Dip on linear time, depth 0.15-0.45, its zoom rate peaking at 1-2.6%/f a quarter of the way in and out. Frame edge at most about 60 px/f. Beyond about 120 f, cut instead (cam-offframe-whip-relay or cam-punch-in-insert).
- **Use when:** Single-take and walkthrough films moving between two areas of one surface more than about a frame width apart (sidebar to canvas, one dashboard panel to another), where the viewer should see how they relate.
- **Avoid when:** Areas less than about a frame width apart (cam-reframe-to-subject), a cursor that should lead the move (cam-cursor-whip-orbit), or a wide view that is cluttered or unfinished, since the hop shows it.

### Crane down with a delayed push

`cam-crane-push` · accent · energy calm · walkthrough, feature, launch

The camera tilts down the page past the chart to the detail cards while a slow push-in builds behind it, as if the operator were leaning in to read.

- **Build:** Sum two vertical components on the anchor camera's sy: a main move of about 240 px on prog(f, a, a + 64, E.smooth), and a 300 px drift on prog(f, a + 40, a + 220, E.rest) that overlaps it, so the motion never stalls and fades out slowly. Multiply k by lmix(1, 1.22, prog(f, a + 40, a + 240, E.rest)) so the push starts 40 f late and peaks while the tilt is decelerating. Put ax on the column the viewer will read so the push doesn't drift sideways.
- **Timing:** Main tilt 64 f on E.smooth, about 240 px, peak about 10 px/f mid-move. Drift 300 px from a + 40 to a + 220 on E.rest (peaks near 5.8 px/f, under 0.5 px/f by the end). Push +22% from a + 40 to a + 240 on E.rest, peak about +0.35%/f near a + 98.
- **Use when:** Moving down a long page or dashboard from the overview to the detail that matters.
- **Avoid when:** Pages too short to travel 500 px or more, or vertical formats where the push crops the column.

### Cursor-led whip orbit

`cam-cursor-whip-orbit` · accent · energy high · walkthrough, feature, launch

Following a cursor that leads the way to the next panel, the camera swings fast across the product, yawing to show the slab's thick edge and rolling slightly.

- **Build:** Keyframe A (the current pose) and B, with ax, ay on the destination panel, yaw about +24 deg, roll about -10 deg and k = 0.77 x A.k, and blend lc(A, B, prog(f, a, a + 74, E.whip)) through camera(shot, 2400). Move the cursor in screen space along cursorArc(start, dest, prog(f, a - 5, a + 69, E.whip), 0.2), so it leads the camera by about 5 f and seems to drag it, projecting its destination with the same transform maths. Give the world container a 24-40 px side face (a darker tone of the surface, hinged on the right edge with rotateY(90deg)) so the yaw reveals the product's thickness. Render with --blur, since the peak is near 47 px/f.
- **Timing:** 74 f on E.whip, peak about 47 px/f at around 40% of the move. Yaw 0 -> 24 deg, roll 0 -> -10 deg, zoom x0.77. The cursor leads by 4-6 f.
- **Use when:** Moving between two distant panels of one product in a single-take or walkthrough film, where a cut would lose the spatial relationship.
- **Avoid when:** There is no cursor or other lead to motivate it (an unmotivated whip reads as a flourish), or the act already uses yaw for something else.

### Directional impact kick

`cam-impact-kick` · accent · energy high · launch, sting, feature, vertical

On a true impact (a card landing, a lock-in, a slam) the whole frame jolts a few pixels in the direction of the hit and pushes a hair closer, then settles within a fifth of a second.

- **Build:** On the impact cue c, add a decaying jolt to the anchor camera: sx += dir.x * 8 * hitPulse(f - c, 1, 4) and sy += dir.y * 8 * hitPulse(f - c, 1, 4), where dir is the unit vector of the incoming object's travel, and multiply k by 1 + 0.015 * hitPulse(f - c, 2, 5). Take c from the contact frame in src/lib/sync.ts so sound and picture peak together, pair it with squash() on the landing object, and never add roll. Use it at most 2-3 times per film, and only where something truly lands.
- **Timing:** Jolt 6-10 px, attack 1 f, tau 4 f (gone in about 25 f). Push +1.5%, attack 2 f, tau 5 f. At most 2-3 per film.
- **Use when:** True landings and lock-ins: a heavy object slamming into a slot, or a statement locking together on a hit.
- **Avoid when:** Every beat or tick (that makes a shake, not a hit), soft UI arrivals, or mid camera move (it fights the move's ease).

### Extrude then crash in

`cam-crash-zoom-through` · accent · energy high · launch, sting

An object grows toward camera (a disc extruding into a tall cylinder) and the camera slams into it, hard-cutting to its interior while still rushing forward.

- **Build:** Extrude first: the object's scaleY goes 1 -> 2.5 over 12 f on E.in, with transform-origin at its base, so it accelerates toward camera. Overlapping the last 8 f of the extrusion, push the anchor camera into its face with k = k0 * Math.exp(0.64 * ((f - s) / 24) ** 3) over 24 f, then hard-cut on the last frame to the interior shot. Open the interior already moving: k starts at 1.76x its rest value and lmix-decays over 40 f on E.outSoft, while the tube walls converge on a vanishing point. Draw the walls as two or three flat, crisp-edged steps of the object's own colour (darker at the rim, lighter toward the vanishing point), with no bloom, halo or bright blurred edges. Render with --blur so the frames either side of the cut streak; spreading the crash across the cut keeps the frame edge under about 80 px/f.
- **Timing:** Extrusion 12 f on E.in. Camera push 24 f on a cubic ease-in, x1.9, reaching about 8%/f (about 77 px/f at the frame edge) on the cut frame. Interior entry x1.76 -> rest over 40 f on E.outSoft.
- **Use when:** A violent spatial jump into the product at the energy peak of a launch film or sting.
- **Avoid when:** Calm films, any second use in the same film, and readable text on either side of the cut.

### Push-in with a roll swing

`cam-push-dutch-roll` · accent · energy medium · launch, feature

The camera dives into one corner of the UI, rolls a few degrees off level mid-dive like a hand-steered move, and rolls back to level as it lands.

- **Build:** Blend lc(WIDE, TARGET, t) with t = prog(f, a, a + 60, E.smooth), where TARGET has ax, ay on the corner element, sx, sy at that element's current screen point (so it stays put while the frame grows around it) and k = 2.09 x WIDE.k. Add the roll on its own curve: roll = t < 0.57 ? mix(0, -4, E.smooth(t / 0.57)) : mix(-4, -0.3, E.smooth((t - 0.57) / 0.43)), passed as the Shot's roll so camera() keeps it rigid outside any tilt. For a tilted landing, ease pitch 0 -> 8 deg over the last 24 f. Keep |roll| under 11 deg.
- **Timing:** 60 f; zoom 1 -> 2.09 on E.smooth in log space, peak about 3.5%/f mid-move. Roll 0 -> -4 deg by 57% of the move, back to -0.3 deg at the end, each segment E.smooth. Optional pitch 0 -> 8 deg over the last 24 f.
- **Use when:** A push that would otherwise feel mechanical: diving into a settings corner, a sidebar or a detail panel.
- **Avoid when:** Next to another rolled or tilted move in the same act (one rotation axis per act), or on moves shorter than 40 f, where the roll reads as a wobble.

### Dolly surge with a foreground pass

`cam-dolly-surge-foreground` · signature · energy high · launch, sting

The camera surges from a wide shot into a 3x medium close-up, with most of the travel in half a second, and at the fastest moment a near object rushes past the lens before a long, slow creep.

- **Build:** Animate k = lmix(1, 3.1, prog(f, a, a + 67, E.smooth)) around the subject (or translateZ of a preserve-3d stage under perspective 2400px), multiplied by lmix(1, 1.04, prog(f, a + 47, a + 107, E.linear)) so the +4% creep starts 20 f before the push ends and the motion never stalls. Put one foreground object on its own layer above the world, 300-400 px off the anchor, and project it with a stronger scale, kFg = k ** 1.6 (screen position = sx + (p - ax) * kFg), so it grows and slides out past the frame edge around the push's peak frame (about a + 33); keep its crossing at 60-80 px/f or less. The motion-blur pass (--blur) streaks it, so never fake the streak with a CSS blur. Optional mid and far layers at 1.0x and 0.3x of the camera's translation add parallax.
- **Timing:** Push 67 f on E.smooth, zoom 1 -> 3.1, 10-90% of the travel in about 28 f, peak about 4.8%/f near a + 33. Creep +4% over 60 f on E.linear from a + 47. Foreground exits on the peak at 60-80 px/f or less, smeared by the blur pass.
- **Use when:** Opening a launch film into a 3D or layered world, or a sting that dives from an overview into the hero object.
- **Avoid when:** Flat UI with no depth layers (nothing to pass the lens), or calm walkthroughs.

### Fly-through of a depth field

`cam-z-field-flythrough` · signature · energy high · launch, sting, feature

Dozens of flat screens or tokens float at different depths and the camera travels forward through them: near ones swell and slide off the frame edges, far ones barely drift, until the move lands square on one hero screen.

- **Build:** Seed 24-36 items with rand(i): x within +-2200 px, y within +-1300 px, z from 800 to 6000 px ahead of the start, keeping a 420 x 260 px corridor around the camera's path empty so nothing hits the lens head-on, and place the hero at (0, 0, Zh), sized in world px at the size it should read. Project each item yourself rather than through preserve-3d: with F = 1200 and d = z - camZ(f), draw it as a flat layer at translate(W/2 + (x - camX) x F/d, H/2 + (y - camY) x F/d) scale(F/d), z-ordered far to near, and unmount it once d < 300. Multiply each item's opacity by a far fade-in (0 -> 1 as d falls from 6000 to 4800) and by a speed gate, clamp((70 - v) / 20), where v is its screen travel since f - 1 (project it again with camZ(f - 1)), so whatever rushes past the lens dissolves instead of breaking the speed cap; sink distant items into the stage with an overlay of the stage colour at 0.5 x clamp((d - 1200) / 4000) instead of blurring 30 layers. For the dive, camZ = (Zh - F) x prog(f, a, a + N, E.cam) lands the hero at exactly scale 1, sharp and readable; for a breadth drift that ends in a cut, pull back 1200 px on E.out, cruise forward at 4 px/f with camY sinking 1.5 px/f, then ramp out over the last 18-24 f on E.contact and hard-cut on the fastest frame (tr-velocity-handoff-cut). Tokens may also turn slowly on rotateY (up to 10 deg/s each), and the whole move renders with --blur.
- **Timing:** Dive: 150-180 f on E.cam through 4,000 px of depth (Zh = 5200, F = 1200), landing the hero at scale 1 on the long settle. Drift: pull-back 40 f on E.out, cruise 90-120 f, exit ramp 18-24 f. Speed gate between 50 and 70 px/f; far fade over 1,200 px of depth; about 12-16 items on screen at once. The hero's copy starts once it moves under 20 px/f.
- **Use when:** Proving breadth (a whole platform, hundreds of templates, every integration) in 3-4 s without explaining any single screen; opening into a layered world; arriving on the one screen the next act is about.
- **Avoid when:** Items must be read in flight, there are fewer than about 15 of them (the field looks sparse), the film is flat with no depth language, or lc-swarm-cluster-burst already spends the film's breadth crescendo.

### Hero push with a 3D turn

`cam-hero-push-yaw` · signature · energy high · launch, feature

From a wide view of the whole app, one continuous move pushes 2.5x into a single panel while yawing, so the panel turns toward the viewer and an empty side of the frame opens for the caption.

- **Build:** Build one scene on one world container with two Shots: WIDE (k = 1, flat) and HERO, with ax, ay on the panel centre, sx at 0.67 x width (0.33 for a panel on the left), k = 2.56, yaw 24-30 deg and pitch about 5 deg, rendered through camera(shot, 2400). Blend with lc(WIDE, HERO, prog(f, a, a + 60, E.smooth)); k already lerps in log space, so the push keeps an even perceived speed. Start the caption in the void at a + 45 (the last 25% of the move) so the word reveal and the camera settle read as one gesture, then keep the hold alive with breath(prog(f, a + 60, next, E.linear), 0.025) instead of a dead lock. Check that the panel's smallest meaningful text is at least 22 px on screen at k = 2.56, and render with --blur for the peak.
- **Timing:** 60 f on E.smooth, 10-90% of progress between 29% and 71% of the move, peak about 4.5%/f scale (around 47 px/f on screen) at 50%. Zoom 1 -> 2.56; yaw 0 -> 24-30 deg and pitch 0 -> 5 deg on the same curve. Caption starts at 75% of the move. Hold breath +2.5%.
- **Use when:** The film's energy peak: the one feature that needs both spatial orientation and close-up legibility, or a scene change inside a single-take film.
- **Avoid when:** More than once per film, or on a lone card with no surrounding app (the turn needs a world to orient against). Keep each act on its own rotation axis.

### Off-frame whip relay

`cam-offframe-whip-relay` · signature · energy high · walkthrough, feature, launch

The cursor accelerates up and out of frame, the camera whips down the product while it's hidden, and the cursor re-enters from the top as a fast streak that brakes onto its target.

- **Build:** Three overlapping keyed parts. Cursor exit: y on E.in toward -10% of the frame height from a to a + 24, after which it stays off screen for 12 f. Camera: sy travels the product distance D (900-1400 px) on E.smooth over N = 2.86 x D / 75 frames (34-54 f), centred on a + 30 so its fastest stretch falls inside the hidden window and peaks at about 75 px/f. Cursor entry: from -10% to the target over 36 f from a + 36 on E.out, entering at about 63 px/f; while it moves faster than 12 px/f, draw a trailing rounded capsule behind the tip, 0.6 x speed long at 40% opacity, and let the blur pass handle the camera.
- **Timing:** Cursor exit 24 f on E.in (2.5 -> 15 px/f). Off screen 12 f. Camera 34-54 f on E.smooth centred on the hidden window, peak 60-75 px/f. Cursor re-enters at about 63 px/f and brakes over 36 f on E.out (speed ratio about 0.92 per frame).
- **Use when:** A big spatial jump within one product (top bar to bottom bar, one page to another) that should feel like a match-on-action without a cut.
- **Avoid when:** Films without a cursor, or destinations less than about one frame height away (a plain reframe is enough).

### Pull out from inside the object

`cam-inside-object-pullout` · signature · energy medium · launch, sting, feature, vertical
