The shot opens on what reads as a full-bleed colour field or a statement card, and one long pull reveals it was the face of a small object (an app icon, a card, a screen, the mark) sitting among its neighbours.

- **Build:** Lay the object out at true size inside its real context (a dock, a grid, a window, the lockup) in the anchor camera's world, with its face, corner radius and shadow as live layout in world units, never a bitmap. Shot FACE puts ax, ay on the object's centre at frame centre with k0 = 1.04 x max(W / objectW, H / objectH), so its edges sit just outside the frame (about 13.3 for a 144 px icon at 1920 wide), and Shot CONTEXT frames the object at k = 1 in its slot. Blend cam = lc(FACE, CONTEXT, prog(f, a, a + N, E.dolly)) with N = 25.7 x ln(k0); this caps the log zoom rate at about 6%/f mid-move, so anything entering at the frame corner moves under about 66 px/f, and the corners, the shadow and the neighbours arrive purely by coverage, with no fades of their own. Draw the opening copy on a screen-space overlay at toScreen(cam, centre), scaled by (cam.k / k0) ** 0.46 so it shrinks more slowly than the object, and fade it out on E.smooth while the object's on-screen width falls from 1.3x to 1.0x the copy's width, so it never spills past the edges. Read the face under a cam-living-hold creep before the pull, land with no overshoot, and start the next beat (an icon hop, a wordmark build) within 12 f of the settle.
- **Timing:** Face hold 24-48 f for the read, with a 0.04-0.07%/f creep. Pull from k0 = 8-14 to 1 over N = 25.7 x ln(k0) frames on E.dolly (about 53 f from 8x, 66 f from 13.3x), log rate peaking near 6%/f mid-move and landing at rest. Copy scale tracks k ** 0.46 and fades over the 8-14 f in which the object's width passes 1.3x -> 1.0x the copy width. Anchor travel to the slot under 10 px/f. --blur for frames above 12 px/f.
- **Use when:** Cold opens and hooks where a calm statement or a colour field should turn out to be part of the product (the question was printed on the app icon, the colour was one card in the grid); landing the mark into the final lockup; any reveal whose point is scale.
- **Avoid when:** The face is a photo or bitmap (it falls apart at 8-14x), the context it lands in is not recognisable at a glance, or a scale-through cut or detail-first pull-back has already used the same object. Once per film.

## Typography in motion

Measured type arrives on expo-out moves that cover 30-45% of their travel on the first frame and settle in 12-24 f at 60 fps, staggered 4-10 f per word (20-24 f for a calm one-word-per-beat read). What matters most is the readable moment: a word is either legible from its first frame (40% strength, rising at most 0.6 em at about 14 px/f) or it flies faded and streaked and resolves only once it slows below 20 px/f, and it always lands sharp, with any blur gone by 60% of the move. Colour carries recency: the newest glyph or word arrives in the one accent and relaxes to ink over 12-24 f. Lines never freeze and never jump: layouts are pre-solved or re-centred on a critically damped spring, a landed line tightens 2-3% or drifts 0.3-0.5 px/f, and a hold swells about 6% on an ease-in into the cut. Typing is time-boxed (any length done in about 68 f, half of it visible within 6 f), and the film's one discrete trick (a step edit, a scramble, a letter morph) acts out the copy instead of decorating it.

### Animated line re-break

`ty-line-rebreak-glide` · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature, walkthrough

A centred one-line statement re-breaks into a two-line stack, or back, with every word gliding from its old slot to its new one, so the layout changes without a cut or a jump.

- **Build:** Pre-solve both layouts with measureTracked and baselineOf. Layout A is one centred line; layout B is two centred lines at pitch = lead x size, the block centred on the same point, optionally at a smaller size s_B. Store each word's centre in both. Move each word i as one FLIP: p_i = prog(f, s + 2i, s + 2i + D_i, E.glide), with D_i = clamp(0.15 x travel_i, 30, 48) f; x = mix(xA_i, xB_i, p_i); scale = lmix(1, s_B / s_A, p_i). Give y its own curve, mix(yA_i, yB_i, arrive(prog(f, s + 2i - 4, s + 2i - 4 + D_i, E.outSoft))), so words that change rows drop first and slide second and never pass through a neighbour. Keep travel under 320 px per word: E.glide peaks at about 3x its mean speed, so D = 0.15 x travel holds readable words near 20 px/f (render the blurred master). If a word would travel further, split the line differently or cut. When an insert causes the re-break (an icon popping into a gap), start it 6 f after the insert lands; once settled, drift the block at 0.3 px/f.
- **Timing:** Per word, D = 0.15 x travel, clamped to 30-48 f, on E.glide (peak about 20 px/f, near 30% of the move). y leads x by 4 f on E.outSoft through arrive. Stagger 2 f in the reading order of the new layout. Travel at most 320 px. Starts 6 f after a causing insert. Settled drift 0.3 px/f.
- **Use when:** An inserted icon or a longer word makes a centred line too wide. A headline must stack to free half the frame for a product shot. Returning a stacked headline to a single line for the payoff.
- **Avoid when:** Lines over about 7 words. Re-breaks that carry the hero word far from where it was being read (keep it as the still anchor). More than one re-break per statement. Vertical formats, where a stack is already the default layout.

### Blur-swap rescale

`ty-blur-swap-rescale` · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature, sting, vertical

A big word blurs out and instantly re-forms smaller as the start of the full line, so the type changes scale without a rubbery size tween.

- **Build:** Use two layers and never animate font-size. Old layer: q = prog(f, s, s + 6, E.in), blur = blurOut(q, 12), scale x lmix(1, 0.85, q), opacity to 0 on E.smooth over the same 6 f, still moving in its current direction. New layer from s + 2: p = prog(f, s + 2, s + 16, E.out), scale = lmix(1.25, 1, p), blur = blurIn(p, 12), opacity 0 -> 1 over 6 f; carry any ongoing drift so both layers travel at the same px/f. Optional tracking collapse on the new line: letter-spacing +0.25 em -> the token's tracking over 16 f on E.out, so the small word arrives spread wide and slams together.
- **Timing:** Old out 6 f (E.in, blurOut 12 px); new in 14 f from +2 f (E.out, blurIn 12 px, scale 1.25 -> 1, edges of a 1000 px line about 51 px/f on frame 1); 4 f overlap; typical cap-height change -35%; tracking collapse 16 f E.out.
- **Use when:** Going from one or two giant words to the full readable sentence; right after tr-giant-word-punch-out; any big-to-small type handoff inside one continuous take.
- **Avoid when:** As a default between unrelated lines (it is not a crossfade substitute); small-to-small swaps; overlaps longer than 10 f, which read as a dissolve.

### Blur-to-focus word rise

`ty-blur-focus-word-rise` · workhorse · energy calm · launch, feature, walkthrough, vertical

Words materialise one per beat out of a soft blur, rising a few pixels and darkening to full ink as they sharpen.

- **Build:** Use src/fx/Words.tsx with stagger 20, dur 28, rise 0.11 (em) and blur 8: each word fades in, rises through arrive(p) and sharpens through blurIn(p, 8), so the blur is gone by frame 4 while the word is still moving and half transparent. Pass wordStyle to resolve colour as well: color = mixColor(C.mist, C.ink, p) on paper (C.mute -> C.white on ink), so a word reads pale and soft first, crisp and dark on landing. Give the whole line a 0.5 px/f translateX drift on E.linear so it never freezes, and start the first word while the camera is still decelerating so reveal and settle read as one gesture. For a URL, start the path segment 8-12 f after the domain.
- **Timing:** Per word 28 f E.out; opacity 8 f; blur 8 -> 0 px, clear by frame 4; rise 13 px at 120 px type (peak about 3 px/f); stagger 20-22 f (one word per beat at 160-180 BPM); line drift 0.5 px/f.
- **Use when:** Calm, premium statements that keep pace with a voice-over or a slow bed; the opening line of a quiet film; light grounds.
- **Avoid when:** High-energy acts or dense beats (the stagger is too slow); pale type on a pale ground (under 4.5:1); any blur left on readable text for more than 6 f.

### Centre-out line unmask

`ty-centre-out-unmask` · workhorse · energy calm · feature, walkthrough, launch, loop

A short line opens from its own centre outward behind a soft-edged mask while the letters stay perfectly still, so a result or status reads as unveiled rather than flown in.

- **Build:** Lay out the final centred line, get its width w from measureTracked, and keep every glyph static. Reveal it with a horizontal mask on the line box: o = w x prog(f, s, s + 18, E.out), and mask-image: linear-gradient(90deg, transparent (50% - o/2 - 20px), #000 (50% - o/2), #000 (50% + o/2), transparent (50% + o/2 + 20px)), computed in px each frame, so both edges travel outward with a 20 px feather (a hard clip-path: inset(0 calc(50% - o/2)) is fine inside a pill). Over the same window, run opacity 0.6 -> 1 and letter-spacing +0.04 em -> the token's tracking on E.out, so the line tightens as it opens. Set it under a centred icon or check that has just landed, starting 4-6 f after the icon's landing frame; for a second line, open it 6 f after the first. Keep the hold alive with a drift of at most 0.3 px/f, and exit with the whole line over 12 f on E.smooth or with ty-reading-order-exit.
- **Timing:** Unmask over 18 f on E.out (31% of each half-width opens on frame 1), with a 20 px feather. Opacity 0.6 -> 1 and tracking +0.04 em -> token over the same 18 f. Starts 4-6 f after the icon lands; a second line follows at +6 f. Hold at least 36 f + 6 f per word, drifting at most 0.3 px/f. Exit over 12 f on E.smooth.
- **Use when:** A result, status or confirmation line under a centred icon ('Published', 'Connected'). A hero word inside a pill that has just formed. A calm sub-line under a headline that has already landed.
- **Avoid when:** Lines over about 40 characters (the edges take too long to reach the ends). Left-aligned layouts (wipe from the left edge instead). Text that is also moving, where the mask fights the glyph motion. Headlines that need energy.

### In-place word light-up on beats

`ty-inplace-light-up-beats` · workhorse · energy calm · launch, feature, walkthrough, vertical

The finished line is laid out from the start and its words light up in place, chunk by chunk on the beat, with the last word held back.

- **Build:** Lay out the final centred line once; every word is a span at its final position with opacity 0, so nothing ever reflows. Group the words into 2-3 chunks that start on beat frames, 6 f apart within a chunk; each word's opacity is tw(f, s, s + 5, 0, 0.75, E.linear) then rises to 1 over the next 40 f on E.outSoft (fast attack, slow brightening tail). Hierarchy without a second colour: keywords at weight 600, connectors at 400 held at 0.55 until the last chunk lands and then raised to 1 over 12 f; the final word or qualifier arrives a full beat late, and a qualifier may sit tucked under the line's right edge at 0.35x size. Across a film, shorten the per-word stagger from 24 f on the title to about 6 f on later captions, because viewers learn the pattern; exit the whole line at once.
- **Timing:** Attack 5 f to 0.75, tail 40 f E.outSoft to 1; 6 f within a chunk, chunks on beats; last token +24-34 f; connectors 0.55 -> 1 over 12 f; title stagger 24 f shrinking to 5-6 f; exit all words together over 26 f E.smooth. If the camera is locked, add a 0.3 px/f line drift.
- **Use when:** Titles and walkthrough captions over a moving camera; lines with an inline glyph or partner wordmark that must not shift; music-led films where each chunk can sit on a beat.
- **Avoid when:** High-energy acts that need motion in the type itself; lines over 6 words (it turns into a slide).

### Masked baseline rise

`ty-masked-baseline-rise` · workhorse · energy medium · any

Each word rises out of an invisible line at its own baseline, tops of the glyphs first, as if cut out of the layout.

- **Build:** Wrap each word in an inline-block with overflow:hidden and padding-bottom 0.15 em (room for descenders); the inner span goes translateY 110% -> 0 on arrive(p), p = prog(f, s_i, s_i + 12, E.out), s_i = start + 6i, with opacity 0 -> 1 linear over the first 3 f, because frame 1 moves about 57 px/f and must be streaked by the blurred master (render.sh --blur). Optional ink resolve: color = mixColor(C.mute, C.ink, prog(f, s_i, s_i + 10, E.linear)). For one short hero word, run it per letter with a 3 f stagger, or drop the letters unmasked from -0.25 em over 8 f, 4 f apart, so a small word falls into place. Exit back into the same mask (translateY 0 -> -110% on depart(q), q on E.in over 10 f) or with ty-reading-order-exit.
- **Timing:** Per word 12 f E.out (10-14 f), travel 110% of the line box (about 132 px at 120 px type): 57, 34, 18 px/f on frames 1-3; opacity 3 f; stagger 6 f (4-10); per letter 3 f stagger; letter drop 0.25 em over 8 f, 4 f apart; mask exit 10 f E.in.
- **Use when:** Editorial headlines and in-UI headings that must land fast (a 3-word line in under 0.5 s) without stealing focus; titles that build while the plane or camera is still moving.
- **Avoid when:** Tight leading where the mask would clip the line above; a calm voice-paced read (use ty-blur-focus-word-rise); per-letter runs on anything but one short hero word.

### Re-centring line build

`ty-recentre-line-build` · workhorse · energy medium · any

Words or typed glyphs join a centred line one at a time while the whole line glides sideways so it is centred on every frame.

- **Build:** Measure the line at each state with measureTracked and set targets x_k = centreX - width_k / 2; drive the container as a sum of springs, x = x_0 + sum over k of (x_k - x_(k-1)) x spr(f, land_k, SPR.firm), which never overshoots and smooths away per-glyph steps when it follows typing. Each new word drops from -0.35 em (or rises from +0.2 em) into its slot on arrive(prog(f, land_k, land_k + 18, E.out)) with opacity 0 -> 1 over 6 f; after the last word keep a residual 0.3 px/f drift. Pre-solved alternative for short typed lines: lay out the final centred line, fade each character in over 5 f at 1.3 f apart, and glide the container +90 px -> 0 on prog(f, s, s + 24, E.out) so it lands centred with the last glyph. Optional: a single-hue pill behind the line whose width follows the measured width + 50 px on the same springs.
- **Timing:** A new word every 26-36 f (0.43-0.6 s); SPR.firm re-centre (peak about 7% of the shift per frame, 97% by 27 f), so shifts up to 280 px stay under 20 px/f; word drop 18 f E.out; pre-solved: 1.3 f per character, 5 f fade, 90 px glide over 24 f E.out; residual drift 0.3 px/f.
- **Use when:** Speaking-pace builds, stat rows that widen as words arrive, centred typed headlines, any line whose final width is unknown while it builds.
- **Avoid when:** Shifts over about 280 px per word (split the line instead); left-aligned layouts; a line that must keep an anchored element still (use ty-inplace-light-up-beats).

### Reading-order word exit

`ty-reading-order-exit` · workhorse · energy any · any

Words leave one by one in reading order, each lifting a few pixels and vanishing, until only the hero element is left on screen.

- **Build:** For each word except the hero, o_i = out + 4i and q = prog(f, o_i, o_i + 10, E.in): translateY = -depart(q) x 0.12 em, opacity = 1 - prog(f, o_i, o_i + 10, E.smooth) (never fade on E.in, which pops), blur = blurOut(q, 4). The hero word, icon or pill stays put, and the next move (zoom, match cut) starts from it within 6 f of the last word clearing. Loosen variant for a calm handoff: words drift apart vertically by sign_i x (10 + 10 x rand(i)) px with a rotation of +-2 degrees, fade toward the ground colour first (mixColor(C.ink, C.mist)) and then to 0, over 20 f on E.smooth, 6 f apart.
- **Timing:** Per word 10 f, lift 0.12 em (about 14 px), stagger 4 f (2-6), a 5-word line clears in about 26 f; loosen variant 20 f per word, 6 f apart, about 32-44 f in all.
- **Use when:** Isolating a hero word or object before a match cut or zoom; clearing a statement gently before a calmer UI moment; mirroring a word-by-word entry.
- **Avoid when:** Walkthrough captions just before a camera move: fade the whole caption at once over 26 f on E.smooth and finish 0-56 f before the move starts; exits that would hurry a payoff line.

### Staggered word roll

`ty-staggered-word-roll` · workhorse · energy medium · any

The words of a phrase roll up and away one after another while their replacements rise in from below, so one sentence mutates instead of cutting.

- **Build:** For slot i, t_i = t0 + 10i. Out: q = prog(f, t_i, t_i + 12, E.in), translateY = -depart(q) x 0.2 em, opacity = 1 - prog(f, t_i, t_i + 12, E.smooth), blur = blurOut(q, 6). In, starting at t_i + 4 (a 4 f overlap): p = prog(f, t_i + 4, t_i + 28, E.out), translateY = (1 - arrive(p)) x 0.25 em, opacity 0 -> 1 over 10 f, blur = blurIn(p, 8). Keep any shared element (an icon pill, an unchanged word) perfectly still as the anchor, always roll in the same direction, and re-centre on SPR.firm when the new words change the width.
- **Timing:** Out 12 f E.in, 0.2 em up; in 24 f E.out from +0.25 em (peak about 7 px/f at 120 px type), 4 f overlap; stagger 6-11 f per word; a phrase swap takes about 50 f; a whole-line conveyor variant leaves exactly 1 empty frame between the lines.
- **Use when:** Swapping one claim for the next in place; a URL replacing a tagline; a category word turning into the product name; a closing bookend that rolls the opening phrase into the brand line.
- **Avoid when:** Swaps where nothing persists (a cut or ty-blur-swap-rescale reads cleaner); more than two rolls in a row without a different move between them.

### Time-boxed eased type-on

`ty-typeon-timeboxed` · workhorse · energy medium · feature, walkthrough, launch, vertical

Text types in with most of the line appearing in the first few frames, and every line, short or long, finishes in the same musical length.

- **Build:** Visible count n = fd(N x prog(f, s, s + 68, E.out)) for prompts and headlines (45% of the string by frame 6, the last letters trickle in), or E.linear at 22-45 characters/s for small mono UI labels; pre-fill the first word so frame 1 already shows text, and pre-solve the layout (left-anchored in a fixed centred box, or a pill sized to the final string) so nothing reflows. The caret is a 0.08 em x 1 em bar that rides the text while typing and blinks at 1 Hz (30 f on, 30 f off, decided with fd) only after completion, and is gone before the hold ends. When the line outgrows 88% of the frame width, translate the container by min(0, 0.88W - caretX), eased over 8 f per character, and fade the head out through a mask-image over the left 25%. To replace a typed line, turn the whole string accent for 6 f, swap it on one frame and retype the new one in 26 f.
- **Timing:** Box 68 f per line whatever its length (26-32 f for a headline under 22 characters, 84 f for giant type); E.out count; mono labels E.linear 22-45 cps; caret blink 30/30 f after completion; caret-follow 8 f per character, head mask 25%; retype: 6 f accent, 1 f swap, 26 f retype. Hold at least 36 f + 6 f per word after the last glyph.
- **Use when:** Prompts, search queries and names typed into the product; UI labels appearing while the camera trucks; keeping a run of typed beats on one musical length.
- **Avoid when:** Statements nobody would type; keystroke clicks on every glyph (let the music carry it); letter-by-letter reveals of a name whose prefixes spell another word.

### Vertical word stack

`ty-vertical-word-stack` · workhorse · energy medium · vertical

In a tall frame each new word lands on its own line under the last while the stack rises one line, so the newest word always sits on the optical centre.

- **Build:** Line pitch 1.05x the font size (110-140 px statement type in 9:16), lines left- or centre-aligned inside safeBox() so the stack clears the feed zones. Word k lands at land_k: translateY +0.35 em -> 0 on arrive(prog(f, land_k, land_k + 18, E.out)), opacity 0 -> 1 over 6 f; the stack container moves up by the sum over k of pitch x spr(f, land_k, SPR.firm), peaking at about 11 px/f for a 150 px pitch. Lines more than two steps old fade out through a feathered top mask (mask-image transparent -> opaque over the top 0.8 pitch), so at most 3 words of one statement are on screen; the final word may arrive in the accent and relax to ink.
- **Timing:** A word every 24-30 f; word rise 18 f E.out; stack step SPR.firm (97% in 27 f); at most 3 lines visible; final hold at least 36 f + 6 f per word with a 0.3 px/f drift.
- **Use when:** Vertical cut-downs where a horizontal line would be too small; speaking-pace statements on a phone-sized frame; one word per beat.
- **Avoid when:** 16:9 masters (use ty-recentre-line-build); statements over 6 words; stacking two separate statements.

### Words spill out from behind a mark

`ty-occlusion-spill-from-mark` · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature, sting

A glyph or icon slides aside and the words shoot out from behind it, clipped at its edge, as if the mark were delivering the message.

- **Build:** Put the words in a container clipped at the mark's current edge (for a leftward spill, clip-path: inset(0 calc(100% - (markX - boxLeft)) 0 0)) and draw the mark above them. Mark: translateX 0 -> +260 px on prog(f, s, s + 20, E.out); words: translateX +320 -> 0 on p = prog(f, s + 1, s + 25, E.out) with blurIn(p, 8) and opacity 0 -> 1 over 6 f, hidden behind the mark at first and readable once they drop below 20 px/f around frame 6. Inline variant: an icon shrinks (lmix 3 -> 1, optionally tilting in 3D) into the bullet slot at the start of a sentence and the words slide out to its right from behind it the same way.
- **Timing:** Mark 260 px over 20 f E.out (peak about 73 px/f, blurred master); words 320 px over 24 f E.out (76 px/f on frame 1, under 20 by frame 6), 1 f after the mark; opacity 6 f; hold at least 54 f with a drift.
- **Use when:** An icon-led claim mid-film, or an opening line pushed out by the mark already in motion; a feature icon that introduces its own line; a mark or number that says the sentence.
- **Avoid when:** The end lockup (it appears once and belongs to the end card); marks smaller than the cap height (nothing to hide behind); spills longer than about 360 px.

### Hard-step edits that act out the copy

`ty-step-edit-performs-copy` · accent · energy medium · launch, feature, sting

The headline does what it says with one-frame edits: broken words click straight one at a time, or words delete from the end faster and faster.

- **Build:** Give each word two states and pick one by fd(f) >= step_i, with no tween at all. Fix variant: broken states are per-letter rotation along an arc (letter j rotated (j - mid) x 6 degrees and raised (j - mid)^2 x 2 px), skewX(15deg) with translateY -0.17 em, or rotate(-20deg), drifting 0.5 px/f while broken; steps land at +6, +26 and +40 f after the cut, each with a 2% scale punch from hitPulse(t, 1, 4) on the fixed word. Delete variant: words.slice(0, n) with n dropping at accelerating intervals (10, 5, 5, 2 f), building pressure into the cut. Each step gets one click, each a little louder than the last.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Keep only the rotation-based broken states (letters fanned along an arc, or the word rotated -20 deg) and drop the skewX(15deg) state, which fakes an italic; the one-frame steps, the 2% punches and the accelerating deletes stay as they are. The full look relies on italic; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** Snap 1 f, no tween; fix intervals 20 then 14 f; delete intervals 10/5/5/2 f; broken-state drift 0.5 px/f; click within 1 f of each step; hold the fixed line at least 42 f.
- **Use when:** Copy about fixing, undoing, cleaning up or simplifying; a deadpan joke beat; a problem line that should visibly go away.
- **Avoid when:** Copy the motion would contradict; calm films; more than one per film.

### Multi-direction slam assembly

`ty-multi-direction-assemble` · accent · energy high · launch, sting, vertical

Each word of a short sentence flies in from a different side, oversized and streaked, and the sentence assembles on one baseline almost at once.

- **Build:** Lay out the final line and give each word a start offset from a different side (+-220 px in x, or +200 px in y) and a start scale of 1.4. Per word: p = prog(f, s + d_i, s + d_i + 20, E.out) with delays d = [0, 4, 10, 12, 16]; translate = offset x (1 - p) (vertical offsets through arrive), scale = lmix(1.4, 1, p), opacity 0 -> 1 over 5 f, so each word stays faint while it moves faster than 20 px/f and the blurred master streaks it along its own direction. One quiet piece may simply fade in over 8 f while the others fly; once the line is complete it drifts from scale 1 to 0.99 over 60 f.
- **Timing:** Per word 20 f E.out, 220 px travel (62, 47, 33, 23, 16 px/f on frames 1-5), scale 1.4 -> 1, opacity 5 f; delays 0/4/10/12/16 f; each word readable from about frame 5, the whole line resolved in about 36 f; then 1 -> 0.99 over 60 f.
- **Use when:** Re-spiking energy after a calm, read-paced card; a payoff line that needs a burst; 3-5 short words.
- **Avoid when:** Long words that would cross each other in flight; straight after another high-energy type move; calm films.

### Scaled-echo extrusion

`ty-scaled-echo-extrusion` · accent · energy medium · launch, sting, feature

A hero title carries two or three faint copies scaled out behind it, a short depth extrusion that compresses as the title lands and then holds.

- **Build:** Stack k = 3, 2, 1 copies of the same text behind the title, with the title on top. Give copy k transform scale(1 + step x k) about a vanishing point, opacity 0.55, 0.35 and 0.2 for k = 1, 2, 3, and color mixColor(C.ink, stage colour, 0.5) (C.white mixed toward the stage on ink). Arrival: step = mix(0.03, 0.012, prog(f, land - 2, land + 20, E.out)), so the extrusion collapses inward as the title lands. Put the vanishing point on the text centre for a straight-on echo, or 0.3 W to one side or below it for a directional depth. Keep the hold alive by sliding the vanishing point about 40 px across the text over the hold, opposite to a 0.3 px/f line drift, so the echoes shift like real depth. Solid-block variant for a giant cropped word: 8-12 copies translated (k x 1 px, k x 1.5 px) behind the face, each a step darker (mixColor toward C.ink by k / 12), with no blur, bevel or shadow.
- **Timing:** Converge over 22 f on E.out (step 0.03 -> 0.012; outer copy edges stay under 7 px/f on a 500 px title). Copy opacity 0.55 / 0.35 / 0.2. Hold the whole card (36-60 f) with a vanishing-point slide of about 40 px on E.linear and a line drift of 0.3 px/f. The solid-block variant uses 8-12 one-pixel steps that do not animate relative to the face; the card still drifts at 0.3 px/f.
- **Use when:** A product name or a hero title of one to three words that needs weight in a flat sans. A giant cropped word that needs physical depth. A title card between two energetic acts.
- **Avoid when:** Body copy or lines over 3 words (the copies tangle inside the counters). Low-contrast stages, where the copies turn to haze. Blur, glow, bevels or drop shadows on the copies. A film that already uses the motion-trail echo of the word slams: pick one echo device.

### Scramble decode

`ty-scramble-decode` · accent · energy medium · feature, walkthrough, sting, loop

A string of random glyphs locks into the real text from left to right, or real letters roll through the alphabet into gibberish and back.

- **Build:** Character i shows target[i] once fd(f) >= lock_i = s + 5i, otherwise a glyph from a fixed pool chosen by rand(`${i}:${Math.floor(fd(f) / 2)}`), which changes on twos and repeats exactly on every render; use tabular or mono figures, or pin each slot to the target glyph's measured advance, so the width never jitters. Unlocked glyphs sit at 50% opacity (or C.mute) and locked glyphs at ink, optionally with a 12 f accent decay on lock. Code-roll variant: each letter steps one character code per frame from an offset toward its target, or away from it as an exit while a container takes its place.
- **Timing:** One lock every 5 f (about 48 f for a 10-character string); unlocked glyphs change every 2 f; accent decay 12 f E.out; code roll 1 step per frame, 4-8 steps per letter.
- **Use when:** Keys, codes, private or encrypted values, numbers resolving, a short technical name in a feature beat.
- **Avoid when:** Prose statements (it delays reading); the brand name in the end lockup; glints or sparkles on the glyphs.

### Shared-letter morph

`ty-shared-letter-morph` · accent · energy medium · launch, feature, sting

One word turns into another: the letters both words share stay and slide into place while the new letters tumble in and click upright.

- **Build:** Split both words into glyph spans at measured, kerned positions; map shared characters (same letter, nearest index) so they keep their element and slide to the new x on prog(f, s, s + 24, E.out), while unshared old glyphs fade out over 6 f and the word spaces collapse over 8 f. Each new glyph starts at an offset of +-150 px in x and +-120 px in y from rand(`g${i}`) with a rotation of 90-180 degrees and animates to rest on E.out over 24 f, opacity 0 -> 1 over the first 12 f so it stays faint while faster than 20 px/f, with start times spread over 56 f and the last glyph dropping from above. Check every frame on a contact sheet so no in-between state spells another word.
- **Timing:** Space collapse 8 f; old glyph fade 6 f; each new glyph 24 f E.out (about 45 px/f on frame 1), opacity 12 f; starts spread over 56 f; hold at least 36 f after the last glyph settles.
- **Use when:** Two words that share letters and whose relationship is the point (before and after, problem and product); one memorable word turn per film.
- **Avoid when:** Fewer than 2 shared letters; words longer than about 8 letters; fast films where 60 f of letter flight is too slow.

### Slice glitch into a speed streak

`ty-slice-glitch-streak` · accent · energy high · launch, sting, feature

A word jolts into sideways-displaced horizontal slices for two frames, then stretches into a solid capsule that races off as a streak, and the next word lands in its wake.

- **Build:** Slice: for 2 f decided with fd, render the word as 6-8 stacked copies, each clipped to one horizontal band with clip-path: inset(), and offset each band by sign x 0.08-0.25 em, both drawn from rand(`${b}:${fd(f)}`). Under 30% of the bands, lay a C.mute copy offset 0.03 em (one hue, no RGB fringes), and raise the variable 'wght' by 100 for those two frames; frame 3 renders clean. Smear: from s, scaleX = mix(1, 1.8, prog(f, s, s + 18, E.contact)) about the word's left edge, so the right edge accelerates to about 70 px/f on the last frame (render the blurred master). Over those last 10 f, fade the text out while a capsule (C.ink on paper or C.white on ink, radius 50%) fades in over the same box and its height shrinks from the cap height to 0.35 of it. Streak: the capsule keeps its handoff speed, with head x = x_e + v_e x (f - e) and a trailing tail of length clamp(v x 1.5, 0, 240) px, until it clears the frame edge. Next word: it enters in the wake, layered under the streak, with translateX -320 -> 0 on p = prog(f, e + 4, e + 28, E.outSoft), opacity 0 -> 1 over 8 f and blurIn(p, 16), so it is faint while fast and readable once it drops under 20 px/f. The 2 f slice alone, with no smear, works as a hit on privacy or obfuscation copy.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Make the streak a flat solid capsule in C.ink or C.white with a speed-scaled tail and true motion blur. No bloom on the type or the streak, the trail keeps the capsule's one tone, and the glitch copies stay in C.mute. The full look relies on glow, purple; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** Slice: 2 f via fd, clean on frame 3. Smear: 18 f on E.contact, scaleX 1 -> 1.8; for a word up to 450 px wide the right edge ends near 70 px/f. Text-to-capsule crossfade over the last 10 f. The streak cruises at that speed and clears a 1920 frame in about 15 f, with a tail of at most 240 px. Next word: 320 px over 24 f on E.outSoft from e + 4 (58 px/f on frame 1, under 20 px/f from frame 7), opacity over 8 f. Hold it at least 54 f.
- **Use when:** A speed or performance claim, where the word itself turns into motion. Handing a name off to a thread, packet or line that carries into the next scene. The 2 f slice alone on 'private', 'encrypted' or 'blocked'.
- **Avoid when:** Calm films. More than once per film. Words wider than about 450 px at the smear, where the edge would pass 80 px/f. Long lines. Coloured fringes or a tint shift along the trail.

### Slice-band glyph assembly

`ty-slice-band-assembly` · accent · energy medium · launch, sting, feature

Each letter builds up from thin horizontal slices that slide in from slightly different offsets at slightly different moments, faint and pale at first, until the word locks solid.

- **Build:** Measure the word with measureTracked. Give each glyph an inline-grid cell holding N = 5 stacked copies of itself (6 copies for type above 160 px), with all copies in grid-area 1/1. Clip copy b to its band with clip-path: inset(calc(b * 100% / N - 0.5px) -0.1em calc((N - 1 - b) * 100% / N - 0.5px) -0.1em), on a line box padded 0.12 em on top and 0.26 em below, so neighbouring bands overlap by 1 px and no descender or overhang gets shaved. Band (i, b) starts at s + d, with d = fd(12 x rand(`${i}:${b}`)) (add 1 f per glyph for a left-to-right bias), and runs on p = prog(f, s + d, s + d + 20, E.out): translateX (1 - p) x sx x 0.12 em, where sx = rand(`x${i}:${b}`) > 0.5 ? 1 : -1; translateY (1 - arrive(p)) x 0.04 em; opacity over its first 8 f on E.linear; and color mixColor(C.mute, C.ink, p) on paper (stage tint to C.white on ink). On the frame the last band lands, swap the band stacks for one intact text layer, decided with fd, so no seam survives antialiasing, then tighten the tracking 0.03 em -> the token over 44 f on E.out. Beside a mark that slides aside, start the build at the slide's peak-velocity frame, so the letters seem to be pulled out by its motion.
- **Timing:** Each band takes 20 f on E.out, with opacity over 8 f on E.linear and colour over the same 20 f. Band delays are 0-12 f from rand (plus 1 f per glyph if biased). The whole word is built in about 32 f (about 40 f with the bias). Offsets are 0.12 em sideways and 0.04 em vertical: about 4 px/f on frame 1 at 120 px type, so no blur. The swap to intact text takes 1 f, then the tracking tightens over 44 f on E.out. Hold at least 60 f with a drift of 0.3 px/f.
- **Use when:** A product or feature name that should feel assembled or digital. A name set beside a modular or pixel mark, including the one end-lockup build when the film bookends with it. A short title after a quiet beat.
- **Avoid when:** Lines over about 3 words, or type under 48 px (bands thinner than 3 px alias into noise). Prose. Delay spreads wide enough that the half-built word reads as broken for more than about 30 f. A film that already has a scramble decode.

### Travelling front restyles a word

`ty-front-restyle-sweep` · accent · energy medium · launch, feature, sting

A front sweeps left to right across a settled word and restyles each glyph as it passes, in colour or weight, sometimes with a cursor riding under it.

- **Build:** After the word has landed, move a front x_F = mix(xL - band, xR + band, prog(f, s, s + 32, E.dolly)) across it, with band about 0.6 em. For glyph i at measured x_i, u_i = clamp((x_F - x_i) / band): its colour runs C.mute -> C.accent at u = 0.5 -> C.ink at u = 1 through mixColor (one hue only), or its variable-font weight runs fontVariationSettings 'wght' 400 -> 700, with each glyph's advance interpolated between measureTracked at both weights so the line re-flows smoothly and stays centred. If the beat is the user switching something on, ride src/fx/Cursor.tsx at the base of the front. For two promise words in a tagline, step the glyphs 2 f apart instead of using a continuous band.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** A one-hue front (mute -> accent -> ink per glyph through mixColor) instead of a multi-hue band, and a variable-weight wave (400 -> 700) in the film's one sans instead of switching glyphs to a serif italic. The full look relies on gradient, serif, italic; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** Sweep 32 f E.dolly (front peaks about 29 px/f across a 600 px word; stretch to 40 f for wider words); band 0.6 em; per-glyph weight morph about 4 f; a second word starts about 20 f after the first; begin at least 10 f after the word lands.
- **Use when:** Turning a static big word into a moment of discovery; emphasising one or two promise words without a highlight shape; a change of voice mid-sentence.
- **Avoid when:** Text still moving; sweeps whose half-restyled frames read as another word; colour and weight sweeps in the same film.

### One-word slam sequence

`ty-kinetic-word-slams` · signature · energy high · launch, sting, vertical

A line is read one huge word at a time: each word hits oversized and blurred, settles, then is sucked away as the next word cuts in.

- **Build:** Each word is its own card, fitted to about 77% of the frame width with fitSize. Entry: scale = lmix(1.35, 1, p), p = prog(f, cue - 1, cue + 21, E.outSoft), opacity 0 -> 1 over 3 f, blur = blurIn(p, 12), then a 6 f drift (scale x 1.01). Never start above 1.35x: a larger start leaves the outer letters of a frame-wide word moving faster than 20 px/f after the blur has cleared. Exit: scale x lmix(1, 0.6, q), q = prog(f, end - 14, end, E.in), opacity to 0 on E.smooth over the same window, then a hard cut to the next word on its slam's first frame, with every cut on an act boundary so the blurred master never smears two words together. Optional echo: two copies behind the word use the entry progress at f - 2 and f - 4, at 0.35 and 0.18 opacity, tinted 50% toward the ground, so they converge into the word by +12 f.
- **Timing:** Entry 22 f E.outSoft from 1.35x (the edges of a 1120 px word start at about 43 px/f, faded and blurred, and are near 22 px/f by frame 4 when the blur clears), blur 12 -> 0 by about frame 4, drift 6 f, exit 14 f E.in to 0.6x (last frame about 72 px/f, nearly transparent); 36-42 f per word (0.6-0.7 s), last word held at least 54 f under a 1-2% scale creep; every hit on a beat.
- **Use when:** A punchy 3-5 word line on a strong beat; a problem statement or rhythmic claim; vertical formats where one word fills the screen.
- **Avoid when:** More than one sequence per film; lines over 5 words; calm films; a card for a lone connector word (fold it into the next word).

### Oversize word slide-in

`ty-oversize-blur-slide-in` · signature · energy high · launch, sting, feature

A huge word arrives streaked from beside the frame and brakes on a long tail, and a trailing word follows from further out and closes the gap so the phrase locks together.

- **Build:** Type height 21-25% of the frame. Word 1: x = x_f + 0.4W x (1 - prog(f, s, s + 90, E.out)) - 0.5 x (f - s), a long braking tail on top of a slow drift that never stops, with opacity 0.2 -> 1 over the 16 f it takes to fall below 20 px/f, so it travels faded. Word 2 starts 16 f later with a larger offset (0.6W) on the same curve, so the gap between the words shrinks from about 1.7x to 1x over about 80 f, and its opacity rises 0.2 -> 1 over 68 f; letters may fade on left to right 2 f apart as each word slows. Frame 1 runs about 52 px/f (78 for word 2), so render the blurred master; blurIn(p, 10) stands in for the sharp preview.
- **Timing:** Brake 90 f E.out (feels like a 33 f time constant); word 1 offset 0.4W (768 px), word 2 0.6W from +16 f; drift 0.5 px/f; opacity from 0.2, readable below 20 px/f from frame 16 (word 2 from frame 21); gap 1.7x -> 1x over 80 f.
- **Use when:** The energy peak of a type act; a two-word claim; a cold open whose first frame already moves.
- **Avoid when:** Long phrases; when screen direction must run the other way across the cut; small type.

### Phrase clamp at a junction

`ty-phrase-clamp-junction` · signature · energy medium · launch, feature, sting, vertical

Two halves of a phrase arrive from opposite directions and lock on one baseline at a fixed junction, like a clamp closing.

- **Build:** Fix a junction (x about 48% of the frame, on the shared baseline): the first half is right-aligned to it and the second half left-aligned, both measured with measureTracked so the junction gap is exactly one word space. Vertical default: hold the first half alone for 1 f at +64 px (the pre-pose), then translateY +64 -> 0 on arrive(p), p = prog(f, s, s + 18, E.out), while each word of the second half drops -40 -> 0 the same way, word i starting at s + 2i; give every piece opacity 0 -> 1 over 3 f and blurIn(p, 8), because frame 1 moves about 20 px/f. Horizontal snap: the line cuts in at full strength with each half 35 px out from the junction, closes to 0.75 of the word space over 10 f on E.out, then eases back to the true gap over 18 f on E.outSoft (the one designed undershoot, never closing the space); calm variant: a 1.7x gap closes to 1x over 80 f on E.outSoft. Put the lock on a beat and give it one 1.5% scale punch with hitPulse(t, 1, 4).
- **Timing:** Vertical: 18 f E.out, 64 px and 40 px travel (peak 19.7 and 12.3 px/f on frame 1), 2 f word stagger, 1 f pre-pose, opacity 3 f. Snap: 35 px per side over 10 f E.out (about 20 px/f on frame 1) to 0.75 of the gap, back over 18 f E.outSoft. Calm close: 80 f E.outSoft. Hold the locked line at least 54 f with a 0.3 px/f drift.
- **Use when:** A two-part claim whose halves mean more together (subject + promise, problem + fix); the payoff line; a junction that a slot roller will reuse.
- **Avoid when:** Lines over 5 words or halves of very unequal length; more than once per film; the end lockup.

### Quiet type swells on the drop

`ty-swell-on-drop` · signature · energy high · launch, sting, vertical

A word appears small and low-contrast and waits through the build, then swells to hero size, with 90% of the growth landing exactly on the beat drop.

- **Build:** Set the word at about 9% of the frame height, centred, in C.mute (or at 0.5 opacity on ink), and bring it in quietly: per-letter opacity pops 5-6 f apart decided with fd, or ty-typeon-timeboxed. Put the drop frame h on the music's downbeat, register it in src/sync.ts, and scale the group about its centre with k = lmix(1, 2.5, prog(f, h - 32, h + 22, E.glide)), so 90% of the log-scale growth lands on h and the rest settles over 22 f. Run color mixColor(C.mute, C.ink, prog(f, h - 32, h, E.smooth)) so size and contrast peak together. Drive the scale with transform, never font-size, and keep the starting width under about 420 px, so the outer edges peak near 17 px/f (21 px/f at 2.9x) and the word stays readable through the swell; render the blurred master for the frames above 12 px/f. After the settle, keep it alive with a 0.3 px/f drift or a cam-living-hold creep, or cut within 54 f.
- **Timing:** Letters 5-6 f apart at 9% of the frame height. Swell over 54 f on E.glide, starting at h - 32 so 90% lands on h: scale 1 -> 2.5 (2.9 at most) in log space, with the outer edges of a 420 px word peaking at about 16.5 px/f around frame 17. Contrast goes C.mute -> ink over the 32 f before h. Hold at most 54 f after h, or 90-120 f if this is the final lockup's one appearance.
- **Use when:** A hero word or product name that should detonate on the drop after a quiet intro. The one appearance of the final wordmark when the music builds into the end. A single-word answer after a question beat.
- **Avoid when:** There is no real musical hit to land on. Words wide enough to swell past the safe area. Using it more than once per film. Stacking a separate scale punch or camera kick on the same hit.

### Slot roller beside a fixed phrase

`ty-slot-roller-fixed-phrase` · signature · energy medium · launch, feature, loop, vertical

A fixed phrase holds still while the word in its slot rolls through alternatives one line at a time, speeding up until the last one lands.

- **Build:** The fixed phrase sits in its own layer and never moves; the slot is a column of alternatives aligned to the junction, line pitch 1.5x the font size, translated by -index x pitch and cut by a feathered mask-image (transparent beyond +-1.2 pitch, opaque within +-0.5 pitch) so neighbours show only as slivers. Each step rolls on E.whip over 20 f (peak about 0.18 x pitch per frame, 12 px/f at a 68 px pitch); above a 110 px pitch, stretch the step to 0.18 x pitch frames so the rolling word stays at or under 20 px/f; the row on the junction baseline is ink and every other row is C.mute at no more than 1.3:1 contrast, flipped binary when |rowY - baselineY| < pitch/2 (no colour tween). For a run of 5 or more items, accelerate: intervals 26, 14, 12, 8, 8, 4, 4 f, where intervals under 12 f are whole-frame swaps chosen by fd(f) with no tween, the final item rolls home on SPR.detent, and every step gets a tick. For a loop, make the last item equal the first and wrap the index modulo the list.
- **Timing:** Step 20 f E.whip (0.18 x pitch frames above a 110 px pitch) every 29-34 f (0.48-0.57 s), 3 steps, then a 28 f hold before the cut. Accelerating run: 26/14/12/8/8/4/4 f (7 items in 76 f), last item on SPR.detent (home in about 9 f), held at least 54 f under a 0.3 px/f line drift. Pitch 1.5x the font size; ticks at least 3 f apart.
- **Use when:** One sentence frame that fits many subjects or capabilities; listing use-cases without spending screen time; a feature loop that cycles items.
- **Avoid when:** Items of very different widths in a centred layout (the fixed phrase would have to move); more than about 7 items; any mask loose enough that the neighbours read as a list.

## UI choreography

UI choreography is layout logic in motion: every rect is a function of the frame and the product's state, siblings reflow from computed positions instead of crossfading, and a container is on screen before its contents, which start once their slot is about 60% open. Entrances decay with no overshoot (a 200 px window rise on E.out covers about half its travel in the first 6 f and settles in 50 f) and exits accelerate, handing over to the next panel or the cut on their fastest frame with at most a 4 f gap. Size every move from peak speed = distance x the token's peak slope / frames (E.out 6.2 on its first frame, E.inOut 7.7, E.contact 4.4 on its last, E.whip 3.8, E.rest 3.5, E.glide 3.0, E.smooth 2.9, E.ui 2.7, E.dolly 1.5), so UI text stays at or under 20 px/f and nothing passes about 70 px/f; scale spawns and collapses with lmix so a small surface does not explode on its first frame. Cadence carries meaning: 4-6 f per row reads as data streaming in, 5 f per dealt card as tactile, a 14 f metronome of inserts as abundance, and uneven gaps such as 4, 15 and 18 f as a person deciding. The strongest moves make one motion do two jobs, an incoming panel's edge pushing its neighbour or a hero holding its exact screen position while the world changes around it, so the edit happens inside the product instead of at a cut.

### Cards dealt or dropped into a grid

`ui-card-grid-arrival` · workhorse · energy medium · any

Cards land in a row or grid one after another, either dealt fast with a small tilt that squares up, or falling from just in front of the camera and shrinking into their slots.

- **Build:** Deal preset: card i appears at t0 + 5*i, its opacity stepping to 1 on the first frame while rotate goes 4 to 0 deg and scale 0.95 to 1 over 7 f on E.out, left to right, with no overshoot. Depth-drop preset: card i starts at delays [0, 4, 10, 14] (row-major, 6 extra frames between rows) and goes translateY 534 to 0 px and scale lmix(1.38, 1, p) on the same progress p over 54 f on E.out, half the distance in about 6 f at up to 62 px/f under the motion-blur pass. In the depth-drop keep each card's text and icons at opacity 0 until the card slows (prog(f, s + 8, s + 16, E.smooth)), so content resolves on landing below 20 px/f. Cards are opaque with a soft shadow (0 8px 30px at 6% black) and a radius of about 32 px at 1080p.
- **Timing:** Deal: 5 f stagger, 7 f settle (E.out), rotate 4 deg, scale 0.95. Drop: 54 f (E.out), stagger 0/4/10/14 f, 534 px, scale 1.38 to 1, peak ~62 px/f, content fades in from +8 to +16 f.
- **Use when:** Revealing a set of options, results, features or integrations that should read as one set with a clear reading order.
- **Avoid when:** There is one hero object, or more than about 8 cards (use a row cascade or a scroll).

### Container morph into its next role

`ui-container-morph` · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature, walkthrough

One element changes shape into what it becomes, a button unfolding into a panel, a card stretching into a detail view, a pill collapsing into an app tile, so there is no navigation cut to explain.

- **Build:** Keep one element mounted and animate its position (x and y inside one transform), width, height and border radius from the old rect to the new role's rect; never swap two elements. Use E.whip over 30-36 f (slow first 5 f, speed peak near 40%, long settle) and lengthen it so the fastest edge stays under about 70 px/f (frames >= 3.8 x edge travel / 70); a pill collapsing to a tile keeps its height locked while its radius goes from 999 px to 22% of its side, and a panel's radius eases from 44 to 36 px. The old content fades out in the first 12 f on E.smooth, a title that survives FLIPs to its header position and scale (1 to 0.6) on the same curve, flying at opacity 1 - 0.45*clamp((v - 20)/30) (v its speed in px/f) whenever it passes 20 px/f so it lands sharp, the new content enters 8 f after the speed peak with a 2-4 f stagger, and a backdrop behind a panel morph dims linearly over the same frames. Optional preface: the card's outline retracts first (SVG rect with pathLength 1, strokeDashoffset 0 to 1 over 15 f); for a content swap inside a card that stays, the old child leaves with depart() and blurOut(q, 8) over 18 f on E.in, the card resizes to the new aspect over 20 f on E.out, and the new child arrives with arrive() and blurIn(p, 8) over 18 f on E.out.
- **Timing:** Morph 30-36 f (E.whip), edges <= 70 px/f. Old content out 12 f (E.smooth); title FLIP to 0.6 scale; new content +8 f after the peak, 2-4 f stagger; backdrop dim linear over the morph. Outline retract 15 f. Content swap: out 18 f (E.in), resize 20 f (E.out), in 18 f (E.out).
- **Use when:** A click that opens something (button to panel, card to detail), a status becoming an icon, an object docking into its slot.
- **Avoid when:** The size change comes from content or a drag (live reflow), or the two states have no visual relation.

### Container resizes, content reflows

`ui-live-reflow` · workhorse · energy medium · feature, walkthrough, launch

A card or window changes size because its content or the user changes it, growing as typed text wraps or narrowing as an edge is dragged, while everything inside reflows to the new width.

- **Build:** Make layout a pure function of the container's current width: measure text with measureTracked or inkBox, derive line breaks and block positions from that width, and evaluate typed text on fd(f) so the substring and the line count change on whole frames only. Content-driven: as the prompt starts, the input card widens from 67% to 77% of frame width over 24 f on E.outSoft (about 18 px/f per edge, centred so both edges move), and each newly wrapped line adds one line height over 12 f on E.out. User-driven: the cursor grabs a window's right edge and drags it 300-400 px inward on E.contact over 40 f, stopping dead like a real release with no settle, while the left edge follows at 15% of the right edge's speed so the window re-centres and the cursor trails the edge by 1 f. When the width crosses a breakpoint, compute both layouts and FLIP every block to its new slot over 16-24 f on E.ui (fastest block under 70 px/f) instead of crossfading the two layouts.
- **Timing:** Widen 67% to 77% FW over 24 f (E.outSoft); +1 line per wrap over 12 f (E.out). Drag 300-400 px over 40 f (E.contact), ends near 40 px/f, hard stop; breakpoint FLIP 16-24 f (E.ui); then a 0.3 px/f push-out.
- **Use when:** Typing into an input, responsive layouts, resizable panels: any moment where the point is that the UI adapts.
- **Avoid when:** The size change is a change of role, such as a button becoming a panel (use a container morph), or text must be read during the resize.

### Drag to reorder, siblings make way

`ui-drag-reorder-makeway` · workhorse · energy calm · walkthrough, feature

An item lifts under the cursor, travels on a slight arc to a new position while its neighbours slide aside one slot at a time, and settles into place with a firm landing and no bounce.

- **Build:** On the press (pressAt(f, grab)) the item moves to its own top layer and lifts: scale 1 to 1.03 and its shadow from 0 6px 16px at 8% to 0 18px 40px at 14% over 8 f on E.ui. It then follows cursorArc(from, to, prog(f, a, a + T, E.glide), 0.15) with T = max(36, 0.15 x distance) f, so it never exceeds 20 px/f and its label stays readable, and rotateZ = -0.15 deg per px/f of horizontal speed, clamped to +-4 deg. Siblings take their y from the computed layout for the currently hovered index, evaluated on fd(f), so each time that index changes the displaced sibling moves one pitch over 12 f on E.ui. On release the item settles into its slot with spr(f, drop, SPR.firm), the lift reverses over 10 f, its marker flashes C.accent and relaxes to neutral over 24 f, and a tick lands on the drop frame.
- **Timing:** Lift 8 f (E.ui), scale 1.03. Drag T = max(36, 0.15 x distance) f (E.glide) on a 0.15 bow, <= 20 px/f, tilt <= 4 deg. Sibling shift 12 f (E.ui) per index change. Drop SPR.firm, shadow back over 10 f, accent relax 24 f.
- **Use when:** Prioritising, scheduling, kanban boards, playlists: any product whose smart part is ordering things.
- **Avoid when:** The reorder is automatic (animate the computed reorder on one curve, with no cursor), or more than 2-3 drags would fall in one shot.

### Lens list scroll

`ui-lens-list-scroll` · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature, loop, vertical

A list scrolls with momentum past an invisible lens line, and each item's size, tint or tilt depends on its distance from that line, like a phone picker, a rolodex cylinder or a smile-shaped arc.

- **Build:** Drive one offset s(f) for the whole list: a flicked picker uses s = D*(1 - (1 - p)^4) with p = prog(f, a, a + 120, E.linear) and D about 900 px (30 px/f at the start, under 20 px/f after 15 f, cut while it still drifts near 2 px/f, or land on an option with spr(f, a, SPR.detent)); a rolodex uses E.inOut over 90 f for about 480 px (peak about 41 px/f). Per item compute d, its distance from the lens line along the path, and map it: flat picker, scale = 1.2 - 0.35*min(|d|/375, 1) with text colour mixColor(C.ink, C.mute, min(|d|/375, 1)); cylinder, theta = d/R with R = 1.4*H, rotateX(theta) and translateZ(-(1 - cos theta)*R) under perspective 1600 px; smile arc, x = cx + R*sin(theta), y = cy + R*cos(theta) and rotate(-theta) with R = 1750 px and the centre about 790 px above the frame. Give each card a soft shadow; the depth comes from the geometry, never from translucent panels.
- **Timing:** Picker: 120 f quartic momentum, D ~900 px, 30 px/f start, < 20 px/f from f15, ~2 px/f at the cut; focus scale 1.2 to 0.85 across 375 px; optional SPR.detent landing. Cylinder: 90 f (E.inOut), ~480 px, peak ~41 px/f, R = 1.4H, perspective 1600 px. Arc: R 1750 px.
- **Use when:** Choosing among options, showing many screens as one continuous surface, or a playful list of choices that read one at a time.
- **Avoid when:** Items must be read while moving fast, or a plain scroll says it more simply.

### Progress spine leads the steps

`ui-progress-spine-steps` · workhorse · energy calm · feature, walkthrough, launch, vertical

A thin line grows down the side of a step list with a dot at its head. Each step appears as the head reaches it, works with a spinner and a typed detail line, then flips to done, and the list scrolls to keep the head in view until the line turns a rounded corner toward the result.

- **Build:** Build the spine as one SVG path: a vertical run down the list's left gutter, then optionally a 40 px-radius arc into a horizontal run toward the result card. Place the head, a flat 10 px dot in C.ink, at getPointAtLength(L(f)) (from @remotion/paths). L moves only between steps, over 40 f on E.rest per step pitch, and waits at each step for that step's work time from the data (machine-timed, 24-60 f). Draw the path twice: a 1.5 px C.line hairline for the whole route, and above it a 2 px C.ink stroke with pathLength 1 and strokeDashoffset = 1 - L / total, so the part already travelled is solid and the rest is a guide. Step row i appears on the frame the head reaches its y (pass_i): opacity prog(f, pass_i, pass_i + 12, E.smooth) with a 12 px rise through arrive(). While the head waits there, the row shows a dashed-ring spinner (one turn per 48 f) and TypeOn types its detail line at about 1.5 characters per frame. On the last frame of the wait (decided on fd), the spinner becomes a C.accent check that draws over 8 f on E.out, a 'Done' tag fades in over 8 f, and the head leaves on that same frame. Scroll the list container, not the camera, with a lagged follow written as a pure function: loop from the shot's first frame to f with c += (headY(i) - 0.4 x H - c) x 0.08, and add a 2 px/f drift, so the head sits near 40% of the frame height and the list never stops dead. At the corner the head turns first, and the horizontal follow inherits the lag as it carries the eye to the result at a constant 10-14 px/f.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Draw the head as a flat 10 px dot in C.ink (white on an ink stage) with no halo, bloom or blur. Mark its state with size instead (12 px while travelling, 10 px while waiting). The spine, the step states, the scroll follow and every timing stay the same. The full look relies on glow; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** Head travel 40 f per step (E.rest), about 10 px/f for a 120 px pitch; wait 24-60 f per step, taken from the data. Row reveal 12 f (E.smooth) with a 12 px rise. Spinner one turn per 48 f; detail line ~1.5 chars/f; check 8 f (E.out); tag 8 f. Scroll lag 0.08 per frame plus a 2 px/f drift, peak about 12.5 px/f. Corner radius 40 px; horizontal run 10-14 px/f.
- **Use when:** An agent, build, deploy, import or onboarding process working through steps, where the point is visible progress toward one result.
- **Avoid when:** There are fewer than 3 steps (one status capsule says it), or the steps finish too fast to read (show the result with a count instead).

### Push-aside with bound layout

`ui-push-aside-reflow` · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature, walkthrough

An incoming panel or card enters from the edge and the neighbouring content moves aside because it is bound to the panel's edge, so one motion moves two elements and nothing overlaps.

- **Build:** Bind instead of tweening twice: each frame set neighbour.x = min(restX, panel.left - gap), so the neighbour reflows from the panel's own position. Shove: a dark card (C.ink2, radius 24 px, about 62% of frame width) enters from beyond the right edge over 72 f on E.whip (peak about 72 px/f at 40% under the motion-blur pass) and is placed so it reaches the headline word only after 58% of its move, where the card has slowed to 20 px/f or less, so the shoved word stays readable. Make room: a side panel 36% of frame width slides in on E.glide over 54 f (peak about 38 px/f) while the content card moves 0.43x the panel's travel on E.smooth, starting 28 f before the panel so it anticipates the arrival; the exit mirrors both over about 50 f. For copy, the product card glides 370 px aside and scales 1 to 0.83 on E.glide over 48 f (peak about 23 px/f) while the headline rises line by line into the freed side (Words, 6 f stagger), starting 4-6 f after the slide.
- **Timing:** Shove: 72 f (E.whip), contact after 58% of the move, word <= 20 px/f. Side panel: 36% FW over 54 f (E.glide); neighbour 0.43x travel with a 28 f lead (E.smooth); exit ~50 f. Copy: 370 px + scale 0.83 over 48 f (E.glide); lines 6 f apart from +4-6 f.
- **Use when:** Introducing a detail panel, a new card or a caption beside existing UI, or a joke where the layout itself does the gag.
- **Avoid when:** The incoming element should float above (modal, popover), or there is no room to move into.

### Row cascade

`ui-row-cascade` · workhorse · energy medium · any

List rows or cards appear one after another from top to bottom, each rising a few pixels as it fades in, so the list reads as data streaming in.

- **Build:** For row i, start = t0 + 4*i (6*i for taller cards); translateY 8 to 0 px through arrive() and opacity 0 to 1, both over 12 f on E.out, placed by transform only. When two columns describe input and output, give both sides the same row index so the build is mirrored and 5 rows complete in about 30 f. Let each row's text land in C.mute and darken to C.ink over 12 f, 40 f after the row arrives (mixColor), so the eye reads the structure first and the words second. Start the cascade about 20 f before the previous move (a transition, a portal edge) finishes, so the start of the scene is hidden inside it.
- **Timing:** Stagger 4 f (rows) to 6 f (cards); each row 12 f (E.out), 6-12 px rise; ink-in 12 f at +40 f; overlap the previous move by ~20 f.
- **Use when:** Populating any list, inbox, table, feed or a pair of mirrored input and output columns.
- **Avoid when:** Rows are added one at a time over a longer beat (top insert), or the list arrives by scrolling (flick scroll).

### Shell first, then contents, then the action

`ui-shell-first-build` · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature, walkthrough, vertical

The empty container is on screen first, its contents arrive left to right, the card unfolds downward in stages, and the primary button fills last as the clear call to act.

- **Build:** Show the container (bar, card, window) at t0 with nothing inside; its children enter in DOM order at a 4 f stagger, each rising 6 px through arrive() with opacity 0 to 1 over 12 f on E.out, and media slots first appear as C.mist rounded rects that fill with their image over 8 f, 8 f apart. The primary action comes last: its background ramps from transparent to solid on E.linear over 16 f from +20 f, and its label colour inverts on a single frame at +28 f. To teach the hierarchy, unfold the card downward in stages with a clip-path inset on its bottom edge on E.smooth (header row first, then 36 f to reveal the stats row, then 24 f to the full card, the bottom edge travelling about 330 px), each stage's content starting only once its slot is 60% revealed. Headlines inside the UI are live text in the camera world, revealed per word with Words (6 f stagger), so they inherit the plane's perspective.
- **Timing:** Children 4 f stagger, 12 f each (E.out), 6 px rise. Media fill 8 f, 8 f apart. Button fill 16 f (E.linear) from +20 f; label inverts at +28 f. Unfold 36 f then 24 f (E.smooth), content at 60% open. In-UI headline 6 f per word.
- **Use when:** The first appearance of any real product screen, especially dashboards, headers and forms whose reading order matters.
- **Avoid when:** The screen should feel already alive on the cut (enter it moving with a rise-in), or the shot is shorter than about 40 f.

### Spawn from the anchor point

`ui-anchor-point-spawn` · workhorse · energy medium · walkthrough, feature, launch

Menus, popovers, drop targets and detail cards scale out of the exact point that caused them, such as the cursor tip or a map pin, and collapse back into it.

- **Build:** Set transform-origin to the trigger point in the element's own coordinates (cursor tip, pin base, the edge of the button) and scale with lmix from about 0.05, opacity reaching 1 within the first 4 f; the log-space scale keeps the far edge from jumping on frame 1. Small surfaces (menus, popovers, a card out of a pin): lmix(0.05, 1, prog(f, a, a + 12, E.out)), no overshoot, adding 2 f per extra 100 px of size, then a small camera reframe toward the surface starting 2 f later over 20-40 f on E.cam. Large surfaces (a drop target filling a panel): lmix(0.036, 1, prog(f, a, a + 48, E.smooth)), a flat C.accent fill with a 12 px radius, its icon and hint text fading in over the last 8 f; it collapses back into the point over 36 f on E.smooth. Keep the cursor (fx/Cursor.tsx) parked on the trigger during the spawn so cause and effect share one point.
- **Timing:** Small: 12 f (lmix, E.out) from 0.05, opacity 4 f, far edge ~63 px/f for a 300 px menu; camera reframe from +2 f over 20-40 f (E.cam). Large: 48 f (lmix, E.smooth) from 0.036, hint over the last 8 f, collapse 36 f (E.smooth).
- **Use when:** Any UI that opens from a click, or a drag target appearing: menus, popovers, dialogs, drop zones, cards from a map pin.
- **Avoid when:** The element enters from off-screen or is a full window (rise-in), or the trigger point is out of frame.

### Top insert pushes the list down

`ui-top-insert-push` · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature, loop, walkthrough

New items arrive at the top of a list one at a time and every earlier item slides down one slot, on a steady metronome that reads as abundance or on a slower cadence where each row resolves as it is generated.

- **Build:** Compute every item's y from the data each frame (listLayout from the product-ui reference, newest at index 0), so earlier items slide down one pitch on E.ui as each new one mounts; overlapping pushes simply add. Metronome: one insert every 14 f with a 155 px pitch pushed over 20 f (about 21 px/f); the new pill reveals left to right with clip-path inset(0 100% 0 0) to inset(0) over 12 f on E.ui, its icon leading and its label fading in 4 f later, while any paired object (an item landing on a stack) drops 60-90 px with opacity over 10 f on E.out; wrap the group in a camera drift whose velocity decays as vStart*0.97^f from about 19 to 3 px/f over 90 f. Generation: one insert every 36-40 f, the row starting at scaleX 0.6 about its left edge with blurIn(p, 6) and an 8% C.accent tint, reaching full width, sharp and neutral over 12 f on E.out while the rows below move 66 px over 10 f on E.ui. Put a tick on each insert frame (LANDINGS) so the cadence is heard.
- **Timing:** Metronome: every 14 f, push 155 px over 20 f (E.ui), pill reveal 12 f (E.ui), label +4 f, camera drift 19 to 3 px/f (x0.97 per frame). Generation: every 36-40 f, resolve 12 f (E.out) from scaleX 0.6 and 6 px blur, push 66 px over 10 f (E.ui).
- **Use when:** Results, messages, subtasks or saved items accumulating: generated rows, imports landing, a feed or a stack filling up.
- **Avoid when:** The whole list should appear at once (row cascade), or there are so many inserts that the pushes blur into noise (scroll instead).

### Clutter pile-up, then strip to one

`ui-clutter-pileup-strip` · accent · energy high · launch, feature, vertical

Clicks spawn copies of a control until the frame is a messy pile, then elements vanish one per beat and the survivors snap to re-centre until a single tile remains.

- **Build:** Pile-up: on each click (pressAt from fx/Cursor.tsx) spawn a clone every 4 f for about 60 f at x = (rand(i) - 0.5)*500 and y = (rand(i + 99) - 0.5)*300 px, each travelling 40-80 px out from the previous clone over 8 f on E.out while scaling 0.9 to 1, so the motion-blur pass smears every spawn, and drift the whole pile up 1.5 px/f. Strip: hold the survivors in an array whose length drops at listed frames, one removal every 5-7 f, choose the state with fd(f), and compute the centred layout from the current array with no tween, so the remaining tiles jump to their new places on the removal frame. Hold the last survivor 17 f under a 0.5% scale drift (breath() from lib/camera.ts), then exit it or let it become the next shot. Put a soft tick on every spawn and removal, rising in level, so the acceleration is heard.
- **Timing:** Spawns every 4 f for ~60 f (12-15 clones), 8 f each (E.out, 40-80 px), pile drift 1.5 px/f. Removals every 5-7 f with an instant re-centre (fd); last survivor 17 f with a 0.5% drift.
- **Use when:** Showing overload (too many tools, buttons, tabs, notifications) and then focus: the product reduces chaos to the one thing that matters.
- **Avoid when:** Calm or premium films, or elements whose text must be read; the jumps are deliberately abrupt.

### Genie launch from an icon

`ui-genie-launch-from-icon` · accent · energy medium · launch, feature, walkthrough

A dock or home-screen icon flares open at its top into a curved funnel that keeps widening until it fills the frame, and the app's first screen is already sitting inside it.

- **Build:** Render the app's first screen full-frame above the current scene and clip it with clip-path: path(), rebuilt every frame from a few numbers. The bottom edge sits on the icon's base with width wb; the top edge is h above it with width wt. Each side is a quadratic curve whose control point is the bottom corner raised by 0.45 h, so the outline pinches like a funnel. Grow it in log space so it leaves the icon slowly and speeds up: h = lmix(iconH, H + 120, p) and wt = lmix(iconW, W + 240, p), with p = prog(f, a, a + 44, E.linear). Over the same 44 f, the top edge's centre drifts from the icon to the frame centre on E.smooth, which peaks mid-way, before the growth gets fast. In the last 24 f, with s = prog(f, a + 20, a + 44, E.smooth), the waist widens toward the top (wb = mix(iconW, wt, s)) and the bottom edge drops from the icon base to 60 px below the frame. With these numbers the fastest edge stays near 70-75 px/f on the final frames, under the motion-blur pass. Start the funnel 4 f after pressAt on the icon (the icon's tile darkens 10% on the press frame). Either keep the revealed screen still at its final size, or let it settle from 1.04 to 1 over the same 44 f on E.outSoft. On the first frame the path covers the whole frame, unmount the clip and the old scene, and start the app's first UI event (a caret, a typed greeting) on that frame, so the launch hands straight over to the product.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Fill the funnel with the app's real first screen on its flat stage colour, or with one flat colour taken from the icon, never the icon's colour ramp. The clip path, the log-space growth and the timing stay the same. The full look relies on gradient; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** Press, then funnel from +4 f: 44 f in log space (about x1.06-1.08 per frame, E.linear progress). Centre drift over the same 44 f (E.smooth). Waist and bottom edge open over the last 24 f (E.smooth). Fastest edge ~70-75 px/f at the end. Optional content settle 1.04 to 1 over 44 f (E.outSoft). Clip removed on full cover; the next UI event starts on that frame.
- **Use when:** Opening an app, a document or a tool from its icon in a dock, launcher or home screen, as a playful product-native scene change.
- **Avoid when:** The product is never launched from an icon, or the film already has a genie (once is a gag, twice reads as a template).

### Path fractures into a fan, then re-converges

`ui-path-fracture-fan` · accent · energy medium · launch, feature

A solid line draws out, breaks into dashes, splits into a fan of curves that end on obstacle pills, and later the curves funnel back into one point that becomes the next diagram.

- **Build:** Draw the trunk from the source node as an SVG path with pathLength 1, strokeDashoffset 1 to 0 on E.linear over 12 f; at +12 f let it degrade by tweening strokeDasharray from 'L 0' to '24 12' over 8 f (dash = mix(L, 24, p), gap = mix(0, 12, p)). At +26 f split it into 6 cubic beziers from one shared point with their ends spread +-200 px in y, each revealed by its own dashoffset on E.glide over 24 f at a 2 f stagger so the drawing head stays under about 70 px/f, and pop a labelled obstacle pill at each end as its curve arrives (opacity step plus scale 0.9 to 1 over 8 f on E.out). Hard-cut to a 2.5x punch-in on the pills about 10 f after the fan completes. To resolve, give each pill a trailing bezier ending on one point, the next diagram's first node, draw them over 24 f on E.smooth while the camera travels the same way with no cut, and finish the camera's travel with an E.out landing of about 210 px over 60 f (22 px/f at its start) through lib/camera.ts.
- **Timing:** Trunk 12 f (E.linear); dashes at +12 f over 8 f to '24 12'; fan at +26 f: 6 curves x 24 f (E.glide), 2 f stagger, complete at +60 f; punch-in cut at ~+70 f (2.5x). Converge 24 f (E.smooth); camera landing 210 px over 60 f (E.out), 22 px/f at its start.
- **Use when:** Explaining the friction of an old way (one simple path turning into many obstacles) before the turn to one clean path.
- **Avoid when:** The viewer needs real product UI on screen; this is diagram language, and a diagram act longer than about 4 s loses the thread.

### Stalled state by dimming

`ui-stalled-state` · accent · energy calm · launch, feature, walkthrough

A token stops on its rail, the destination greys out, short status words appear one after another, and the frame goes briefly still so the blockage is felt.

- **Build:** Split the rail at the stalled token: the travelled part solid, the part ahead dotted (strokeDasharray '2 4'), both drawn from the same path and clipped at the token's position. On the stall frame the destination node dims to 30% (opacity, or mixColor toward C.mute) over 8 f on E.smooth; status words then appear beside the token at +6, +28 and +40 f, each an opacity step with a 6 px rise through arrive() over 8 f on E.out, and at +51 f the first word dims to 40% so the decisive word (the reason, the day) stands alone. Bring the camera to zero velocity for a designed freeze of at most 15 f on a gap in the sound, then resume a 0.3 px/f drift so nothing sits static past 48 f.
- **Timing:** Node dim 8 f (E.smooth) to 30%. Status words at +6/+28/+40 f, 8 f each (E.out, 6 px rise); first word dims at +51 f. Freeze <= 15 f on a silence, then 0.3 px/f drift.
- **Use when:** The problem beat: money, a message or a task stuck waiting (closed, pending, rejected) just before the product unblocks it.
- **Avoid when:** The film has no problem act, or the block would sit longer than about 1.5 s; stillness only works as a short contrast to the motion around it.

### Fanned stack resolves into slots

`ui-fan-resolve-to-slots` · signature · energy medium · launch, feature, vertical

A tilted, overlapping stack of cards spreads into an even row, or each card flips to show its face and flies small into a slot of a list grid where its label resolves.

- **Build:** Start with 4-6 cards stacked 20 px apart with seeded tilts (rand(i) mapped to +-6 deg), or a fan (rotateZ -20 deg, rotateY 25 deg, 40 px offset), z-order from the stack. Row preset: x = mix(stackX + 20*i, slotX_i, p) and rotate = mix(seed_i, 0, p) with p = prog(f, t0 + 2*i, t0 + 2*i + T, E.out) and T = max(24, 0.09 x travel) f, so the farthest card stays under 70 px/f and nothing overshoots. Flip preset: card i starts at t0 + 6*i, turns rotateY 0 to 180 deg on E.linear over 6 f, or 8 f for cards wider than 200 px so the edge stays near 50 px/f at edge-on (swapping from its muted back to its full face at 90 deg), drifts on E.out for 12 f (28 down to 7 px/f), then FLIPs to its grid slot rect (scale about 0.25, rotateZ to 0) over max(12, travel/20) f on E.rest; its label then rises 6 px and clears from blurIn(p, 6) over 8 f. Six cards should land within about 60 f.
- **Timing:** Row: 2 f stagger, T = max(24, 0.09 x travel) f (E.out), tilt +-6 deg. Flip: 6 f stagger, flip 6 f (8 f over 200 px wide, E.linear), drift 12 f (E.out), FLIP to slot max(12, travel/20) f (E.rest), label 8 f; six cards in ~60 f.
- **Use when:** Many options, offers, integrations or tools becoming an orderly set: the 'all in one place' or 'compare them all' beat.
- **Avoid when:** The cards must be read while they move, or there is only one card.

### Orbit gather and merge

`ui-orbit-gather-merge` · signature · energy medium · launch, feature, loop

Tokens swing into orbit around a node, slow to a lazy spin, then accelerate one by one into a single exit point from which a line shoots out.

- **Build:** Place 4 tokens on a 95 px radius around the source node (above the node, below the exit line) and drive each angle in closed form: theta_i(f) = theta0 + 90*i - (132.5*(1 - exp(-f/10)) + 2*f) deg, a 13 deg/f swing (about 22 px/f of arc) that decays to a 2 deg/f spin within 30 f. Token 0 is there at f0; tokens 1-3 spawn at f10, f18 and f28, each scaling 0 to 1 over 10 f on E.out. Pick theta0 so each token is 90-120 deg short of the exit angle (3 o'clock) when its merge starts; token i then covers that remaining angle forward over 16 f on E.contact, landing at f72, f82 and f86 at under 60 px/f, its scale cutting to 0 on arrival while the exit node takes scale 1 + 0.08*hitPulse(t) and a tick. At f92 a line draws out of the exit point (pathLength 1, strokeDashoffset 1 to 0 over 12 f on E.out) and carries the story to the next diagram.
- **Timing:** omega = 13.25*exp(-f/10) + 2 deg/f, radius 95 px at 1080p. Spawns f10/f18/f28, 10 f each (E.out). Merges 16 f each (E.contact), landing f72/f82/f86 at < 60 px/f; hitPulse(t, 2, 5) on the exit node. Exit line f92, 12 f (E.out). About 105 f in all.
- **Use when:** Several inputs, funds or sources gather before one action (pooling, batching, syncing, sending) and the idea should be told by physics with no words.
- **Avoid when:** The tokens are UI cards carrying text (unreadable while orbiting), or the story has no single output point.

### Outline-led insert and spawn

`ui-outline-led-reveal` · signature · energy medium · feature, walkthrough, launch

A thin accent line or a heavy outline appears first and opens into a new row or a modal, then the stroke decays to a hairline so the content takes over.

- **Build:** Row insert: a 2 px C.accent line appears across the list in one frame at the insert position, then the row opens from height 0 to row height over 10 f on E.ui, pushing the rows below through the computed list layout at 20 px/f or less; its 2 px border decays from the accent to 40% over 24 f on E.linear and then to nothing, and the row's content fades in over the last 4 f of the open. Repeat inserts every 41 f so three new rows read as a countable rhythm, each with a tick on its line frame. Modal spawn: the modal scales lmix(0.07, 1, prog(f, a, a + 26, E.out)) about the trigger point while an overlay stroke in the accent runs 6 to 10 to 1 px wide (interpolate(p, [0, 0.6, 1], [6, 10, 1]) on the same progress); after landing it thins to 1 px over 12 f and its opacity falls to 0.3, leaving a clean modal. At its peak the stroke can carry a faint outer glow, which the hard bans rule out; build it flat (see the variant).
