- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Use a flat 2 px stroke in the film's single accent with no box-shadow, bloom or blur; express the flash as stroke width (2 to 3 px for 4 f via hitPulse) and an opacity decay from 1 to 0.4 to 0 over 24 f, and frame the modal with a solid 6-10 px accent stroke that thins to 1 px. The full look relies on glow; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** Line 1 f; open 10 f (E.ui); border decay 24 f (E.linear); content in the last 4 f; inserts every 41 f. Modal 26 f (lmix on E.out) from scale 0.07, far edge ~52 px/f; stroke 6/10/1 px; thin 12 f; opacity to 0.3.
- **Use when:** A click that creates something (a new account, row, record or dialog) that must read from a wide shot, or repeated creation shown as a rhythm.
- **Avoid when:** The accent already means something else in the film, or the shot is a calm monochrome close-up where a bright stroke would shout.

### Toss into a bin with one rebound

`ui-discard-into-bin` · signature · energy high · launch, feature, vertical

Icons or chips are thrown into a container that rises in to catch them, drop through its mouth and peek back out once before settling.

- **Build:** Layer order, back to front: bin body, thrown items, bin front lip, with the items clipped by a clipPath at the mouth so they vanish inside; the bin rises 160 px on E.out over 24 f. Toss: each item rises about 260 px on E.out over 24 f (about 68 px/f on its first frame), hangs 3 f, then falls about 340 px on E.contact over 22 f while rotateZ goes to +-15 deg (sign from rand(i)) and x eases to the mouth on E.smooth, entering at no more than 70 px/f under the motion-blur pass. Chain variant: chips follow an SVG path into the bin, chip i at path.getPointAtLength(L*E.contact(prog(f, t0 + 5*i, t0 + 5*i + 60, E.linear))) rotated to the tangent (atan2 of a 1 px look-ahead), the element they trail squashed to a 6 px tall tail. Six frames after the last entry the contents peek back up about 24 px on spr(f, hit, SPR.land) and settle within 16 f, the rim takes squash(t), and a low 60 to 30 Hz thud lands on that frame; this counts as one of the film's two spring landings.
- **Timing:** Bin rise 160 px, 24 f (E.out). Item rise ~260 px, 24 f (E.out); hang 3 f; fall ~340 px, 22 f (E.contact), <= 70 px/f; tilt +-15 deg. Chain: 60 f per chip (E.contact along the path), 5 f lag. Rebound at +6 f, ~24 px, SPR.land, settled in 16 f.
- **Use when:** A comic or decisive 'throw the old way away' beat: replacing old tools, clearing clutter, deleting the problem.
- **Avoid when:** Serious, calm or enterprise tone, or the film has already used its two spring landings.

## Data and numbers

Numbers are proof, so they must read at a glance and stay true on any paused frame: tabular figures, a fixed digit count, and every shown value computed from fd(frame) so no motion-blur sub-sample shows two values. Hero counts are short, 28-46 f, starting from a credible 85-90% of the target on a quad-out (E.type) so the last unit lands in the final ~6 f instead of stalling; ambient UI counters may run 36-104 f. Charts draw in 24-96 f, bars grow 12-20 f each at 1.6-5 f staggers with any group landing within 30 f, and every bar tip, scan edge or line head stays at or under about 60-70 px/f at 1080p. A figure starts changing on the frame its cause lands (a press, a landing, a tab; effects follow the interaction by 2 f) and then holds at least 36 f plus 6 f per word of its label under a 2-3% breath. The one accent marks the hero series or the chosen item while comparison data stays grey, and two numbers are never crossfaded in place: cut them, count them or roll them.

### Constant-speed bar sweep with lit caps

`dn-bar-sweep-lit-caps` · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature, loop, walkthrough

A row of bars grows in a wave that travels at constant speed; each bar eases up on its own and flashes a bright cap that relaxes to the resting tone.

- **Build:** Bar i starts at at + 1.6i, a linear wave travelling at bar pitch / 1.6 px per frame (about 25 px/f at 1080p). It grows with height = h_i * prog(frame, start_i, start_i + 12, E.out) from a bottom anchor; make the grow last at least 0.09 x the bar height in px so the top edge never passes 70 px/f. A 3 px cap on each bar arrives in C.accent and relaxes to the bar's resting tone over 20 f after the bar lands (mixColor, cap opacity 1 to 0.6), because the accent means 'just landed'. For a centre-out symmetric wall, use tr-stepped-column-fill instead.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Solid single-tone bars (or a single-hue tonal ramp) whose cap uses the film's one accent and relaxes to the bar tone: never a multi-hue gradient and never a warm amber cap. The full look relies on orange, gradient; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** 1.6 f per bar (~25 px/f wave). Each bar 12 f on E.out (at least 0.09 x its height in px). Cap relaxes over 20 f.
- **Use when:** Volume, activity or histogram data streaming in; an opening equaliser or skyline that hints at growth.
- **Avoid when:** Bars that must be compared precisely, since the wave delays reading; fewer than 6 bars.

### Ease-out count-up from a near-final value

`dn-ease-out-count-up` · workhorse · energy medium · any

A proof figure counts up in place from a credible value just below its target and decelerates, so the last units tick in one at a time and it reads in about half a second.

- **Build:** Compute the shown value on whole frames: v = Math.round(mix(a, b, prog(fd(frame), at, at + 28, E.type))), with a at 85-90% of b (173 to 195, 734 to 799), so early frames jump 2-3 units and the last ones step by 1. Use E.out only for ranges over ~500 units, where its long tail still has digits to tick. Render the value as plain text through typeStyle (tabular-nums), with a fixed digit count and Intl.NumberFormat separators so the box never changes width, and let the digits replace in place each frame: no roll, no crossfade. Start the count on the frame its cause lands and put ticks on countSteps(a, b, at, 28, E.type) frames, thinned to at most one every 2 f. After it lands, keep the block alive with breath() on the camera (2-3%) until the next element covers it.
- **Timing:** Hero count 28 f on E.type (quad-out: 2x the mean rate at the start, so the last unit lands in the final ~6 f). Prices and recounts 36-46 f; ambient UI KPIs 36-104 f. Start at 85-90% of the target. Hold the landed figure at least 36 f (plus 6 f per word of any label) under a 2-3% breath before anything covers it.
- **Use when:** A single proof figure (countries, users, a price) must register in under a second, or a number inside a UI shot should feel live.
- **Avoid when:** The number is the film's hero reveal and deserves a reel or a snap-out; nothing on screen causes the count to start.

### Flag cascade, then one chosen

`dn-flag-then-select` · workhorse · energy calm · feature, walkthrough, launch

Status marks appear on a set of cards one after another, then a single card switches to the accent state: many flagged, one picked.

- **Build:** Card i gets its flag at at + 6i: its border mixes from the card fill to a mid grey over 6 f on E.ui, and a 10 px hollow dot scales from 0 to 1 on SPR.micro. Flags stay neutral so the one accent can mean 'chosen'. About 28 f after the first flag, the chosen card switches over 8 f on E.ui: border to C.accent, a 6% accent inner tint, the dot filled, and scale 1 + 0.02 * hitPulse(t, 2, 6). Hold for at most 48 f with a slow 2% push toward it, then the chosen card leaves first on E.in into the cut.
- **Timing:** Flags 6 f apart, 6 f each. Selection ~28 f after the first flag, an 8 f change. Hold at most 48 f with a 2% push. The chosen card exits on E.in.
- **Use when:** Triage, review, matching, anomaly detection: anything that narrows many down to one.
- **Avoid when:** The pick isn't what the product actually outputs; grids of more than ~12 cards, where the cascade reads as a queue.

### Line chart draws with a tracking head

`dn-line-draw-tracked-head` · workhorse · energy medium · any

A line or stepped series draws left to right behind a solid dot at its head that the eye can follow, accelerating through the middle and creeping into its last point.

- **Build:** Draw the series as an SVG path with pathLength={1}, strokeDasharray 1 and strokeDashoffset 1 - p. Put a solid head dot (r 6 px at 1080p, with a 2 px ring in the stage colour) at the point at fraction p along the polyline, sampled from the data in JS rather than measured from the DOM. Beneath the line, add an area fill in the line's hue fading from 18% to 0% opacity, clipped by a rect whose right edge follows the head. Drive p from 0 to 1 over 96 f on E.rest in a single link: it starts from rest, peaks near 29% of the draw and spends its last third creeping into the last point, so the head never stops and restarts. The head peaks around 40-60 px/f, so the blur pass streaks it while the drawn line stays crisp; when the head lands, roll in the endpoint value with Roll.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** A solid head dot with a 2 px stage-colour ring and no blur, drop-shadow halo or bloom. The area fill stays a single-hue opacity ramp. The full look relies on glow; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** Full draw 96 f on E.rest (peak near 29%, 3.5x the mean speed; the last 30 f creep at about 2-3 px/f on a 1,400 px path). Short form: 24 f on E.out, with the area fill fading in from 8 f later over 16 f. Head peaks at 40-60 px/f at 1080p. Endpoint value rolls over 14 f.
- **Use when:** Growth, price or usage over time; any chart where the trend is the message.
- **Avoid when:** Invented up-and-to-the-right data; charts under ~400 px wide, where the head reads as noise.

### Mechanical digit reel

`dn-digit-reel-detent` · workhorse · energy medium · any

Each digit sits in its own masked column and rolls vertically like an odometer: the low columns spin while the high ones step once, landing column by column.

- **Build:** Use Roll from src/fx/Roll.tsx in count mode (from, to, start, dur 60, ease E.out, roll 14, group ','). countSteps places a step on every whole frame where the integer changes, so the low columns spin a slot per frame while each high column rolls once on its own E.out, and the fixed column count keeps the width still. For an event counter, pass steps at the landing frames of their causes, with roll 6-8 f. For a single column that matters (a badge going 9 to 10, the leading digit of a total), build that strip by hand and drive its slot with spr(frame, step, SPR.detent), so it clicks home with the one small overshoot a detent is allowed. Ticks go on step frames, thinned to one per 2-3 f while they are dense, with each of the last three steps ticked.
- **Timing:** Count 60 f on E.out. Column roll 14 f (6-8 f for event counters). Detent landing ~16 f. Ticks at least 2 f apart.
- **Use when:** Counters with a tactile, product-like feel: totals, balances, counters that step on visible events.
- **Avoid when:** The film already counts with plain in-place digits (keep one counting style per film); fewer than 3 changes, where one roll is enough.

### Mini bar-chart answer card

`dn-answer-card-bars` · workhorse · energy calm · walkthrough, feature, launch

Inside a chat or a panel, an answer arrives as a small card of labelled horizontal bars that grow in sequence, followed by a one-line insight that states the key figures.

- **Build:** The card rises 24 px on SPR.firm (opacity over 10 f on E.smooth). Each row holds a label, a bar track (C.mist on paper, C.ink2 on ink) and a value. Bar i's width is value% x track x prog(frame, at + 5i, at + 5i + 20, E.outSoft), and its value counts on the same progress. Keep tracks at or under 300 px, or stretch the grow to track/15 frames, so the bar tip stays at or under 70 px/f. Only the row the insight is about takes C.accent; the rest stay neutral. Six frames after the last bar lands, type the insight with TypeOn with its two figures at weight 600. Keep the card under a 2% camera breath while it is read, and optionally hard-cut on the next 8th to a 2.4x punch-in on the highlighted row (cam-punch-in-insert) that pans sideways with inertia(f, cut, 20, 0.89), starting at the 20 px/f text limit and settling in about 30 f.
- **Timing:** Rows 20 f each on E.outSoft at a 5 f stagger (the group lands within 30 f). The insight types over ~40 f, starting 6 f after the last bar. Card visible ~180 f under a 2% breath. Optional 2.4x punch-in cut, then a pan from 20 px/f decaying 0.89 per frame (settled in about 30 f).
- **Use when:** An AI or analytics product answers a question with data; a walkthrough needs one piece of quantitative proof.
- **Avoid when:** More than 6 rows, where the group outruns 30 f and the labels shrink; bars that carry no real meaning.

### One control drives several live numbers

`dn-linked-control-counters` · workhorse · energy calm · feature, walkthrough, launch

Dragging a slider visibly drives every dependent figure in lockstep, and the fill changes tint once it passes a marked threshold.

- **Build:** Drive everything from one progress, p = prog(frame, at, at + 90, E.smooth). The slider fill is mix(0.35, 0.84, p) x track, the thumb (with a 2 px ring) rides the same value, and each dependent figure (percentage, amount, headroom) is computed from that value on fd(frame), rounded and set in fixed-width tabular figures. Past the threshold marker, draw the fill from the marker to the thumb in a brighter tint of the fill hue, and switch the affected figure's colour on the crossing frame. The cursor (Cursor.tsx) grabs the thumb 8 f before the drag starts and rides it. Figures that fall (headroom 44K to 13K) count down on the same p, and the formula is asserted in data.ts so every frame stays consistent.
- **Timing:** Drag 90 f on E.smooth (fastest change mid-drag). Cursor grabs 8 f before. Figures update every whole frame. Hold the end state at least 36 f under a breath.
- **Use when:** Calculators, pricing, risk limits, utilisation: any feature whose logic is 'move this and those follow'.
- **Avoid when:** The dependent figures aren't computed consistently from one formula; more than 3 dependents.

### Ring gauge filling with its centre number

`dn-ring-gauge-sync` · workhorse · energy calm · any

A circular gauge sweeps to its value while the number at its centre counts on the same progress, and the ring's end cap leads the eye around.

- **Build:** Draw an SVG circle rotated -90deg over a C.line track ring, with pathLength={1}, strokeLinecap round and strokeDasharray `${v} 1`, where v = target * prog(frame, at, at + N, E.outSoft) and N = max(48, 0.48 x radius x target) frames, which keeps the end cap at or under 60 px/f (48 f covers a 160 px ring up to 63%; a full 160 px ring needs 77 f). The centre figure is Math.round(100 * v) on fd(frame), in tabular figures with a tucked % at 0.4x size. The arc arrives in C.accent and relaxes to the ink tone over 20 f after landing; for nested rings, stagger them 6 f apart with stagger() so the group lands within 30 f.
- **Timing:** Fill over N = max(48, 0.48 x radius x target) f on E.outSoft (48 f for most gauges, 77 f for a full 160 px ring). Centre count on the same progress. Accent relaxes over 20 f after landing. Nested rings 6 f apart.
- **Use when:** Percentages, scores, completion and utilisation; status pills and KPI tiles.
- **Avoid when:** Values that aren't parts of a whole; more than 3 concentric rings.

### Area-true ratio comparison

`dn-area-ratio-compare` · accent · energy calm · launch, feature, vertical, loop

A multiplier claim ('10x smaller') plays as a block that shrinks in log space to the area the ratio implies, leaving an outline of its old size behind.

- **Build:** Draw block A at side s in C.mute, anchored bottom-left on a baseline. At the cue, scale it from that corner with lmix(1, 1/sqrt(ratio), prog(frame, at, at + 48, E.smooth)), so its area ends at 1/ratio and the shrink keeps an even ratio per frame. Its fill mixes to C.accent over the last 12 f, and a 1.5 px C.line outline stays at the original size as the reference. The ratio figure counts beside it on E.type over 36 f and lands on the same frame as the block. For speed or time claims, compare bar lengths (a linear ratio) instead of areas.
- **Timing:** Shrink 48 f on E.smooth via lmix. Fill mixes to the accent over the last 12 f. Ratio count 36 f on E.type, landing with the block. Hold at least 36 f under a 2% breath.
- **Use when:** Multiplier and reduction claims about size, cost, time or footprint.
- **Avoid when:** Ratios above ~25x, where the block shrinks to a dot (show the number alone); claims that aren't really proportional.

### Before-to-after with a delta chip

`dn-delta-chip-compare` · accent · energy medium · launch, feature, vertical, walkthrough

The old figure steps back to a small grey 'before', the new figure counts in at hero size, and a delta chip ('-38%') pops in the accent on the landing frame.

- **Build:** At the cue the old hero figure lifts out (0.3 em up, 12 f on E.in through depart, opacity on E.smooth), while a smaller 'before' copy rises into a secondary slot above-left through MaskRise, so the two values never sit crossfaded in one place. The new figure counts at hero size from the old value to the new on E.type over 36 f, and a 2 px C.mute strike draws across the 'before' value over 10 f on E.out. On the count's landing frame, the delta chip (C.accent fill) scales from 0.6 to 1 from its left edge on SPR.micro (no overshoot) with a tick, then its fill relaxes to C.ink2 with accent text over 20 f.

### Companion glyph swaps mid-count

`dn-count-glyph-swap` · accent · energy medium · launch, feature, loop

A small icon riding a counting number (a flag, an avatar, a status glyph) swaps to its destination state when the count crosses a threshold, then drops from superscript to the baseline.

- **Build:** Set a 0.45 em glyph at the number's top-right as a superscript (translateY -0.35 em). Swap its source on the first whole frame where the shown value reaches the threshold (an fd-based v >= T compare, about 60% of the way through the count), cutting between the two images with no crossfade. On that frame start the drop: translateY from -0.35 em to 0 over 8 f with arrive(prog(frame, swap - 1, swap + 7, E.out)), so the new glyph seats on the baseline while the count is still finishing. Put a soft tick on the swap frame, separate from the count ticks.

- **Avoid when:** The glyph would only be decoration; counts shorter than 20 f, where the swap gets lost.

### Process-status pill with ring progress

`dn-status-pill-ring` · accent · energy calm · walkthrough, feature, launch

A compact capsule shows where a process stands in one glance: a live dot, a mono step label, a ring filled to the current percentage, the step count and a grey date.

### Top-to-bottom row refresh

`dn-row-cascade-value-swap` · accent · energy medium · walkthrough, feature

When a filter changes, a thin scan line crosses each table row in turn from top to bottom, and the row's icon, label and values change behind it.

- **Build:** Two frames after the filter chip lands, row i gets its own scan, x_i = rowW * prog(frame, at + 3i, at + 3i + 20, E.linear). Clip the old row content with inset(0 0 0 x_i px) and the new with inset(0 (rowW - x_i) px 0 0), so each cell changes as the line crosses it and nothing is crossfaded. A 1.5 px hairline in C.line rides x_i and fades over its last 6 f; only the row the story is about gets the accent. Figures that change by a small amount roll with Roll (12 f) from the frame the line reaches their cell, instead of wiping.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** One neutral hairline per row (the accent only on the row the story cares about), with no rainbow-tinted streak and no glow. The full look relies on glow, gradient; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** Starts 2 f after the chip lands. 3 f row stagger. 20 f per row, linear (at most 60 px/f across a 1,250 px row). Six rows finish within ~35 f. Hairline fades over 6 f.
- **Use when:** Tables, activity feeds or leaderboards that refresh on a filter or a new period.
- **Avoid when:** Only one cell changes, so a Roll on it is enough; more than 8 rows, where the cascade reads as a queue.

### Tucked unit under the last digits

`dn-tucked-unit-label` · accent · energy calm · any

A small lowercase unit word fades in right-aligned under a big number's last digits, its top overlapping the numeral's baseline, so number and unit read as one mark.

- **Build:** Set the unit at 0.35x the numeral's font size in the film's one sans (weight 450, C.mute or the stage's secondary ink). Align its right edge with the numeral's right edge (measureTracked, minus the last glyph's trailing tracking) and its top with the numeral baseline minus 0.3x the label's line height, so it tucks under the last two digits. Fade it in over 19 f on E.smooth with a 4 px rise through arrive, starting at least 12 f after the number settles so the figure reads first. It then holds with the number under the shot's breath.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Same placement and size in the film's one sans at weight 450, in C.mute or the stage's secondary ink: no second display typeface and no cream or gold tint. The full look relies on serif, beige; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** Starts at least 12 f after the number settles (36 f is a good default). Opacity over 19 f on E.smooth with a 4 px rise via arrive. Label at 0.35x the numeral size, overlapping its baseline by 30% of the label height.
- **Use when:** A hero figure needs its unit (views, users, ms) without a second line pushing the layout down.
- **Avoid when:** The unit is longer than one short word; numbers ending in narrow digits (1, 7) that leave no room to tuck under.

### Unit grid that fills to the count

`dn-unit-grid-tally` · accent · energy calm · launch, feature, vertical

A grid of small squares, each standing for a fixed number of units, fills in a diagonal wave while a counter beside it reaches the total, and one cell lands in the accent.

- **Build:** Lay out an n x m grid of 14-20 px rounded squares as a C.line track, each square standing for a fixed number of units. Fill cell (r, c) from at + stagger(r + c, n + m - 1, 30, E.out), with opacity over 8 f on E.smooth and scale from 0.6 to 1 on SPR.micro, and fill the last cell by its fraction through a width clip. The counter beside the grid shows filled cells x unit on fd(frame) in tabular figures, so the number and the grid can never disagree. The cell that carries the point (the last one, or 'you') lands in C.accent with scale 1 + 0.15 * hitPulse(t, 2, 8).
- **Timing:** Diagonal wave over 30 f on stagger with E.out. Each cell fades over 8 f, with an SPR.micro scale. Accent cell pulse: attack 2 f, tau 8 f. Hold at least 36 f with a 2% push.
- **Use when:** Shares and proportions ('3 in 10 teams'), quotas, capacity; making a large count tangible without a chart.
- **Avoid when:** Exact values with many significant digits, which the grid can't show honestly; cells under 12 px on vertical phone formats.

### Hero bar in close-up, then pull back

`dn-hero-bar-pullback` · signature · energy medium · launch, feature

The winning bar (or the hero chart) grows across a tight frame, then the camera eases back to show the whole chart, with the grey comparison bars and their values.

- **Build:** Lay the whole chart out in world space with the anchor camera (src/lib/camera.ts): the hero bar in C.accent, the comparison bars in C.mute, values at the bar ends. Shot A frames the hero bar at k of about 1.33-1.5. Grow its width over 50 f on E.smooth while the camera pushes 4% and tracks the tip at about 60% of frame width; keep the tip at or under 70 px/f on screen (on-screen length x 2.86 / frames). On the landing frame, pull back with lc(A, B, prog(frame, land, land + 80, E.cam)) to the full chart at k = 1. The grey bars are already at value, the labels type in with TypeOn, and the percentages count on E.type over 28 f, 4 f apart top to bottom, starting 12 f into the pull-back.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** A flat accent bar with no outer glow or bloom. It stands apart from the grey bars by colour and 4-6 px of extra thickness only. The full look relies on glow; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** Bar fill 50 f on E.smooth (no overshoot) with a 4% push. Pull-back 52-80 f on E.cam to 0.65-0.75 of the close scale. Values count over 28 f on E.type at a 4 f stagger. Hold the full chart at least 36 f under a breath.
- **Use when:** Benchmarks and comparisons the product wins; any chart whose hero value should be felt before it is compared.
- **Avoid when:** Narrow wins, which the close-up would oversell; more than ~6 bars, whose labels go unreadable after the pull-back.

### Metric as the first statement

`dn-metric-cold-open` · signature · energy high · launch, vertical, feature

The film opens on its proof number already moving, with no title and no logo, and the brand waits for the end lockup.

- **Build:** Frame 0 is the number mid-count or mid-roll (an ease-out count-up, a digit reel or the macro snap-out) at hero size, cap height about 11% of frame height, centred on the stage colour. The first visible change comes by frame 2, with no fade-up from black. The number settles by frame 40, stays readable for at least 72 f including its unit under a 2% breath push, then hands off on a cut at a motion peak into the problem. Run the story as metric, problem, solution, process, lockup, and keep the logo and product name off screen until the lockup, which stays the only brand moment. Mark the landing with an audio drop: thin or cut the music on the landing frame and allow a designed freeze of at most 15 f there.
- **Timing:** First change by frame 2. Settled by frame 40. Readable for 72 f (about frames 41-113). Hand-off cut near frame 113. Optional freeze of at most 15 f on the landing silence.
- **Use when:** The product has one strong, true outcome number (users, views, savings) that should earn attention before the name does.
- **Avoid when:** The number is weak, generic or can't be verified; films where the mark itself must lead.

## Product demo

A product shot depends on cause and effect: every action has a visible cause, the state changes on the cause frame itself (a 1 f swap, never a crossfade), and the result holds at least 36 f before the camera leaves. Give small UI hero weight through scale contrast, not length: alternate a wide with a 2-5x macro of the exact control, or open on the value moment at 1.6-2.2x and pull back to context over about 56 f, landing the next UI event within 2 f of the settle. Product arrivals are real motion. A device or window enters already moving (about 20 px/f on its first frame, settled by 44 f on E.out), and scrolls, sheets and widening bars peak at 35-60 px/f under the motion-blur pass. Holds stay alive with a 2-4% breath push instead of a dead lock. A person types at 30 cps. A fast product types at 50-72 cps, or to a fixed 68 f time box, with the newest characters arriving in the accent. Wherever possible let the product's own behaviour do the editing (a headline that grows into the input bar, an element that stays put while the page rebuilds around it, a window that recedes to its corner), so every transition also shows a feature.

### Agent status beat, then streamed answer

`pd-agent-status-then-answer` · workhorse · energy calm · launch, feature, walkthrough, vertical

The product's tiny working status is shown at hero size, as a black capsule with a spinner and a typed label or as bare headline type, holds for a beat with a looping ellipsis or shimmer, then dissolves as the answer streams in.

- **Build:** Build the status as a capsule (height ≈ 8.4% of frame, border-radius 999 px, C.ink fill, an 8-dot spinner stepping 45° every 6 f, label typed with TypeOn) or as bare type at 72-100 px with a clock or spinner glyph at cap height, its trailing word arriving in C.accent and relaxing to ink with mixColor over 24 f. Keep the hold alive with a looping ellipsis '.'.repeat(1 + (Math.floor(fd(f) / 16) % 3)) and a one-hue shimmer (background-clip: text over three lightness stops of the label grey, band ≈ 120 px, position linear in f), while the camera settles 1.62 → 1 with lmix over 56 f on E.outSoft. Dissolve the status over 12 f on E.smooth, then stream the answer with TypeOn at about 60 cps, the newest three characters at 0.3/0.6/0.85 opacity and each new character in the accent relaxing to ink over 12 f. When the status itself is the payoff, type it, hold 30 f and dim it to C.mute over 12 f instead of streaming.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Keep the same beat but build every decoration from one hue: a flat C.ink capsule with a plain soft neutral drop shadow instead of coloured light blobs behind it, a dot spinner or clock glyph instead of a sparkle icon, a shimmer made of three lightness stops of one grey instead of a multi-hue sweep, and an accent-to-ink trail on the newest characters instead of a multi-colour wake. The full look relies on gradient, sparkle, glow; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** Label types in about 30 f (40 f at headline size); hold 60-74 f with the ellipsis stepping every 16 f and one shimmer sweep per 60 f (≈ 20 px/f); camera 1.62 → 1 over 56 f on E.outSoft; dissolve 12 f; stream ≈ 1 character per frame (41 characters in about 42 f); payoff variant: hold 30 f, dim 12 f.
- **Use when:** An AI or agent product needs its invisible work made visible, and a moment of anticipation before the payoff.
- **Avoid when:** The product is not autonomous; the hold would run past about 74 f; a second status beat in the same film.

### Change applied as a visible diff

`pd-diff-hunks-apply` · workhorse · energy calm · feature, walkthrough

A proposed edit lands in a code or document view as a diff: outgoing lines strike through and fold away, incoming lines open in place with a marker in the gutter, and the view steps hunk by hunk before the change is accepted.

- **Build:** Render the file as live lines from data (FONT.mono for code, the text face for prose) beside a gutter of line numbers, and drive each hunk from its own start frame. An outgoing line first gets a 1.5 px C.mute strike that draws left to right over 8 f on E.ui (scaleX 0 → 1 from the left) while its text dims to C.mute; 6 f later it folds from line height to 0 over 12 f on E.ui, its opacity gone in the first 8 f. On that same frame an incoming slot opens from 0 to line height over 12 f on E.ui (the lines below are pushed through the computed layout), a 3 px C.accent bar appears in the gutter on its first frame, the new text appears whole once the slot is 70% open, and a C.accent 10% row tint relaxes to clear over 36 f while the bar stays; line numbers below recompute on fd(f) and are never tweened. Step to the next hunk 60-90 f later with the anchor camera (lc to a Shot centred on it) over 48 f on E.glide, keeping each hop under about 300 px (peak ≈ 19 px/f) and hard-cutting on the same axis to anything farther; on Accept (a Cursor press with pressAt on the button) every gutter bar fades over 12 f on E.smooth and the clean file holds under breath(t, 0.02).
- **Timing:** Strike 8 f on E.ui; fold 12 f on E.ui starting 6 f later; slot open 12 f on E.ui with the text in at 70%; tint relax 36 f; hunks 60-90 f apart, camera hop 48 f on E.glide (≤ 300 px); accept fade 12 f; final hold 36-48 f under a 2% breath; at most three hunks.
- **Use when:** AI coding or writing assistants and review, versioning or migration tools, when the claim is 'it changes exactly the right lines and shows you which'.
- **Avoid when:** The code is unreadable at frame size (macro in first), or the change needs more than three hunks (show a summary instead); never give removals a second colour.

### Command runs, output prints in bursts

`pd-terminal-burst-output` · workhorse · energy medium · feature, walkthrough, launch

A command is typed at human speed and entered; the terminal answers machine-fast, printing whole lines in uneven bursts with a stepping spinner and a progress bar, and ends on a single success line.

- **Build:** Set the terminal in FONT.mono at no less than TYPE.ui size, in a C.ink2 window with a 1.5 px edge, with every line laid out from data on a fixed line height, and keep breath(t, 0.02) on the camera for the whole run. Type the command with TypeOn at a human 30 cps with fade 0 (keys appear whole), hold the caret 10 f, then enter on a quiet tick. Output never types: each line appears whole on its own frame from a hand-written schedule of uneven bursts (for example 3 lines on consecutive frames, a 14 f gap, 5 lines 2 f apart, a 22 f gap), decided on fd(f), with the newest line in C.white and older ones relaxing to C.mute over 24 f; once text reaches the bottom row, each burst scrolls the content up by its total height as one move over max(6, 0.14 × distance) f on E.ui, so text never passes 20 px/f. A working line steps the four-glyph ASCII spinner (bar, slash, dash, backslash) every 4 f beside a text progress bar whose filled cells advance on fd(prog(f, a, a + 60, E.smooth) × cells), and the run ends on one success line whose check mark and key word arrive in C.accent and stay, followed by a fresh prompt with the caret blinking 30 f on, 30 f off.
- **Timing:** Command at 30 cps, caret hold 10 f; bursts of 2-6 lines 1-2 f apart with 10-24 f gaps (40-80 lines in 120-180 f reads machine-fast); line relax 24 f; burst scroll max(6, 0.14 × px) f on E.ui; spinner step 4 f; progress bar 60 f on E.smooth; success line held 48-60 f under the breath with the caret blinking 30/30.
- **Use when:** Developer tools, CLIs, infrastructure and build products, where the contrast between a human-typed command and machine-fast output is the speed claim.
- **Avoid when:** The audience is not technical, or the output itself must be read line by line (show the result screen instead); never type the output.

### Device rises already moving

`pd-device-rise-on-cut` · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature, walkthrough, vertical

A phone or app window enters from below already travelling on the cut frame and decelerates into place near centre while the whole shot slowly scales down.

- **Build:** Drive the device group's translateY = tw(f, cut − 1, cut + 43, rise, 0, E.out) with rise 140-160 px, so it already moves about 20 px/f on the cut frame (prog is 0 on its first frame, hence cut − 1); no fade-in, since the cut hides the start, and the shadow travels with the device. Under it, scale the whole shot 1 → 0.9 over 48 f on E.outSoft; a desaturated photo backdrop (grayscale(1) contrast(1.1) brightness(0.7)) keeps the device the only colour. When the device must push a title off screen without a cut, rise it from a full frame height below over 48 f on E.glide (peak ≈ 59 px/f at 31%, motion blur on), fade the title on E.smooth starting 16 f before the device moves, and keep the device above the title in z. For anticipation, peek first: 170 px in 14 f on E.out, hover 4 f, then launch the rest on E.whip over 40 f (peak under 70 px/f) and drift the scale 1 → 0.93 over 60 f.
- **Timing:** On a cut: 140-160 px over 44 f on E.out, first frame ≈ 6.2 × rise / 44 (about 20-23 px/f), 75% of the travel by f9, settled by f44; shot scale 1 → 0.9 over 48 f on E.outSoft. Over a title: ≈ 1,000 px in 48 f on E.glide, title fade 36 f starting 16 f early. Peek variant: 14 f peek, 4 f hover, 40 f launch on E.whip, 60 f scale drift.
- **Use when:** The first product shot after a type card or a photo, when the previous shot's energy should carry straight into the product.
- **Avoid when:** The device is already on screen; a calm film where a 20 px/f arrival feels pushy; it would be the third rise in a row (vary with a tilt or a pull-back).

### Edit with the product's own UI

`pd-ui-native-transitions` · workhorse · energy medium · walkthrough, feature, launch

Instead of cuts, the film moves between product areas the way the app does: a window recedes to a corner, a sheet slides up, a popover pops from its anchor, a button or card unfolds into a full panel.

- **Build:** Model the app as stacked layers in one scene, park the cursor on the control that would trigger each change 6 f before the press, and use the matching native behaviour instead of a cut. Minimize: transform-origin at the trigger corner, scale 1 → 0.7 on E.in over 22 f while opacity falls 1 → 0 over its last 12 f on E.smooth (the far corner is mostly gone before it passes 60 px/f), with the next layer 4 f later. Sheet: translateY 100% → 0 of the window over 52 f on E.glide, clipped to the window. Popover: scale 0.5 → 1 from the trigger point over 12 f on E.outSoft with opacity over its first 4 f, then a 20-40 f camera reframe starting 2 f later. Launch: the sidebar glides left 31% of frame width over 96 f on E.smooth while the main canvas mounts whole on the trigger frame and its greeting starts typing on that frame. Unfold: one element interpolates rect and border-radius from the button or card to the full panel over 28 f on E.rest (longer for a big panel: at least edge travel / 20 f, so no edge passes about 70 px/f) and its title FLIPs to the header slot (scale 1 → 0.6), flying faded whenever it moves faster than 20 px/f; the old content fades out over the first 12 f, the panel content fades in 8 f after the morph peaks, and the stage behind dims over 24 f (a RackFocus at 40 px for a blurred desktop).
- **Timing:** Generic chain: exit on E.in 22 f, gap 4 f, entrance on E.out 52 f. Minimize 22 f; sheet 52 f (peak ≈ 50 px/f); popover 12 f plus a 20-40 f reframe; launch slide 96 f (peak ≈ 18 px/f); unfold 28 f on E.rest (at least edge travel / 20 f), content in 8 f after the peak, stage dim 24 f.
- **Use when:** Walkthroughs across several product areas; any film where each transition can also demonstrate how the product navigates.
- **Avoid when:** A purely conceptual or type-led film; desktop chrome that is not part of the brand world; more than one native transition every 3 s (it starts to feel like a screen recording).

### Fast prompt at true scale

`pd-fast-prompt-true-scale` · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature, walkthrough, vertical

The real prompt bar fills with a long, honest instruction in about a second at full legible size, the card growing as lines wrap, then the text is sent up into a chat bubble.

- **Build:** Type with TypeOn (src/fx/TypeOn.tsx), either time-boxed (dur 68, ease E.linear, so prompts of any length finish in 68 f and every ask beat keeps its length) or at a fixed 50-72 cps; pre-fill the first word so frame 1 already shows text, and draw the newest three characters at 0.3/0.6/0.85 opacity, each arriving in C.accent and relaxing to ink over 12 f. Grow the card from the measured text box: width ≈ 67% → 77% of frame over the first 24 f, then one line height over 12 f on E.out at each wrap, decided on fd(f). Keep the frame alive with breath(t, 0.025) from src/lib/camera.ts on the camera; the caret is solid while typing and blinks 16 f on / 16 f off only once done. On the send press the composer text fades out over 12 f while the bubble rises 12-20 px through arrive() and fades in over 16-18 f, starting 4 f later.
- **Timing:** Time box 68 f, or 50-72 cps (0.8-1.2 characters per frame); card width 24 f, +1 line per wrap in 12 f on E.out; read hold after typing at least 36 f + 6 f per word, kept alive by the breath; send: 12 f out, bubble 16-18 f in with a 4 f offset.
- **Use when:** An AI, search or command product whose real input is the story; showing a real task without a dull typing wait.
- **Avoid when:** The prompt runs past about 100 characters (cut it); a human-paced beat is the point (use 30 cps with human rhythm); the product is not input-driven.

### Flick scroll lands the target

`pd-flick-scroll-lands-target` · workhorse · energy medium · any

A list or page scrolls like a trackpad flick, entering already fast or ramping up briefly, then glides on an exponential tail until the target row rests at its reading position.

- **Build:** On a cut, start at peak speed with inertia(f, cut, v0, 0.943) from src/lib/anim.ts (v0 ≈ 54 px/f: travel ≈ 920 px, readable after ≈ 49 f, within 0.5 px after its settle). Inside a shot, ramp first: position = vmax·t³/(3·tp²) for t < tp, then vmax·tp/3 + inertia(f, s + tp, vmax, d).x after tp, with decay d 0.93-0.98. Solve vmax = D / (tp/3 + tau), tau = −1/ln d, so the target lands about 15% from the top (a section heading) or at centre, and cap vmax at 60 px/f. Drive text through total · arrive(x / total, 0.98) so the slow tail does not tick, keep the camera itself crisp, and let the motion-blur pass streak the rows above 12 px/f; rows are not meant to be read until they drop below 3 px/f.
- **Timing:** Cut entry: v0 54 px/f, decay 0.943 (tau 17 f), ≈ 76 f to rest. In-shot: ramp tp 28-40 f, vmax 35-60 px/f, tail decay 0.93 for a form section, up to 0.98 for a long volume reel (≈ 277 f for ≈ 2,600 px); readable below 3 px/f.
- **Use when:** Showing volume (many results, a long page, a feed), or moving down a form to its next section with a human feel.
- **Avoid when:** The viewer must read during the move; the list is shorter than two screens; it would be the third scroll in a row.

### Ghost suggestion accepted with a key

`pd-ghost-suggestion-accept` · workhorse · energy calm · feature, walkthrough, launch

As someone types, the product proposes the rest of the line as pale ghost text after the caret; a small key chip appears, the key is pressed, and the ghost text inks in left to right as the caret jumps to its end.

- **Build:** Type the user's prefix with TypeOn at a human 30 cps; 12 f after the last key, draw the suggestion as one span starting at the prefix's caretX from typeOn(), in the same font and baseline and in C.mute, appearing whole on one frame (or streaming at 2 characters per frame for a longer block), so nothing already typed reflows. Twelve px past its last glyph (or under the line end if that would cross the field edge), mount a key chip (a FONT.mono label at 0.6 em in a 6 px-radius box with a 1.5 px C.line border and a 3 px bottom edge) on spr(f, s, SPR.micro) from scale 0.8 with opacity over 6 f, and keep the 30-40 f wait alive with breath(t, 0.02) on the camera. On ACCEPT the chip presses with pressAt (translateY 2 px and its bottom edge 3 → 1 px, both times the press value), and on that frame a recolour front runs through the ghost text, k = fd(prog(f, ACCEPT − 1, ACCEPT + 10, E.linear) × n): each character behind the front switches from C.mute to C.accent on its frame and relaxes to C.ink over 12 f by its own age (mixColor), while the prefix caret is removed (caretOut = ACCEPT) and a caret appears at the suggestion's end on the same frame. The chip fades out over 8 f on E.smooth from ACCEPT + 4; in a multi-line block each line's front starts 3 f after the line above, and a rejection uses the same chip labelled Esc with the ghost text fading out over 8 f on E.smooth.
- **Timing:** Prefix at 30 cps; ghost text 12 f after the last key, whole in 1 f (or 2 characters per frame); chip on SPR.micro with a 6 f fade; wait 30-40 f under a 2% breath; press 4 f down, 8 f recoil; recolour front 10 f per line (lines 3 f apart), accent relax 12 f; chip out over 8 f from ACCEPT + 4; read hold after acceptance 36-48 f.
- **Use when:** An assistant that completes text, code, email or form fields inline: the moment the product does the work is one key away, and the cause (the key) and the effect (the ink) share a frame.
- **Avoid when:** The product generates whole answers rather than inline completions (stream the answer instead), or the suggestion runs past about two lines at readable size; never show more than two accepts in a row.

### Hard swap on the cause frame

`pd-hard-swap-on-cause` · workhorse · energy medium · any

On a click or selection the product image, view or value changes in one frame with no crossfade, any price or count rolls up from just below its new value, and a physical card can hide the swap in a small 3D kick.

- **Build:** Export the cause frame once (the press of pressAt from src/fx/Cursor.tsx after a hover state shown 6 f earlier, or a selection marker's landing) and switch state on fd(f) >= CAUSE so every motion-blur sub-sample agrees; never crossfade the two states. Re-count numbers with Roll fed countSteps(next − delta, next, CAUSE, 40, E.out), delta about 5-10% of the value, so the digits roll instead of cutting. Punch the swapped object with scale 1 + 0.02 · hitPulse(f − CAUSE, 2, 5). For a print or card beside a list, kick it: perspective 900 px, transform-origin on its left edge, rotateY = 12° · hitPulse(f − CAUSE + 1, 1, 2.5) with skewY 2° on the same envelope and a soft shadow (0 18px 40px rgba(0,0,0,.18)), while the list's selection marker moves 6 f before the swap.
- **Timing:** Swap 1 f on the cause frame; hover 6 f before the press; recount 36-46 f on E.out with 14 f digit rolls; punch attack 2 f, tau 5; kick peaks on the swap frame and settles in 6-8 f; at most one swap per 30 f, 54 f apart in a repeating sequence.
- **Use when:** A choice changes the product instantly: a variant picker, filter, plan selector, theme switch, a canvas that appears whole on launch.
- **Avoid when:** The change is a process the viewer should watch; two numbers would sit half-and-half in place; swaps faster than one per 30 f (the clicks read as a macro).

### List narrows with each keystroke

`pd-live-filter-narrows` · workhorse · energy medium · feature, walkthrough, launch

A shortcut opens a command palette or search field, and as the query types the list answers every key: non-matching rows fold away, survivors slide up, matched letters ink in, and the highlight rides the top result until Enter.

- **Build:** Open with the shortcut if the product has one: two key chips (FONT.mono labels, 1.5 px C.line border, 3 px bottom edge) appear 4 f apart and press together with pressAt, and on the press frame the palette scales 0.96 → 1 about its top centre with opacity over 10 f on E.outSoft while the app behind racks to 8 px through RackFocus under a 20% C.ink veil over 12 f. Type the query with TypeOn at 30-40 cps and recompute the matches from the data on each key frame (typeFrames(), decided on fd(f)), so the list is a pure function of the characters typed: rows that stop matching fold from row height to 0 over 10 f on E.ui with their opacity gone in the first 6 f, and survivors FLIP to their new slots from the computed list layout over max(12, 0.14 × distance) f on E.ui, so no label passes 20 px/f. In every surviving label the matched characters switch to C.ink on the key frame while the rest drops to C.mute (colour only, never weight, so nothing reflows), and one shared highlight (C.mist, 8 px radius) always sits behind the top result and FLIPs to its new rect over 8 f on E.ui. On Enter (a single chip press) the chosen row takes a C.accent 12% tint for 6 f and the palette closes, scale 1 → 0.98 with opacity out over 8 f on E.smooth, while the result mounts underneath on the press frame.
- **Timing:** Chips 4 f apart, press 4 f down + 8 f recoil; palette 10 f on E.outSoft, backdrop rack and veil 12 f; query 30-40 cps; row fold 10 f on E.ui (opacity 6 f); survivor FLIP max(12, 0.14 × px) f on E.ui; highlight 8 f on E.ui; 4-7 keys narrow 8-10 rows to 1-3; final list held 24-36 f under a 2% breath before Enter; close 8 f.
- **Use when:** Search, command menus, filters and pickers: any product whose speed claim is 'type a few letters and it is there', proving instant results without a spinner.
- **Avoid when:** The rows are illegible at frame size (punch in first), or the query is long (past about 12 characters it becomes a typing beat); do not FLIP more than about ten rows at once.

### One native control as the demo

`pd-single-control-hero` · workhorse · energy calm · feature, launch, vertical, loop

Instead of a screenshot, the feature is shown as the single control that embodies it (a picker wheel, a toggle, a segmented switch) at large scale, centred, with no chrome, doing only its native interaction.

- **Build:** Build only that control at 3-5x its native size, centred on an empty stage with no app chrome. For a picker, scroll the column with inertia(f, s, 20, 0.975) from src/lib/anim.ts (≈ 790 px, tau ≈ 40 f, starting at the 20 px/f readable-text limit) and style each item from its distance d to the centre line: scale 1.2 − 0.35 · min(d / 375, 1), colour mixColor(C.ink, C.mute, min(d / 375, 1)), opacity 1 → 0.35 on the same ratio. Either cut while it still drifts, or click the chosen item home with SPR.detent. Toggles and segmented controls keep their real geometry (knob 8 f on E.ui, the selected pill gliding between labels on E.glide).
- **Timing:** Shot ≈ 120 f; picker v0 20 px/f, decay 0.975 per frame, an item crossing focus about every 30 f early on and slowing after; detent settle ≈ 12 f; toggle knob 8 f; segment glide 18-24 f.
- **Use when:** A settings, targeting or compatibility claim in a type-led film, where one interaction says it is a real product faster than a full UI.
- **Avoid when:** The feature needs context to make sense; the control is generic (every app has a toggle) and says nothing about the claim.

### Scrub a chart with a live readout

`pd-chart-scrub-readout` · workhorse · energy calm · feature, walkthrough, launch

The cursor glides across a chart; a hairline and a dot ride the series beneath it and a small readout shows the date and value at that point, stepping from data point to data point until it lands on the one that makes the claim.

- **Build:** Build the chart from data in one SVG and make the scrub a pure function of the cursor's x: move src/fx/Cursor.tsx along a shallow cursorArc (bow 0.05) on E.smooth at 6-10 px/f, and take the active point i as the data point nearest that x, decided on fd(f). Layer back to front: series, a 1.5 px C.line hairline at point i's x, a 6 px solid dot on the series at point i with a 2 px ring in the stage colour, the readout, then the cursor; the hairline and dot snap from point to point as i changes (use 40 or more points so each snap is small; with sparse data let the hairline follow the cursor x and snap only the dot and value). The readout is a small card (8 px radius, C.ink on paper or C.white on ink) with a FONT.mono date in C.mute above the value in tabular figures; it rides along the plot's top edge at the cursor's x, clamped inside the plot so it never flips sides, and its value changes through Roll fed one step per index change (roll 8) so digits roll instead of cutting. The hairline and readout fade in over 6 f as the cursor crosses into the plot, and the scrub ends on the point that carries the claim, where the dot pulses at scale 1 + 0.25 · hitPulse(f − LAND, 2, 6) and the value arrives in C.accent and relaxes to C.ink over 24 f.
- **Timing:** Scrub 90-150 f on E.smooth at 6-10 px/f (the readout never moves faster than the cursor); hairline and readout in over 6 f; value roll 8 f per index change; landing pulse attack 2 f, tau 6; accent relax 24 f; hold on the landing point 36-48 f under a 2% breath.
- **Use when:** Analytics, finance, health or monitoring products whose value is reading any point in history; a calm interaction beat after a fast one.
- **Avoid when:** The chart has no point worth landing on, or the readout is illegible at the framing (punch in to 1.6-2x first); never scrub faster than the readout can be read.

### Before/after drag divider

`pd-before-after-drag-wipe` · accent · energy medium · feature, launch, walkthrough

The cursor grabs a vertical divider on the product and drags it across, wiping away the old state to reveal the new one in the same layout.

- **Build:** Stack two renders of the same layout: before below, after above, clipped with clip-path inset(0 0 0 X px) where X is the divider's position; draw the divider as a 2 px C.white line (C.ink on paper) with a 40 px round handle holding two small chevrons. The cursor arrives on cursorArc over 36-48 f on E.out, presses the handle (pressAt) and drags it across the product panel on E.smooth over 60 f (≈ 1,100 px, peak ≈ 52 px/f). Optionally it pauses once at the midpoint for up to 24 f under a breath push so both states read side by side. Values that differ between the states change exactly where the divider passes them, because they sit on separate layers, so the halves are never crossfaded.
- **Timing:** Cursor approach 36-48 f on E.out; press 4 f down, 8 f recoil; drag 60 f on E.smooth, or 36 f to the midpoint on E.glide (peak ≈ 46 px/f), a hold of ≤ 24 f, then 36 f on to the edge.
- **Use when:** Redesigns, image or audio cleanup, performance gains, any this-got-better claim with a visible difference.
- **Avoid when:** The two states differ in layout (the wipe then reads as a glitch); the difference is invisible at frame size; the film has no human gesture anywhere else.

### Drag assets in, skeletons fill

`pd-drag-assets-skeleton-fill` · accent · energy medium · feature, walkthrough

The cursor drags a fanned stack of images into the input; after the drop they appear as grey skeleton thumbnails that fill with the real images one by one.

- **Build:** Build the stack as four image cards rotated −12°, −4°, 4° and 12° that travel with the cursor along cursorArc (src/fx/Cursor.tsx, bow 0.2) on E.smooth, each card evaluated 1 f behind the one above so the fan trails slightly; pressAt marks the pickup and the release. On the drop frame (or just after a cut), mount the thumbnails as C.mist rounded rects in the input's attachment row and fade each image up over 8 f on E.smooth with a 1.04 → 1 scale, i × 8 f apart. The input's other contents shift by FLIP as the row opens over 18 f on E.ui, and the drag path stays clear of any text being read.
- **Timing:** Drag ≈ 72 f on E.smooth; thumbnails 8 f each at a 6-10 f stagger (≈ 36 f for four); attachment row opens over 18 f on E.ui.
- **Use when:** The product takes real material as input (files, photos, documents) and the viewer should see that context going in.
- **Avoid when:** The input is text only; the drag path would cross text being read; more than six assets (show a count chip instead).

### Generated view resolves from soft

`pd-blur-resolve-load` · accent · energy medium · launch, feature, walkthrough, loop

A freshly generated window or row appears as a soft, out-of-focus shape over a flat placeholder plate and snaps into crisp UI in about a third of a second.

- **Build:** Mount the finished UI over a flat placeholder plate (C.mist, or C.accent at 12% opacity: one hue only). Render the UI through RackFocus (src/fx/RackFocus.tsx) with blur 20 px and t = 1 − p, p = prog(f, s, s + 20, E.out); fade its opacity 0.6 → 1 and scale it 1.03 → 1 on the same p so the focus pull rides a move, and fade the plate out over the same 20 f on E.smooth. For a list, insert rows one at a time: width 60% → 100% with RackFocus 6 → 0 px over 12 f, siblings pushed down one row over 10 f on E.ui, rows 34-40 f apart; inside an unfolding card, start a row's rack only once 60% of its height is revealed. t must reach 0 by the end, so text lands fully sharp.
- **Timing:** Window: 20 f on E.out (blur 20 → 0 px, opacity 0.6 → 1, scale 1.03 → 1), plate fade 20 f on E.smooth. Rows: 12 f each, push-down 10 f on E.ui, cadence 34-40 f. Card stats row: 12 f, starting once 60% of it is revealed.
- **Use when:** An AI or build step produces a result and it should read as just arrived, without a spinner.
- **Avoid when:** The UI was already on screen (use a state change); more than two resolves in one sequence (it becomes a fog filter); type so small that 12 f of softness hurts legibility.

### Long page flown like a runway

`pd-page-runway-flyover` · accent · energy high · launch, feature, walkthrough

A whole long page lies on a steeply tilted plane that recedes to a horizon, and the view travels along it faster and faster, so the page reads as one landscape and is cut at full speed.

- **Build:** Lay the whole page out as live components at desktop width inside a runway plane about 75% of frame width and 2x frame height long (overflow hidden), in a full-frame parent with perspective 1200 px and its perspective-origin at frame centre; give the plane transform-origin 50% 100%, rotateX(55deg) and put its bottom edge on the frame's bottom edge, so its far edge recedes to a horizon about 25% down the frame and its sides converge like a runway. Move the page inside the plane, never the camera: translateY = Y0 + 6n + 0.225n² for n = f − s up to 54 (plane speed 6 → 30 px/f), then +36 px per frame to the cut, so content streams toward the viewer and the page's upper sections emerge from the horizon (start with its lower sections on the plane so the hero arrives last); at the near edge the screen speed is about 0.95x the plane speed and the far half moves much slower. Fade the far end with an alpha mask on the plane, mask-image linear-gradient(to top, #000 45%, transparent 95%), so the stage colour swallows the horizon in one hue, and keep the empty stage above the horizon as the caption band, where one short line lands with src/fx/Words.tsx in screen space while the page streams below it. Nothing on the plane is meant to be read: keep the motion-blur pass on for the whole flight and cut on its last, fastest frame into a shot that opens moving the same way.
- **Timing:** Flight 80 f: plane speed 6 → 30 px/f over 54 f (closed form 6n + 0.225n², linear acceleration with no ease-out), then 36 px/f for 26 f into the cut, about 1,900 px of travel (page at least plane length + 2,000 px); near-edge screen speed ≈ 6 → 34 px/f, under the blur pass throughout; rotateX 55°, perspective 1200 px, plane 2x frame height; caption words 6 f apart, landed by f40 of the flight; cut on the final frame.
- **Use when:** Showing the length or completeness of a page, document, feed or site in about a second without asking anyone to read it; a fast connective beat between two readable product shots, or the carrier for a change made mid-move, such as a theme switch.
- **Avoid when:** The content must be read, the page is short (it reads as a tilted card instead), or the frame is vertical and leaves too little runway; use it once per film.

### Mark docks into the app

`pd-mark-docks-into-app` · accent · energy medium · launch, feature, sting

An integration mark or icon travels to an app tile or page and settles overlapping its face, rising in front of it at the moment of contact, so it reads as plugging in.

- **Build:** Move the mark toward the tile centre minus a small offset (15-20% of the tile) over 25 f on E.outSoft so it decelerates into contact; at overlap (frame 17 of the approach) raise its z-index and translateZ above the tile, and let it come to rest on frame 25. On contact the tile answers with scale 1 + 0.02 · hitPulse(f − contact, 2, 3); the tile is a matte solid with a 1.5 px C.line edge and a soft neutral shadow. Shared-element variant: lift a small icon out of its row (scale 0.53 → 1 over 27 f on E.out while its tile inverts light/dark over 18 f), float it 45 f with a linear rotateZ 1.5° and rotateY 4° drift, then shrink it over 12 f on E.inOut into the logo slot of a page that swings in from the bottom right (perspective 1000 px, rotateX 55° → 40°, rotateZ −30° → −22° over 50 f on E.out). Position the icon through the page's own transform and, on the frame it reaches the slot, replace it with the page's own logo in one frame (decided with fd, identical transform) instead of crossfading the two copies.
- **Timing:** Approach 25 f on E.outSoft, overlap at f17, rest at f25; tile bump 2% (attack 2 f, tau 3, about 8 f). Variant: lift 27 f, colour invert 18 f, float 45 f, shrink 12 f on E.inOut, page swing 50 f on E.out, one-frame swap to the page logo on arrival.
- **Use when:** An integration, plug-in or works-inside claim; handing off from a settings screen into the platform it acts on.
- **Avoid when:** The mark would pass over text being read; the mark is also the end lockup (it would appear early, so dock an integration icon instead).

### Pin field pull-back

`pd-pin-field-pullback` · accent · energy medium · feature, launch, walkthrough

A map pulls back from a close view to reveal a field of location pins that drop in as accent marks and relax to ink, then a card grows out of the pin the cursor picks.

- **Build:** Scale the map group with k = lmix(2.2, 1, prog(f, s, s + 50, E.outSoft)) about the focus point. Pop the pins during the pull with SPR.micro (no visible overshoot: a field of pins is not a landing) on scale 0 → 1 and translateY −12 → 0 px, transform-origin at the bottom centre, with offsets from stagger(i, n, 30) so the whole group lands within 30 f; each pin arrives in C.accent and relaxes to C.ink over 24 f (mixColor). The cursor clicks one pin and its card grows from the pin tip (transform-origin at the pin, scale 0.6 → 1 over 12 f on E.out), with a leader line drawing over 8 f and its label sliding 25 px over 12 f on E.out.
- **Timing:** Pull 50 f on E.outSoft (first frame ≈ −7% scale per frame); pins ≈ 11 f each on SPR.micro, the group within 30 f (2-6 f apart); colour relax 24 f; card 12 f, leader 8 f, label 12 f.
- **Use when:** Location, coverage, store-finder or delivery features; any everywhere claim backed by real places.
- **Avoid when:** Fewer than about five locations; a map style busy enough to hide the pins; a route arc has already run on the same map.

### Several people at work at once

`pd-presence-cursors` · accent · energy medium · feature, walkthrough, launch

Two or three named cursors move and act on the same canvas at the same time, each in its own rhythm, while presence avatars stack in the corner, so collaboration reads without a word.

- **Build:** Draw each collaborator as src/fx/Cursor.tsx plus a name flag pinned 14 px right and 18 px below the tip (a 6 px-radius label with an initial and first name in C.white on C.ink, C.ink2 or C.mute), so identity comes from the label rather than from colour and the one accent stays free for the newest edit. Script each person as a list of {to, at, action} beats: travel on cursorArc (bow 0.15-0.25, its sign from rand(name)) on E.smooth at 6-14 px/f, with every start shifted by rand(name + i) × 10 f so no two cursors arrive or press on the same frame. Between beats each cursor wanders: every 24 f it eases on E.smooth to a new point within 6 px of its rest, picked with rand(name + floor(f / 24)), so no hand ever freezes. Each action lands on that person's press frame (pressAt): a note dropped onto the canvas on SPR.firm, a shape dragged with the item evaluated 2 f behind the cursor, or a label typed with TypeOn at 30 cps beside the flag; the newest edit takes a 2 px C.accent outline for 24 f, then relaxes to C.line. In the top bar, overlapping 28 px avatar circles with initials scale in on spr(f, join, SPR.micro) as each cursor first enters the frame.
- **Timing:** Shot 180-240 f; travel 6-14 px/f on E.smooth, arrivals and presses at least 6 f apart; wander ≤ 6 px per 24 f; one action every 30-50 f across all cursors; note settle on SPR.firm ≈ 16 f; accent outline 24 f; avatars on SPR.micro 6-10 f each; at most three cursors.
- **Use when:** Collaborative documents, whiteboards, design and planning tools: anything whose claim is 'together, live'.
- **Avoid when:** A single-user product, or a frame where the name flags would be too small to read; never more than three cursors, which turns into noise.

### Headline becomes the product input

`pd-headline-becomes-input` · signature · energy medium · launch, feature, vertical

Without a cut the headline turns into the product: a caret appears in the gap between two words, swells into a capsule and widens into the input bar that shoves the words aside, or the sentence inside a card dissolves while the card reshapes into the input.

- **Build:** Lay out [wordL][slot][wordR] from data, centred, and bind each word's x to the slot's edges (wordL's right edge = cx − slotW/2 − gap) so the line reflows with no separate tween. Grow the slot as a 3 px C.accent caret (height 0 → line height over 6 f on E.out), hold 8 f, thicken to a 36 px capsule over 14 f, then widen to ≈ 92% of frame on E.rest over 60 f (edge peak ≈ 50 px/f, motion blur on) while its fill goes straight to the opaque input colour; the flanking words ride the edges and, once they pass 20 px/f, fade on E.smooth with blurOut as they leave frame. Populate container-first: icons, a C.mute placeholder and the send button fade in left to right 4 f apart over 12 f each with a 6 px arrive() rise, and the primary button fills last on a 16 f linear ramp. If the sentence already sits in a card, exit its words 6 f apart (the out props of src/fx/Words.tsx), tween the card's height to the input's over 30 f on E.out and fade the placeholder in over 16 f.
- **Timing:** Caret 6 f, hold 8 f, capsule 14 f, widen 60 f on E.rest (a short bar: 23 f in all on E.out); contents 12 f each at a 4 f stagger, button fill 16 f linear. Card variant: word exits 6 f apart, resize 30 f on E.out, placeholder 16 f.
- **Use when:** Bridging from message to demo in a type-led film; the product's core surface is an input, search or command bar.
- **Avoid when:** The product is not input-led; the headline has no natural gap; the bar would have to stay translucent over a busy backdrop (go straight to opaque).

### Shared element survives the page change

`pd-shared-element-page` · signature · energy medium · walkthrough, feature, launch

The cursor clicks a row; the page drains away except the row's icon (or the clicked card), which stays exactly in place while the next page assembles around it with a short zoom-out.

- **Build:** Duplicate the anchor (a row's icon, a card or a modal) into a top overlay at its exact screen rect. On the press frame fade page A to its background colour over 6 f on E.smooth and hold the lone anchor 2-4 f. Then mount page B at scale 1.2 about the anchor and settle it with lmix over 24 f on E.out, while the overlay interpolates from A's rect to B's (both computed from layout data, so FLIP by construction) and B's blocks fade in 2 f apart over 10 f. Cross-app variant: keep one card container mounted, take child A out through RackFocus to 8 px with opacity over 36 f, resize the card to the new aspect over 20 f on E.out, and bring child B in from 8 px over 24 f. Cut variant: keep the anchor fixed on a top layer while only the background layer switches on the cut frame, then drag the anchor into its new slot over 40 f on E.whip.
- **Timing:** Hover 12 f, press (pressAt), page A out 6 f, anchor alone 2-4 f, page B 1.2 → 1 over 24 f on E.out (≤ 50 px/f at 960 px from the anchor), block stagger 2 f over 10 f: about 48 f from click to settled. Cross-app: 36 f out, 20 f resize, 24 f in. Cut variant: anchor drag 40 f on E.whip.
- **Use when:** Navigating into a detail view, or carrying a piece of content between apps, where spatial continuity should make the product feel instant.
- **Avoid when:** Nothing exists in both states; the anchor is under about 40 px and cannot carry attention; it would need to travel more than a third of the frame (use a native transition).

### Tilted product plane flattens

`pd-tilted-plane-flattens` · signature · energy medium · launch, feature, walkthrough

A real product page lies tipped back in perspective, rises toward the camera and rotates flat to face the viewer, landing the product as a frontal screen.

- **Build:** Give the page's parent perspective 1800-2000 px; on the page set transform-origin 50% 100% and tween translateY 270 → −60 px, rotateX 25° → 8° and scale 1 → 1.3 over 68 f on E.out, then drift linearly at about 3.5 px/f and leave on E.in. Resolve the last 8° → 0 as follow-through on its own E.out over 20 f, starting 6 f before the translate lands, so position and tilt settle at different moments. Hero version: hold the plane tilted for up to 34 f with progressive depth of field (4-6 horizontal bands, each a RackFocus at 0/2/4/6/8 px by distance from the focal row), then rotate rotateX and rotateZ to 0 over 80 f on E.glide while every band racks to sharp as the rotation reaches zero. Edge the page with a 1.5 px solid C.line hairline rather than a lit rim; an in-page headline may build with src/fx/Words.tsx while the plane still moves, but nothing is meant to be read until it lands.
- **Timing:** Rise 68 f on E.out: top edge ≈ 35 px/f on the first frame, ≈ 12 px/f by f4, ≈ 5.5 px/f by f8, then ≈ 3.5 px/f drift and an exit at ≈ 5.5 px/f on E.in; tilt follow-through 20 f, starting 6 f before the position lands; hero de-skew: hold ≤ 34 f, then 80 f on E.glide (peak edge speed ≈ 60-70 px/f at about 31%).
- **Use when:** Introducing a real web page or app screen as the real thing while keeping the camera alive; the first frontal look at the product.
- **Avoid when:** The UI must be read during the move; the plane would need more than about 30° of tilt (text shears and aliases); the same flatten ran within the last 10 s.

## Logo and end card

The end card is the film's poster. The lockup appears once, sized at 28-45% of frame width, resolves within about 36-80 f, then holds 90-120 f (1.5-2.0 s, never past ~150 f) while it keeps building: a 10-20% push on E.dolly and tracking that tightens 0.03-0.06 em over ~46 f. Anything static past 48 f reads as a stalled player. The strongest endings come out of the story instead of starting a new logo animation: the last object lands on the mark's exact position and size, or the product clears the stage to uncover it, or the opening's mechanic returns carrying the name. Scale moves run in log space (lmix). Collapses from 9-12x settle in 36-66 f, and the fastest frames are flat fill, low contrast or motion-blurred. The name follows the mark at 55-60% of its slide, with letters 2-3.5 f apart and readable type never faster than 20 px/f. Sound carries half the weight: cut the music dead on the end-card frame, leave ~36 f of near-silence, put one hit on the frame the name resolves, and let its tail decay to digital zero inside a tail of at least 60 f. The last frame must show the mark plus the name, with at most one CTA at 44-56 px that stays readable for at least 1.7 s, and it never fades to black.

### End card replays the opening

`le-bookend-replay` · workhorse · energy any · any

The ending reuses the opening's stage and its mechanic, now carrying the brand, so the film closes on a rhyme the viewer has already learned.

- **Build:** Build the opening's stage (a Background component with an intensity prop) and its signature mechanic (a gap opening in a line, a word-roll, a mark slide, a window rise) as components with props, and call them again at the end with the same type size, position and curves. Run the mechanic mirrored, or with the brand as its payload. The window's exit is its entrance time-reversed: 1 - entrance(1 - t). The flanking words roll up and away (Words exit at half the stagger, E.in) and 'made with' plus the name roll in while the centre object holds. The opening's mark slide plays again, this time with the name. Bring the stage back only for brand beats: intensity 0 on product beats, then a 25 f rise from the bottom edge on E.out at the lockup. Never replay a reveal identically; the third use must add the name or the CTA.
- **Timing:** Word-roll: 28 f with a 5 f stagger. Mirrored exits keep the entrance's distance and duration. Stage rise: 25 f on E.out. Final hold: 96-120 f under the push.
- **Use when:** Films with a distinctive opening mechanic or stage. The signature move's third use. Loops, where the end hands back to frame 0.
- **Avoid when:** The opening was generic (replaying it only repeats a template). The reprise would be a frame-for-frame replay that adds nothing. Films under 10 s, where the rhyme has no time to land.

### Lockup keeps building through the hold

`le-living-hold` · workhorse · energy calm · any

Once resolved, the lockup never freezes: the card slowly pushes in (or exhales back), the tracking tightens a touch and the stage dims, so the last 1.5-2 s read as intentional rather than stalled.

- **Build:** Wrap the whole end card in one camera transform and push it about the lockup's optical centre with k = lmix(1, 1.15, prog(f, resolve, end, E.dolly)), a 10-20% push. Under that, tighten the name's letter-spacing from +0.03-0.06 em to its token track over 46 f on E.out, starting at its resolve. For a calm close, use the exhale instead: k = lmix(1, 0.9, prog(f, resolve, resolve + 120, E.out)) while only the stage dims to 35% over 36 f on E.smooth. The lockup stays at full strength to the last frame, because the last frame is the poster and never fades to black.
- **Timing:** Hold 90-120 f (1.5-2.0 s, never more than ~150 f). Push 10-20% over the hold on E.dolly. Tracking: 46 f on E.out. Exhale: 10% over 120 f on E.out, with a 36 f stage dim. Tail of at least 60 f after the last event, inside the hold.
- **Use when:** Every lockup and URL hold, and any card that must sit for more than 48 f.
- **Avoid when:** A designed freeze of at most 15 f on a silence (then stop everything, the push included). Loops whose hold must end at the frame-0 scale (ease the push back down instead).

### Mark slides aside, name follows

`le-mark-slide-name-follow` · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature, sting, walkthrough, vertical

The centred mark glides sideways, shrinking if it was hero-sized, to open its slot, and the name resolves beside it just before the mark stops, so the lockup forms in one gesture.

- **Build:** Lay the finished lockup out first: LOCKUP token with mark height = the name's cap height, gap = 0.25-0.4x the mark height, and the name's width from measureTracked. Then slide the mark from frame centre to its lockup slot with x = tw(f, a, a+D, 0, -(nameW + gap)/2, E.smooth). If it was larger as a hero, scale it lmix(heroK, 1, same progress) with heroK about 1.6. Start the name when the slide passes 55-60% of its progress. As one block: opacity on E.smooth, blurIn(p, 10), translateX +30 -> 0 on E.out. Per letter: the same over 16 f at a 3 f stagger, with colour mixColor(C.mute, C.ink, p) so letters arrive grey and settle to ink. From the name's resolve, tighten its letter-spacing from +0.04 em to the TYPE.display track over 46 f on E.out; this hands into the hold's push. For a round mark, add roll: rotate = -(dx / r) * 180/pi degrees, so it rolls without slipping and stops exactly when x does. In 9:16, stack instead: the mark rises by (nameH + gap)/2 and the name rises in under it with MaskRise.
- **Timing:** Slide: 36 f for up to ~250 px (E.smooth peaks ~20 px/f), 60 f for ~350 px (~17 px/f). Motion-blur pass on the mark whenever it moves faster than 12 px/f. Name starts at 0.55-0.6 x D: a block takes 14 f; letters take 16 f each at a 3 f stagger (10 letters inside ~43 f). Tracking: 46 f on E.out. Lockup resolved by about D + 20 f, then hold 90-120 f.
- **Use when:** Any end card whose mark is already on screen (it was the story device or the hero) and the name still has to arrive. The default lockup build.
- **Avoid when:** The mark has not been seen yet (give it its own beat first). The film already used a slide-to-make-room for the product. Long names that would push the slide past ~400 px (stack vertically instead).

### Seed build with stroke draw-on

`le-seed-stroke-build` · workhorse · energy medium · launch, sting, feature, loop, vertical

The mark grows from a small seed while its strokes, stripes or arcs draw on in a quick stagger, so it assembles itself in about half a second and the label rises in beside it.

- **Build:** Build the mark from named parts (Mark pieces with per-piece transforms). Grow the body from a seed with scale lmix(0.2, 1, prog(f, a, a+54, E.out)) about its centre. Draw each line part on with stroke-dasharray = its length L and stroke-dashoffset = L * (1 - p). Reveal each filled stripe through a mask rect whose scaleX goes 0 -> 1 from one end. Part i starts at a + 6 + 6i and runs 10 f on E.out. When the last part lands, raise the label letter by letter from behind its baseline: each glyph sits in an overflow-hidden line box and moves translateY 100% -> 0 through arrive (or use MaskRise for whole words). Then push the whole group gently through the hold.
- **Timing:** Seed growth: 54 f on E.out (about 0.2x -> 1; first-frame edge speed ~4 px/f). Parts: 10 f each, 6 f apart (3 parts inside ~28 f). Label glyphs: 2 f apart, 12 f each on E.out. The whole mark reads within ~0.5 s. Then a 90-120 f hold that pushes from 1.0 to 1.10-1.15 on E.dolly (le-living-hold).
- **Use when:** Geometric marks made of a body plus lines, stripes or orbits. A fresh logo reveal after a hard cut to a clean stage. Stings that must show the mark within 0.5 s.
- **Avoid when:** Solid single-shape marks (there is nothing to draw). Marks with more than ~5 parts (it turns into a slow queue). The mark already exists on screen as the story device.

### Story object becomes the mark

`le-device-becomes-mark` · workhorse · energy any · any

The film's last object (a dot, circle, coin or pill) ends at exactly the mark's screen position and size, and the mark replaces it by a hard cut or an in-place morph, so the logo arrives as the answer to the story.

- **Build:** Compute the mark's final rect first (placeMark). Drive the story object so its last frame lands on that rect, or on 0.57 of it for the cut-and-grow ending, with matched centre, size, radius and colour. Examples: a coin turning rotateY 90 -> 10 deg on E.outSoft while it rises 20% of H; a word deleting from both ends (slice(k, n - k), k + 1 every 5 f) while its pill hugs the text down to a circle; a pill whose width collapses to the icon's rounded square (Morph on E.inOut). Then either hard-cut to the flat mark at exactly the object's last position and size (0.57 of the rect) and grow it lmix(0.57, 1, prog(f, cut, cut + 18, E.out)) about its centre, with half the growth in the first 2 f and no overshoot. Or finish in place: the dot's fill darkens to the mark's ink (mixColor over 12 f on E.smooth) and its glyph fades in over the last 4 f. Nothing may blink, double or change style across the seam, not even for one frame.
- **Timing:** Coin flip: 22 f on E.outSoft. Two-ended delete: 5 f per letter pair, pill width eased 4 f per step on E.ui. Pill-to-square morph: 30-40 f on E.inOut. Cut pop: 18 f on E.out (0.57 -> 1). In-place darkening: 12 f. Then hold ~20 f before the name follows.
- **Use when:** Every film that has a story device: the default way to arrive at the mark, especially as the device's third and final use.
- **Avoid when:** There is no recurring object (a mark forced out of an unrelated shape reads as a pun). The object's shape and the mark's disagree (a square into a circle needs a morph, never a cut).

### The product clears the stage

`le-stage-clears-to-brand` · workhorse · energy any · launch, feature, walkthrough

The last product element leaves (dropping out of frame, accelerating away, or bursting outward toward camera), and the brand, already waiting behind it, starts its reveal on the exact frame it is uncovered.

- **Build:** Keep the brand layer (stage plus lockup) mounted under the product for the whole shot, so the exit uncovers it instead of cutting to it. Exit the product one of three ways. (1) Time-reverse its own entrance with progress = 1 - entrance(1 - t); for a window this is typically a ~1000 px drop over 44 f on E.smooth. (2) Float a lone card up from its drift over 25 f on E.in while it grows 1 -> 1.33.
