(3) Burst a card cluster outward: each card translates 300-450 px along its vector from the cluster centre and scales lmix(1, 3) over 20 f on E.in, and the card layer is removed on the frame its fastest card passes ~75 px/f. Start the brand reveal on the frame the product's edge clears the lockup's box, computed from the exit curve. Either the mark grows lmix(0.48, 1, prog(..., E.out)) over 68 f, or a letterspaced wordmark (0.08 em) fades up over 40 f on E.smooth with no scale.
- **Timing:** Drop: 44 f on E.smooth (~1000 px, peak ~64 px/f, motion-blur pass on). Float-out: 25 f on E.in (5 -> 22 px/f, scale +33%). Burst: 20 f on E.in, cut at ~75 px/f. The brand reveal starts within 0-1 f of the clear frame. Mark growth: 68 f on E.out (edge speed ~17 px/f, no overshoot). Then hold 90-120 f under a 10-15% push (le-living-hold).
- **Use when:** Walkthroughs and feature films whose last shot is the product itself. The opening was a window or card entering, so the reverse bookends it. A crescendo of many screens that should give way to calm.
- **Avoid when:** The film's last beat is type, not product. A lockup that is already visible would be crossed by the exiting product. A burst with no build-up earlier to justify the energy.

### Accent icon cools to its neutral mark

`le-hot-to-neutral-cool` · accent · energy medium · launch, feature, sting, vertical

The app icon pops up from tiny in the film's hot accent, cools through darker tones to its neutral final colours, lifts a little to make room, and the name fades in beneath it.

- **Build:** Pop the icon from tiny with scale mix(0.19, 1, prog(f, a, a+38, E.out)), its tile filled C.accent. Cool it as one object, never as two crossfaded copies: tile fill mixColor(C.accent, C.ink, p) and glyph mixColor(C.ink, C.white, p), with p = prog(f, a+6, a+34, E.smooth). OKLab mixing passes through darker shades of the same hue instead of muddy grey. Then lift it to make room: translateY 0 -> -102 px and scale 1 -> 0.945 over 36 f on E.smooth. As the lift passes 60%, fade the label up under it: opacity 0 -> 1 and translateY 8 -> 0 through arrive, over 15 f.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Start the tile in the film's single accent as a flat fill, not a multi-hue gradient, and cool it through darker shades of that same hue to the neutral ink with mixColor. Any accent hue carries the idea, so it never needs a warm orange-to-red ramp. The full look relies on gradient, orange; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** Pop: 38 f on E.out (0.19 -> 0.72 by f6). Colour: 28 f (f6-34) on E.smooth. Lift: 36 f on E.smooth. Label: 15 f. Then hold 90-120 f under a push.
- **Use when:** Films whose accent stood for heat, urgency or the problem early on and should cool into the product. App-icon lockups.
- **Avoid when:** The accent already means something else in the film (one accent, one meaning). Icons whose final colour is the accent itself.

### Card shrinks to a pill, words close in

`le-card-to-pill-flank` · accent · energy medium · launch, feature, walkthrough

The last content card empties and shrinks into a small pill while the tagline words slide in from beyond the frame edges, blurred to sharp, to sit on either side of it; then the logo appears inside the pill.

- **Build:** Build a flex row [wordL][slot][wordR] and animate the slot's width from the card's width to the pill's width. Use Morph for the slot's box: radius to h/2, fill from the card surface to a solid tonal step of the stage. The words are then carried in from off-frame by the layout alone. Fade the card's content out over the first 6 f, before the slot moves fast, and shrink on E.whip. The words get blurIn(p, 8) and opacity prog(..., E.smooth), so they fly faded and resolve sharp on landing. When the pill lands, fade the Mark in inside it over 14 f on E.smooth. The row stays centred on the frame throughout.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Make the pill opaque: a solid tonal step of the stage (C.ink2 on C.ink, C.mist on C.paper), optionally with a 1.5 px C.line stroke. No translucent fill and no backdrop blur over the background. The full look relies on glass; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** Content fade: 6 f. Shrink: 30 f on E.whip (card ~1240 -> ~310 px; each word travels ~470 px at a peak of ~58 px/f with the motion-blur pass on, faded until it lands). Logo fade: 14 f, starting 8 f after the pill lands. Then hold 90-120 f under a 10-15% push (le-living-hold).
- **Use when:** Films that opened with a gap or pill inside a headline (the reverse closes the bookend). Products whose output is a card, post, message or result. A tagline that brackets the brand: [wordL] [mark] [wordR].
- **Avoid when:** There is no card on screen to collapse. Words too long to fit beside the pill inside the safe width. Light-on-light stages where the pill loses its edge.

### CTA line closes its gaps

`le-accordion-cta-collapse` · accent · energy calm · launch, feature, walkthrough

The end line starts with exaggerated spaces between its words, which close as the line settles centred; the last word, often the URL, travels farthest, so the eye ends there.

- **Build:** Lay the final line out centred. Give word i a start offset off_i = 70 + 80 * i px (capped at 290 px) in the direction of travel, so the last word travels farthest. Drive each word as x_i = finalX_i + off_i - inertia(f, a, off_i/14.6, 0.934).x: a pure exponential close with tau = 14.6 f and no overshoot (horizontal moves need no arrive). Enter on a hard cut from a larger line whose total width matches this line's stretched width. Optionally keep the URL soft for 8 f after it stops, then resolve it over 14 f with RackFocus, so focus is the last thing to settle.
- **Timing:** tau = 14.6 f: 55% closed in 10 f, 95% by 44 f. The last word starts at no more than 20 px/f and only slows from there. Gaps of ~150/115/80 px close to a normal word space (~0.25 em). URL focus: soft for 8 f, resolved over 14 f.
- **Use when:** A one-line CTA (a sentence plus a URL) after a large type beat. Type-led films whose last beat is a phrase locking together.
- **Avoid when:** Lines that wrap to two rows. Films that already closed a word gap earlier. Vertical frames where the stretched line would exceed the safe width.

### Device keeps time inside the lockup

`le-mark-ticks-in-lockup` · accent · energy calm · launch, feature, loop, sting

During the hold, the story device that became part of the mark (a dot, a bar, a stripe) gives one or two small ticks on the beat, so the bookend plays inside the finished lockup instead of after it.

- **Build:** Keep the device as its own Mark piece (e.g. MARK.D). During the hold, pulse only that piece: scale 1 + 0.12 * hitPulse(f - beat, 2, 6) about its own centre, or a nudge of 3 * hitPulse(f - beat, 2, 6) px along the device's signature direction. If the accent means 'what just landed', flash the piece to C.accent on the pulse and return it to its resting colour over 12 f with mixColor. Place 1-2 ticks on downbeats in the first second of the hold, in time with the stinger's tail, and none in the last 30 f, so the final frame is calm and identical to the poster.
- **Timing:** 1-2 ticks at least 30 f apart. hitPulse attack 2 f, tau 6 f (gone in ~38 f). Amplitude 10-14% scale or 2-4 px. None in the final 30 f.
- **Use when:** Films whose story device became a piece of the mark. Ends that should close the device's loop without ending on the device alone.
- **Avoid when:** Marks without a separable piece. Very still closes, where any pulse breaks the calm. Loops that need the device to travel back to its frame-0 position instead.

### Mark turns through a key light

`le-mark-glint-turn` · accent · energy calm · launch, sting, feature

The mark (an extruded glyph, a coin or a tile) turns a few degrees in 3D, and its face passes through a light, so a single specular sweep crosses it as it settles face-on.

- **Build:** Give the mark depth with CSS 3D: perspective 1200 px on the parent, the front face plus 6-10 copies stacked 1 px apart in z in a darker tonal step for the extrusion (or a mesh in Three.js). Rotate it rotateY tw(f, a, a+40, -35, 0, E.outSoft) with a small rotateX 20 -> 0 so it settles face-on. Sweep the light in 2D: a white band 30% of the mark's width, with opacity 0 -> 0.9 -> 0 across its width, masked to the mark (mask-image of the mark SVG) with mix-blend-mode screen, translated across the face over 14 f. Time it so the band's centre crosses as the rotation passes ~70%.
- **Timing:** Turn: 40 f on E.outSoft (~4 deg/f peak for 35 deg). Glint: 14 f on E.smooth, starting ~f20. One glint per film.
- **Use when:** Premium, material or physical brands (finance, hardware, collectibles). 3D marks. A mark that needs one moment of life early in its hold.
- **Avoid when:** Flat, playful or line marks (a sheen on a stroke looks like a template effect). Films with no other 3D. A second glint anywhere in the film (it reads as a preset).

### Name types backwards, group stays centred

`le-reverse-type-recentre` · accent · energy calm · launch, feature, sting, vertical

The name appears from its last letter to its first while the mark is pushed outward, so the lockup grows out of the mark's edge and stays centred on every frame.

- **Build:** Lay out [mark][gap][name], with every character laid out from the start and untyped characters at opacity 0. Measure each character's advance with measureTracked. Character i of n shows from frame t0 + 3.5 * (n-1-i), decided on fd, with a 4 f opacity ramp on E.ui, so the name grows leftward from its last letter. Keep the group centred without stepping: markLeft = cx - (markW + gap + ws(f))/2, where ws(f) = sum of adv_k * spr(f, t_k, SPR.firm) over the characters revealed so far. That is one critically damped spring per character, which glides the mark outward as each letter lands. If the story device is a dot, let it become the mark in place first: fill mixColor(C.mist, C.ink, p) over 12 f on E.smooth, with the glyph inside fading in over the last 4 f.
- **Timing:** 3.5 f per character (10 characters in 36 f), each fading in over 4 f on E.ui. Each width step eases on SPR.firm (no overshoot, ~20 f to settle). The mark travels ~270 px at 7-8 px/f on average. Dot-to-mark darkening takes 12 f. The lockup settles ~20 f after the last character, then holds 90-120 f under a 10-15% push (le-living-hold).
- **Use when:** Agent, assistant or persona products whose mark is an avatar or a disc. Names of 4-12 characters. A centred lockup that must never jump.
- **Avoid when:** Two-word names whose second word makes no sense on its own first. Right-to-left scripts (it becomes an ordinary type-on). The headline already used a typewriter.

### Staircase echo shape morph

`le-clone-stack-morph` · accent · energy medium · launch, feature

A large brand shape collapses into a slim pill around the URL, and mid-morph its moving edges show stepped echoes from staggered copies, like a mechanical transformation.

- **Build:** Animate one rounded rect from the big shape to a pill that hugs the URL over 48 f on E.smooth, using morphBox from Morph.tsx or width, height and radius directly. Render 7 copies behind it: copy k samples the same morph at frame f - 2k and draws as a 1.5 px stroke (no fill) with opacity 0.6 * (1 - k/9) in one tonal step of the stage colour. The copies show only where the shape moves, stack into a staircase along the moving edges, and coincide and vanish once it rests. The URL swaps in at the start of the morph (8 f fade on E.smooth) and stays still once the pill lands.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Draw the echoes as plain 1.5 px strokes in one tonal step of the stage (C.ink2 on C.ink, C.line on C.paper) with a linear opacity falloff. No rim light, bloom or coloured edges on the copies. The full look relies on glow; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** Morph: 48 f on E.smooth, height 983 -> 227 px (edge peak ~22 px/f), width 1878 -> 997 px with a long tail. 7 copies at a 2 f delay each (14 f of echo after the leader stops). The URL stays readable for at least 102 f afterwards, under the card's 10-15% push (le-living-hold).
- **Use when:** Turning a big brand shape or frame into the CTA container. Mechanical, engineered or developer-tool brands. One moment that should feel designed rather than tweened.
- **Avoid when:** Short moves (under ~150 px the echoes collapse into a smear). Elements that already carry motion blur (double trails). More than once per film.

### Stop-motion brand strobe

`le-strobe-sting` · accent · energy high · sting, launch, loop, vertical

A burst of hard-cut brand states (the poster, the lockup tiled in ever denser grids, one flood, the boxed wordmark, the glyph) flickers past in under a second as a punchy sign-off.

- **Build:** After the lockup's hold, cut through an array of full-frame states with no interpolation: const seq = [[poster,7],[grid3,5],[grid4,5],[gridA,2],[gridB,2],[flood,5],[ink,5],[boxedName,5],[glyph,7]], accumulated into Sequences or chosen with fd(frame). The grids are a CSS grid of the lockup with n = 3, 4, 5, 5 columns and a half-tile offset on alternate states, so the cuts read as a stepped pull-back. Keep every state on the same dark stage, with the accent flood as the only bright state, so there are no more than 3 large light-dark flips per second. End on the glyph alone for at most 30 f, and export the poster from the lockup frame, not the last frame. A quiet version keeps only the last two states (boxed name 5 f, glyph 7 f) as a loop point.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Replace the cream flood with the film's single accent flood (or C.ink2), keep every other state on the dark stage, and allow only one bright state, so the strobe changes shape and density rather than luminance. The full look relies on beige; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** Holds 7, 5, 5, 2, 2, 5, 5, 5, 7 f (43 f, ~0.72 s). Glyph ~2% of H, centred, for at most 30 f. A tick cluster under it that matches the opening's sound.
- **Use when:** Social stings and launch films with a poster-driven or stop-motion identity. A re-energising coda after a quiet end card. Autoplay loops that need a clean reset point.
- **Avoid when:** Calm or premium brands. Any film where you cannot keep large light-dark flips under 3 per second (photosensitivity). Any case where it would cut the lockup's hold below 1.5 s.

### Words part, URL types into the gap

`le-words-part-url-types` · accent · energy calm · launch, feature, walkthrough

The closing line splits at its middle, both halves slide outward and dim, the URL types letter by letter into the gap, and the flanks fade so the URL holds alone.

- **Build:** Set the closing line as two spans that meet at the centre. Split them apart by +/-(urlWidth/2 + 40 px) over 44 f on E.smooth, with colour mixColor(C.ink, C.mute, p) so they dim but stay legible. From 40% of the split, type the URL centred in the gap with TypeOn: 1 character per 4 f, head fade 4 f, caret hidden once done. After the last key, fade the flanks to 0 over 16 f on E.smooth. Keep the URL still on the card while the card pushes 10-15% on E.dolly; the mark then joins above it, or the URL becomes the lockup's secondary line.
- **Timing:** Split: 44 f on E.smooth over 250-300 px (peak 20 px/f or less). URL starts at 40% of the split, 4 f per character. Flank fade: 16 f after the last key. URL readable and still for at least 102 f.
- **Use when:** The closing line is a two-word phrase or pun built around the product, and the CTA is a URL. Minimal, type-only films.
- **Avoid when:** Lines longer than ~4 words. Films with no typing anywhere else (it would add a new device at the very end). URLs too long for the gap to open within the safe width.

### Dark slam, spin and brighten

`le-slam-spin-pullout` · signature · energy high · launch, sting

After a near-still beat, giant low-contrast arms of the mark sweep over the frame, and the mark rushes back to logo size while spinning into place and brightening to full contrast.

- **Build:** Hold the card before it (the URL or last line) almost still, drifting at most 0.3 px/f, and end that hold with a designed freeze of at most 15 f on silence. Then start the mark at full speed with no ease-in, centred on the frame. Scale s = lmix(12, 1, prog(f, a, a+66, E.outSoft)); rotation tw(f, a, a+60, -70, 0, E.outSoft) degrees; fill mixColor(C.ink2, C.white, p*p) with p = 1 - ln(s)/ln(12). The fastest frames are then dark grey on a C.ink stage and cannot strobe, and full contrast arrives only as the mark slows. Blur the previous text out underneath (blurOut over 10 f), and keep the motion-blur pass on while the log rate is above 0.05/f (about the first 18 f).
- **Timing:** 66 f. Log rate 0.17/f at f0, 0.10 at f10, 0.04 at f20. Spin 5.2 deg/f at the start, 2.8 deg/f by f10, at rest by f60. Fill 31% of the way to white at f10, 70% at f20, 97% at f40. Preceded by a near-still hold of 60-90 f that ends in a freeze of at most 15 f.
- **Use when:** The finale of a high-energy film, where the single biggest motion spike follows the single biggest stillness. Radially symmetric or rotational marks (asterisks, petals, rings).
- **Avoid when:** Marks with an obvious up direction that look wrong at -70 deg (lettermarks). Calm films. Films that already used a spin or a fast zoom-out seam.

### Liquid blob resolves into the mark

`le-gooey-merge-to-mark` · signature · energy medium · launch, sting, loop

A dot, or two soft lobes sliding in from the sides, swells into a liquid blob that stretches, splits and snaps into the crisp geometric mark.

- **Build:** Draw the mark's primitives as SVG circles and rects in one group, all starting stacked on the seed dot, and move each to its final place on E.smooth with a 2-4 f stagger. Two-lobe version: two large rounded shapes move translateX +/-600 -> +/-160 px on E.outSoft, fuse at centre and frame the closing line. Filter the group with feGaussianBlur stdDeviation 10, then feColorMatrix (type matrix, alpha row '0 0 0 18 -7'), which thresholds the blur into a liquid neck wherever parts are close. Over the last 8 f, ramp stdDeviation 10 -> 0. On the frame it reaches 0, swap the filtered group for the crisp Mark at the identical transform: a one-frame swap of identical shapes, never a crossfade. Use flat fills only; the threshold makes hard edges, and rim lights or inner highlights would be eaten or look like neon.
- **Timing:** 46 f. Parts travel f0-38 on E.smooth at a 2-4 f stagger, and the blob visibly splits ~26 f in. Blur ramp and crisp swap over the last 8 f. Two-lobe version: converge in 40 f on E.outSoft (first frame ~49 px/f, motion-blur pass on), then drift 0.3-0.5 px/f under the line.
- **Use when:** Products about raw input becoming structure, or about merging and joining. The story device is a dot. Marks made of a few separate primitives.
- **Avoid when:** Marks with thin strokes or text inside (the threshold eats them). Brands that need crisp precision throughout. Films already using a soft morph seam.

### Pull out of the mark, undershoot, breathe

`le-macro-pullout-breathe` · signature · energy high · launch, sting, feature, vertical

The mark arrives so large that only fragments of it fill the frame, collapses to slightly smaller than its final size, then gently breathes up to rest, as if the camera had found it.

- **Build:** Place the Mark with placeMark at its final spot; centre it where the lockup needs it, e.g. 80 px left of frame centre to leave room for the name. Pick the start scale s0 so the mark's outer edge starts about 750 px from its centre (s0 = 750 / the mark's half-width at rest, about 5x for a 300 px mark), so only fragments fill the frame. Scale it about its own centre in log space: s = lmix(s0, 0.93, prog(f, a, a+N, E.outSoft)) * lmix(1, 1/0.93, prog(f, a+N-24, a+N, E.smooth)), with N = 43 x ln(s0 / 0.93) frames (72 f from 5x). The log rate then starts near 0.105/f, so the outer edge never passes about 80 px/f; from 5x it crosses 1.0 near f35, bottoms out at 0.94 near f52 and breathes up to rest at 1.0 by f72 with no velocity step. Enter it on a cut: the outgoing shot shrinks into its centre on E.in over its last 24 f and cuts at a matching log speed (or start from zoomHandoff in camera.ts at the outgoing log speed). Render with the motion-blur pass. Keep the mark's counters and small parts outside the frame until the log rate falls below 0.07/f (~f10). Put the bottom of the undershoot on the strongest low hit after a ~15 f bass gap.
- **Timing:** Collapse: N = 43 x ln(s0 / 0.93) frames on E.outSoft (72 f from 5x; log rate about 0.105/f at the start, outer edge under about 80 px/f, under 0.07/f by f10). Breathe: the last 24 f on E.smooth (0.93 -> 1.0), bottoming at 0.94 near f52. Settled by f72. Hold the mark ~20 f before the name follows.
- **Use when:** The mark's first full appearance at the end, or a logo sting. A hit after a short bass gap. Marks with a strong silhouette or inner shapes that read as abstract fragments when huge.
- **Avoid when:** Thin line marks (at macro scale they become two hairlines crossing the frame). Right after another zoom-through seam. The mark was already shown at hero size earlier (that makes this a replayed reveal).

## Colour and light

Colour carries meaning, so ration it. Keep one accent with one job. It should cover roughly 0.05-6% of frame pixels on average (peaking near 12%) on a stage that fills 85-90% of the frame, and it should change on cut or impact frames, never through slow fades. Brightness is the strongest lever here: give every shot a planned mean luma, spend polarity flips of 160-240 levels on downbeats and act changes, and use at most one inverted card (about 60 f) in a dark film. Light moves are short and asymmetric: accent floods rise in 10-12 f and release over 20-26 f, sheens cross in about 36 f, and washes rise over about 40 f and recede over about 90 f. Stages never freeze: breathe them ±15% luma on a period of about 160 f, or drift them under 1 px/f. Build every gradient from tonal steps of one hue mixed in OKLab with mixColor, on normal blend, and let a hard edge or a one-frame white flash do the work a glow would.

### Accent on the newest arrival

`cl-accent-on-newest` · workhorse · energy medium · feature, walkthrough, launch, vertical

Whatever just arrived (a typed character, a snapped word, a generated pill) wears the accent for a moment and then settles to neutral, so a short coloured wake leads the eye.

- **Build:** Store each item's birth frame. Type-on: give each glyph span colour = mixColor(C.accent, C.white or C.ink, clamp((frame - birth) / 12)); at 1-1.7 chars/f this leaves a wake of 10-20 characters behind the caret. Word builds work as either a wave or a step. Wave: each word is grey for 4 f, accent at about 8 f and ink by 16-20 f, on E.out. Step: the word that snapped last holds the accent (fd(frame) >= snap[i] && fd(frame) < snap[i+1]), and the final word keeps it until 1 frame before the cut. Objects (generated pills, pins, cards, an end-card icon): stack an accent-tinted duplicate clipped to the shape (mix-blend-mode: color) and fade it from 1 to 0 on E.out. Use one accent hue only: no multi-stop hue cycle, no bloom, no text-shadow.
- **Timing:** Glyph decay takes 12-16 f on E.linear. A word wave takes 16-20 f per word with an 8-12 f stagger. A step holds 16-20 f per word. An object's tint resolves over 20-40 f on E.out.
- **Use when:** Prompts typing, statements building word by word, AI-generated items appearing, or any build where the newest piece should lead.
- **Avoid when:** The accent already means something else in the shot (a focus ring or a pressed button), or long paragraphs where the wake becomes noise.

### Drain the stage, keep the hero

`cl-drain-stage-keep-hero` · workhorse · energy calm · walkthrough, feature, launch

Everything around the hero fades and the world drops to dark or bleaches to white, while the hero stays crisp in place, isolating it or closing a section.

- **Build:** Duplicate the hero onto a top layer at identical coordinates so nothing under it can shift. Isolate: fade the rest of the layer to 0 on E.linear to reveal a mid-grey plate, then mix the plate from C.mist toward C.ink2 on E.in (world luma from about 238 to 87) while the hero gains a 20 px radius and a soft shadow; in a light film, drain the surroundings to C.white instead and assemble the next page around the parked hero. Focus variant: render the side columns through RackFocus (t 0 to 1, blur 8; never an animated blur filter on the columns) and drop them to 0.6 opacity while the centre stays untouched and the parent scales from 1 to 1.06. Exhale: after a peak, or once the lockup has held 90-120 f, dim the stage first (stage opacity 1 to 0, or brightness 1 to 0.6 during a push-in) and fade the hero 8 f later, ending on a hard cut mid-film or on a short C.ink tail only at the very end.
- **Timing:** Neighbours fade over 12 f on E.linear, the world dims over 10 f on E.in, then hold about 30 f. A white drain takes 6-16 f on E.linear. Column focus takes 18 f on E.smooth. In the exhale, the stage fades over 36 f and the hero over 30 f starting 8 f later, with a tail of up to 22 f; a push-in dim takes 8 f on E.in.
- **Use when:** Search results, a found item, a selected post or row, the moment before a detail view, and the ends of sections or of the film.
- **Avoid when:** The hero itself must move during the isolation, or the neighbours carry context the viewer still needs.

### Ink resolve on arrival

`cl-ink-resolve` · workhorse · energy any · any

Text never simply fades in: it arrives pale (or dim on a dark stage) and darkens or brightens to full ink as it settles.

- **Build:** For each word or line, mix its colour from a pale tone to the ink with mixColor from src/lib/color.ts (interpolateColors stair-steps), while opacity goes from 0.3-0.4 to 1. On paper, go from mixColor(C.ink, C.paper, 0.65), or a pale accent tint mixColor(C.accent, C.paper, 0.8), to C.ink; on a dark stage, go from C.mute to C.white. Pair it with a short rise inside an overflow-hidden line mask (translateY 100% to 0 through arrive(), or at most 60 px), with words staggered and no blur on slow rises; src/fx/Words.tsx can carry the motion while you apply the colour per word. Connector words ('on', 'and', 'the') reach half strength in 2 f and finish over the next 6-12 f, so the nouns read first.
- **Timing:** Colour takes 12-16 f per word on E.out (a headline-scale darkening may run 40 f). The rise takes 20 f, peaking under 20 px/f. Stagger words 8 f apart (4-10). Connector words go 0 to 0.5 in 2 f, then to 1 over 6-12 f.
- **Use when:** Every headline and caption reveal, especially over textured or busy backgrounds where an opacity fade alone looks washed out.
- **Avoid when:** Numbers that must read instantly on a cut (land them at full ink), or type that already sits inside a colour-band fill.

### Key-light edge hairline

`cl-key-light-edge-hairline` · workhorse · energy calm · launch, feature, walkthrough, sting

Every card, device bezel and bevelled shape on a dark stage carries a hairline edge that is bright on the side facing one fixed key light and fades to nothing on the far side, so surfaces separate from black without shadows or halos.

- **Build:** Declare one light direction for the whole film in brand/tokens.ts (LIGHT = 135, meaning light from the top-left, the same key light cl-tilt-linked-sheen assumes). Give each surface an edge layer above its content: position absolute, inset 0, border-radius inherit, padding 1.5 px, background linear-gradient(calc(LIGHT - rotateZ) deg, rgba(255,255,255,0.40) 0%, rgba(255,255,255,0.10) 35%, transparent 65%), masked to a ring with mask: linear-gradient(#000 0 0) content-box, linear-gradient(#000 0 0) and mask-composite: exclude (-webkit-mask-composite: xor). Recompute the angle every frame as LIGHT minus the object's own rotateZ, so the lit edge stays on the light's side while the object turns. Add box-shadow inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.06) as a top inner highlight. In 3D, multiply the lit-edge alpha by clamp(1 + 0.04 x degrees tilted toward the light, 0.6, 1.4), so an edge brightens as it turns into the light. For bevelled decorative shapes drawn in SVG (stars, tiles, extruded marks), stroke each facet edge at 1 px with a linearGradient in gradientUnits='userSpaceOnUse' running along the light vector (white at 40% fading to 0), and keep facet fills within 2-4% luma of the stage. Use no blur and no outer halo. On light stages, replace the hairline with a 1.5 px C.white top edge and a C.line bottom edge.
- **Timing:** Static styling with no clock of its own: it rides every entrance and move of its surface. Lit-edge alpha is 0.40 at the light corner, 0.10 at 35% of the gradient line and 0 by 65%. The inner top highlight is 0.06. The angle is recomputed every frame as LIGHT - rotateZ. Tilt gain is 0.04 per degree, clamped to 0.6-1.4x. On a tilt resolve (for example rotateX 25 deg to 0 over 68 f on E.out), the edge brightness settles on the same curve.
- **Use when:** Dark UI films with flat cards, panels, device bezels or bevelled brand shapes on near-black, where a drop shadow disappears and a glow is off-limits.
- **Avoid when:** Light-mode shots, where a white hairline vanishes on paper. Also avoid it on cards that already carry cl-rim-light-sweep's travelling streak, and on layouts so dense that every lit edge turns the frame into wireframe noise.

### Monochrome world, one accent

`cl-mono-one-accent` · workhorse · energy any · any

Everything is black, white and grey, and one saturated accent marks the single element in each shot that carries the meaning.

- **Build:** Declare neutrals plus one accent in brand/tokens.ts: C.ink for the stage, C.ink2 for surfaces, C.mute for labels, C.line for strokes, C.white for type, C.accent, and a press step of mixColor(C.accent, C.ink, 0.08). Grade every photo, map, clay render or backdrop screenshot with filter: grayscale(1) so mixed media reads as one world. Paint the accent on exactly one thing per shot (the payoff word, the pin, the pressed button, the focus ring) and keep one meaning for it all film. Focus devices use three steps of it: the full accent for strokes, mixColor(C.accent, C.ink, 0.65) for fills and a mid step for decaying outlines. Colour arrives on a cut or an impact frame (fd(frame) >= cue), never through a slow fade, and when you audit rendered stills the accent should average 0.05-6% of frame pixels (peak about 12.5%) with the stage at 85-90%.
- **Timing:** The palette stays the same for the whole film. The accent swaps on the cue frame (a step, 0 f). Focus outlines land 6-10 px wide with their container (26 f, E.out), thin to 1 px over 12 f on E.in, then decay to 30% opacity over 24 f on E.linear.
- **Use when:** Films that mix photos, 3D, maps and UI, multi-cell layouts, or any shot where several things compete and the eye needs exactly one target.
- **Avoid when:** The product's own colourful UI is the subject of every shot and greying it would misrepresent it, or the story needs two semantic colours on screen at once.

### Now, was, next tone ladder

`cl-read-state-tone-ladder` · workhorse · energy any · any

Items in a sequence sit on three neutral tones: the one being read is at full ink, the ones already read step down to a mid grey and stay as context, and the ones still to come wait in a dim grey.

- **Build:** Declare three tones in brand/tokens.ts. NOW is C.white on an ink stage (C.ink on paper). WAS is C.mute. NEXT is mixColor(C.ink, C.white, 0.24) on ink (mixColor(C.paper, C.ink, 0.2) on paper). Give every item in the sequence (caption words, list rows, step labels, roller slots, status words) a cue frame, and compute its state with fd(): NEXT before its cue, NOW from its cue, and WAS from the next item's cue. Promote NEXT to NOW over 6 f on E.ui. Start the previous item's NOW-to-WAS demotion on the same frame, over 10 f on E.smooth, so the eye is handed over and only one item is at full ink after each handoff. Rollers and ratchets step their tones on the slot frame with no tween. Show pending items at NEXT only when 'there is more' is the message (lists, slot ratchets, step lists, with at most three visible); otherwise they do not exist yet. Exits go through WAS: an item drops to WAS before it leaves, never straight from NOW. Keep weight and size the same so tone alone carries the order. The accent stays out of the ladder because it marks meaning (cl-mono-one-accent).
- **Timing:** Promotion takes 6 f on E.ui. Demotion takes 10 f on E.smooth, starting with the next item's arrival. Each item holds NOW for at least 24 f. Rollers and ratchets step on the slot frame (0 f). An exit starts at least 8 f after the item reaches WAS. On ink, the tones sit at about 100% (NOW), 40% (WAS) and 24% (NEXT) of the way from the stage to white.
- **Use when:** Captions that build in steps, lists and checklists that grow, slot rollers, status sequences, and flanking words that make way for a new focal word.
- **Avoid when:** A single statement that lands all at once, or real product UI whose own text colours must stay true. In lens lists, tone should follow distance from the focus line, not reading order.

### One-hue light ramp

`cl-one-hue-light-ramp` · workhorse · energy calm · launch, sting, feature, loop

Every lit thing (rims, rings, stage lifts, the end-card field) comes from adjacent lightness steps of one hue on a single near-black stage.

- **Build:** Build five tokens of one hue with mixColor, running from the stage to a pale tint: C.ink, then mixColor(C.ink, C.accent, 0.2 / 0.45 / 0.75), then mixColor(C.accent, C.white, 0.5). Only ever draw a gradient between two adjacent steps, so the whole film's light comes from one decision. Rims, rings and orb lobes use the upper steps as crisp strokes or flat fills, never as soft halos or bloom, and the stage holds 63-99% of pixels on dark frames. For an end-card field behind a wordmark, use linear-gradient(to top, step0, step2 45%, step4) plus a repeating-linear-gradient(90deg) of flat, hard-edged 60-120 px bands at ±6% lightness (no blur, so they never read as fluted glass); the band layer drifts 0.3 px/f so the hold never freezes. Against banding, bake the field as a dithered PNG with scripts/dither-gradient.py and let the film's global 1.5-2% grain sit over it.
- **Timing:** The palette stays the same. The end-card field holds 90-120 f with the bands drifting 0.3 px/f on E.linear.
- **Use when:** Dark launch films with many light-built shapes (orbs, rings, rims) that need a recognisable look. It also makes a single bright card hit harder.
- **Avoid when:** Light-mode walkthroughs where the UI's own colours dominate, or films already using the monochrome-plus-accent system (pick one system).

### Palette shift as context cue

`cl-context-palette-shift` · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature, walkthrough

The world's colour changes behind a steady foreground, for a whole act or for one beat, to say 'new context' or 'this is the moment' without words.

- **Build:** Keep two or three token sets keyed by act in brand/tokens.ts: for example, a loud act on C.paper with C.ink and C.accent, a technical process act in pure neutral greys, and a calm product act in pale tints of one hue with the accent withdrawn. Read colours through a palette(act) helper so a whole act switches at once, on a hard cut or hidden inside a zoom-through. For a single beat, park the hero (card, composer, device) and shift only the backdrop. Drive one blurred backdrop layer's filter brightness() and saturate() so its luma rises about 100 levels over 42 f on E.smooth, or step it on the cut into the hero beat and step back on the next wide. The hero never moves during the shift, so the eye stays parked.
- **Timing:** Act switches happen in 0 f on a cut. A neutral process act can be as short as 74 f. A backdrop shift takes 42 f on E.smooth. A hero-beat backdrop holds for up to about 300 f before stepping back.
- **Use when:** Act changes without title cards, entering another app's world, or flagging the key moment (the user's prompt, the reveal).
- **Avoid when:** The foreground is moving at the same time (the cue gets lost), or the film is shorter than two acts.

### Specular sweep

`cl-specular-sweep` · workhorse · energy calm · launch, sting, feature, loop

A soft bright band glides once across a settled number, word or logo face, so the element looks locked and made of a real material without moving.

- **Build:** Duplicate the settled text or mark and fill the duplicate with linear-gradient(100deg, transparent 0, C.white at 35% alpha 50%, transparent 100%). Make the band about 40% of the text height wide (about 30% of the width for a logo glyph, with peak opacity up to 0.9), clip it to the glyphs with background-clip: text or an SVG mask, and use mix-blend-mode: screen on dark stages. Drive the band's x from -20% to 120% of the element width on E.smooth, so its speed peaks mid-sweep, starting 6-10 f after the element lands. For a looping working state, use a light-grey label with a 120 px lighter band whose background-position is (frame % 60) / 60 on E.linear, and stop it on the frame the state resolves. Keep the sheen inside the glyphs, with no blur or halo outside them.
- **Timing:** A one-shot sweep takes 36 f on E.smooth (about 16 px/f mid-sweep, peaking near 26 px/f). A logo glint brightens over 9 f, holds about 11 f and is clear by 36 f. The loop has a 60 f period on E.linear and is held for up to about 74 f before the result.
- **Use when:** A final number, price or logo that has landed and must hold attention through a still beat, or loading and generating labels.
- **Avoid when:** The element is still moving, or you would need more than one sweep in the shot (it turns into decoration).

### Accent hit envelope

`cl-accent-hit-envelope` · accent · energy medium · feature, walkthrough, launch, loop

On a press or an impact, the element floods with the accent and peaks for one frame with its label inverted, then either bleeds back like decaying light or stays as the new state.

- **Build:** Put a solid C.accent overlay inside the button, with the same corner radius. Drive its opacity with hitPulse(frame - cue, 10, 8): a fast rise, a one-frame peak, and an exponential release about twice as long as the attack. Switch the label to C.ink when the overlay passes 0.6, and change no scale (the cursor may dip 1 to 0.9 to 1 over 12 f). For an impact that changes state, swap the object's fill to the accent on the contact frame (decided with fd), add a flat C.white overlay at 0.8·hitPulse(t, 1, 2), apply squash(t) anchored at the contact edge, and leave the accent on. No ring blur and no outer halo.
- **Timing:** Attack 10-12 f, a 1 f peak, then a release of 20-26 f (tau 8): an asymmetric 1:2 envelope. On an impact, the swap takes 1 f, the white flash about 4 f and the squash 8 f.
- **Use when:** Primary-button clicks, send or confirm moments, and contact hits that turn an object into its new state.
- **Avoid when:** Secondary controls and hovers (save it for the decisive action), or when the accent already floods the ground.

### Brightness rides the move

`cl-brightness-rides-move` · accent · energy high · launch, sting, feature

A mark or icon takes its brightness from the same progress that drives its scale or depth, so an oversized pass stays a dark shape and the object reaches full brightness exactly as it lands.

- **Build:** Never give the fill a clock of its own: derive it from the transform. Log-scale slam: s = lmix(s0, 1, prog(f, a, a + 66, E.glide)) with s0 = 6-8. Then p = 1 - Math.log(s) / Math.log(s0), and fill = mixColor(mixColor(C.ink, C.white, 0.14), C.white, p * p * p) on a dark stage (on paper, mix from mixColor(C.paper, C.ink, 0.12) to C.ink). While the mark is three or more times its final size and covering much of the frame, it stays a dark grey under about luma 60, so the frame's mean luma never flashes. Lift toward camera: an icon tile peeling out of its row inverts as it travels, with the tile going mixColor(C.ink2, C.white, q) and the glyph mixColor(C.white, C.ink, q), where q = clamp(travel progress / 0.75), so the inversion finishes before the last quarter of the move. Depth field: in a multi-depth parallax field, mix each layer's fill from C.ink toward its own colour by a weight read from its current z (0.45 far, 0.75 mid, 1.0 near), and keep reading it during a push so objects brighten as they approach. Turn on true motion blur while |delta log s| > 0.1 per frame, and check with scripts/measure-speed.py that edges stay under 80 px/f.
- **Timing:** Slam: 66 f on E.glide from s0 = 6-8. The fill follows p^3, so it passes mid-grey only in the second half of the move and reaches full brightness on the landing frame. Lift-out: 24 f of travel on E.inOut, with the inversion complete at 75% (about 18 f); a mid-grey tile goes from about luma 160 to 248. Depth weights are 0.45 / 0.75 / 1.0 by z, re-read every frame of the push. Motion blur stays on while |delta log s| > 0.1 per frame, and edges stay under 80 px/f.
- **Use when:** A logo mark or icon slams in oversized and shrinks to size, an icon lifts out of the UI toward camera, or a field of objects at several depths is pushed through on a dark stage.
- **Avoid when:** Text (use cl-ink-resolve, which runs on time), and moves under about 150 px or 1.5x, where the change would not show. On a light stage a giant near-black pass would itself be the flash, so mix toward the paper there.

### Duotone until featured

`cl-duotone-until-featured` · accent · energy medium · launch, feature, walkthrough

Screenshots and photos sit in a two-tone grade until their beat. Then full colour opens out from the point of interaction, and the previous item returns to duotone.

- **Build:** Give every non-featured media layer an SVG filter: feColorMatrix type saturate 0, then feComponentTransfer tables mapping shadows to C.ink and highlights to C.mist (or to a pale accent tint, mixColor(C.accent, C.paper, 0.85), for a branded duotone). On the featured item's beat, place the full-colour copy of the same image above it and reveal it through clip-path circle(r at x y), growing from the click or impact point to 150% on E.out, or swap it on the cut frame. When focus moves on, return the previous item to duotone by animating the matrix's saturate value from 1 to 0. Only one item is ever in full colour.
- **Timing:** The colour iris takes 18 f on E.out from the interaction point. The return to duotone takes 20 f on E.smooth. A swap on a cut takes 0 f.
- **Use when:** Grids of integrations, galleries, template pickers, and multi-cell layouts where one item at a time is the subject.
- **Avoid when:** Only one hero screenshot is on screen (nothing to contrast with), or the UI's colours are its selling point in every frame.

### Graphic softens into the stage

`cl-graphic-blurs-into-stage` · accent · energy calm · launch, sting, loop

A crisp graphic that has just finished its move, such as a wall of bars or a stripe field, loses its edges, widens and keeps drifting until it has become the soft backdrop for the next title, with no cut.

- **Build:** Keep the graphic's own elements mounted after their build and render them through src/fx/RackFocus (render = the bar group, blur 48, mid on). Drive t from 0 to 1 over 72 f on E.smooth. RackFocus crossfades a sharp copy and a copy at constant blur, so the softening does not step the way an animated filter: blur() does. On the same progress, widen each element (scaleX 1 to 1.5 about its centre) so the gaps close, and mix the whole field 25% toward the stage colour so its contrast drops under the type to come. Fill every element with a vertical gradient between two adjacent steps of the film's one-hue ramp (cl-one-hue-light-ramp). Slide each element's background-position-y at its own speed, 0.3 + 0.5 x rand(i) percent per frame, so the bands shift tone at different rates and the field never freezes once it is soft. Bring the next foreground in from frame 36 of the soften, when the stripes no longer read as objects. If banding shows, add 1-2% feTurbulence noise over the field, or bake a matching still with scripts/dither-gradient.py. In full colour, the field shifts through several hues as it softens.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Fill the bars with tonal steps of one non-banned hue (from the stage to a light tint), not a periwinkle-pink-orange spectrum, so the softened field becomes a single-hue living stage. Keep the RackFocus soften, the widen and the per-bar drift. The full look relies on gradient, orange, purple; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** The soften takes 72 f on E.smooth (RackFocus t from 0 to 1, blur 48 px at 1080p). The widen from 1 to 1.5 and the 25% contrast drop run on the same curve. Each element's gradient drifts at 0.3-0.8% per frame on E.linear and keeps drifting for 60-120 f under the next element. The next foreground enters from frame 36.
- **Use when:** After a graphic build (a bar wall, a stripe or tile field, a filled pattern), when the next beat is a title or the end-card mark and needs a backdrop born from what was just on screen.
- **Avoid when:** The graphic carries data the viewer still needs to read, or it is a UI act where the stage should stay flat. When no graphic build comes before the title, use cl-living-stage directly.

### Living gradient stage

`cl-living-stage` · accent · energy calm · any

Behind static cards the background never freezes: soft pools of colour at the corners breathe in brightness or drift slowly, like light through water.

- **Build:** Start from a C.ink base with two or three huge pools (radius 55-60% of the frame, for example one centred at 85% 15% and one at 10% 95%) in dark tints of one allowed hue (never violet, warm brown or a multi-hue mesh), each baked once as an RGBA PNG with scripts/dither-gradient.py rather than drawn as a CSS radial-gradient under a live blur(), which bands at 8 bits and costs render time. Breathe mode: each pool's opacity moves between 0.85 and 1.0 on sin(2π·frame/162), the second half a period out of phase, with no translation (about ±15% luma). Drift mode: 4-5 pools, each centre moving ±6% of the frame on sine loops of 360-660 f at different phases, with opacity ±8%. The pools light the stage, never an element: none sits centred behind type or a card. Let the film's global 1.5-2% grain sit over it, and give the stage an intensity prop (0-1) so brand beats (open, tagline, end card) raise it while UI beats sit on flat C.ink.
- **Timing:** The breathe period is 162 f. Drift loops run 360-660 f, at under 1 px/f. On brand beats the stage rises over 50 f on E.out (translateY +40% to 0) and drains to flat in 8 f.
- **Use when:** Holds, end cards and statement cards that would otherwise sit still for more than 48 f.
- **Avoid when:** Busy UI shots where any background motion competes, or films built on a hard flat-stage look. Behind a product window or readable type, where soft pools read as a generic gradient backdrop or as haze; light stages, where they read as smudges. A flat stage with one tonal step is the stronger default.

### Rim streak on card edges

`cl-rim-light-sweep` · accent · energy calm · feature, launch, walkthrough

A bright streak travels along a dark card's border while its edges carry a faint lit rim, separating it from a black stage without a drop shadow.

- **Build:** Fill the card with C.ink2 on a C.ink stage and give it a 1 px border of C.white at 8% alpha. Above it, place an SVG rect of the same size and radius with pathLength=1, a 1-2 px stroke of C.accent or C.white, strokeDasharray '0.12 0.88' and strokeDashoffset driven by the frame, so a 120 px segment runs along the top edge or around the whole perimeter. For the whole UI act, breathe the static rim's opacity between 0.6 and 0.8 on sin(2π·frame/180). For a brand that supplies glow, add soft box-shadow halos in a different colour on each of three sides.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Drop the coloured halos entirely. Use one 1 px single-colour border highlight sweeping along the edge, plus a neutral low-opacity drop shadow (0 24px 48px of C.ink at 50%) for lift. The full look relies on glow, gradient, orange; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** The streak crosses one edge in 20-30 f on E.linear. The rim breathes ±20% over 180 f and stays on for the whole UI act.
- **Use when:** Flat dark UI cards floating on pure black that need depth and separation without tilting or shadows.
- **Avoid when:** Light-mode UI (use a soft neutral shadow instead), or several cards on screen at once (the streaks compete).

### Rising colour wash carrier

`cl-rising-wash-carrier` · accent · energy medium · launch, feature, sting, vertical

A soft single-hue field rises from the bottom edge behind the type, swells and sweeps up across the frame on the change, then recedes off the top, so the foreground swap reads as one move.

- **Build:** Place a full-frame layer under the type with background radial-gradient(ellipse 70% 60% at 50% Y, C.accent 0%, transparent 70%). The gradient is soft on its own, so use no blur filter, keep normal blend and keep the saturation low. Animate Y from 110% to 75% on E.out (coverage 0 to 47%). Then swell the ellipse from 70% to 110% and wipe it up (centroid from about 487 to 154 px at 1080p) on E.inOut, changing the foreground underneath on the fastest frame, and finally let it recede to Y -20% on E.outSoft. Short version into a hard cut: a bottom-anchored band of 40% height, linear-gradient(to top, mixColor(C.accent, C.ink, 0.5), transparent), translateY from 100% to 20% on E.in, with the cut landing mid-rise. Use it to preview the accent ground that is coming.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Keep the move and lose the soft falloff: a flat accent band with a crisp, straight top edge (a clip-path inset driven by the same Y curve) rises behind the type, sweeps up across the frame on the change and leaves off the top, at full opacity in a light tint of the accent. The swap still happens on its fastest frame; no radial gradient, no feathered edge. The full look relies on glow; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** The rise takes 39 f on E.out. The swell and wipe take 12 f on E.inOut (about 28 px/f). The recede takes 90 f on E.outSoft. The pre-cut band takes 16 f on E.in (about +14 luma levels).
- **Use when:** Changing cards behind continuous colour, leading into an accent-ground claim or the end card, or smoothing a hard cut into a new scene.
- **Avoid when:** Shots already on an accent ground, or dense UI that the wash would tint. A soft accent haze behind type reads as glow.

### Shadows tinted by the stage

`cl-hue-tinted-shadow` · accent · energy calm · feature, walkthrough, launch

On a tinted light stage, lifted cards and solid pills cast soft shadows in a dark step of the stage's own hue instead of grey, so depth reads as part of the world's colour rather than dirt on it.

- **Build:** Derive one shadow colour from the stage, never from the accent: SH = mixColor(stageHue, C.ink, 0.6), where stageHue is the act's tint (for example, the pale-tint act of cl-context-palette-shift). Give each lifted card two shadows: a contact shadow, 0 2px 6px of C.ink at 0.10, and an ambient shadow, 0 24px 56px -16px of SH at 0.22 (convert mixColor's rgb() output to rgba). Under a solid black pill or icon tile, use a single tinted ellipse instead. Make it 80% of the element's width and 30% of its height, offset downward by 40% of its height, filled with radial-gradient(SH at 0.35, transparent 70%) and blur(32px), on multiply, below the element. Tie the shadow to lift: with lift = scale - 1 (or translateZ / 200), multiply offset and blur by 1 + 3 x lift and alpha by 1 / (1 + 3 x lift), so a rising card's shadow spreads and fades. Because SH reads from the act's tokens, a palette switch retints every shadow on the same frame. In its richer form, the look puts blurred blobs of two pastel hues beside a black pill and coloured halos on three sides of cards floating on black.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Use only one dark step of the stage's own hue, on light stages only, with shadows that fall downward and never spread past about half the element's size. On dark stages, drop the tint entirely and separate cards with cl-key-light-edge-hairline instead of a coloured halo. The full look relies on glow, gradient, orange, purple; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** Static while parked. On a lift (scale 1 to 1.04 over 20-26 f on E.out), the ambient blur goes from about 56 to 63 px and the alpha from 0.22 to 0.20 on the same curve. On seating, it returns on the seat move's own easing. A palette switch retints the shadows in 0 f, on the cut.
- **Use when:** Light-mode acts on pale tinted stages, pastel product worlds, and black pills or tiles floating on a tinted field where a grey shadow looks muddy.
- **Avoid when:** Dark stages, where a coloured shadow becomes a glow. Keep shadows neutral in neutral C.paper films, and skip the tint wherever it would echo the accent and spend its meaning.

### Tilt-linked sheen

`cl-tilt-linked-sheen` · accent · energy calm · launch, feature, sting

As a card or device tilts in 3D, a faint highlight band slides across its face in step with the angle, so the surface reads as a real material catching a key light.

- **Build:** Inside the tilted element, add an overlay above the content and below its 1 px border: linear-gradient(105deg, transparent 40%, C.white at 18% alpha 50%, transparent 60%) at background-size 300%, with screen blend on dark UI or soft-light on light UI. Compute background-position-x from the same rotation value that drives the transform (50% plus 2.5% per degree of rotateY, with rotateX nudging it vertically), so the highlight moves only while the object turns and parks when it settles. Multiply its opacity by clamp((|rotateY| - 2) / 6) so a flat card stays clean. Assume one key light 45° camera-left for the whole film, so every card catches it from the same side.
- **Timing:** It follows the tilt move: for example, rotateY going from 12° to 0 over 40 f on E.out moves the band about 30% and parks it. Peak overlay opacity is 0.18 on dark UI and 0.10 on light UI.
- **Use when:** Perspective UI tilt-ups, cards flipping or settling out of 3D, device turns, and logo tiles yawing.
- **Avoid when:** Flat 2D layouts with no rotation (use the one-shot specular sweep instead).

### Travelling tone band fill

`cl-tone-band-fill` · accent · energy medium · launch, sting, feature

A word, URL or logo mark fills through a band of colour (dark, then accent, then light) that sweeps across it and settles on the final ink.

- **Build:** Text: set background to linear-gradient(90deg, final ink 0 35%, light accent tint 50%, C.accent 65%, stage colour 80%) at background-size 300%, with background-clip: text and color: transparent, and animate background-position from 100% to 0%. For a domain plus path, delay the path span. For accent words in a tagline, step each letter from ink to C.accent with a 2 f stagger after the line lands. Mark: use the mark as an SVG mask over a tall gradient rect, reveal the fill bottom-up with clip-path from inset(100% 0 0 0) to inset(0), then translateY the rect by one gradient period so the tone scrolls and settles on solid accent, just before the colour floods the frame. The type itself stays still; only the fill travels.
- **Timing:** A word sweep takes 32 f on E.smooth (the front peaks at about 25 px/f). A URL takes 42 f, easing into the final ink on E.out, with the path lagging 8-12 f. A mark wipe takes 8 f on E.linear, then the tone scrolls for 36 f on E.smooth. Letters stagger 2 f.
- **Use when:** Hero words, the URL card, or a logo mark that should introduce the accent before it fills the frame.
- **Avoid when:** Small UI text, or type that is still moving (the band and the motion fight).

### Type solidity arc

`cl-type-solidity-arc` · accent · energy calm · launch, feature

The type gains body across the film. Early statements are translucent white that lets the coloured stage show through, and the closing line and lockup are solid, so the payoff reads as more certain than the promise.

- **Build:** Add a typeAlpha value to each act in timeline.ts, for example [0.65, 0.85, 1.0] for opening, middle and end, and read it through one helper so every caption in an act shares it. Apply it as the opacity of the C.white line container, not as per-glyph rgba, which darkens where glyphs overlap, so the stage colour shows through the letters. Keep weight, size and tracking identical across acts so that only confidence changes. Step the value only on cuts or act changes, never inside a line or a shot. cl-ink-resolve still handles each arrival; the arc only sets where that resolve ends. Keep translucent acts to display type (at least 64 px at 1080p) over stage areas darker than about luma 110, and check contrast on rendered stills (Stills.tsx). The end-card line and lockup are always solid C.white.
- **Timing:** Act values are 0.65, 0.85 and 1.0 (opening, middle, end), stepped in 0 f on cuts or act changes. Each arrival's ink resolve (12-16 f on E.out) lands at the act's value. The end-card line and lockup stay at 1.0 for their whole 90-120 f hold.
- **Use when:** Brand films and launches on a coloured or living stage, built as question to answer or promise to proof, where the closing line should feel firmer than the opening.
- **Avoid when:** Neutral black or grey stages, where translucent white just reads as dim grey. Also avoid it for small UI text, in films under about 10 s, and on light stages, where translucent ink loses contrast.

### Accent ground for claims only

`cl-accent-claim-grounds` · signature · energy medium · launch, feature, sting, vertical

Narrative shots sit on the neutral stage, other claims flip to the opposite neutral, and the single full-bleed accent ground is saved for the hero claim or the closing card, so colour works as punctuation.

- **Build:** Use two ground tokens (C.paper or C.ink, and C.accent) and one ink. Tag each shot 'story' or 'claim' in timeline.ts. The accent floods the frame once per film: give the full-bleed accent ground to the one hero claim (about 72 f) or to the closing card, and set every other claim on the opposite neutral stage (C.ink after C.paper, or the reverse) with the accent only on its one key word, so accent pixels stay near 8% across the film. Switch grounds on hard cuts; elsewhere the accent appears only as a one-word highlight or a soft single-hue wash that previews the flood. Let the accent ground arrive as a radial flood. Layer order: the accent ground; a disc of radius 640 px whose fill steps mixColor(C.accent, C.paper, 0.75), then 0.4, then 0; a 60 px ring of mixColor(C.accent, C.ink, 0.1) at r 600 px, which appears with the last step and stays for the shot to frame the hero word; then the type.
- **Timing:** Grounds swap on cut frames. The radial flood takes 6 f, with tint steps on f0, f2 and f4 decided with fd(). The ring stays from f4 to the end of the shot. Claim shots run 60-120 f each.
- **Use when:** Films with a few big statements that must feel louder than the walkthrough around them, and endings that need to feel conclusive.
- **Avoid when:** The accent fails contrast as a ground for display type, or the film has no distinct claims (a pure UI tour).

### Light swell bridge into the hero

`cl-light-swell-bridge` · signature · energy high · launch, sting

Light swells around a small panel until the frame is bright, the film cuts on the brightest frame to the hero card sitting in the same light, and that light slowly exhales back to dark.

- **Build:** Shot A: a radial gradient centred on the panel with four stops (stage, dark tint, mid, light tint), whose radii grow at 12-25 px/f on E.linear so mean frame luma climbs about 2.25 levels per frame (from 15 to about 78); cut on a downbeat at the peak. Shot B opens on the identical gradient with the hero title already in place, then pulls the stops back inward so luma falls from about 112 to 43, handing off to the next dark shot. Put the cut on an act boundary so it stays crisp.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Replace the soft multi-hue bloom with four hard-edged concentric discs in tonal steps of one hue (the stage, then 15%, 35% and 60% lightness toward the accent), their radii expanding with a 2 f stagger on normal blend. Keep the same swell, cut and exhale timing. The full look relies on glow, gradient; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** The swell takes 28 f on E.linear. Cut at the peak, on a downbeat. The exhale takes 86 f on E.smooth (a fade-out never runs on an expo-out).
- **Use when:** Releasing a dark section into the hero card or title: the biggest reveal in a dark film.
- **Avoid when:** Light-mode films, or a second time in the same film.

### Rolling band flood

`cl-rolling-band-flood` · signature · energy medium · launch, feature

A light frame fills with the brand colour as soft horizontal bands of it roll upward and grow opaque. The text tints and dissolves into it, and the film arrives on its end-card field without a cut.

- **Build:** Over the last product frame, add a full-frame overlay holding a strip three frames tall: a linear-gradient(to bottom) that repeats six soft tonal bands of one hue (mixColor(C.accent, C.paper, 0.7), then 0.45, then 0.2, then C.accent, then back up). Make each band about half the frame height, with its stops blending over about 10% of the band. Drive the strip's translateY from 0 to -1 frame height on E.linear, so the bands roll up at constant speed. Drive its opacity with p * p, where p = prog(f, a, a + 60, E.linear), so the colour arrives late and decisively (quarter strength at the halfway point). Mix the foreground text to mixColor(C.accent, C.ink, 0.4) over the first 12 f, then fade it from 1 to 0 over f12-f40 on E.smooth, so the colour absorbs it rather than covering it. End on the end-card field, with the same bands slowing to a 0.3 px/f drift, and let the lockup appear on it afterwards. Bake the strip once with scripts/dither-gradient.py (space oklab) so the soft bands do not contour. In full colour, the flood runs through several hues.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Build the bands only from tonal steps of one non-banned hue (light tint, mid tint, the accent), not a lavender-pink-peach-orange spectrum. Keep the roll, the p^2 opacity ramp and the text absorption. The full look relies on gradient, orange, purple; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** 60 f in total. The bands roll one frame height on E.linear (about 18 px/f at 1080p), and the opacity follows p^2 over the same 60 f. The text tints over 12 f and fades over f12-f40 on E.smooth. Frame mean luma goes from about 250 to 215: a light-to-mid flood, not a polarity flip. The bands then ease to a 0.3 px/f drift for the end card's 90-120 f.
- **Use when:** Closing a light product act into the end card, or returning to the brand world after the last UI beat (a success state, a published page) without a hard cut.
- **Avoid when:** Dark films, where the flood reads as fog over black. Also avoid it a second time in the same film, and before an end card whose ground is not the flood's hue.

### Single inversion card

`cl-inversion-card` · signature · energy medium · launch, feature

In an otherwise dark film, one card cuts to a near-white field with dark type for one second, marking the key promise.

- **Build:** At about 40% of runtime, inside a gap in the music, hard-cut to an AbsoluteFill of cream C.paper whose edges carry a soft ring of colour, fading from white at 55% of the radius through two accent hues to the frame edge. Set the line in C.ink and rise it out of a line mask: overflow hidden, translateY from 100% to 0 through arrive(), on E.out. Let the ring breathe, with its scale moving between 1.00 and 1.02 on sin(2π·frame/120). Frame mean luma jumps from about 9 to about 232, so this must be the film's only light frame; cut out hard on the next beat.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Keep a neutral C.paper field, never a cream one. Draw the ring as a single hard-edged accent stroke (a 6-10 px ellipse at 88% of the frame) that breathes in scale, with no soft colour falloff and no second hue. The full look relies on gradient, beige; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** Hold for 60 f. The type rises over 18 f on E.out, starting on f4. The ring breathes with a period of 120 f, ±2%. Place it at about 40% of runtime.
- **Use when:** A dark film's single most important promise needs to stop the viewer halfway through.
- **Avoid when:** Light-mode films, films that already alternate dark and light, or when the music has no gap to place it in.

### Theme flip mid-move

`cl-theme-flip-in-motion` · signature · energy high · feature, launch, walkthrough

In the middle of a camera fly-over, the dark page and stage flash to their light versions, top first, and the motion never pauses.

- **Build:** Render dark and light versions of the same page as two identical layers on the same moving plane, inside one world container driven by src/lib/camera.ts so they share every transform. Reveal the light layer through mask-image: linear-gradient(to bottom, black X%, transparent X+30%), with X running from -30% to 100%, so the top bands lead by about 2 f. On the same span, swap the stage from the C.ink grid to the C.paper studio. Keep the camera at cruise speed through the flip: it shows theme support and doubles as the film's dark-to-light act change.
- **Timing:** 6 f in total, with the mask edge on E.linear (frame luma goes about 40, 140, 205, 235). The top leads by 2 f. Leave the camera's own easing untouched.
- **Use when:** Products with dark and light modes, or as the single dark-to-light act transition of a film.
- **Avoid when:** The camera is static (the flip turns into a plain crossfade), or the light version would not match the dark one pixel for pixel.

## Texture and finish

Texture and finish decide whether a film built from code reads as photographed or as a slideshow, and almost all of it works at the edge of perception: grain at a sigma of 1-2 code levels (a 1.5-2% layer), dot fields about 4% off their ground, photo plates graded to 5-8% mean luma, gobo shadows drifting under 0.5 px/f. Speed is finished in the render, not faked per layer: anything over 12 px/f gets the 240-degree float-accumulated blur pass, holds sit under 2 px/f so they render pin-sharp, and no element passes about 70-80 px/f. Every soft ramp ships as a dithered PNG, because a CSS gradient spanning fewer than about 30 code values bands, and every texture that animates is keyed to fd(frame) so the motion-blur sub-samples agree. Each texture must name its job (context, material, concealment, a hit) and keep one strength for the whole film. One signature surface move (a 34 f scanline transmutation, a ring field, a locked mosaic) is plenty for a film.

### Feathered edge mask

`tx-feathered-edge-mask` · workhorse · energy any · walkthrough, feature, loop, vertical

Lists, reels and overflowing lines dissolve into the stage at a soft edge instead of being cut by a hard crop, so content feels endless and the eye stays in the clear middle.

- **Build:** Put the moving content inside a fixed container with `maskImage` (and `WebkitMaskImage`) set to `linear-gradient(to bottom, transparent 0%, #000 14%, #000 86%, transparent 100%)`, so rows enter and leave by fading into the stage; move the content inside by transform only, with inertia() for a flicked reel or E.glide for single steps. For a typed line that must follow its caret, use a left feather `linear-gradient(to right, transparent 0, #000 140px)` on the line's box and slide the text left by exactly its overflow each frame. Size the feather at 10-15% of the container (120-160 px at 1080p): shorter reads as a crop, longer greys out readable rows.
- **Timing:** Feather 10-15% of the container; list steps 26-40 f on E.glide, or inertia(f, s, 30-60, 0.89) for a proof reel; text under the mask at most 20 px/f while it must read; the mask itself never moves.
- **Use when:** Endless-feeling lists, proof reels, logs, chats, card stacks, and type that overflows its line as it is typed.
- **Avoid when:** Content that must be read right at the container edge; a hard-cropped bento look; as a full-frame vignette (that is lighting, not a mask).

### Fog floor

`tx-fog-floor` · workhorse · energy calm · launch, feature, walkthrough

The bottom fifth of the frame lightens toward the stage's brightest tone, as if the UI hovers above a softly lit floor that receding planes can sink into.

- **Build:** Bake a full-frame RGBA PNG with scripts/dither-gradient.py: linear, angle 0 (bottom to top), stops [floor tone at 0, floor tone at alpha 0.6 at 0.12, transparent at 0.22], where the floor tone is a near-white just above the stage in the same hue (OKLCH L about 0.98). Layer it above the background and below the UI. When a panel tilts back into depth (perspective 2000-2400 px, transformOrigin at its bottom edge, rotateX 0 to 60 degrees over 30-40 f on E.in), render a second copy of the fog above that panel so it dissolves into the floor, and take the panel's opacity to 0 on E.in over the last 12 f. On an ink stage the floor tone is C.ink raised OKLCH 0.04.
- **Timing:** The floor band is 22% of frame height and fixed to the stage; tilt-backs 30-40 f on E.in with the fade over their last 12 f.
- **Use when:** Light or pastel stages with 3D tilt-backs, lifts and recedes; any film that wants a horizon without drawing a floor.
- **Avoid when:** Flat, front-on UI with no depth moves; dark stages that already have a light pool; vertical frames where captions sit in the bottom fifth.

### Global frame-keyed grain

`tx-global-grain` · workhorse · energy any · any

A fine, even grain sits over the whole film at one strength, breaking banding in soft ramps and blurred plates and giving flat colour fields a tactile surface.

- **Build:** Bake 8 seeded noise tiles offline (512x512 PNG, numpy gaussian noise with sigma about 90 levels, centred on the stage's own luma so the stage is not lifted); never Math.random or an animated feTurbulence. Add one full-frame top layer: a div with the tile as backgroundImage, normal blend at opacity 0.015-0.02, tile index Math.floor(fd(frame) / 2) % 8, and backgroundPosition offset by Math.floor(rand(index) x 512) px in x and y so the repeat never shows. Keep the same strength from the first frame to the last (never per scene), verify on a flat mid-grey crop (sigma about 1.5-2 code levels) and confirm forensics.py reports no smear. Grain does not replace baked dither: soft gradients still ship as dithered PNGs from scripts/dither-gradient.py.
- **Timing:** New tile every 2 f; constant strength (sigma ~1-2.3 code levels) for the whole film; no fades and no per-scene changes.
- **Use when:** Films with large flat or saturated colour fields, soft lighting ramps, blurred photo plates, or a tactile, filmic brand.
- **Avoid when:** Crisp, clinical UI films where any texture reads as dirt; when the strength would have to change between scenes; as a fix for banding that dithered PNGs should solve.

### Gobo-lit studio backdrop

`tx-gobo-studio-shadows` · workhorse · energy calm · launch, feature, walkthrough

The UI floats over an off-white studio backdrop crossed by huge, very soft diagonal shadows, like window light through leaves, so flat screens feel photographed.

- **Build:** Stage C.paper (a cool off-white around #F7F7F7). Bake 3-5 shadow bands as RGBA PNGs at 120% of frame size with scripts/dither-gradient.py: linear gradients at 30-40 degrees, each going transparent to rgba(0,0,0,0.05-0.08) to transparent across 10-18% of the gradient line (the look of grey shapes blurred 100-150 px at 8-15% opacity, without the banding). Layer them above the stage and below the cards, and drift each along its own axis by A x sin(2 pi f / P + phi) with A = 40-80 px and P = 600-900 f, which keeps them under 0.5 px/f. Cards get `0 30px 60px rgba(0,0,0,.12)` and a 1 px C.line border.
- **Timing:** Band drift under 0.5 px/f on sines with 600-900 f periods and spread phases; present in every light shot of the act, unchanged between shots.
- **Use when:** Light-stage product films and walkthroughs that need depth and physicality without glass, colour or a 3D set.
- **Avoid when:** Dark stages; dense UI that fills the frame edge to edge; strictly flat graphic brands.

### Hairline edge and key shadow

`tx-surface-edge-finish` · workhorse · energy any · any

Every floating surface gets a 1 px edge plus one soft key shadow on paper, or a top inner highlight on ink, so flat UI reads as a physical object in a lit space.

- **Build:** On paper: `boxShadow: '0 30px 60px rgba(0,0,0,.12)'` with a 1 px C.line border, optionally over a tight `0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,.06)` contact shadow. On ink: no shadow, a C.ink2 fill (a luminance step from C.ink), a 1 px border at C.ink plus about OKLCH 0.06 lightness, and `inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.08)` as the top highlight. Tie the finish to motion: when a card lifts (z 0 to 120 px) grow its shadow with the lift formulas (offset 0.1z, 0.22z; blur 3 + 0.06z; alpha 0.2 - 0.1 x min(1, z / 200)), and when a panel tilts toward camera raise the inset highlight from 0.08 to 0.12 with |tilt| / 15 degrees, so the edge catches light as it moves.
- **Timing:** Static finish; shadow and highlight follow the element's z and tilt every frame (lift 14 f on E.out, drop 10 f on E.in); highlight alpha changes by at most 0.04 over a tilt.
- **Use when:** Any floating card, panel, modal or window, in every format.
- **Avoid when:** Flush full-bleed UI or gutterless grids whose cells should merge into one canvas; anything tempting a glass panel or a coloured halo instead.

### Low-luma photo plate

`tx-low-luma-photo-plate` · workhorse · energy calm · launch, feature, walkthrough

A real photograph sits behind the UI or type, graded almost to black or thrown out of focus, adding context and tonal texture without stealing contrast from the copy.

- **Build:** A full-bleed <Img> overscanned 6% sits under everything, in one of two settings: (a) a sharp texture plate behind statements, `filter: grayscale(1) brightness(0.25) contrast(1.15)` tuned until its mean luma is 5-8%; (b) a defocused context plate behind a moving panel, pre-blurred offline at a 40 px radius (PIL GaussianBlur saved as PNG, so the browser never animates a blur; use src/fx/RackFocus.tsx if focus must change) with `brightness(0.6) saturate(0.4)`, translated at 0.3x the panel's or camera's translation for parallax. Keep plate hues neutral or cool, run the film's global grain over it so the dark ramps do not band, and separate the panel on top with a luminance step (C.ink2) and `inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.08)`. Plates may hard-cut on beats under a locked foreground whose pill or headline stays pixel-identical across the cut.
- **Timing:** A plate holds its shot (90-420 f) with 0.3x parallax or a 0.5-1.5 px/f drift; montage cuts under a locked foreground every 15-30 f on beats; never a fade on the plate.
- **Use when:** Dark-stage films that need real-world context (a desk, a city, a workspace) or a material, crafted feel behind sparse type or a floating panel.
- **Avoid when:** Light stages; a busy photo that stays above ~12% mean luma and fights the type; stock imagery unrelated to the product's world; decorative bokeh that names no job.

### Micro-tick UI sound

`tx-micro-tick-ui-sound` · workhorse · energy any · any

(Sound) Typing and UI changes get tiny, dry ticks at or under the music, and once the drums run the UI goes silent, so the picture feels tactile without a loud keyboard sample.

- **Build:** In src/sync.ts emit `key` events from the same CHAR_AT array the picture types with (variant 'word' on word starts) and `tick` or `click` events on UI appearances, at weight 0.2-0.35 (12-18 dB under the landing hit), and set "typing": "soft" in score.json ("muted" over a denser section). Emit none of them in sections whose drums are "groove" or "drive": there the hats carry the typing. When typing is fast, place one tick per word as it becomes legible rather than one per letter, and let a run of UI ticks climb about 1 dB per event into a payoff. Read score.py's typing block: 15-20 dB A under a full bed and never brighter than the music above 2 kHz.
- **Timing:** Ticks 2-6 ms long, at least 60 ms (3.6 f) apart, sigma 3.5 ms timing jitter and +-1 dB gain jitter; peaks -23 to -36 dBFS, at or under the bed's RMS; zero UI sounds once the drums enter.
- **Use when:** Typed prompts, word-by-word builds, cold opens before the beat drops, any UI moment that wants touch without an effect announcing itself.
- **Avoid when:** Under voiceover syllables; inside a dense drum section; loud keyboard samples; a film whose idea is silent UI over a beat bed throughout.

### One grade across mixed media

`tx-mixed-media-grade` · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature, loop

Desaturated photography, matte grey 3D, flat vector maps and line diagrams cut freely against each other without clashing, because every medium shares one dark value range and only the hero prop carries the accent.

- **Build:** Normalise each medium before it enters a shot: photos get `filter: grayscale(1) brightness(0.65) contrast(1.05)`; 3D or clay renders use matte grey materials (base around 40% grey, no coloured speculars) with C.accent on the hero prop only; vector maps fill land at C.ink plus OKLCH 0.03-0.04 lightness with 1.5 px borders at 15-25% white; line diagrams draw in white at 60-80% with the accent on the one active path. Check that every medium's mean luma lands within 8-25% and that nothing except the accent exceeds OKLCH chroma 0.03, then hard-cut or swap media inside a shot or grid cell on beats. The accent keeps the same single meaning in every medium.
- **Timing:** Swap media inside a shot or cell every 48-90 f, on beats; hard cuts between media need no transition because the value range already matches.
- **Use when:** Films that must combine photos, renders, maps, diagrams and UI, especially grid or bento layouts with several media on screen at once.
- **Avoid when:** Light, pastel or colourful brands; single-medium films; hero product photography that must keep its true colour.

### Speed-gated motion blur

`tx-speed-gated-motion-blur` · workhorse · energy any · any

Fast whips, flings and flicked scrolls streak like a real shutter while holds and slow drifts stay pin-sharp, so the eye rests on the readable frames.

- **Build:** Never fake speed blur per layer in the browser (CameraMotionBlur and an animated filter: blur() quantise to 8 bits and step); design the moves and let the master's render pass make the blur: `bash scripts/render.sh Film out/film.mp4 --blur` renders a 240-degree shutter centred on each frame, takes samples from measured speed (1 under 2 px/f, 4 up to 18 px/f, 14 at 60, 18 at 80) and averages them in float. Shape every fast move so its peak sits between 12 and 70 px/f (E.whip or E.inOut, or inertia() for a flicked scroll) and both ends fall under 2 px/f, so the streak exists only mid-move. Put every hard cut on an act boundary so samples never smear across it, and drive typed text, counters, carets and grain from fd(frame) so all sub-samples of a frame agree.
