Where optical flow cannot see the speed (a flat band wiping the whole frame) pass `--floor A-B:px` or analytic speed; in HyperFrames render at 4x fps and run `accumulate.py --uniform 4`, which is clean only to about 12-18 px/f.
- **Timing:** Whip 12-20 f on E.whip with a 40-70 px/f peak, the shots either side at 0.3-1.5 px/f; streak length is about 2/3 of the per-frame travel (a 60 px/f card smears ~40 px); a flick is inertia(f, start, 50-70, 0.89), coasting ~8.6 x v0 px and under 0.5 px/f after its `settle` frames; nothing above 80 px/f.
- **Use when:** Any film with whips, flings, drops or flicked scrolls; walkthroughs that travel fast between setups and need every hold razor-sharp.
- **Avoid when:** Moves that would need more than 80 px/f (redesign as a cut on the beat, a match cut or a mask wipe); readable text moving above 20 px/f; a deliberately stepped on-twos section.

### Brushed micro-streaks

`tx-brushed-micro-streaks` · accent · energy calm · launch, feature, sting

Fine directional streaks and a satin grain across a hero object's face make it read as machined material instead of flat vector.

- **Build:** Bake a brushed texture PNG offline at 2x the hero's on-screen size: seeded noise stretched along one axis (numpy noise, then a 1-D box blur 60-200 px long, normalised to sigma about 6 levels around mid-grey) so streaks are 1-2 px wide. Apply it as a child of the object inside its transform, masked to the face (`maskImage` of the face shape), blend overlay at opacity 0.06-0.10; a CSS `repeating-linear-gradient(90deg, rgba(255,255,255,.04) 0 1px, transparent 1px 3px)` is the quick version for a face that never scales down. As the object turns, slide the texture's backgroundPosition along the streak axis in proportion to its rotation so the satin seems to catch the light.
- **Timing:** Constant while the object is at hero scale (at least 30% of frame height); fade it out over 10-14 f on E.smooth before the object shrinks below that.
- **Use when:** Hero objects shown big enough for micro detail (coins, cards, devices, extruded marks); hardware and finance brands with a physical metaphor.
- **Avoid when:** Small or minified objects, where 1 px streaks alias and crawl; soft, friendly brands; flat UI.

### Faint dot-matrix silhouette

`tx-dot-matrix-silhouette` · accent · energy calm · launch, feature, vertical

Behind a claim, a barely visible field of dots forms a meaningful silhouette (a world map, a region, the product's own shape), adding literal context without competing with the type.

- **Build:** Precompute dot centres on a 20 px grid at 1080p, keeping only those inside a silhouette bitmap (a land mask, a region outline, the mark), and render them as one SVG of 13 px circles (or bake it to PNG). Fill the dots with the ground colour shifted about 4% in lightness, same hue (OKLCH 0.03-0.04: lighter on dark grounds, darker on light ones), and place the layer under the type. Keep it alive with a scale of lmix(1.00, 1.02, prog(f, s, e, E.linear)) across the shot or a translate under 1 px/f, and let it leave with the shot's cut rather than fading.
- **Timing:** Holds one shot of 80-100 f; scale 1.00 to 1.02 linear across it (well under 1 px/f); arrives and leaves on cuts, no fades.
- **Use when:** Claims about reach, coverage, location or scale, and any shot where a silhouette adds literal meaning behind the copy.
- **Avoid when:** Generic decoration with no meaning; contrast above ~6%, where it starts competing with the copy; small vertical frames where 13 px dots read as noise (scale the pitch up instead).

### Glyph-grid shock pulse

`tx-glyph-grid-pulse` · accent · energy high · launch, sting

On the film's biggest hit, the dark background flashes a grid of tiny monoline marks that bend outward from the impact like a shockwave, then settles back to a quiet grained field.

- **Build:** One SVG or canvas layer over the stage holds a grid of 36 px cells at 1080p, each with a 10 px monoline mark picked by rand(cellIndex) from plus, L, T and slash, stroked 1.5 px in white. With t = f - hit and pulse = hitPulse(t, 4, 3), each mark at distance d from the impact point gets opacity 0.6 x (1 - d / R) x pulse and a radial offset of 30 x pulse x (1 - d / R) px outward (R about 900 px), so the grid bulges like a tunnel and dies away. Play it once, on the payoff or the lockup's landing, with the hit sound on the hit frame.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Keep it strictly grid-locked so it reads as structure, not a burst: plus marks only, every cell on the grid with no scatter or random drift, opacity capped at 0.35, a single displacement ring, monochrome, and no streaks of light. The full look relies on particles; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** About 12-14 f visible, peaking 4 f after the hit (hitPulse(t, 4, 3)); 30 px radial push at peak; once per film.
- **Use when:** A digital or developer brand's payoff hit or lockup landing that needs a shockwave without colour or glow.
- **Avoid when:** Calm films; more than once per film; light stages; behind type that is still arriving.

### Halftone shading

`tx-halftone-shading` · accent · energy calm · launch, sting, feature

A flat hero shape gains volume from a single-colour halftone dot field whose dots swell in the shadow side and shrink toward a slowly moving light.

- **Build:** Over the shape, lay an SVG grid of circles on a 12 px pitch, clipped to the shape (clipPath), in C.ink on paper or C.white on ink. Each dot's radius is 5.5 x E.smooth(clamp(dist(L, dot) / R)) px, with L a light point and R about 0.8 x the shape's diagonal; drop dots under 0.8 px radius so nothing aliases. Move L along a slow arc at under 0.5 px/f so the shading breathes, and reveal the field as a diagonal wave in which each dot grows from 0 to its radius over 12 f on E.out, offset by stagger(i, n, 24) with i ordered by x + y.
- **Timing:** Reveal 36 f (a 24 f diagonal stagger plus 12 f per dot on E.out); light point drift under 0.5 px/f; holds as long as the shape stays the hero.
- **Use when:** Flat marks, icons or objects that need volume without 3D; technical or print-minded brands; alongside other dot-matrix devices.
- **Avoid when:** Shapes under ~200 px, where the dots turn to mush; photographic or 3D scenes; busy UI behind the shape.

### Stepped cadence on twos

`tx-on-twos-cadence` · accent · energy medium · sting, feature, walkthrough

One designated layer or section updates only on every second frame, so its motion reads crisp, precise and slightly mechanical against an otherwise smooth 60 fps film.

- **Build:** Inside the chosen layer compute `const f2 = 2 * Math.floor(fd(frame) / 2)` and pass f2 instead of frame to every prog, tw, spr and hitPulse call it makes (or use interpolate(..., { posterize: 2 }) for a single value), so every motion-blur sub-sample of a frame agrees and each held pair renders sharp. Because a held frame cannot carry blur, keep every stepped element under 24 px per step (12 px/f average) and type under 20 px per step; leave the camera, backgrounds and grain on the native frame. Apply it to a whole act (a UI-precision section, a sting) or to the type layer only, never switching on and off inside a shot.
- **Timing:** Steps every 2 f (30 Hz in a 60 fps file); moves of 60-150 px over 24-40 f on E.glide or SPR.firm evaluated at f2, peaking at or under 24 px per step; at least one full shot or act long.
- **Use when:** Mechanical, developer or precision brands; a UI section that should feel like a live screen; a short sting that wants a punchy graphic cadence.
- **Avoid when:** Slow drifts and camera pushes (they judder); moves that would exceed 24 px per step; a few isolated shots in a smooth film, where it reads as dropped frames.

### Stepped mosaic resolve

`tx-mosaic-resolve` · accent · energy medium · feature, launch, sting

An image or screen arrives as coarse grey blocks that halve in size every two frames until the real picture snaps in, sharp and in full colour.

- **Build:** Render the target's final look as a still (`npx remotion still` for a live component, or the image itself) and pre-bake downsampled copies at 48, 24, 12, 6 and 3 px blocks (PIL resize with BOX), shown upscaled with `imageRendering: 'pixelated'`. From cue c, pick the copy by Math.floor((fd(frame) - c) / 2) so each size holds 2 f, and hand over to the live component on the frame the block would reach 1 px; run `filter: saturate()` from 0 to 1 and brightness from 0.7 to 1 across the same 12 f on E.smooth. The stepping is discrete state read from fd, so it stays crisp under the blur pass.
- **Timing:** 48, 24, 12, 6, 3, then 1 px over 10-12 f (2 f per size); saturation and brightness over 12 f on E.smooth; an optional 4-6 f hold at 48 px so the resolve starts on a beat.
- **Use when:** Revealing an image, avatar, map or screen in a digital or tech brand; the resolve after a locked state; a beat-synced reveal.
- **Avoid when:** Text-heavy screens (half-resolved text looks broken); calm, quiet brands; more than twice per film.

### Stipple only in lit ramps

`tx-ramp-masked-stipple` · accent · energy calm · launch, feature, loop

A visible dithered stipple lives only inside lit edges and light falloffs, while the flat stage around them stays perfectly clean.

- **Build:** Bake each lit ramp (a lit edge on a shape, a light pool, a floor falloff) as an RGBA PNG with scripts/dither-gradient.py, then give the element that carries it a child layer of a static seeded noise tile (sigma about 64 levels around mid-grey) masked by that same PNG (`maskImage: url(fx/rim.png)`, `maskSize: '100% 100%'`), blend overlay at opacity 0.08-0.12. The noise sits inside the ramp's own transform so it travels with the light instead of swimming through it, and wherever the ramp's alpha is 0 the stage gets no texture at all. Check it with the x12 stretch from `dither-gradient.py --preview`: stipple inside the ramp, none on the stage.
- **Timing:** Static texture that moves rigidly with its ramp; high-pass sigma about 1.9 code levels in the brightest ramps, 0.5-0.9 in faint falloffs, 0.0 on the flat stage.
- **Use when:** Dark films with lit edges, light pools or soft falloffs that risk banding, where a global grain would dirty a deliberately clean stage.
- **Avoid when:** Films already running global grain (double texture); light stages; hard-edged flat design with no ramps.

### Intersecting ring field

`tx-ring-field` · signature · energy medium · launch, loop, sting

Above and below a centred band of type, families of huge overlapping ellipse outlines rotate slowly in opposite directions and whip on every copy swap, giving the words an ownable abstract environment.

- **Build:** One full-frame SVG holds two groups of 6-8 ellipses (rx about 47% of frame width, ry about 32% of frame height, centred just above and just below the text band), each a crisp 2 px stroke in one hue whose opacity steps from 0.6 on the outer ring to 0.15 nearest the band. Rotate the groups in opposite directions, angle = +-(0.2 x f + 14 x the sum over swap cues s_k of prog(f, s_k, s_k + 12, E.smooth)), so each copy swap adds a 14-degree whip, and swap the text hard on each whip's peak frame (s_k + 6) so the motion masks the change. The text stays static at the band's centre; the rings' fastest edges (~50 px/f at the whip peak) get the blur pass.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Drop the soft-lit two-hue gradient strokes, the inner blur and the screen blend: every ring is a crisp 2 px stroke in one neutral (white at 15-60% on ink), normal blend, with depth carried by per-ring opacity alone. Keep the rings out of the accent so the accent keeps its one meaning. The full look relies on glow, gradient; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** Drift 0.2 degrees/f between swaps; whip +12-16 degrees over 12 f on E.smooth (peak ~3 degrees/f, ~50 px/f at the outer rim); copy swaps every 60-120 f on the whip's peak frame.
- **Use when:** Type-led launch cards or a statement sequence on a dark stage that needs a signature environment and a motivated way to change copy without cuts.
- **Avoid when:** UI demos, where it competes with the product; light stages, where 2 px rings vanish; more than ~4 s of pure ambience.

### Locked-state mosaic

`tx-locked-mosaic` · signature · energy medium · launch, feature

Withheld content shows as pixelated, desaturated, darkened art with a lock glyph and thin light lines sliding across it, until an unlock snaps it to clean full-tone art.

- **Build:** Pre-render each card's art at 1/40 of its width (blocks about 2.5% of the card width), show it upscaled with `imageRendering: 'pixelated'` and `filter: saturate(0) brightness(0.3)`, and over it 2-3 slightly curved strokes (1.5-2 px, white at 30%) translating linearly along the card at 2-4 px/f, clipped to the card, with a 32-40 px line lock glyph at centre and no caption. Unlock: the strokes brighten to 60% over the 12 f before it, then the art dips from brightness 0.3 to 0.18 over 4 f on E.smooth while the shackle rotates open on SPR.firm; on the next frame swap to the full-resolution art at brightness 1.12 easing to 1.0 over 10 f on E.out, and fade glyph and strokes over 10 f on E.smooth. In a run of cards make each later unlock about 25% faster.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Replace the soft, screen-blended gaussian light ribbons with crisp 1.5-2 px strokes at 30-60% white, and keep the unlock's brightness overshoot inside the card: no burst or rays past its edge. The full look relies on glow; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** Locked state 54-108 f (the strokes keep moving, so nothing is static); unlock = 12 f brighten, 4 f dip, swap, 10 f settle; repeated unlocks 30-45 f apart, each ~25% quicker.
- **Use when:** Premium, gated or upcoming features; a reveal sequence where concealment builds desire; access or unlock stories.
- **Avoid when:** Products with nothing gated; text content (pixelated text reads as broken); more than one reveal device in the same act.

### Scanline transmutation

`tx-scanline-transmute` · signature · energy medium · launch, feature, sting

A bright bar sweeps down a hero object: above the bar the object has already become its digital form, a dot-matrix disc with a crisp rim, while below it the original solid object remains.

- **Build:** Stack two copies of the object in one container: the solid version and a dot-matrix version (an SVG <pattern> of 5 px-radius circles on a 16 px pitch, clipped to the object's outline, plus a 2 px rim stroke). Drive one value y (percent of the object's height) and clip the dot layer with `clipPath: inset(0 0 ${100 - y}% 0)` and the solid layer with `inset(${y}% 0 0 0)`; draw the bar as a hard-edged rect centred on y, 3-4% of the frame height thick, clipped to the object's column so it enters already moving from 8% above the object. Chain three segments: -8% to 45% over f0-11 on E.linear, 45% to 50% over f11-17 on E.linear (a near-hold that catches on the object's symbol), 50% to 100% over f17-34 on E.glide; the fast segments run 20-40 px/f and get the blur pass. Put a whoosh apex on the third segment's velocity peak and a snap on f34.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Keep the sweep but drop the bloom and the tint: a flat, hard-edged bar 12-24 px thick in white or the accent (or a 2 px hairline with a 10% tint band 40 px behind it), dots in white or the accent, never violet, and nothing lit outside the object's outline. The full look relies on glow, purple; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** 34 f in all: 11 f fast (20-30 px/f at 1080p), a 6 f near-hold at ~4-6 px/f on the symbol, 17 f on E.glide to rest; bar 36-40 px; the transformed object then holds 24-40 f with a drift under 1 px/f.
- **Use when:** One hero transformation per film: an object becoming its private, digital, encrypted or connected form; the moment the concept turns.
- **Avoid when:** More than once per film; ordinary UI state changes; objects under ~25% of frame height, where the dot pitch cannot read.

### Wireframe-to-product scan

`tx-wireframe-scan-build` · signature · energy medium · launch, feature

A thin accent line sweeps across a UI card: ahead of it the card is still a wireframe of outlines and skeleton bars, behind it the finished product is already there.

- **Build:** Render the component twice in one container: the real UI, and a wire version of the same component (backgrounds transparent, every box a 1.5 px C.line outline, text replaced by rounded bars at the measured text width and 40% opacity, icons as outlined circles). Drive x from -4% to 100% of the card width with prog(f, s, s + 44, E.smooth) and, clamped to 0-100, clip the real layer with `inset(0 ${100 - x}% 0 0)` and the wire layer with `inset(0 0 0 ${x}%)`, and draw a 2 px C.accent line at x reaching 24 px past the card's top and bottom, with no glow. Add a soft swell event across the sweep and a snap as the line leaves the card, then fade the line over 10 f on E.smooth.
- **Timing:** Sweep 40-48 f on E.smooth across a 600-900 px card (edge peak ~40-58 px/f; the UI itself never moves); line fade 10 f; the finished card then holds at least 30 f under a 0.5-1.5 px/f camera drift.
- **Use when:** Idea-to-product, design-to-code, generation or build stories; the first appearance of the hero UI.
- **Avoid when:** More than once per film; UI too sparse to read as a wireframe; a film that already uses another scan device such as scanline transmutation.

## Layout and composition

In motion, layout means two things: where the eye lands, and how space gets made when something new arrives. The default is one subject per frame. That is a UI card at 72-92% of frame width or one line of type no wider than 80%, with captured UI shown at about 2x so body text is at least 27 px at 1080p, and everything that is not the hero dimmed to 0.6-0.7 brightness or defocused. When something enters, the layout makes room physically rather than overlaying it: neighbours move 0.43x the newcomer's travel and start up to 28 f early, and centred lines re-centre on a critically damped spring (20-45 px over 16-38 f) and then keep a 0.4-1.5 px/f drift so type never freezes. Captions go in the space the subject leaves: a 25-30% band, at most 24% of the frame width, inset 8-10% from the edge, starting in the last 25% of the move. To show breadth, use flush cells with no gutters on one shared stage, looping on coprime periods so a change lands somewhere about every 20 f. Any mark inside a sentence sits on the baseline at cap height, in a reserved slot.

### Caption in the subject's negative space

`lc-negative-space-caption` · workhorse · energy calm · walkthrough, feature, launch

Each camera move ends on a pose where the product covers about two-thirds of the frame and leaves a clean band of empty stage, and the caption builds inside that band.

- **Build:** Design each anchor-camera end Shot (src/lib/camera.ts) so the subject covers 65-75% of the frame and leaves a clear 25-30% band on the side it turns away from (a right band when yawed left, a top band when pitched down); check the subject's corners with toScreen. Set the caption in that band: at most 24% of the frame width, 2-3 words per line, left-aligned, inset 8-10% from the frame edge and inside SAFE. Start its Words reveal in the last 25% of the camera move, or within 6 f of landing, so type and camera settle as one gesture; fade it out as a block before the camera moves again.
- **Timing:** Caption starts at 75% of the move, or within 6 f of landing; Words stagger 8 f, dur 26 f. Block exit 12-16 f on E.smooth, ending as the next move starts. Camera moves on E.cam.
- **Use when:** Single-take product walkthroughs and 3D UI slabs where each feature gets one pose and one caption; any shot where text laid over the UI would fight it.
- **Avoid when:** The subject must stay full-frame to be legible (caption above or below it instead), or a 9:16 frame, where the band should be top or bottom only.

### Live cause-and-effect split

`lc-live-split-view` · workhorse · energy calm · walkthrough, feature

Two panels share the frame side by side, the cause on one side (a chat, a list, an input) and the effect on the other (a generated page, a photo, a result), both live, while the camera creeps in.

- **Build:** Lay out two panels inside SAFE at 40/60 (the cause narrower), separated by a 3% W gutter, both the full height of the safe box and aligned on the same top edge; render the composition at 2x so a slow push stays sharp. Keep both sides moving: the cause streams text or steps (a typed reply, a marker hopping down a list) and the effect updates on the frame each cause completes (sections drawing in, or an image swapping on the marker's frame with a small kick of rotateY = 12 deg * hitPulse(f - s, 1, 2.5)). Push the world container linearly by about +0.017%/f, then leave on an accelerating pan (E.in over the last 40 f) and cut on its fastest frame, at most 60 px/f.
- **Timing:** Hold 180-240 f. Creep about +0.017%/f (+4% over 4 s) on E.linear. Swaps every 54 f with a 6 f settle. Exit pan 40 f on E.in, cut at the peak (at most 60 px/f).
- **Use when:** Showing that an input produces an output (prompt to page, list to detail, setting to preview), where seeing both at once is the point.
- **Avoid when:** Phone-first or vertical films (stack the two instead), or when either side's text would drop under 24 px at 1080p.

### One huge centred subject

`lc-one-centred-subject` · workhorse · energy any · any

Every frame has exactly one subject, centred and large: a single line of type, or one UI card scaled to most of the frame width and often bleeding past the edges, with everything else dimmed.

- **Build:** Compose every shot on the frame centre (on safeBox cy in a tall frame) with exactly one subject: a single line of type sized with fitSize to at most 80% of the frame width, or one UI card scaled through the anchor camera to at least 0.85 of the frame width and bleeding past the edges wherever its content allows, so it reads as the product filling the frame rather than a centred floating card. Show captured UI at about 2x native, so body text is at least 27 px at 1080p. Dim anything that is not the hero to brightness 0.6-0.7, or defocus it with RackFocus (blur 8-40); never leave it at full strength. Keep each hold alive with breath(t, 0.025) on the camera.
- **Timing:** Holds of 30-72 f per hero. Cards at 85-100% of frame width or bleeding past it, header bars up to full width, tables at least 80%; type 5-8% of frame height per line. Dims and rack focus 12-20 f on E.smooth.
- **Use when:** Fast, phone-first films; walkthroughs where the viewer must never search for the subject; the default framing between more designed compositions.
- **Avoid when:** Comparison or cause-and-effect beats that need two things on screen at once (use a split), or bento-style loops.

### Subtract to the one

`lc-subtract-to-one` · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature, walkthrough

A busy board loses its elements one by one until a single survivor remains, which either re-centres or stays exactly where it was while the world around it dims.

- **Build:** Staccato version: keep an array of tiles and an index that drops by one at keyframes 5-7 f apart, decided with fd(). Recompute the centred flex layout for each state with no tween, so the survivors jump to their new centred positions on each removal, and hold the last one for 17 f with a +0.5% scale drift. Graded version: duplicate the survivor into a top layer at identical coordinates, fade every neighbour over 12 f on E.smooth, then darken the stage plate from C.paper to C.ink with mixColor over 10 f on E.in, leaving the survivor crisp in place. Words in a line leave in reading order, each lifting 12 px and fading over 4 f on E.in, 3 f apart; if the survivor must end centred, slide it home with spr(f, s, SPR.soft) once the others are gone.
- **Timing:** Staccato: a removal every 5-7 f; last survivor held 17 f. Graded: neighbours fade over 12 f, world dims over 10 f, hold 30 f. Word exits 4 f each, 3 f apart (a line clears in about 12 f). Re-centre 20-40 f on SPR.soft.
- **Use when:** Isolating the deliverable, the found result or the keyword before entering its world; turning a crowded problem state into one focus.
- **Avoid when:** The removed elements are themselves the message (show them first), or the survivor is small enough to float lost in an empty frame (push in after isolating it).

### Vertical clear-band stack

`lc-vertical-band-stack` · workhorse · energy any · vertical

In a 9:16 frame, the caption and the subject stack vertically inside the band the feed leaves clear, with their combined mass centred on that band rather than on the frame, and nothing important under the bottom caption zone or the right action rail.

- **Build:** Get the band from safeBox('feed9x16', W, H): 896 x 1230 px at 1080x1920, centred near y = 885. Stack inside it: the caption on top (fitSize to the band width, at most two lines), a 48 px gap, then the subject below (a UI card at 0.86 of the band width, or a phone screen cropped to its key region), with the stack's combined height centred on the band's cy. Moves are vertical: the subject rises 120 px into place through arrive(prog(f, a, a + 40, E.glide)), the caption reveals with Words 8 f later, and scene changes flow upward (the old stack exits up on E.in over 16 f while the new one rises from below). Never place things side by side, and check every frame with the layout audit so nothing crosses the feed zones.
- **Timing:** Subject rises 120 px over 40 f on E.glide; caption Words (stagger 8 f, dur 26 f) start 8 f after the subject; exits 16 f on E.in; hold 60-90 f per stack.
- **Use when:** Any vertical cut-down or vertical-first film for feeds.
- **Avoid when:** 16:9 masters (use a side-by-side composition there), or full-bleed moments where one giant word fills the screen anyway.

### Words part for an inserted object

`lc-gap-open-insert` · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature, sting

Inside a finished line, the words slide apart to open a gap and an object pops into it (an icon, a photo, a token, or a caret that grows into a container), so the sentence becomes a frame for the object.

- **Build:** Split the line into a left group, a slot and a right group. Animate the slot width w(f) from 0 to the object's width on prog(f, a, a + 16, E.glide), and move the groups with transforms (left translateX -w/2, right +w/2 for a centred line) rather than by reflowing flex widths. Pop the object into the slot once the gap is 70% open: scale 0 to 1 on spr(f, b, SPR.micro), with no overshoot. Container variant: a hairline caret grows to cap height, thickens into a capsule, then widens into the next UI element, pushing the words aside. Hold at least 14 f; to make the object the next scene, accelerate the groups apart on E.in over 16 f (faded, with blurOut) while the object scales up into the next shot's rect.
- **Timing:** Gap opens over 16 f on E.glide, which keeps a 200 px gap under 20 px/f per side. Object pop 6 f on SPR.micro. Hold 14-60 f. Exit: words 16 f on E.in, object scale-up 8-20 f into the cut. Caret variant: grow 6 f, hold 8 f, thicken 14 f, widen 24-62 f.
- **Use when:** Making a sentence about the object literally contain it (a product photo in a claim, a lock icon beside 'private', a prompt box between two words); morphing a headline into the first UI element of the next scene.
- **Avoid when:** Long lines whose parted words would leave the frame unintentionally, or an object that needs more room than a word gap can give (use a push-aside or a cut).

### Centre object with mirrored flanks

`lc-symmetric-flank` · accent · energy medium · launch, feature, walkthrough

A narrow centre object (a phone-width window, a pill, a big number) holds the middle while matching elements sit on both sides: the two halves of a caption, or two mirrored columns of items.

- **Build:** Build a three-column row centred on (W/2, H/2): [left flank, right-aligned] [centre object] [right flank, left-aligned], with a 3% W gutter (58 px at 1080p) between each flank and the object. Caption version: split the sentence so the object stands in for a word, and reveal the halves with Words (blur to focus), the right half 20-42 f after the left. Column version: two columns of 80 px items, rows offset alternately by half a row, the right column built as the mirror of the left. Rows appear top to bottom in sync on both sides, 6 f per row (opacity plus a 10 px rise, 12 f on E.out); then both columns drift outward with a U-shaped speed while the centre statement rises 50 px over 38 f on E.outSoft.
- **Timing:** Caption halves 20-42 f apart; hold about 60 f. Column rows 6 f apart (five rows in about 30 f); outward drift 3.8, then 0.7, then 1.8 px/f over about 120 f. Centre numeral rises 50 px over 38 f.
- **Use when:** A narrow device or pill leaves empty sides; a stat that needs visible volume on either side; inputs and outputs around one product; the tagline that frames a logo pill before the end.
- **Avoid when:** Wide centre subjects (each flank gets squeezed under 20% of the frame), or vertical formats (stack above and below instead).

### Headline over a ghost of the UI

`lc-headline-over-ghost-ui` · accent · energy calm · launch, feature, walkthrough

A headline inks in from light grey to near-black while a faint copy of the product interface sits behind it, then the UI resolves to full strength as the headline leaves.

- **Build:** Use two layers: the product UI (a full-frame capture or live component) at opacity 0.15, and the headline centred on top of it. Ink the headline from C.mute to C.ink through mixColor on prog(f, a, a + 40, E.outSoft) (on a dark stage, C.mute to C.white). As the headline exits (Words with out, or a 16 f fade on E.smooth), raise the UI's opacity from 0.15 to 1 over 60 f on E.smooth with a slow scale from 1.03 to 1.0 on the same curve, so the next shot is already composed. If the UI is busy, defocus the ghost with RackFocus (t = 1, blur 10) and rack it sharp as it resolves.
- **Timing:** Ink resolve 40 f. Ghost UI at 10-20% opacity under the headline; it resolves to 100% over 60 f, starting when the headline's exit begins.
- **Use when:** Setting up a demo during a statement, so the move into the product needs no transition; a claim that names the product area about to be shown.
- **Avoid when:** High-contrast UIs whose ghost would muddy the type, or UI text at the same scale as the headline sitting directly behind it.

### Hero icon becomes the inline glyph

`lc-hero-flips-to-inline-glyph` · accent · energy medium · launch, feature, sting

The centred hero icon shrinks and travels into a slot at the start of, or inside, a sentence, and the words of the claim spill out of it, so the icon becomes a word.

- **Build:** Lay out the final line first with an empty inline slot one cap height square (inkBox gives the cap height, measureTracked the widths), and read the slot's rect. FLIP the hero from its centred rect to that rect with translate and scale on prog(f, a, a + 26, E.smooth), with motion blur while it exceeds 12 px/f; for extra life add a wobble of rotateY = sin(pi p) * 25 deg and rotateX = -sin(pi p) * 15 deg under perspective(800px). The words start behind the icon in z and spill outward: each word's translateX runs from -24 px to 0 over 14 f on E.out while its opacity rises and its colour moves from C.mute to C.ink through mixColor over 12 f. The first word starts 2 f after the icon lands and the rest follow 4 f apart; then the line drifts at 0.5 px/f.
- **Timing:** Icon travel 22-30 f on E.smooth, scaling to about 0.42 (cap height). Words at icon landing + 2, + 6 and + 10 f, each a 14 f slide of 24 px with a 12 f colour resolve. Residual drift 0.5-1 px/f.
- **Use when:** Bridging from a hero object to a claim about it: an icon becoming the bullet of its benefit, a mark becoming the subject of a sentence, a feature glyph leading a metric line.
- **Avoid when:** Detailed icons that will not read at cap height (50-90 px), or sentences long enough to wrap.

### Hub-and-spoke concept diagram

`lc-hub-spoke-diagram` · accent · energy calm · walkthrough, feature, launch

A central product tile sits inside two thin concentric rings with a short streak orbiting it, inputs on the left and outputs on the right, under a centred one-line headline.

- **Build:** Centre an opaque 64-96 px icon tile with a soft shadow, and draw two SVG circles around it at 1.8x and 2.8x the tile size: 1.5 px strokes at 15% opacity. The orbiting streak is an SVG arc of about 70 deg on the outer ring, with stroke opacity ramping from 0 to 1 toward its head (a one-hue linearGradient in C.accent), turned by rotate(1.5 * f deg). Inputs (left) and outputs (right) are small opaque labelled chips in mirrored rows that enter together, 6 f per row (opacity plus a 10 px rise, 12 f on E.out); then connector lines from each chip to the outer ring draw with stroke-dashoffset over 16 f on E.out. The headline above reveals with Words, and the orbit keeps the hold alive.
- **Timing:** Rows 6 f apart, 12 f each; connectors 16 f on E.out; streak 1.5 deg/f (a quarter turn per second) on E.linear. Hold 120-200 f; the rotation keeps it moving.
- **Use when:** Explaining a many-inputs, many-outputs product (integrations, sources to results) in one still composition without narration; the concept beat before a walkthrough.
- **Avoid when:** More than five chips per side, or when the real product UI can show the same thing directly.

### Icon-led ragged word stack

`lc-icon-ragged-stack` · accent · energy medium · launch, feature, vertical

A short lead word is followed by three or four keywords on separate lines, each with a small line icon, set at staggered x positions so the list has a rag instead of bullets.

- **Build:** Build a flex column with one row per keyword. Each row is a 1 em inline SVG line icon (stroke width matching the type's stem, coloured like the text) followed by the word, shifted by translateX from a fixed rag table such as [0, +120, -60, +180] px. The lead word sits above in C.mute; the keywords are C.ink at TYPE.secondary size or larger. Each row enters with translateY 12 px to 0 through arrive(prog(f, s_i, s_i + 22, E.out)) and opacity on the same progress, rows 10 f apart; while held, the whole stack drifts upward at 0.4 px/f.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Drop the muted lead word above the stack: fold it into the first row as a full-strength word at the keywords' size ('Built for teams', then 'agencies' and 'founders' on the rag), or cut it and let the keywords stand alone. Use an icon only where it is the product's own mark for that item, never a stock line icon; otherwise keep the rag with words alone. Keep the rag table, the 10 f row stagger and the 0.4 px/f drift. The full look relies on filler-text; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** Rows 8-12 f apart (10 by default), 22 f each on E.out, 12 px rise. Hold the full stack 60-80 f with the drift, then exit in reading order 4 f apart.
- **Use when:** Listing three or four abstract capabilities, platforms or audiences that would otherwise be a bullet list; a 'works across X, Y, Z' beat.
- **Avoid when:** More than four items, items longer than two words, or icons that decorate rather than mean something (then drop them and keep the rag).

### Mark set as a word

`lc-mark-as-inline-word` · accent · energy calm · launch, feature, sting

A logo, partner mark or icon sits inside a sentence on the baseline at cap height, as if it were a word, appearing with its own delayed fade or swapping with a word in the same slot.

- **Build:** Lay out the final centred line with the mark in its own inline slot: height equal to the cap height from inkBox, bottom on the baseline, margin-left one space width (measureTracked(' ')), so the slot is reserved and nothing reflows. Reveal the words first (Words, stagger 8), then fade the mark in on its own about 17 f after the first word: opacity 0 to 1 on prog(f, s, s + 6, E.smooth), with no scale pop. To swap something in the slot, stack two spans: the outgoing one moves to translateY -8 px as it fades out while the incoming one rises from +8 px as it fades in, both over 8 f on E.ui.
- **Timing:** Mark appears about 17 f after the first word with a 4-6 f fade. Slot swap 8 f with 8 px travel. The line then drifts at 0.5 px/f.
- **Use when:** Co-branding inside a claim, naming a platform or integration without a separate logo slate, or turning a generic noun into the product name in place.
- **Avoid when:** Marks with fine detail or wide aspect ratios that cannot read at cap height, or the film's own final lockup, which appears once, at the end, on its own.

### Opposite-corner caption relay

`lc-opposite-corner-relay` · accent · energy calm · walkthrough, feature

One caption fades out of one upper corner while the next starts building in the mirrored corner, so the eye travels across a locked frame and that travel is the motion.

- **Build:** Place caption A top-left and caption B in the mirrored position top-right, on the same baseline and at the same inset from the safe edge. A exits with a 28 f opacity fade on E.smooth and does not move. B's Words reveal starts 10 f after A's exit begins, so the two overlap for 18 f in different places. Keep the product shot on a slow breath(t, 0.02) or a 0.3 px/f drift rather than fully locked, since each caption holds 48-60 f; the relay is the event.
- **Timing:** A fades over 28 f on E.smooth; B starts 10 f after A's exit begins; 18 f of overlap. Each caption stays readable for at least 48-60 f.
- **Use when:** Two consecutive beats over one held product shot with no camera move or cut; alternating claims about one screen.
- **Avoid when:** Captions longer than a short line (the eye cannot finish A while B starts), or as the default for every caption change; repeated more than twice it reads as a device.

### Arc carousel

`lc-arc-carousel` · signature · energy medium · launch, feature, loop

A row of cards rides a wide smile-shaped arc across the lower part of the frame, each tilted tangent to the curve, rushing in, coasting slowly through the middle and speeding out.

- **Build:** Use a circle of R = 1750 px centred at (960, -790) at 1080p. Card i sits at angle theta_i = theta0(f) + i * 11 deg, with x = 960 + R sin(theta_i), y = -790 + R cos(theta_i) and rotateZ(-theta_i), so the arc bottoms out at y = 960 and the cards lean outward toward the edges. Drive it with a U-shaped speed: theta0(f) = 12 deg * (1 - prog(f, 0, 45, E.out)) - 0.25 deg * (f - 45) - 7.6 deg * prog(f, 45, 90, E.in), over 12 opaque cards with soft drop shadows, z-ordered so the centre card is on top. Behind them, a large flat ellipse (or one accent hue fading to transparent) centred above the arc acts as the dome. Apply the motion-blur pass while card speed exceeds 12 px/f (roughly the first 15 f and the last 20 f).
- **Timing:** 90 f per pass. Card speed 58 px/f on entry, about 8 px/f through the middle, 39 px/f on exit (angular 1.9, then 0.25, then 1.3 deg/f). Spacing 11 deg, about 336 px of arc, for cards 260-300 px wide.
- **Use when:** Showing an inventory or collection (templates, cards, products, integrations) where several items should read at once and the set should feel endless; a looping feature beat.
- **Avoid when:** Items with dense text that must be read at the edges (tilted edge cards are glanced at, not read), or vertical frames where the arc gets too tight.

### Bento cell takes over the frame

`lc-bento-cell-takeover` · signature · energy high · loop, launch, feature

In a flush four-cell grid, one cell grows to fill the whole frame while its siblings are pushed off the edges, still playing as they go, turning a breadth overview into one focused shot without a cut.

- **Build:** Build a flush 2x2 grid as in oh-live-grid-cold-open: gap 0, cells exactly W/2 x H/2 on whole pixels, overflow hidden and C.ink in every cell so the seams vanish, with every cell's scene rendered at full 1920x1080 inside a wrapper with scale(0.5) and transformOrigin '0 0'. Scale the whole grid container from 1 to 2 with lmix on prog(f, a, a + 64, E.smooth), about the chosen cell's outer corner (transformOrigin '0 0' for the top-left cell, '100% 100%' for the bottom-right). That corner stays fixed, the chosen cell lands exactly on the frame at native resolution, and the other cells slide out of frame. Keep every cell's loop running through the move and apply motion blur while the far edge exceeds 12 px/f; on landing, drop the grid and continue the cell's scene as a normal shot.
- **Timing:** 64 f on E.smooth; content at the far frame edge peaks around 60 px/f (the far corner about 68 px/f), with motion blur. Cells keep playing throughout. Follow with at least 90 f of the full-frame scene. To return to the overview, run it in reverse (scale 2 to 1, 64 f, E.smooth).
- **Use when:** A loop or launch that opens on four-up breadth and then dives into one feature; returning to the overview between features.
- **Avoid when:** A chosen cell whose scene was not composed for full frame (it will look sparse), or more than twice per film.

### Swarm, cluster and burst reveal

`lc-swarm-cluster-burst` · signature · energy high · launch, sting

About twenty cards or screenshots fly in from every edge, swirl, pack into a dense overlapping cluster that slowly swells, then blow outward past the camera to uncover a hero object that was waiting behind them.

- **Build:** Place the hero (lockup, stat card, product) centred at z 0, already at final size, with N = 16-24 cards above it. Give card i a slot in a packed cluster (a grid jittered by rand(i): up to 40 px and 6 deg, overlapping, larger cards higher in z) and a unit radial vector from the centre through that slot. Fly-in: set the card's offset along its vector to total - inertia(f, s_i, 56, 0.95).x, so it starts about 1090 px out and coasts into its slot, with start frames spread by stagger(i, N, 24, E.out). Over the next 60 f the slots rotate about the centre by an angle that decays from 24 deg to 0 on E.outSoft (the swirl), contract to 73% spread over 32 f on E.out, and then the whole cluster scales up linearly by 0.2% per frame. Burst: each card travels along its vector by d(n) = 3n^2 px for n <= 12, then 432 + 72(n - 12), with scale 1 + 2(n/24)^3 under a true motion-blur pass, so the hero is uncovered in about 18 f.
- **Timing:** Fly-in 28-40 f, entering at 56 px/f and decaying. Swirl 60 f. Converge 32 f (cluster width 1474 to 1076 px at 1080p). Build 104 f at +0.2%/f, E.linear. Burst 24 f, peaking at 72 px/f with motion blur; the last cards clear by f24, then hold the hero. Shorter scatter-only version: cards leave on E.in over 22 f, with travel scaled by (1 + 0.1 * index).
- **Use when:** A crescendo near the end that proves breadth (many apps, templates, outputs) and clears the stage for the lockup or a hero stat; the film's single biggest motion spike.
- **Avoid when:** Calm or minimal films, more than once per film, or when the cards' content has to be read (nothing in the swarm is legible). If it reveals the lockup, the lockup still holds only 1.5-2.0 s.

## Pacing and structure

Pacing is the shape of speed over time, and the strongest films control it at three scales. Per shot the shape is a U: arrive on E.out over 20-50 f, keep living through the hold at 0.3-1 px/f (no near-dead run longer than about 22 f), then accelerate over the last 18-24 f so the cut lands on the fastest frame at 17-38 px/f and the next shot opens already moving. Stillness is spent like money. One near-still hold of 60-90 f on the key claim, or a 12-15 f freeze on true silence before the lockup, reads as intent only because everything else moves. Per sequence, repetition teaches the viewer: a fixed 180 f ask beat with answers of varying length, a second instance at 0.6x length, phrase chunks landing one per beat. Per film, acts sit on the bar grid (a 30-60 s launch splits roughly 19/14/58/9%), stage polarity flips 3-5 times, and the score's arrangement follows the acts, with 12-24 f music holes before key statements and every slam within ±1 f of a picture event.

### Breath envelope per card

`ps-breath-envelope` · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature, vertical

Every card arrives fast and decelerates, keeps moving gently through its hold, then accelerates away and is cut on its fastest frame.

- **Build:** Drive each card's container with one summed transform of three terms. Arrival: tw(f, 0, 36, 90, 0, E.out) px of translate (or scale lmix(1.08, 1, prog(f, 0, 36))), with arrive() on vertical text moves and blurIn only while the card travels faster than 12 px/f. Hold: a linear drift of 0.4-1 px/f, or breath() from src/lib/camera.ts at about +0.06%/f, optionally with letter-spacing tightening 2-3% over 40 f on E.outSoft from the landing frame. Exit: tw(f, T-16, T, 0, 100, E.in) px (or +6% scale) with blurOut, and the hard cut on frame T, which is the exit's fastest frame. Because the terms add, speed follows a U (fast, slow, fast) and never touches zero mid-card; the hold length follows the copy rule (36 f + 6 f per word).
- **Timing:** Arrival 20-50 f E.out (default 36, peak about 15 px/f). Hold = 36 f + 6 f per word at 0.4-1 px/f or +0.06%/f scale; the drift rate is never 0 for more than 6 f. Exit 14-20 f E.in, reaching 19-39 px/f on the cut frame. Example U: 14 then 3 then 39 px/f across 56 f. No near-still run over about 22 f before the end card.
- **Use when:** Statement cards, kinetic type and feature cards in a fast-cut film where nothing should ever look frozen.
- **Avoid when:** Dense UI that needs a dead-still read (lock the camera instead), and the final lockup hold.

### Camera locks, the interface performs

`ps-locked-camera-holds` · workhorse · energy calm · walkthrough, feature, launch

After each move the camera stops dead, and for a 1-4 s read only the caption, the cursor and one micro-interaction move.

- **Build:** Between poses, blend with lc(A, B, E.cam(p)) from src/lib/camera.ts. At each pose, hold the Shot exactly: no breath(), scale constant, 0.0 px/f. Schedule events from the move's end so that no gap between visible changes exceeds 40 f: the UI action at moveEnd - 10 f, the caption word reveal (src/fx/Words.tsx) at moveEnd - 0.25 * moveDuration, cursor travel (src/fx/Cursor.tsx) on E.glide. Ambient life lives only in the background, for example a single-hue wash breathing ±3% opacity on a 240 f sine. The caption leaves as one block, opacity on E.smooth over 26-28 f with no stagger, and is gone 0-56 f before the next move starts.
- **Timing:** Holds 60-240 f (median about 150 f) at exactly 0 px/f; an in-frame event at least every 40 f; moves between holds 56-108 f E.cam; caption exit 26-28 f E.smooth, ending 0-56 f before the next move.
- **Use when:** Dense product UI that must be read, walkthroughs, and films where every move should feel deliberate because it contrasts with stillness.
- **Avoid when:** Kinetic type or fast montages where a dead camera reads as a stalled player, or holds with nothing in the UI to animate.

### Each repeat runs faster

`ps-faster-each-repeat` · workhorse · energy medium · any

The first instance of a repeated action plays at full length, the second runs about 40% quicker, and later ones are implied or ratchet faster still.

- **Build:** Give the repeated component a duration parameter: dur_k = max(minDur, base * 0.6^k) for k = 0, 1, 2, and so on. It is the same curve compressed, so an E.out rise stays E.out. Show two full instances, then cut away or batch the rest. For lists, swaps and deletes, schedule start frames from shrinking gaps and pick the visible state with fd(frame). Across a film, the caption word stagger in src/fx/Words.tsx can fall the same way from the title to the last feature. Bind a repeat run with one low pad swell under the whole run (attack 6-9 f, release over about 84 f), with one tick per step growing by about 1 dB each time.
- **Timing:** Second instance at 0.6x length (for example a rise of 12 f becomes 7 f), starting about 46 f after the first. Ratchet gaps 26, 14, 12, 8, 8, 4, 4 f. Caption word stagger falling from 24 f on the title to 5 f on late captions.
- **Use when:** Repeated unlocks, card reveals, list items, word deletes, and captions that recur across a film.
- **Avoid when:** Items that each need a full read, and the first instance, which must teach the pattern at full length.

### Fixed-length ask, variable answer

`ps-fixed-ask-variable-answer` · workhorse · energy medium · feature, walkthrough, launch

A demo repeats a fixed-length ask beat followed by a result whose length varies with its importance, so the rhythm teaches itself and the variations prevent fatigue.

- **Build:** Write the ask beat as one component with a fixed internal script, 6 beats long (180 f at 120 BPM). Typing takes 68 f however long the prompt is: visibleChars = fd(len * prog(f, 0, 68, E.linear)), with the first word pre-filled. Then an icon drop of 28 f, a chip morph of 16-20 f, cursor travel of 14 f on E.glide, a press of 32-40 f, and a plus-to-x rotation of 8-12 f as the cut cue. Results last 4-8 beats, and one hero result runs 2-3x the others. From the third cycle on, split the ask beat into a big-type or 3-4x close-up insert plus the card: the template stays and the framing changes.
- **Timing:** Ask beat 180-188 f (6 beats); results 138-234 f, the hero result about 490 f; 4-5 cycles; close-up insert from cycle 3.
- **Use when:** Prompt-to-result products, feature tours with one repeated action, and walkthroughs of 3-6 capabilities.
- **Avoid when:** Fewer than 3 instances (there is no pattern to learn), and stings.

### Hard stop into a silent sign-off

`ps-silent-sign-off` · workhorse · energy high · launch, feature, sting

Tension rises under the back half, the music stops dead on the cut to the last line or URL, the picture all but freezes, and the lockup arrives at full speed under a single low stinger.

- **Build:** About 180-300 f before the end card, add a riser event in src/sync.ts that ends on the first frame of the silence, and thin the score section (layers {drums: 0, arp: 0}). Skip the riser if a whoosh already leads into the same downbeat. On the cut to the URL or last line, stop the music with a score.json drops entry and hold the picture near-still (scale drift at most 0.03%/f). The final 12-15 f before the logo sit on a silences entry with zero transforms. The logo move starts at full speed (its E.out curve begins on frame 0 of the move, with no ease-in), and one drop or hit stinger lands on the frame the wordmark resolves; its 1.2-1.5 s tail covers a 90-120 f lockup hold that keeps building with a push of at least 10%.
- **Timing:** Riser 180-300 f ending where the silence begins; music falls to silence within 2 f; URL readable for at least 102 f with drift of at most 0.03%/f; designed freeze 12-15 f on true silence; logo move 30-68 f E.out from full speed; stinger on the wordmark's resolve frame; lockup hold 90-120 f; tail of at least 60 f.
- **Use when:** The last 4-6 s of launch films and feature reels for fast, confident brands.
- **Avoid when:** Calm brands, where a sub stinger reads as trailer noise (end on one soft chord instead), and loops with no ending.

### Image act, then type act

`ps-image-act-then-type-act` · workhorse · energy medium · feature, vertical

A short spot splits in half: the first half is pure imagery with no words at all, the second is pure type with no imagery.

- **Build:** Storyboard two contiguous ACTs at about 47/53%. Act 1 is three image shots of about 80 f each with no text layer at all, each ending on an accelerating exit (E.in). Act 2 is type only on a plain stage: the claim, then the headline, then the CTA and the lockup. Its first card continues act 1's screen direction across the seam. Keep text and imagery in separate Sequences so neither act can leak into the other, and run each type card on the breath envelope.
- **Timing:** Total 480-600 f. Act 1: 3 shots of 70-90 f. Act 2: claim 70-80 f, headline 60-70 f, CTA 60 f, then lockup 90-110 f.
- **Use when:** 6-12 s spots and social cut-downs with one claim and a strong visual metaphor, especially when watched on mute.
- **Avoid when:** Product walkthroughs that need captions on the UI, and films over 20 s.

### Light and dark as chapters

`ps-luma-act-map` · workhorse · energy any · launch, feature, walkthrough

Acts are planned by stage polarity, dark for the abstract or problem beats and light for the product, so chapter changes read without any title cards.

- **Build:** Add a LUMA map beside ACT in src/timeline.ts ('dark' or 'light' per act) and two stage token sets in src/brand/tokens.ts (dark at value 0.10-0.30, light at 0.85-0.95; the accent colour stays the same). Pick one plan. Alternation: about 50/50 dark and light, flipping at each ask/answer change. Arc: dark open, mixed middle, light product finish. Flips land on downbeats, 3-5 per film, and never use the same device twice in a row: an inverse hard cut, an inverse match cut on a shared icon, an iris from a glyph (20 f E.inOut), a bleach to white (26 f E.smooth), or a theme flip during a move (6 f). An optional second channel is a single-hue brand wash (one Background component with intensity 0-1) that shows only on brand beats: it rises from the bottom edge (translateY 40% to 0, 50 f E.out) and drains in 8 f E.in.
- **Timing:** 3-5 flips per film, each on b(n); iris 20 f E.inOut; bleach 26 f E.smooth; theme flip during a move 6 f; wash rise 50 f E.out, drain 8 f E.in.
- **Use when:** Films with distinct problem/solution or prompt/result halves, and 20-60 s pieces that need a rhythm at the scale of whole acts.
- **Avoid when:** Very short stings, and brands locked to a single stage colour.

### Long-tailed beat lengths

`ps-long-tail-beat-lengths` · workhorse · energy any · launch, walkthrough, feature

Beat lengths follow a long tail instead of an even grid: most beats sit near one median length, a few connective beats snap past at a third of it, and one or two hero beats run about three times as long, so the film never settles into a slideshow rhythm.

- **Build:** Before animating anything, write the cut list in src/timeline.ts as a BEATS array of cut-to-cut lengths in 8ths, and derive the ACT and CUE start frames from its running sum with b() so every boundary sits on the grid. Pick a median M of 60-72 f (2-2.4 beats at 120 BPM, inside the house shot median of 60-90 f) and fill the list from four bins. Core beats run 0.75-1.33x M (about 60%: features, claims, answers). Connective beats run 0.25-0.5x M and never under 24 f (about 20%: a punch-in insert, a whip, a one-word card, an isolate hold). Long beats run 1.5-2x M (10-15%: a walkthrough setup, a two-step interaction). One or two hero beats run 2.5-3x M, capped at 180 f, the house shot maximum (the hero result or the key feature), placed in the back half before the sign-off. Put one or two connective beats directly before each hero beat so the hero lands as a release, and never let three neighbouring beats sit within 10% of each other in length. Beats under 42 f carry no readable text (the copy rule is 36 f + 6 f per word). A hero beat is filled with continuous action, either a camera journey or a UI event at least every 40 f, never a long hold. Beside grid-check, add a node check asserting that max/M is 2.5-3.0, min/M is 0.16-0.5, no beat exceeds 180 f and the coefficient of variation is 0.4-0.8. An evenly spaced cut list scores about 0.1 and reads as a slideshow.
- **Timing:** M = 60-72 f. Connective beats 24-36 f (never under 24 f); core 0.75-1.33x M; long 1.5-2x M; hero 2.5-3x M, at most 180 f and at most 2 per film; coefficient of variation 0.4-0.8. Example 28.75 s cut at 120 BPM: 75, 60, 30, 75, 120, 45, 60, 75, 30, 75, 60, 45, 105, 60, 30, 180, 75, 45, 30, 180, 90 and 60 f, then a 120 f lockup (M 60, max/M 3.0, CV 0.56).
- **Use when:** Launch films and walkthroughs of 15 s or more with eight or more beats, any cut list that came out evenly spaced, and deciding where the hero feature gets its time.
- **Avoid when:** Polyrhythm loops and fixed-length ask cycles, where equal length is the point; stings under about 8 s, which have too few beats for a distribution; accelerando runs, which set their own length ratios.

### Loop seam hidden at a motion peak

`ps-loop-seam-on-motion-peak` · workhorse · energy medium · loop

A loop wraps around on the fastest frame of a whip or push, so the last frame flows into the first with no visible restart.

- **Build:** Make the clip length L a whole number of bars (for example 4 bars = 480 f at 120 BPM). Design frame 0 as the second half of a move, opening already travelling on E.out from full speed, and the last 12-24 f as the first half of the same move, an E.in ramp to the same speed and direction. Make every state a pure function of frame % L. Verify the seam by rendering frames L-2, L-1, 0 and 1: per-frame position deltas should match within 10%, and every discrete fd() state at L should equal frame 0. Wrap motion-blur sub-frame times modulo L so the seam frame smears like its neighbours, and loop the music bed on the same bar line.
- **Timing:** L = whole bars (240, 480 or 960 f); seam move at 20-40 px/f with true motion blur; entry E.out 30-50 f, exit E.in 12-24 f; seam on the downbeat.
- **Use when:** Autoplay loops for social, landing pages and product pages.
- **Avoid when:** Pieces that end on a lockup (it appears once, at the end), and loops whose first frame must work as a readable poster.

### Machine on the grid, hands off it

`ps-machine-grid-human-gaps` · workhorse · energy medium · walkthrough, feature, launch

Work the product does (rows inserting, items stacking, text streaming) ticks on a strict metronome, while what a person does (moving the cursor, flipping toggles, clicking) arrives on uneven, deliberating gaps, so the viewer can feel who is acting.

- **Build:** Tag every scheduled event in src/timeline.ts with who performs it: SYS for work the product does (rows inserting, items stacking, text streaming, status steps) and USER for what a person does (cursor travel, clicks, toggles, drags). SYS start frames come from b() on a fixed step: 15 f (an 8th at 120 BPM) for inserts, or 16ths via b(bar, beat, sub) for bursts. Every SYS instance uses the same curve and duration (for example a 12 f E.ui reveal) at a constant or ratcheting rate. Streamed text uses TypeOn with cps at 25-40 characters per second, or one fixed time box, and never jitters. USER start frames come from a hand-written list of uneven gaps, with at least 2x between the shortest and longest gap and no two neighbouring gaps within 15% of each other ([0, 4, 19, 37] f for four toggles, or gaps of 10, 26 and 14 f). Cursor travel runs through cursorArc (bow 0.15-0.25) on E.glide and lasts max(14, D / 20) f for a trip of D px, which keeps its peak under 60 px/f. A dwell of 6-18 f, chosen per instance with rand(seed), separates arrival from the press, and pressAt drives the click. Only the decisive press of each scene lands on a beat (±1 f); the rest of the user layer stays off the grid. Sound follows the same split: each SYS insert gets one soft tick so the metronome is heard (dropped once inserts pass about 3 per second over a bed), and USER actions stay silent except the decisive click.
- **Timing:** SYS: one event every 15 f (an 8th at 120 BPM), or every 7-8 f (16ths) in bursts; identical 12 f E.ui reveals; streams at 25-40 characters per second. USER: gaps such as 4, 15 and 18 f, or 10, 26 and 14 f; cursor travel max(14, D/20) f on E.glide, peak under 60 px/f, with motion blur above 12 px/f; dwell 6-18 f; press 12 f via pressAt; the decisive press on the beat ±1 f.
- **Use when:** Product demos where a person gives an instruction and the product or an agent responds, walkthroughs that mix input with generated output, and any sequence where automation should feel tireless next to a human.
- **Avoid when:** Pure type films or brand stings with no user in the story; polyrhythm grids, which run their own clocks; musical montages where every event must land on the beat.

### Music hole, then slam on the cut

`ps-music-hole-slam` · workhorse · energy high · launch, feature, vertical

The low end, or the whole bed, vanishes for a fraction of a second under a key statement, then slams back on the exact frame of a picture event.

- **Build:** For a single statement, add a score.json drops entry ({at, silence: '1/8', suck: 0.2}) so the bed sucks down and stops 12-24 f before at. Then choose one of two placements. Either at is the cut itself, so the slam lands on the cut, or the statement card cuts in 3-12 f inside the silence and at is the next 8th, about 15-17 f after the cut. For a whole line, give its bar a section with layers {drums: 0, bass: 0} so only the pad holds, and put the next picture event (a cut, a mask click, a reveal) on the return downbeat within ±1 f. Keep the card's own sound tiny, and use 2-4 holes per minute, the deepest before the hero cut.
- **Timing:** Hole 12-24 f for one statement or 2-4 beats for a line; the bed drops 10-20 dB or the sub goes fully silent; re-entry on a downbeat within ±1 f of a picture event; 2-4 holes per minute.
- **Use when:** Statement cards, key claims and the hero cut in any film with a groove bed.
- **Avoid when:** Calm brands with no drums, or more than one hole every 8 bars, where it stops working as an accent.

### One screen direction per act

`ps-direction-per-act` · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature, sting, vertical

Each act owns one direction of travel, so every entrance, exit, drift and camera ramp in it runs the same way, and the direction turns only at an act seam, where the turn itself marks the new chapter.

- **Build:** Add a DIR map beside ACT in src/timeline.ts with one unit vector per act ({x: 1, y: 0} for left to right, {x: -1, y: 0} for right to left, or {x: 0, y: -1} for an upward feed), plus a helper along(act, d) that returns {x: d * DIR.x, y: d * DIR.y}. Route every directional number through that helper. Entrances start upstream at along(act, -O), with O = 8-15% of frame width, and brake on E.out. Holds drift downstream at 0.3-1 px/f. Exits and accelerate-into-cut ramps leave downstream on E.in, and whoosh pan takes the sign of DIR.x. Inside an act nothing travels against the vector except a settle tail or a final move to centre. Across each cut inside the act, the hero leaves by the downstream edge and comes back in from the upstream edge, still travelling the same way. Turn the vector only at an act seam, on its downbeat (a seam may also keep it). Make each turn coincide with a second channel change (a polarity flip, a score section change, or the switch from imagery to type) so it reads as a new chapter rather than a continuity slip. The last act's vector delivers the lockup: the mark arrives along it and settles centred. Check it in a node test beside grid-check: sample each act's text positions at f and f + 1 from the same functions the acts use, and assert that every text element moving faster than 2 px/f has a velocity whose dot product with DIR is positive, except settle tails of at most 6 f.
- **Timing:** 2-4 vectors per film, one per act, each turn on b(n) at an act seam. Entrance offsets 8-15% of frame width (150-290 px at 1080p), braking on E.out over 30-50 f; hold drift 0.3-1 px/f downstream; exit ramps 18-24 f on E.in, reaching 17-38 px/f; counter-motion above 2 px/f lasts at most 6 f and only in settle tails.
- **Use when:** Films built from hard cuts with velocity handoffs, two-act spots (imagery, then type), runs of statements (an upward feed), and vertical films with a rising vector.
- **Avoid when:** Oners and single camera journeys, where the layout of the surface sets the direction; films whose motion is mostly radial zooms; multi-cell grids; a film with no act change, which should keep one vector throughout.

### Phrase chunks on the beat

`ps-beat-quantized-chunks` · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature, sting, vertical

A line arrives in two or three chunks split by meaning, each landing exactly on the next beat, so the reading rhythm is performed by the track.

- **Build:** Split the copy into 2-3 chunks by meaning (subject | object | qualifier). Chunk k starts at b(bar, beat + k) minus half its first word's rise, so the rise's 50% frame lands on the beat. Words inside a chunk follow 4 f apart, each on a baseline line-mask rise (an overflow-hidden line box, translateY 100% to 0 on E.out with arrive()). For a calmer build, use one beat per word with a blur-to-focus reveal: opacity 0 to 1 over 8 f, blurIn from 8 px across 18 f, a 13 px rise over 28 f on E.out, plus a 1 px/f line drift. Hold the finished line for at least 36 f + 6 f per word.
- **Timing:** One beat per chunk (30 f at 120 BPM); 4 f word stagger inside a chunk; masked rise 6-8 f E.out, stretched to 10-12 f for words over 60 px tall so legible glyphs stay under 20 px/f; calm variant 20-22 f per word.
- **Use when:** Statement lines over music with a clear pulse, launch openers, and 3-7 word claims.
- **Avoid when:** No music or a free-time score, and sentences of more than 8 words.

### Silent UI over a steady bed

`ps-silent-ui-steady-bed` · workhorse · energy high · loop, feature, vertical, walkthrough

In dense, fast-changing sequences the interface makes no sound of its own, with no per-key or per-event effects, and a steady groove carries all the energy.

- **Build:** When visible events exceed about 3 per second (multi-cell loops, speed-typed prompts, counters), set the score.json typing style to off or muted and emit no key or tick events for them in src/sync.ts. Let the section's hats and kick carry the rhythm (style groove or drive, low end in mono). Allow at most one soft tick per word or label: high-passed above 2-3 kHz, 18-24 dB under the bed, 40-80 ms decay, with ±2 dB and ±80 cents of variation seeded by rand(). Save 6-8 accent ticks per 45 s for real clicks, and keep cuts on the 8th grid, where the hats already sound.
- **Timing:** No per-character sounds; at most 1 tick per word; 6-8 accent ticks per 45 s; ticks 5-15 ms attack, 40-80 ms decay, 18-24 dB under the bed.
- **Use when:** Loops, grids, speed-typed prompts, counters, and any sequence with more than 3 events per second.
- **Avoid when:** Sparse, calm films where each event deserves its own tuned sound, and the payoff moment.

### Spectacle, diagram, walkthrough, sign-off

`ps-four-sequence-launch` · workhorse · energy medium · launch

A launch film in four sequences: a short spectacle open, one concept diagram, a long real-product walkthrough and a brief brand close.

- **Build:** Split the runtime about 19/14/58/9%, each part a contiguous bar-aligned ACT in src/timeline.ts. The open (surge) gets the biggest moves and the strongest use of the accent colour. The diagram (dip) is one centred concept figure that names the idea, paced slower. The walkthrough (plateau) is 10-14 shots built from wide/close pairs: render the UI once and frame each close-up as the same composition at 4-4.5x scale on the control, with the cuts velocity-matched. The close (a small peak, then calm) replays the open's mechanic and lands the lockup. Map score.json sections onto the same contour: intro/build, breakdown, groove, resolve, hold.
- **Timing:** Shares 19/14/58/9% (at 30 s: about 342/252/1044/162 f). Walkthrough shot median 75-100 f; wides 90-180 f, close-ups 76-154 f at 4-4.5x. Lockup hold 90-120 f inside the close.
- **Use when:** 30-60 s launch films that have to earn attention, explain an idea and then prove it in the product.
- **Avoid when:** Spots under 15 s (use the image-then-type plan instead) and products with nothing to diagram.

### Accelerando into the climax

`ps-accelerando-to-climax` · accent · energy high · launch, sting, feature

Shot lengths shrink step by step toward the climax, then one designed freeze on silence resets the clock just before the payoff lands.

- **Build:** Plan the last 5-7 shots before the climax on the beat grid, each about 0.7x the length of the one before: for example 4, 3, 2, 1.5, 1 and 1 beats at 120 BPM (120, 90, 60, 45, 30 and 30 f). Text only goes on shots long enough for the copy rule, and shots without text can go down to 24 f. Each shot ends on the accelerate-into-cut ramp, scaled to its last 40% on E.in, while the score section steps from groove to build beneath it. The run ends on a 12-15 f freeze sitting exactly on a score.json silences entry, and the climax move starts at full speed on the next downbeat.
- **Timing:** Shots 120, 90, 60, 45, 30, 30 f (about x0.7 each, minimum 24 f without text); exit ramps on the last 40% of each shot, E.in; freeze 12-15 f on true silence; climax on the next downbeat.
- **Use when:** The run-up to a reveal, a collage burst or the lockup in launch films and stings.
- **Avoid when:** Walkthroughs where each shot carries UI that must be read, and films already cutting under 60 f per shot throughout.

### Empty ground after a cut

`ps-empty-ground-after-cut` · accent · energy medium · launch, feature, vertical

Right after some hard cuts the new stage shows for two empty frames before its type appears, a tiny palate cleanser that makes the cut read crisply without any flash.

- **Build:** On selected statement-to-statement hard cuts, not every cut, delay the incoming card's first element by 2 f: the new background is on screen at the cut frame, and the card's Sequence starts at cut + 2, its first element arriving on its normal E.out entrance. Use it where the outgoing card has already left by its own exit (an E.in move, or a fade over its last 8 f) and both stages are flat, so the two empty frames read as a breath and not as a dropped frame. Never use it on the film's first frame, where the hook has to open composed and moving.
- **Timing:** 2 empty frames at 60 fps; the incoming card starts at cut + 2 on its usual entrance; on at most a third of the cuts.
- **Use when:** Type-led films on white or flat stages with many statement cuts.
- **Avoid when:** Velocity-matched cuts, where the gap kills the momentum, and frame 0.

### The one long hold

`ps-one-long-hold` · accent · energy any · launch, feature, vertical

In a film that otherwise never stops, a single key claim sits nearly still for over a second, which tells the viewer it is the line to remember.

- **Build:** Reserve exactly one statement per film for this. After it settles (words on SPR.word or src/fx/Words.tsx), hold it 60-90 f with the type effectively still: breath(t, 0.015-0.02) from src/lib/camera.ts on its container (under 0.3 px/f at the edges) and a background breathing ±3% opacity, with no new element entering. Every other shot keeps a breath envelope or a camera move, so this hold is at least twice as long as any other near-still stretch. Leave on an E.in scale creep of +6% over the last 18 f, cutting on the creep's fastest frame.
- **Timing:** Settle 20-36 f; hold 60-90 f at under 0.3 px/f; exit creep +6% over 18 f E.in. Every other near-still run stays at or under 30 f.
- **Use when:** The single claim or number the film exists to say, in a launch film or short spot that is relentless everywhere else.
- **Avoid when:** Films already built on long holds, where it stops reading as special, or when two lines compete for the slot.

### One camera journey across one surface

`ps-single-camera-journey` · signature · energy calm · walkthrough, feature, launch

Every product state lives on one large surface and the film is a single camera path between poses; scene changes are pushes, pulls, orbits, whips and the interface's own window actions.

- **Build:** Lay out every UI state on one world container and keyframe 12-17 Shot poses (src/lib/camera.ts). Between poses, blend with lc(A, B, E.cam(p)) over 56-108 f, using E.inOut for at most one or two whips. At each pose the camera holds dead still while the UI acts (see locked holds). Move between product areas with the product's own behaviour instead of cuts: a window minimizing into a corner (20-22 f E.in), a bottom sheet (52 f E.out), a popover scaling from the cursor point (8-12 f), a modal (26 f). Chain them as exit, 4 f gap, entrance. Keep camera roll at or under 11 degrees on orbits, and give moves over 12 px/f the motion-blur pass.
- **Timing:** 0 cuts; about 3 moves per 10 s; moves 42-108 f E.cam; holds 18-252 f (median setup about 170 f); window actions 8-52 f.
- **Use when:** Walkthroughs of a single app, features where spatial orientation matters, and calm, premium product films.
- **Avoid when:** Multi-app or abstract stories, and films under 10 s.

### Oner through a morph chain

`ps-oner-morph-chain` · signature · energy medium · launch, feature, walkthrough

The whole film plays as one continuous shot, every new scene growing out of an object already on screen, with no hard cuts at all.

- **Build:** List one handoff object per beat boundary: a word gap, a box, a dot, a button, an icon, a card or a pill. At each boundary, duplicate the handoff element onto a top layer and swap the world beneath it: blur it 0 to 12 px while fading it to 40% opacity over the next scene's stage colour, swap, then clear the blur, so the luminance never dips toward black. Then interpolate the element's box (x, y, width, height, radius) from its old slot to the next scene's anchor: 5 f on E.in to break it loose, then 10-16 f of E.out geometry, all inside one global camera group (src/lib/camera.ts). Allow at most one masked cut, hidden behind a 3-6 f blur dip at a motion peak.
- **Timing:** About 3.6 morphs per 10 s; beats median 72-144 f, minimum 23-34 f, maximum 194-410 f; each morph 5 f E.in plus 10-16 f E.out; world swap 10-14 f under the held element.
- **Use when:** Multi-step workflows and multi-app stories, or any film where the viewer should never have to re-orient.
- **Avoid when:** Films that use polarity cuts as punctuation, or footage-based shots that cannot share elements.

### Score arranged to the acts

`ps-score-mapped-to-acts` · signature · energy any · launch, feature

The music's arrangement tells the story's structure: a sparse filtered intro, the drop on the first product frame, a breakdown for the calm act, a return for the proof, a final hit on the climax and the logo in silence.

- **Build:** Cut the picture first, then write audio/score.json sections bar-aligned to each ACT. Start with an intro of sparse layers (no sub, no kick, filtered pad and plucks, wide) that sounds at intent from frame 0 and builds about 10 dB. Put the drop on the first product shot (a drops entry on that act's downbeat, sub 8-12 f before the cut, kick on the cut frame). Run groove or drive for the proof, a breakdown (layers {drums: 0}) for the calmest act, a return on the next act's downbeat, a hit on the climax burst, and a hold with the lockup in silence. Hard cuts inside sections snap to onsets within ±4 f, act seams fall within ±4 f of the section change, and on the big drop the picture may lead the downbeat by up to 8 f.
- **Timing:** Intro 120-160 f; the drop and its cut within 1 f (or the picture leads by up to 8 f); cuts within ±4 f of onsets; breakdown 2-4 bars; the final hit's tail reaches -60 dB in about 35-55 f.
- **Use when:** 20-60 s launch films with clear acts, when the score is generated or its stems can be edited.
- **Avoid when:** A supplied track with a fixed structure (retime the picture to its bars instead), and 3-6 s stings.

### Silence as the default bed

`ps-silence-first-sound` · signature · energy calm · sting, feature, vertical

There is no running music: most of the film is true silence, sound appears only on decisive events, one low swell carries the single reveal act, and the audio cuts dead on the frame a key value lands.

- **Build:** Leave the sections array in audio/score.json empty, since bars outside every section get no music, and build the soundtrack only from src/sync.ts events, each tied to a decisive picture event. Open on a tick cluster whose first onset sits on frame 0 (five tick events at +0, 4, 8, 11 and 14 f under the opening mechanic). Give each appearance cut one centred tick (pan 0, weight 0.35, 1-3 f after the cut), and let a run of removals multiply the weight by 1.26 per tick so the run gets louder as the edit speeds up. The only sustained sound is one low pad under the reveal act: a section with style breakdown, layers {drums: 0, arp: 0, bells: 0, bass: 0} and level about 0.5 spanning that act, a swell event that peaks on the first reveal, and a one-bar tail section after it so the pad rings out instead of stopping. On each resolution frame (a number lands, a polarity cut), schedule nothing after the last tick so the sound stops within a frame, and put one bell there at weight 0.15 with pitch 'D8' as a faint high shimmer. Close by repeating the opening cluster at the same spacing under the stinger, then let the lockup's single land ring into silence over a slow push. The picture never sits still longer than 48 f, any designed freeze also gets a silences entry, and master.lufs is -16.
- **Timing:** At least 50% of the runtime silent, in gaps of 30-96 f between sound clusters. Opening cluster: 5 ticks over 14 f from frame 0. Reveal pad: on from the act's first frame, swell peak on the first reveal, about 42 f of plateau, about 84 f of ring-out. Sound stops within 1 f of each resolution; the shimmer bell (weight 0.15) fades over about 54 f. Removal ticks rise about 2 dB each. Lockup hold 90-120 f in silence after its single land, under a push of at least 10% across the hold.
- **Use when:** Short stings and feature spots under about 15 s, calm or premium tones, number and unlock reveals, and films with fewer than about one decisive event per second.
- **Avoid when:** Launch films and walkthroughs over about 20 s, dense sequences with more than about 3 visible events per second (use a steady bed instead), briefs that supply a music track, or feeds where the brief asks for high energy.

### Travelling thread object

`ps-continuity-thread` · signature · energy high · launch, feature

One small accent object (a dot, a packet or a streak) recurs across shots and acts, carrying the idea from problem to feature to feature as a single causal chain.

- **Build:** Build one Thread component: a round head 2-3% of frame height plus a tapered tail whose length scales with speed (tail = clamp(v * 1.5, 0, 240) px). Each scene drives it along a path (SVG getPointAtLength) with a speed curve that is always fast: E.contact into an impact or E.out into the distance. Across a cut it re-enters from the same screen side and at the same angle it left by, and it hands off by becoming the next scene's element (a check, a pin, a button fill), with squash() on contact. The full look surrounds the head with a bloom halo and shifts its tint on each beat (one beat goes violet). Use 3-5 appearances over 9-15 s at the same size every time.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Same Thread component in the single brand accent: an opaque head with a solid tapered tail and no halo or bloom, and the same hue on every beat. Impacts read through squash() and a hitPulse scale bump on the struck element rather than a flash of light. The full look relies on glow, purple; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** 3-5 appearances of 20-60 f each; head 2-3% of frame height; travel 20-60 px/f with true motion blur; contact squash over about 8 f; hitPulse(t, 2, 5) on the struck element.
