# Kinetic type — the reveal taxonomy (render-verified)

Load this when setting type in motion. Type is choreography: every law
already binds it — reading holds (A12), staggers (A3), exits (A1), the
ledger (A14), boundaries (A15), golden scale/leading (A10), only the
user's words (A8). This file is the device kit, each class verified in a
labeled demo against a real track.

## The reveal classes

| Class | Mechanics (verified numbers) | Reads as | Watch out |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Masked slide-up** (per word) | word rises through an `overflow:hidden` span, 108% travel, ~11f EASE_OUT, one word per beat; variation: descend from above | THE premium classic — editorial, Apple-adjacent | the mask must hug the line (pad ~0.08em) or descenders clip; last/emphasis word takes the glow |
| **Letter cascade** | per-letter rise 42px + fade, **1.5f stagger ±1f jitter** (A3/A4), ~9f each; variation: reverse direction | crafted, boutique | total = chars × 1.5f — budget against the reading hold; NEVER on long lines (>25 chars ≈ blur of motion) |
| **Emphasis slam** | ONE word, `heavy` spring (d16 k80 m1.6), squash on land + 2–4f shake echo, fired on a **bar-aligned kick** (A16) | the hit — stat/verdict moments | one per scene max (A3 rank-1); hero-scale overshoot territory (A1) |
| **Word swap** | sequential replace inside a SHARED mask: outgoing exits up as incoming rises — **the A15 continuation**; never a bare crossfade | list rhythm — "X · Y · Z" | give each word its A12 hold; the swap movement itself doesn't count as legible time |
| **Typewriter** | variable accelerating rhythm (start ~3.2f/char → ~1.4f, ±0.8f seeded jitter) + blinking caret (8f cycle) | device/terminal voice (A4) | the hold counts from typing START (A12 — viewers read along with the caret); scope it — it's a scene device, not a system |

Banned as primary reveals: bare opacity fade-in (A3's cheap-fade law applied
to type), per-letter opacity twinkle (dated), anything that moves crisp
focal text while it's being read (A5).

## Binding laws, applied to type

- **Hold math first** (A12): the floor `max(0.70s, 0.25s + chars ÷ 17)` per
  line — and the comprehension target `0.3s × words + 1.5s` for standalone/
  hero lines read cold — reveal and exit excluded. The reveal budget is
  what's LEFT of the phrase after the hold — if a cascade doesn't fit,
  shorten the cascade, never the hold.
- **Legibility thresholds while moving** (A12): `v_crit = h × fps ÷ k`
  (k ≈ 1.5–2.0) for text read in flight; entrances may exceed it only if
  the following hold carries the full reading time. Rotation ±15° max while
  being read (±45° = display-only territory); ≥24px rendered height for
  animated body text. **Past ±15° the hold pays A12's rotation tax
  `× (1 + |θ| ÷ 90)`** — ×1.33 at 30°, ×1.50 at 45° — charged on θ *as
  delivered to the reader*, so budget it before choosing the reveal class.
- **Emphasis words** (the SSOT's bolds): land them on strong beats, give
  them the glow/scale/color — and let the vocal LEVEL drive the aura when
  building to music (A16: the copy is the vocal's visual).
- **Exits**: 60–70% of entry duration, EASE_IN, usually upward — and every
  line boundary continues (A15): the next line enters from the departing
  line's origin or through the same mask.
- **Ledger** (A14): reveal class + direction + stagger rate is a device
  signature. Same class twice = vary an axis (direction, rhythm, color
  role) — the demo shows every class twice, varied.
- **Scale**: steps on the golden ratio (A10); display leading 0.95–1.1;
  one glow per frame (the boss).

## THE INERTIA LAW — real physics, three phases (F = ma throughout)

A letterform moved by its base is a mass with an anchored baseline. Newton
gives it exactly three behaviors, and the animation must produce all three
— nothing else reads as real (two failed models are recorded below):

**1 · LAUNCH — drag.** The base accelerates first; the mass above lags →
brief lean BACKWARD (opposite to travel), ∝ acceleration, ramping in over
the accel phase and decaying (~2.5f) once acceleration ends. Vertical
launches compress (up) / stretch (down). This is A2.5's drag, derived.

**2 · CRUISE — upright.** Constant velocity = no net force = NO
deformation. **The motion profile must be a trapezoid** (ramp → cruise →
hard stop): an eased arrival spends the momentum before the stop and
leaves nothing to whip — profile and reaction must agree or the physics is
fake regardless of the curve quality.

**3 · ARREST — the velocity-seeded ring-down.** The base stops dead; the
mass continues at v; linear momentum becomes angular momentum about the
baseline. **The angle does not jump — it starts at ZERO with maximal
angular velocity**, rises to its peak a quarter-period later, and rings
down through 2–3 visible rocks:

```ts
// θ(t) = A·e^(−t/τ)·sin(ω_d·t)   — ω_d ≈ 0.55 rad/f (period ~11f), τ ≈ 7f
// PEAK ∝ ARRIVAL SPEED: peakSkew = min(24°, 2.3·√v) · peakStretch = min(0.24, 0.021·√v)
// launch drag: dragPeak = min(8°, 1.1·√v), ramps in over accel, decays e^(−t/2.5)
// skew = ux·(drag − peakSk·ring) · scaleY = 1 − uy·peakSt·ring + uy·(launch term)
```

Speed-scaled peaks mean every dart whips differently — variance for free
(A14). Failed models, kept as warnings: **displacement-seeded** ("jump to
max angle, spring back" — the angle has no reason to be at max at t=0) and
**lean-while-moving** ("sprinter lean" — models an accelerating body, not
a cruising one). Velocity-seeding is the fix for both.

## The preset library (self-labeling glossary, all render-verified)

| Preset | Mechanics | Signature |
|---|---|---|
| **inertia** | LETTER BY LETTER, multi-directional: each letter darts in along its own LANE and shows the full three-phase law at ITS arrival (per-letter speed → per-letter ring); **lanes are collision-free by construction** — middle letters travel vertically (a column is exclusive), horizontal entries only at the word's ENDS where nothing is parked in the path — **horizontal → skewX rock · vertical → scaleY stretch/squash settle**, all `transformOrigin` baseline | momentum you can see, letter by letter |
| **gravity** | full deterministic physics sim (precomputed at module load, seeded → A0 holds): letters as heavy bodies + raining balls, circle-circle impulse collisions, letters knocked + spun but spring-restored to home/upright — the word survives readable | a physics playground — letters as objects among objects |
| **fade** | pure staggered opacity (2.5f stagger, 12f ease) — NO movement | the humblest entrance; motion disappears |
| **typing** | accelerating 3→1.4f/char + block caret | terminal voice (scoped device) |
| **trace** | stroked outline draws per letter (dashoffset, ~16f) then fill blooms | skeletal → solid; "written" territory |
| **painted** | CURSIVE STROKE-CONSTRUCTION: **no font, no mask** — each letter IS its ductus, connected so the pen never lifts inside the word, ribbon-rendered with the pressure model (thick downstrokes, thin connectors), i dotted and t crossed at the end; see the painted system below | real writing, weight and all |
| **morph (TRUE)** | vector letterforms reshape point-by-point into geometry and back — see the morph system below | fluid typography — the letter IS the shape |
| **flip** | per-letter card flips rotateX between words, 2.5f stagger | mechanical swap (kept as its own device) |
| **arc** | the rail DRAWS FIRST (dashed, ~14f), the word rides it with tangent rotation, the rail fades — signaling law applied: a path move is illegible until the path is visible | path motion that explains itself |

**A face per voice.** Presets carry their own typographic voice — pick the
family that IS the motion: Impact-class for inertia slams · geometric sans
for physics · high-contrast serif (Didot class) for fades · monospace for
typing · the extracted vector face for true morph · painted has NO font —
its ductus skeletons are its face. One scoped face per device (A14 / the
C2 brand allowance governs what's permitted per project).

**Face weight is mass.** Heavier letterforms move with more inertia —
slower acceleration, heavier springs, more follow-through; light faces are
nimble — snap/smooth springs, quicker settles. Pair the face's weight to
the spring preset (Impact → `heavy`, a light Didot → `snap`) and the
physics comes free (A2.1). A hairline face on a heavy slam, or Impact
fluttering in on a feather ease, is a face/motion contradiction — same
family as A17's meaning contradictions.

## Exits in the device's voice (render-verified set)

A preset's exit is the same device run BACKWARDS or ONE STEP TOO FAR —
never a transform on the scene container (A15's element-exit law). The
verified vocabulary:

- **inertia** — each letter launches back out its arrival lane: pure
  acceleration, so only the growing launch lean shows (it never arrives,
  so it never rings).
- **gravity** — the floor gives way; the container is the physics world,
  the one case where moving it IS moving the elements (½gt², slight
  tumble).
- **fade** — staggered letter fade-out in reverse reading order (legal:
  an element's own decay, not a crossfade between unrelated things).
- **typing** — BACKSPACE at accelerating key-repeat, caret alive to the
  end. (A CRT-collapse wrapper was the rejected first cut.)
- **trace** — strokes retract in reverse stagger while the fill drains.
- **painted** — the brush RETRACES its own ribbons in reverse writing
  order, head riding the retreating tip. Failed model: "painting it out"
  in ground color — over any gradient ground the cover stroke reads as a
  floating flat bar; cover-strokes only work on flat grounds.
- **morph** — letters morph out to their shapes once more and each shape
  collapses to zero where it stands (fixed-point scale: translate by
  `(1 − s) · center` so it shrinks about its own centre — A15's
  convergence).
- **flip** — one flip too many, per letter, to edge-on (90°) and gone —
  with the swap cycle FROZEN at its last rest pose first (a cycling
  device exits from rest).

Timing: exits run ~60–70% of entries (A1), staggered per element, and
OVERRUN the cut a few frames painted on top of the successor (A15).

**Continuity law for composed motions (render-found on inertia v1):** when a
travel phase hands off to a settle spring, the driven value must be EQUAL on
both sides of the handoff — v1 leaned ∝ velocity (≈0 by arrival) then the
spring re-kicked from full lean = a one-frame jitter. v2: lean into the run
(~5f), HOLD while travelling, spring-rock from the held value. Same family
as klik-cam's global-frame continuity trap.

## Motion semantics — the alignment table (A17 applied to type)

Motion is a semantic channel; pick the strategy that says what the words
say. Contradiction weakens the line even when the move is beautiful
(the canonical pair: "BREAKING THROUGH" — staccato letter-snaps at 3f
intervals with ±5° jitter, then the second word driving through with a
hard overshoot = visceral; the same phrase on a gentle fade = self-refuting).

| Semantic quality | Motion strategy | Timing pattern | Typical use |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Urgency** | fast, direct paths | short (<0.5s) | alerts, breaking moments |
| **Authority** | slow, centered motion | long holds (>3s) | brand statements, titles |
| **Playfulness** | bouncy, overshoot | elastic easing (`bounce`) | casual, character |
| **Precision** | grid-aligned, constant velocity | quantized, dead stops | specs, data, terminals |
| **Chaos** | erratic, multi-axis | seeded-irregular timing (A0) | disruption, glitch |
| **Elegance** | smooth curves, soft fades | `EASE` 1–2s | luxury, formal |

Directional/velocity/rhythm/transformation semantics are the law itself
(A17). Chaos rows still render deterministically — "random" timing is
seeded, always.

## THE PRECISION DEVICE (scoped linearity — A1's one exception)

The physics: a *driven* system (stepper motor, print head, CNC) is
velocity-controlled — it moves at constant speed and **stops dead**; the
controller absorbs the momentum. A *free* mass rings down (the inertia
law). Both are real; what's fake is mixing them. The device's grammar is
all-or-nothing:

- Constant-velocity moves and **hard stops with ZERO settle/overshoot** —
  a linear move that bounces is incoherent (nothing is left to bounce);
  an eased move that dead-stops reads as a glitch. Profile and reaction
  agree — the inertia law's rule, resolved to the opposite pole.
- Distances and durations **quantized**: whole beats/frames, snap-to-grid
  positions. Machine timing sits naturally on the bar grid (A16/B1).
- **Semantic gate:** only when the subject IS mechanical/technical/data —
  never emotive copy, never a default keyframe accident.
- **Scope:** one context per piece (A14), technical/monospace voice,
  ledger-recorded, never in the same shot as inertia devices.
- `lint-motion.mjs` flags the linear easing — waive it by name:
  `// klik-lint-disable-next-line — PRECISION device (A1/A17)`.

## THE PAINTED SYSTEM (stroke construction — render-verified)

Painting is CONSTRUCTION, not revelation. If the letterform exists before
the brush touches it and paint merely uncovers it, it is not painting —
two failed models are recorded below. The real system (cursive + pressure):

1. **Break each letter into its ductus** — the ordered stroke skeleton a
   writer actually uses. For script: one continuous body stroke per letter
   (entry upstroke from the baseline → body → baseline exit), letters
   CONNECTED exit-to-entry so the pen never lifts inside the word; the
   **deferred strokes (i-dot, t-cross) draw AFTER the word completes** —
   real writing order. Hand-author each stroke as a few-point skeleton in
   a per-letter box (baseline y=100, x-height ~52, ascender ~30, descender
   ~135); per-letter advance widths, never monospace; slant is a shear on
   the points (`x += (baseline − y) × tan(slant)`), not a CSS transform.
2. **Catmull-Rom the skeletons** into dense polylines — the hand-authored
   points stay few, the pen path curves like a real stroke, and all
   arc-length math works on the result.
3. **Line weight is the pressure model — never constant.** A uniform
   stroke width is the flat-weight tell. Render each stroke as a **ribbon**
   (offset the path ±width/2 along its normal, fill the polygon): width
   per point = `wMin + (wMax − wMin) × downwardComponent` — **downstrokes
   thick (pressure), upstrokes and connectors thin** (the broad-nib/
   pointed-pen law), tapered over the first/last ~30px of arc (touchdown
   and lift). Retraces (p, n) redraw thin over their thick downstroke,
   exactly as ink does.
4. **The brush draws at constant px/f speed** — ribbon cut at the live
   tip, round start cap, bristle turbulence (`feTurbulence` +
   displacement) for edge, a **brush-head ellipse riding the tip rotated
   to the tangent**. SPEED sized so word + diacritics complete with the
   A12 hold still left in the window — hold math first, as always.
5. **Mid-frames must be real partial letterforms** — a cursive `n` is a
   single leg before its arch; the `i` sits undotted until the word is
   done. That is the proof it's construction; a reveal never produces
   those states.

Failed models, kept as warnings: **outline dash-trace** (reads as
graffiti/neon tube, user-rejected), **clipPath-stencil zigzag fill** (a
masked reveal wearing paint texture, user-rejected — the letter
pre-exists), and **constant-width polyline strokes** (block letterforms
with butted caps: every junction shows a seam cut and the weight is dead
flat, user-rejected — ribbons + pressure are the fix).

## THE TRUE MORPH SYSTEM (fluid typography — render-verified v1)

"Morph" means RESHAPING the letterforms, not swapping them. Pipeline:

1. **Remake the font in vector at build time** — `opentype.js` loads the
   TTF, glyph outlines flatten to polylines (14 samples/curve).
2. **Canonicalize** every contour: resample to a fixed N (96) points by
   arc length · force clockwise winding · rotate the index so point 0 is
   the topmost — this stops morphs twisting.
3. **Targets are rings in the same canonical form** (N points, clockwise
   from top): circle/tri/square/star — or another glyph's contours.
4. **Morph = lerp the point sets** (easeInOut ~14f), render as
   `<path fill-rule="evenodd">`.
5. **Holes** (O/R/P counters): pair the inner contour with a sub-pixel
   degenerate ring (r ≈ 0.01) at the target's centre — the counter
   collapses on the way out and re-emerges on the way back. (r = 1 leaves
   a visible dot — render-found.)

Known v1 limit: arc-length correspondence can pinch mid-morph on
donut-like glyphs (O briefly waists). v2 upgrade when needed: angular
resampling around the centroid, or match by normalized angle.

## Study — the canon (Hackernoon guide taxonomy)

The guide's examples are external embeds (Dribbble/Tumblr; Gfycat is dead)
so they couldn't be frame-extracted — this study is from its taxonomy and
the named artists' documented signatures, to be refined against real refs
via the method's reference-analysis pass. **A separate seven-title canon
HAS been frame-verified** (Honda, MK12 ×2, Picturemill, BUCK, Oxfam,
Ginetta) — see the study table in `references/layout.md`; where the two
disagree, the frame-verified numbers win:

- **Fluid typography / morphing** (TAPE, Al Boardman) — the prize: letters
  as living vector material. Boardman-style state transitions keep VOLUME
  roughly constant mid-morph and land on grid-crisp end states — morph
  wants soft middles, decisive ends (our easeIO does this).
- **Create/destroy** (David Stanfield) — words aggregate from shapes /
  dissolve into them: our morph system run one-directional, with staggered
  particles. Hero device (A14). **Frame-verified variant (Ginetta "We
  simplify"):** aggregate from *letter-parts* rather than shapes — stems,
  bowls and dots scattered at deconstructed positions, converging into the
  word, each fragment carrying its own colour that resolves to mono on
  arrival. The colour convergence is what makes the assembly read as order
  emerging from chaos; without it the fragments read as debris. A worked
  example of A17 — the reveal enacts the word.
- **Inventive metaphor** — serifs become feet, counters become eyes:
  per-glyph character rigs; pairs with the expression-rig pattern.
- **Arc/path motion** (dudenas) — baselines are paths, not rails.
- **Signaling motion** — the small move that cues the big one (=klik-cam's
  motivation law, element side).

## Imported laws (kinetic-typography canon)

- **Maintain linearity** — reading order survives the animation; letters may
  arrive playfully but never out of reading sequence for running copy (A12's
  gaze law applied to reveals; display single words may break it for effect).
- **Maintain relativity** — typographic elements move relative to EACH
  OTHER; a line is a system, not independent sprites (A3's phrase law).
- **Signaling motion** — a subtle pre-move can cue a larger one (pairs with
  klik-cam's motivation law: the signal is what the camera reacts to).
- **Fluid/create-destroy territory** (type ⇄ shapes, aggregation builds) —
  powerful, expensive; treat as hero devices, one per piece (A14).

Sources: Hackernoon "Kinetic Typography Quickstart" taxonomy + principles;
Material Design type anatomy (baseline/x-height as physical structure).
Springs/curves come from `references/motion-library.md`.

# Layout & positioning — the composition models (frame-verified)

Load this when deciding **where copy lives and how the frame relates to it
across a sequence** — the axis above the reveal device. `kinetic-type.md`
answers *how a word appears*; this file answers *where it sits, what else is
on screen with it, and what the frame does while it's read*. Camera grammar
stays klik-cam's (C0, CAM-1..6); this file only says which model the camera
is serving.

**Pick ONE model per passage and record it in the spec** — like a dial value,
never a silent drift. Mixing models inside one passage is the failure mode:
copy that half-accumulates and half-replaces reads as a broken system.

Provenance is labelled throughout: **[measured]** = extracted from the
reference frames · **[observed]** = read off frames, not counted ·
**[proposed]** = ours, to be render-verified.

## The five models

| Model | Copy lives | The frame | Canon ref | Reach for it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Fixed anchor** | one slot, all copy cycles through it | locked | Honda "Keep Up" | manifestos over a live plate; maximum negative space |
| **Accretion artboard** | a persistent 2D canvas; copy accumulates, nothing exits | travels across the canvas | MK12 "Brazil Inspired", Oxfam Ebola | dense energy, editorial montage, sequences that must feel authored as one artefact |
| **Growing line** | one line, anchored at its start, extending | locked | Childline "First Step" | long-form narration, quiet emotional copy |
| **World-space type** | a static object in the 3D scene | reveals it by parallax | Picturemill "Panic Room" | type as architecture; live-action integration |
| **Annotation layer** | hairline overlay tracked to the plate | follows the plate | MK12 "Stranger Than Fiction" | measuring/annotating a world rather than stating over it |

Only **Fixed anchor** matches the default enter → hold → exit assumption the
rest of this skill is written against. The other four need the resolutions
below, or the laws read as violated when they are not.

---

## 1 · FIXED ANCHOR

One slot. Every word cycles through it; nothing else on screen moves.
The entire craft is hold timing — there is no reveal to hide behind.

- **The anchor is a feature of the PLATE, not the frame centre.** Honda sets
  the word's baseline exactly on the horizon at ~48.5% frame height, dead
  centre horizontally — not the geometric 50% **[measured]**. Type anchored
  to a real line in the footage sits *in* the shot; type at frame centre sits
  *on* it. Find the plate's line (horizon, table edge, architectural rule)
  and set the baseline there.
- **Scale is small and constant.** Cap height ~10% of the active image
  height **[measured]**; the count-in and the logo are the only scale
  changes. Emphasis is weight and colour, not size.
- **Everything else is the plate.** Product/subject enters the plate itself
  and shares the anchor line — never a second graphic layer competing.

Reading holds are A12's, unchanged — unless the passage is a declared
**SPEED-READ device** (A12's licensed exception), whose measured grammar is:

| | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| Base rate | **4f/word @25fps** (0.13–0.16s) | [measured] |
| Sentence-end hold | **12–18f**, 3–4.5× base | [measured] |
| Ratchet across the piece | 5f → 4f → 3f, bursting to 2f | [measured] |
| Overall | ~5.9 words/sec | [measured] |

**The long hold is the punctuation** — it is literally the full stop, and it
is the only reason the passage stays parseable. A speed-read passage with an
even rate is unreadable noise, not a device. Honda: 204 word events over
34.9s of manifesto.

---

## 2 · ACCRETION ARTBOARD — and the reading pocket

Copy is **never replaced**. It accumulates on one persistent 2D canvas, and
the camera travels across that canvas. Old copy exits by leaving frame under
camera motion — never by animating out.

### The reading pocket (resolves A12 × CAM-6)

The naive read is that accretion violates A12 ("the eye reads at rest") and
CAM-6 ("gaze-anchored, margin-capped — the focal centroid never leaves the
inner ~8%"). It does not, because **in accretion the reading frame is not the
video frame.**

- Define a **reading pocket**: a fixed region in *screen* space where the
  active run is always delivered — comfortable scale, near-horizontal angle.
- The camera moves so **the pocket stays put while the canvas travels
  beneath it.**
- A12 holds: the eye *is* at rest — in the pocket. Reading time is budgeted
  for the run while it occupies the pocket, and the pocket's contents are
  what `v_crit` is measured against — not the canvas.
- CAM-6 holds: the margin cap is measured against **the pocket**, not the
  canvas centroid. The boss never leaves the pocket; the canvas does.

If a run is read while crossing the frame rather than while parked in the
pocket, that is the ordinary A12 violation and the ordinary fix applies.
The pocket is a coordinate change, not a licence.

### The armature

- **A new phrase gets a new baseline at a new angle, anchored to the previous
  run's terminus** — the hinge. Baselines run 30–45° off horizontal
  **[observed]**; letters build *along* the baseline rather than the word
  popping in whole.
- **The camera counter-rotates** so the active baseline reads near-horizontal
  in the pocket while older runs skew away. This is what buys the ±45°
  display allowance in A12 — the copy is rotated *in canvas space*, not in
  reading space. **This is also what makes accretion affordable:** A12's
  rotation dwell tax `× (1 + |θ| ÷ 90)` charges θ **as delivered**, so a run
  authored at 45° on the canvas but presented at ~5° in the pocket pays ~6%,
  not 50%. A pocket that delivers copy still tilted pays the full tax — and
  at accretion's ~0.87s composition cycle there is no room for it. Counter-
  rotation is a timing requirement, not a stylistic flourish.
- **Adjacent runs at different angles must differ in colour role.** Brazil
  alternates its two inks between neighbouring runs precisely because
  geometry alone leaves the reading order ambiguous where two baselines meet
  **[observed]**. Two adjacent runs in the same ink at different angles is
  the ambiguity bug.
- **Scale ratio is extreme** — hero:caption ≈ 10–20:1 **[observed]**. The
  caption tier is *texture, not information* (see the ladder below).
- **A fixed corner mark** (both MK12 pieces hold one bottom-right for the
  full runtime **[observed]**) establishes a stable UI plane above the
  moving canvas. Cheap, and it is what stops a constantly-moving canvas
  reading as unmoored.

### The demotion ladder (resolves A10)

In accretion the boss is **the newest run**. A10's one-boss law is satisfied
by demotion, not by exit — and the demotion is mechanical, not art-directed:

1. On the next run's arrival, every existing run steps **down one tier**:
   hero → secondary → caption/texture.
2. Each step is **scale ÷ φ** (A10's golden steps, 1.618 default).
3. A completed block may additionally **rotate to the margin** — Oxfam turns
   its finished stack 90° and parks it at the left edge, holding it as
   context **[observed]**.
4. **Caption tier is texture: it is NOT budgeted for reading time.** This is
   load-bearing beyond A10 — without it, accretion blows A12's Σ-holds
   feasibility sum on the third run. Anything that must be *read* has to be
   at hero or secondary tier while it is read.

### How A15 resolves

Accretion has no departing line, so "boundaries continue, never reset" is
satisfied **trivially** — continuity is total because nothing resets, and
A15's element-exit clause is moot where there are no exits. The boundary
that does need continuing is the **hinge**: each new run's baseline anchors
to the previous run's terminus. That is A15's principle in layout terms.
Likewise A15's "incoming attractor within ~2f of every cut" applies at
passage boundaries only — inside an accretion passage there are no cuts.

### Rhythm

Brazil runs **~175 settle/move cycles in 152s — a new composition roughly
every 0.87s** **[measured]**; settled runs median 3f, moving runs median 6f
**[measured]**. It is almost never at rest: the "holds" are micro-settles,
and only hero compositions rest (max ~1.2s). Budget accretion as a high-C0.5
device — at pacing 1–2 the model reads as sludge.

---

## 3 · GROWING LINE

One line, anchored at its start, extending as the sentence completes.
Position stable; content grows. Childline carries a four-minute film on it.

- Left-anchored (or start-anchored for RTL), vertically centred, in a large
  empty field. The anchor **does not** re-centre as the line grows — optical
  re-centring on every word is the tell that kills it **[observed]**.
- The A12 hold counts from the point the line is **complete**, not from the
  first fragment — the viewer reads the finished sentence.
- **Emotional register drives type register** (A17, layout side): quiet copy
  sits small, low-contrast, in maximum negative space; emotional peaks
  switch to large display type. Two registers, switched on story beats, not
  on a timer **[observed]**.
- Ground-colour flip (Childline alternates a cream and a near-black
  aubergine **[observed]**) is the scene-change device — the model needs no
  camera at all.

---

## 4 · WORLD-SPACE TYPE

Type is a static object standing in the 3D scene at architectural scale.
**The reveal IS the parallax** — nothing animates. Camera grammar is
klik-cam's; what this file owns is the integration checklist:

- **Occlusion is the tell that sells it.** Scene geometry must pass *in front
  of* the type — Panic Room runs buildings across the letterforms
  **[observed]**. Type that never occludes reads as an overlay no matter how
  good the track is.
- **Grade-match, never pure white.** The type takes the plate's white point
  (a dirty, desaturated white against that sky) **[observed]**.
- **Atmospheric haze with distance** — far type sits back in the same fog
  curve as the far buildings.
- **DOF applies to type** — far names soften. Type exempt from the lens is
  type that isn't in the world (A5).

---

## 5 · ANNOTATION LAYER

A hairline vector overlay tracked to the plate that **measures and annotates**
the world rather than stating over it. Distinct from every other model: it is
not the message, it is a data layer about the message.

- **1px hairlines, light, low opacity** — it must never compete with the
  plate **[observed]**.
- **It counts and measures things that are actually there**: paving slabs
  numbered under a walking figure, the eight steps of a tie knot, arithmetic
  floating beside the character doing it **[observed]**. Annotation that
  annotates nothing is decoration.
- **Rectangles crop the plate into inset panel grids** — the overlay
  supplies a composition grid on top of the footage.
- Perspective-matched to surfaces; numbers pin to objects and track them.
- A fixed corner mark again holds the UI plane.

Expensive to author. Treat as a hero device (A14) — one piece, one system.

---

## Study — the canon (frame-verified 2026-08-06)

Seven references pulled and studied frame-by-frame; measurements above come
from these. This supersedes the inference-only study note in
`kinetic-type.md` for these titles.

| Piece | Model | What it proves |
|---|---|---|

| MK12 "Brazil Inspired" | Accretion | the armature, the hinge, colour disambiguation, the ~0.87s composition cycle |

# The motion library — canonical springs & curves (measured)

The A1 law says "define curves once in `src/motion.ts`, never inline" and
names the presets — this file IS those presets, with values **measured from
the real `spring()` implementation** (overshoot % and settle time read off
rendered plots, not guessed). Copy the code block as the project's
`motion.ts`; pick by the move-class tables; vary per the A14 ledger.

## Springs (physics moments: land, pop, gather, arrival)

| Preset | config | Measured | Feels like | Use for |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **snap** | d13 · k180 · m0.6 | **8.1% overshoot · settled 400ms (f12@30)** | a finger-flick | UI presses, micro-accents, kick hits on small elements |
| **bounce** | d9 · k150 · m0.8 | **23.8% overshoot · settled 833ms (f25)** | a dropped ball, two visible bounces | playful lands, mascots, hero/stat moments that may exaggerate (A2.10) |
| **smooth** | d26 · k120 · m1.0 | **0% overshoot · settled 633ms (f19)** | a door with a damper | elegant arrivals, panels, anything near body text |
| **heavy** | d16 · k80 · m1.6 | **4.3% overshoot · settled 933ms (f28)** | mass arriving | big cards, bass-led moments (A16 weight), full-frame objects |

Rules: overshoot budget follows A1 (2–4% UI · more only on heroes — so
`snap` is already at the UI ceiling and `bounce` is hero-only). Heavier =
slower settle; if a heavy element must settle fast, it isn't heavy — change
the element, not the physics. Springs drive HITS; beziers drive TRAVEL.

## Easing curves (travel)

| Name | cubic-bezier | Character | Use for |
|---|---|---|---|
| **EASE** | (0.83, 0, 0.17, 1) | the house thin-peak | most travel — the default |
| **EASE_OUT** | (0.16, 1, 0.30, 1) | instant burst, long settle | entrances |
| **EASE_IN** | (0.70, 0, 0.84, 0) | building acceleration | anticipation wind-ups & exits ONLY |
| **WHIP** | (0.90, 0, 0.10, 1) | near-vertical peak | slams, transitions, C0.5-dial-5 moves — pair with smear frames (A5) |
| **GLIDE** | (0.40, 0, 0.20, 1) | gentle, materials-style | dense UI walkthroughs, moves near reading text |

## Canonical `src/motion.ts`

```ts
import { Easing, spring } from "remotion";

// travel curves — never redefine inline (A1)
export const EASE      = Easing.bezier(0.83, 0, 0.17, 1);
export const EASE_OUT  = Easing.bezier(0.16, 1, 0.30, 1);
export const EASE_IN   = Easing.bezier(0.70, 0, 0.84, 0);
export const WHIP      = Easing.bezier(0.90, 0, 0.10, 1);
export const GLIDE     = Easing.bezier(0.40, 0, 0.20, 1);

// spring presets — physics moments (measured: see motion-library.md)
export const SPRING = {
  snap:   { damping: 13, stiffness: 180, mass: 0.6 },
  bounce: { damping: 9,  stiffness: 150, mass: 0.8 },
  smooth: { damping: 26, stiffness: 120, mass: 1.0 },
  heavy:  { damping: 16, stiffness: 80,  mass: 1.6 },
} as const;
export const hit = (frame: number, from: number, fps: number,
  preset: keyof typeof SPRING = "snap") =>
  spring({ frame: frame - from, fps, config: SPRING[preset] });

// beat grid (B1) — fill from the music map / analyzer
export const FPS = 30;
export const BPM = 0;                // ← project value
export const FIRST_BEAT = 0;         // ← project value
export const FRAMES_PER_BEAT = BPM ? (60 / BPM) * FPS : 0;
export const beat = (n: number) => Math.round(FIRST_BEAT + n * FRAMES_PER_BEAT);
export const bar  = (n: number) => beat(n * 4);
```

**A14 note:** the ledger tracks spring/curve choices as device parameters —
two elements may share `snap`; they may not share `snap` at identical
amplitude, delay, AND duration. Vary at least one.

# Music → motion recipes — implementing §A16

Load this when building anything that moves to music. It turns the method's
analyzer output (`analyze-audio.py --json`: the music map + `events` +
`levels`) into element motion. **Every recipe here was render-verified against
a real song in an isolated POC** — kick impacts, snare echoes, hat shimmer,
vocal glow, bass mass, and a tier-driven section shift, checked in frames.

Camera-side mappings live in `klik-cam` CAM-5 — do not mix the layers.

## The data

```jsonc
// analyze-audio.py --json out.json  (stem mode via demucs when installed)
{
  "frames_per_beat": 14.52, "first_downbeat_frame": 33,
  "energy_tier_per_bar": "111222155543…",        // tier 1–5 per bar
  "music_map": [ { "bars": [4,12], "start_frame": 265, "tier": 1.8,
                   "lead": "bass", "attack": "sharp (~23ms)", … } ],
  "events": { "kick": [267,272,…], "snare": […], "hats": […],
              "vocals": […], "bass": […], "guitar": […], "piano": […] },
  "levels": { "kick": [0.01,…], "vocals": […], … }  // per-frame, 0–1
}
```
Import it into `src/` (`resolveJsonModule: true`) — it's data, deterministic,
pure function of frame (A0). Band mode gives `low/mid/high` keys instead;
same recipes, coarser sources.

## Core helpers (verified — copy into `src/music.ts`)

```ts
/** Latest event ≤ frame → exp-decay intensity 1→0. Attack is INSTANT —
 *  a transient's rise is under one frame (A16); the decay is the settle.
 *  decay 3–4 ≈ tight percussive · 8–10 ≈ ringing/heavy. */
export const hitPulse = (events: number[], frame: number, decay = 3.5, window = 18) => {
  let lo = 0, hi = events.length - 1, best = -1;
  while (lo <= hi) {
    const m = (lo + hi) >> 1;
    if (events[m] <= frame) { best = events[m]; lo = m + 1; } else hi = m - 1;
  }
  if (best < 0 || frame - best > window) return 0;
  return Math.exp(-(frame - best) / decay);
};

/** Smoothed level follower — sustain-shaped amplitude. ±4f ≈ 130ms box
 *  average: musical, not jittery. Hits ride EVENTS; glow/mass ride LEVELS. */
export const levelAt = (levels: number[], frame: number, smooth = 4) => {
  let s = 0, k = 0;
  for (let f = frame - smooth; f <= frame + smooth; f++)
    if (f >= 0 && f < levels.length) { s += levels[f]; k++; }
  return k ? s / k : 0;
};

/** Energy tier (1–5) of the bar under this frame. */
export const tierAt = (frame: number) => { /* bar = (frame−DOWN0)/(FPB·4) → TIERS[bar] */ };

/** Every nth event — "mapped, not literal" (A16/A4): sample the hats. */
export const everyNth = (ev: number[], n: number, off = 0) => ev.filter((_, i) => i % n === off);

/** THE INTEGRAL LAW (render-found): any rotation/travel whose SPEED rides
 *  a music signal must drive its position from the ACCUMULATED rate —
 *  `pos = frame × rate(frame)` JUMPS whenever the rate moves, by
 *  frame × Δrate: measured 733° in ONE frame at f≈3000 on a track whose
 *  tiers alternate bar-to-bar ("the oval jitters"); the integral's worst
 *  step was 1.15° — its top speed, smooth by construction. Same
 *  continuity family as the handoff/glide laws. Precompute at module
 *  scope (A0-pure, like a physics sim): */
export const rateIntegral = (base: number, gain: number): number[] => {
  const n = ((LEVELS.full ?? LEVELS.low ?? []).length || 4000) + 90;
  const out: number[] = new Array(n);
  let a = 0;
  for (let f = 0; f < n; f++) { a += base + gain * heatAt(f); out[f] = a; }
  return out;   // usage: const ORBIT = rateIntegral(0.25, 0.9)  →
};              //        rotate(ORBIT[clamp(frame)]) — never frame × rate
```

## The mappings (each render-verified)

| Source | Drives | Recipe |
|---|---|---|
| **kick** | THE primary hit | squash-pop `scale(1+0.05p, 1+0.10p)` (A2.1) + seeded screen-shake ±3px·p + shadow/ground pulse. `decay 4` — heavy things settle slower (A16 weight). One rank-1 mover at a time (A10). |
| **snare** | secondary echo | accent elements (side bars, underline flicks) driven by `hitPulse(snare, frame - 3)` — the **3f lag** makes it an A3 echo, not a competitor. Amplitude ≤ ~60% of the kick's. |
| **hats** | micro life | `everyNth(hats, 2)` → shimmer field, per-element phase offset (`frame - (i % 4)`), amplitude tiny (opacity/scale ticks). Never every hat — that's mickey-mousing. |
| **vocals** | the focal's aura | `levelAt(vocals)` → glow radius/intensity on the copy (the focal element, A10). Vocal *onsets* can cue word-emphasis in kinetic type. |
| **bass** | mass & ground | `levelAt(bass, 6)` (slower smooth — bass is slow) → background blob scale, vignette depth, drift amplitude. Weight, not flashes. |
| **guitar/piano** | melodic accents | mid-amplitude accent events where the arrangement leads with them (check the map's per-section patterns — don't invent hits the section doesn't have). |
| **tier** | density + local pacing | element count, idle-life amplitude, palette heat all step with `tierAt(frame)`; tier ≥ 4 unlocks the piece's hero devices (A14: never spent on verses). |
| **section boundary** | scene character | `music_map[i].start_frame` is where palettes/density/devices switch — boundaries continue per A15; the switch rides a transition, never a hard swap mid-hold. |

## Discipline (what keeps this from being a visualizer)

- **Match each parameter to its signal's TIME-SCALE.** Transient pulses →
  frame-scale (hits, squash). Levels → word/beat-scale (glow, mass). Bar
  tiers → density and speed. **Temperature/palette → SECTION-scale only**:
  average the tier over ±2 bars before mapping to hue — a color that
  flickers with bar-to-bar tier changes reads as noise, not heat
  (render-found on a track whose tiers alternate every bar). Drastic
  palette maps (blue → violet → red → gold across the tier range — the
  cool→hot path that never passes green) want the SLOW signal; give the
  fast signals to geometry.

- **Reactive motion is garnish, not choreography.** The scene's designed
  moves (entrances, travels, reveals) stay authored on the beat grid (B1);
  events drive *impacts and life*, levels drive *amplitudes*. If removing the
  music data would leave nothing moving, the scene was never designed (A6/A12
  still bind).
- **Amplitude subordination (A10):** reactive accents never outrank the focal
  move. A hat shimmer that pulls the eye off the copy is a defect.
- **Swells have no events** — sections marked "no transients: swell/pad
  territory" are ramp territory: long `EASE_IN` pushes and blooms driven by
  `levelAt`, no pulses (A16 attack law).
- **Verify with both checks (A9):** stills at event frames prove the hits
  land; the arithmetic (event frame vs visual peak ≤ 1f apart) proves sync a
  still can't show. Watch one section boundary with audio before shipping.

#!/usr/bin/env node
/**
 * klik-anim motion lint — the craft laws that a machine can check.
 *
 *   node lint-motion.mjs [paths...] [--strict] [--json]
 *
 * Defaults to scanning `src`. Zero dependencies; Node 18+.
 *
 * This catches ONLY the mechanical laws — determinism, easing hygiene, the
 * layout-property ban, the perspective/filter conflict, and a heuristic for
 * unvaried device reuse. Everything that needs eyes (hierarchy, gaze path,
 * reading holds, copy discipline, material) is still the A9 look-pass and the
 * Part D checklist. A clean lint is not a pre-flight pass.
 *
 * Waivers, when a law is being broken deliberately:
 *   // klik-lint-disable-next-line animated-layout-prop — deliberate container morph (A7)
 *   // klik-lint-disable inline-curve                     (file scope, anywhere in the file)
 * Use `*` for the rule id to waive every rule. Always give a reason.
 */

import { readdirSync, readFileSync, statSync } from "node:fs";
import { join, relative, resolve, sep } from "node:path";

const SOURCE_EXT = new Set([".ts", ".tsx", ".js", ".jsx", ".mjs"]);
const SKIP_DIR = new Set([
  "node_modules", "dist", "build", "out", "coverage",
  ".git", ".next", ".cache", "public", "assets", "out-tsc",
]);

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *
 * Source blanking — comments become spaces, so a rule never fires on
 * `// never call Math.random()`. Offsets and line numbers are preserved
 * exactly, so both variants share one set of line numbers.
 *
 *   blankNonCode(src)        → comments AND string contents blanked.
 *                              Use for anything that must not match a
 *                              literal: determinism, timers, easing.
 *   blankNonCode(src, false) → comments only, strings intact. Use where
 *                              the evidence legitimately lives inside a
 *                              string or template: `blur(...)`,
 *                              'cubic-bezier(...)'.
 * ------------------------------------------------------------------ */

function blankNonCode(src, blankStrings = true) {
  const out = src.split("");
  const tpl = []; // brace depth per open template interpolation
  let mode = "code";
  let i = 0;

  const space = (n) => { if (out[n] !== "\n") out[n] = " "; };
  const spaceString = (n) => { if (blankStrings) space(n); };

  while (i < src.length) {
    const c = src[i];
    const d = src[i + 1];

    if (mode === "code") {
      if (c === "/" && d === "/") { space(i); space(i + 1); mode = "line"; i += 2; continue; }
      if (c === "/" && d === "*") { space(i); space(i + 1); mode = "block"; i += 2; continue; }
      if (c === "'") { mode = "single"; i++; continue; }
      if (c === '"') { mode = "double"; i++; continue; }
      if (c === "`") { mode = "template"; i++; continue; }
      if (tpl.length) {
        if (c === "{") tpl[tpl.length - 1]++;
        else if (c === "}") {
          if (tpl[tpl.length - 1] === 0) { tpl.pop(); mode = "template"; i++; continue; }
          tpl[tpl.length - 1]--;
        }
      }
      i++; continue;
    }

    if (mode === "line") {
      if (c === "\n") { mode = "code"; i++; continue; }
      space(i); i++; continue;
    }

    if (mode === "block") {
      if (c === "*" && d === "/") { space(i); space(i + 1); mode = "code"; i += 2; continue; }
      space(i); i++; continue;
    }

    // inside a string literal
    if (c === "\\") { spaceString(i); if (i + 1 < src.length) spaceString(i + 1); i += 2; continue; }
    if (mode === "single" && c === "'") { mode = "code"; i++; continue; }
    if (mode === "double" && c === '"') { mode = "code"; i++; continue; }
    if (mode === "template") {
      if (c === "`") { mode = "code"; i++; continue; }
      if (c === "$" && d === "{") { tpl.push(0); mode = "code"; i += 2; continue; }
    }
    spaceString(i); i++;
  }

  return out.join("");
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *
 * Small scanning helpers
 * ------------------------------------------------------------------ */

function lineIndex(src) {
  const starts = [0];
  for (let i = 0; i < src.length; i++) if (src[i] === "\n") starts.push(i + 1);
  return (offset) => {
    let lo = 0, hi = starts.length - 1;
    while (lo < hi) {
      const mid = (lo + hi + 1) >> 1;
      if (starts[mid] <= offset) lo = mid; else hi = mid - 1;
    }
    return { line: lo + 1, col: offset - starts[lo] + 1 };
  };
}

/** Text between `from` (index of the opening char) and its balanced close. */
function balanced(src, from, open, close) {
  let depth = 0;
  for (let i = from; i < src.length; i++) {
    if (src[i] === open) depth++;
    else if (src[i] === close) {
      depth--;
      if (depth === 0) return { text: src.slice(from, i + 1), end: i };
    }
  }
  return { text: src.slice(from), end: src.length - 1 };
}

/** The value of an object property: from after `:` to the next top-level `,` or `}`. */
function propValue(src, colonIdx) {
  let depth = 0;
  for (let i = colonIdx + 1; i < src.length; i++) {
    const c = src[i];
    if (c === "(" || c === "[" || c === "{") depth++;
    else if (c === ")" || c === "]") depth--;
    else if (c === "}") { if (depth === 0) return src.slice(colonIdx + 1, i); depth--; }
    else if (c === "," && depth === 0) return src.slice(colonIdx + 1, i);
  }
  return src.slice(colonIdx + 1);
}

const FRAME_DERIVED = /\binterpolate\s*\(|\bspring\s*\(|\buseCurrentFrame\s*\(|\bframe\b/;

/**
 * Names bound to a frame-derived value, so indirection doesn't hide a
 * violation: `const w = interpolate(frame, …)` … `style={{width: w}}`.
 * One pass, one level deep — enough for the shape this actually takes.
 */
function frameDerivedNames(code) {
  const names = new Set();
  const re = /\b(?:const|let|var)\s+([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)\s*=/g;
  let m;
  while ((m = re.exec(code))) {
    let depth = 0;
    let end = m.index + m[0].length;
    while (end < code.length) {
      const c = code[end];
      if (c === "(" || c === "[" || c === "{") depth++;
      else if (c === ")" || c === "]" || c === "}") { if (depth === 0) break; depth--; }
      else if ((c === ";" || c === "\n") && depth === 0) break;
      end++;
    }
    if (FRAME_DERIVED.test(code.slice(m.index + m[0].length, end))) names.add(m[1]);
  }
  return names;
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *
 * Rules
 * ------------------------------------------------------------------ */

const MOTION_MODULE = /(^|[\\/])motion(\.(t|j)sx?)?([\\/]|$)/;

const RULES = [
  {
    id: "nondeterministic-source",
    level: "error",
    law: "A0",
    run(ctx) {
      const re = /\b(Math\.random|Date\.now|performance\.now)\s*\(|\bnew\s+Date\s*\(/g;
      return matches(ctx, re, (m) => {
        const call = (m[1] || "new Date") + "()";
        return `${call} in composition code — same frame will not produce the same pixels, so parallel renders flicker. Use Remotion's seeded random("seed"), or frame-based noise.`;
      });
    },
  },
  {
    id: "wall-clock-timer",
    level: "error",
    law: "A0",
    run(ctx) {
      const re = /\b(setTimeout|setInterval|requestAnimationFrame)\s*\(/g;
      return matches(ctx, re, (m) =>
        `${m[1]}() drives motion from wall-clock time, not from the frame. Components are pure functions of their props — derive the value from useCurrentFrame() instead.`);
    },
  },
  {
    id: "linear-easing",
    level: "error",
    law: "A1",
    run(ctx) {
      const re = /\bEasing\.linear\b/g;
      return matches(ctx, re, () =>
        `Easing.linear — the house default is thin-peak velocity (wind-up → fast burst → soft settle). Linear is only ever correct for genuinely constant motion (a marquee, a rotating rig).`);
    },
  },
  {
    id: "inline-curve",
    level: "error",
    law: "A1",
    run(ctx) {
      if (MOTION_MODULE.test(ctx.file)) return [];
      // Strings intact: the CSS form lives inside a quoted literal.
      const re = /cubic-bezier\s*\(|\bEasing\.bezier\s*\(/g;
      return matches({ code: ctx.text }, re, () =>
        `Curve defined inline. Curves are defined once in src/motion.ts (EASE / EASE_OUT / EASE_IN) and imported — a curve redefined at the call site is how a piece ends up with six near-identical eases and no consistent feel.`);
    },
  },
  {
    id: "unclamped-interpolate",
    level: "warn",
    law: "A1",
    run(ctx) {
      const out = [];
      const re = /\binterpolate\s*\(/g;
      let m;
      while ((m = re.exec(ctx.code))) {
        const open = ctx.code.indexOf("(", m.index);
        const { text } = balanced(ctx.code, open, "(", ")");
        if (/extrapolate(Left|Right)?\s*:/.test(text)) continue;
        out.push({
          offset: m.index,
          message: `interpolate() without extrapolateLeft/Right — Remotion extends the curve past its range by default, so values keep drifting outside the window. Clamp unless the overshoot is deliberate.`,
        });
      }
      return out;
    },
  },
  {
    id: "animated-layout-prop",
    level: "error",
    law: "A7",
    run(ctx) {
      const out = [];
      const animated = frameDerivedNames(ctx.code);
      const viaName = animated.size
        ? new RegExp(`\\b(${[...animated].join("|")})\\b`)
        : null;
      // Style-object form only (`width:`), never the JSX-attribute form
      // (`width={…}`) — SVG geometry attributes are legitimate to animate.
      const re = /(?<![A-Za-z0-9_$.])(width|height|top|left|right|bottom|minWidth|maxWidth|minHeight|maxHeight|margin|marginTop|marginRight|marginBottom|marginLeft|padding|paddingTop|paddingRight|paddingBottom|paddingLeft|flexBasis|gap)\s*:/g;
      let m;
      while ((m = re.exec(ctx.code))) {
        const colon = m.index + m[0].length - 1;
        const value = propValue(ctx.code, colon);
        if (!FRAME_DERIVED.test(value) && !(viaName && viaName.test(value))) continue;
        out.push({
          offset: m.index,
          message: `\`${m[1]}\` is animated from the frame — layout properties trigger layout + paint every frame. Animate transform / opacity / filter instead. If this is a deliberate container morph, waive it with a reason.`,
        });
      }
      return out;
    },
  },
  {
    id: "blur-on-perspective",
    level: "error",
    law: "A5",
    run(ctx) {
      const out = [];
      // Strings intact: `filter: \`blur(${x}px)\`` hides its evidence in a template.
      const src = ctx.text;
      const re = /\bperspective\s*:/g;
      let m;
      while ((m = re.exec(src))) {
        // Widen to the enclosing object literal, then look for a filter on it.
        const objStart = src.lastIndexOf("{", m.index);
        if (objStart === -1) continue;
        const { text } = balanced(src, objStart, "{", "}");
        if (!/\b(filter|backdropFilter)\s*:/.test(text)) continue;
        if (!/\b(blur|url)\s*\(/.test(text)) continue;
        out.push({
          offset: m.index,
          message: `A filter and \`perspective\` on the same element — a CSS filter flattens the 3D space it is applied to, collapsing every depth plane inside it. Apply blur to the individual planes, never to the shared perspective wrapper.`,
        });
      }
      return out;
    },
  },
];

/** Cross-file heuristic: the same device, called identically, everywhere. */
const BUILT_IN_COMPONENTS = new Set([
  "AbsoluteFill", "Sequence", "Series", "Composition", "Still", "Folder",
  "Audio", "Video", "OffthreadVideo", "Img", "IFrame", "Loop", "Freeze",
  "Player", "Thumbnail", "Fragment", "Suspense", "StrictMode", "ErrorBoundary",
]);

function collectDeviceUses(ctx, registry) {
  const re = /<([A-Z][A-Za-z0-9_.]*)/g;
  let m;
  while ((m = re.exec(ctx.code))) {
    const name = m[1];
    if (BUILT_IN_COMPONENTS.has(name) || BUILT_IN_COMPONENTS.has(name.split(".").pop())) continue;

    let i = m.index + m[0].length;
    let depth = 0;
    while (i < ctx.code.length) {
      const c = ctx.code[i];
      if (c === "{") depth++;
      else if (c === "}") depth--;
      else if (c === ">" && depth === 0) break;
      i++;
    }
    const props = ctx.code.slice(m.index + m[0].length, i).replace(/\/$/, "").trim();
    if (!props.includes("=")) continue; // generics and bare tags carry no props

    const key = `${name}|${props.replace(/\s+/g, " ")}`;
    if (!registry.has(key)) registry.set(key, { name, uses: [] });
    registry.get(key).uses.push({ file: ctx.file, ...ctx.at(m.index) });
  }
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *
 * Engine
 * ------------------------------------------------------------------ */

function matches(ctx, re, message) {
  const out = [];
  let m;
  while ((m = re.exec(ctx.code))) out.push({ offset: m.index, message: message(m) });
  return out;
}

function readWaivers(raw) {
  const file = new Set();
  const byLine = new Map();
  raw.split("\n").forEach((text, idx) => {
    const next = text.match(/klik-lint-disable-next-line\s+([\w-*,\s]+)/);
    if (next) {
      const set = byLine.get(idx + 2) || new Set();
      next[1].split(/[,\s]+/).filter(Boolean).forEach((r) => set.add(r));
      byLine.set(idx + 2, set);
      return;
    }
    const whole = text.match(/klik-lint-disable\s+([\w-*,\s]+)/);
    if (whole) whole[1].split(/[,\s]+/).filter(Boolean).forEach((r) => file.add(r));
  });
  return { file, byLine };
}

function waived(waivers, rule, line) {
  if (waivers.file.has(rule) || waivers.file.has("*")) return true;
  const set = waivers.byLine.get(line);
  return !!set && (set.has(rule) || set.has("*"));
}

function walk(target, acc) {
  let stat;
  try { stat = statSync(target); } catch { return acc; }
  if (stat.isFile()) {
    if (SOURCE_EXT.has(target.slice(target.lastIndexOf(".")))) acc.push(target);
    return acc;
  }
  if (!stat.isDirectory()) return acc;
  for (const entry of readdirSync(target)) {
    if (entry.startsWith(".") && entry !== ".") continue;
    if (SKIP_DIR.has(entry)) continue;
    walk(join(target, entry), acc);
  }
  return acc;
}

function lint(paths) {
  const files = [];
  for (const p of paths) walk(resolve(p), files);

  const findings = [];
  const devices = new Map();

  for (const file of files.sort()) {
    const raw = readFileSync(file, "utf8");
    const code = blankNonCode(raw);
    const text = blankNonCode(raw, false);
    const rel = relative(process.cwd(), file) || file;
    const at = lineIndex(raw);
    const waivers = readWaivers(raw);
    const ctx = { file: rel, code, text, at };

    for (const rule of RULES) {
      for (const hit of rule.run(ctx)) {
        const { line, col } = at(hit.offset);
        if (waived(waivers, rule.id, line)) continue;
        findings.push({ file: rel, line, col, rule: rule.id, level: rule.level, law: rule.law, message: hit.message });
      }
    }
    collectDeviceUses(ctx, devices);
  }

  for (const { name, uses } of devices.values()) {
    if (uses.length < 3) continue;
    const where = uses.map((u) => `${u.file}:${u.line}`).join(", ");
    findings.push({
      file: uses[0].file,
      line: uses[0].line,
      col: uses[0].col,
      rule: "repeated-device",
      level: "warn",
      law: "A14",
      message: `<${name}> is used ${uses.length}× with byte-identical props (${where}). No device is reused unvaried — direction, magnitude and period must differ between uses. Parameterising is not varying: verify the variation reaches the render, not just the call site.`,
    });
  }

  findings.sort((a, b) => a.file.localeCompare(b.file) || a.line - b.line || a.col - b.col);
  return { files: files.length, findings };
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *
 * Reporting
 * ------------------------------------------------------------------ */

const tty = process.stdout.isTTY;
const paint = (code, s) => (tty ? `\x1b[${code}m${s}\x1b[0m` : s);
const red = (s) => paint("31", s);
const yellow = (s) => paint("33", s);
const dim = (s) => paint("2", s);
const bold = (s) => paint("1", s);

function report({ files, findings }, strict) {
  const errors = findings.filter((f) => f.level === "error").length;
  const warns = findings.length - errors;

  if (!findings.length) {
    console.log(`${bold("klik-anim motion lint")} — clean across ${files} file${files === 1 ? "" : "s"}.`);
    console.log(dim("Mechanical laws only. The A9 look-pass and Part D still apply."));
    return 0;
  }

  console.log(`${bold("klik-anim motion lint")} — ${red(`${errors} error${errors === 1 ? "" : "s"}`)}, ${yellow(`${warns} warning${warns === 1 ? "" : "s"}`)} across ${files} file${files === 1 ? "" : "s"}\n`);

  let current = null;
  for (const f of findings) {
    if (f.file !== current) { current = f.file; console.log(bold(current)); }
    const tag = f.level === "error" ? red("error") : yellow(" warn");
    console.log(`  ${dim(`${f.line}:${f.col}`.padEnd(8))} ${tag}  ${f.rule} ${dim(`[${f.law}]`)}`);
    console.log(`           ${f.message}\n`);
  }

  const failing = errors > 0 || (strict && warns > 0);
  console.log(failing
    ? red("Fix before rendering — Part D gates on these (items 1, 2, 11).")
    : yellow("Warnings only. Review each; waive with a reason if deliberate."));
  return failing ? 1 : 0;
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *
 * CLI
 * ------------------------------------------------------------------ */

const argv = process.argv.slice(2);
if (argv.includes("--help") || argv.includes("-h")) {
  console.log(`klik-anim motion lint — the craft laws a machine can check.

  node lint-motion.mjs [paths...] [--strict] [--json]

  paths     files or directories to scan (default: src)
  --strict  warnings fail the run too
  --json    machine-readable output

Rules: nondeterministic-source [A0] · wall-clock-timer [A0] · linear-easing [A1]
       inline-curve [A1] · unclamped-interpolate [A1] · animated-layout-prop [A7]
       blur-on-perspective [A5] · repeated-device [A14]

Waive a deliberate violation, always with a reason:
  // klik-lint-disable-next-line animated-layout-prop — deliberate container morph`);
  process.exit(0);
}

const strict = argv.includes("--strict");
const json = argv.includes("--json");
const targets = argv.filter((a) => !a.startsWith("--"));
const result = lint(targets.length ? targets : ["src"]);

if (json) {
  console.log(JSON.stringify(result, null, 2));
  const errors = result.findings.filter((f) => f.level === "error").length;
  process.exit(errors > 0 || (strict && result.findings.length > errors) ? 1 : 0);
}

process.exit(report(result, strict));

---
name: klik-cam
description: >-
  The camera-movement craft layer for Remotion motion graphics — the companion
  to klik-anim (which governs everything moving WITHIN the shot; this skill
  governs the shot itself). Read and obey this WHENEVER a Remotion piece moves,
  or considers moving, its camera: pushes, dollies, orbits, pans, parallax and
  2.5D depth moves, "camera shake", momentum handoffs between shots, or any
  request mentioning camera work, camera energy, or a moving/locked camera. It
  owns the Camera Motion Dial (C0, 1–5) that sets a video's camera energy as a
  branding decision, and the camera grammar: anti-AI-camera move pairing,
  monotone-spline pose interpolation, shutter blur at velocity peaks, camera
  signature variation scene to scene, focus discipline (the focal plane sits
  on the words), and 3D-space hygiene. klik-anim's base laws (determinism,
  thin-peak easing, pacing dial C0.5) still bind every camera parameter. No
  camera move ships without passing the CAM checklist at the end.
---

# klik-cam — Camera Movement Craft

> **The camera is a character, not a viewport.** Its energy is a branding
> decision made once per video, its moves are phrases with anticipation and
> settle like any other animation, and its repetition reads as lazy exactly
> the way a copy-pasted element does.
>
> **Scope contract:** `klik-anim` governs elements *within* the shot; this
> skill governs the shot itself. klik-anim's base laws bind every camera
> parameter — determinism (A0), thin-peak easing (A1), the pacing dial
> (C0.5), zero-static (A6, which the camera never satisfies on its own), and
> the render-and-look discipline (A9). Where this document says "A-law" or
> "C0.5", it means klik-anim's sections.
>
> *v1 scope: the dial + the grammar laws. The deeper camera language — named
> pose-graph recipes, rig implementations, per-genre move vocabularies — is
> deliberately deferred to a later expansion.*

---

## C0. The Camera Motion Dial (1–5)

Set this **once per video, during the brand/style phase** — camera energy is a branding decision, not a per-shot whim. It replaces the moving-vs-locked binary with a continuous dial. Record the value in the project's style profile / spec (the method's SSOT §8 if in use), set in the same pass as klik-anim's pacing dial C0.5. The dial governs the **camera only**; the zero-static law (A6) still applies to *elements* at every setting — even at 1, something in the frame is always moving; it's the camera that holds.

| Dial | Name | Camera behavior | Scale changes come from | Typical looks |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | **Locked** | Zero camera movement. Hard cuts only. | Cuts, or an element growing/travelling in-frame. | Editorial / kinetic-type, poster, "stage-not-scene", fast meme edits |
| **2** | **Anchored** | Reads as static; only imperceptible life — at most one slow single-axis push/scroll per scene, ≤0.5% creep on holds. | Mostly cuts; the occasional slow push. | Clean product explainers, UI / testimonial walkthroughs |
| **3** | **Motivated** | Camera moves *when the action motivates it* (push on a reveal, settle after), then rests. Movement is punctuation. Rests still carry micro-drift. | Motivated pushes **and** cuts. | Most brand / product films — **the default if unsure** |
| **4** | **Flowing** | Camera is usually in motion — connected moves between named poses, brief settles decaying into residual drift; momentum handed shot-to-shot. | Camera moves + element travel; cuts are rarer. | Dimensional 2.5D brand work, "premium tech" |
| **5** | **Perpetual** | No single frame where the camera is still. Continuous pose graph; every move pairs zoom with ≥1 rotation axis; velocity never resolves to zero — always drifting / orbiting. | Almost entirely camera + depth; cuts hidden behind motion. | Apple / Buck / Mill maximal-momentum sizzle |

**Rules that scale with the dial:**
- **Anti-AI-camera (3–5):** never a pure `scale()` / truck move — always pair zoom with a rotation axis or lateral vector; resolve every move into residual drift, never a dead stop.
- **Monotone-spline poses (4–5):** interpolate the pose graph so velocity is continuous but never overshoots a key — a direction reversal crests gradually, like a thrown ball. No bounce on the camera unless explicitly requested.
- **Camera motion blur (3–5):** fast segments need real shutter blur at the velocity peak (2–5f), landing sharp (`@remotion/motion-blur` `CameraMotionBlur`, or a shutter-angle frame blend). Missing it is the usual cause of judder.
- **Depth pays off with movement:** DOF + parallax do the most work at 4–5 (a moving camera separates the `translateZ` planes); at 1–2, depth is carried by static layering and cuts instead.
- **Don't jump non-adjacent settings inside one video** without a deliberate reason — a locked (1) editorial passage that suddenly hits a dial-5 orbit reads as two different videos. A **one-step** bump for a single hero moment is fine and effective.

---

## CAM-1. Signature variation — no two scenes share a camera move

The camera column of klik-anim's device ledger (A14). A single rig applied
uniformly makes a piece feel repetitive — "boring real fast" — even when every
individual move is correct. A1 bans single-speed within a scene; this law bans
single-signature across the piece.

- **Direction, magnitude, and drift period must differ scene to scene.** Two
  scenes may share a rig; they may not share its numbers.
- **Parameterising is not varying.** A rig with variants whose every call
  site passes the same explicit overrides ships identical moves — that exact
  dead-code failure ran for a whole session. Verify the variation **reaches
  the render**: compare frames from two scenes (A9), not the code.
- Drift on rests varies too — same period on every hold reads as a metronome.

## CAM-2. Focus discipline — the focal plane sits on the words

In any DOF rig, `focusZ` follows the narrative target, and the narrative
target is almost always the **copy**. A camera push that ramps `focusZ` off
the type plane ships permanent blur on a hero line (a real 2.25px shipped
defect). Camera moves change *where the camera is*, not *what is in focus* —
unless the rack is the point, and then it lands ON the next target, crisp.

## CAM-3. 3D-space hygiene

- **No grouping property on the space or its ancestors — filter OR
  opacity < 1.** Either one **flattens the perspective** — every plane
  collapses to one (render-verified: a sample-stacking motion-blur wrapper's
  fractional opacity vanished the mid/near planes). Blur/warp/fade individual
  planes only (klik-anim A5 owns the blur budget).
- One `perspective` space per scene; planes mounted on `translateZ`, the
  screen-flat reset plane for text/modals (A5).
- The camera is a transform on the space, elements are transforms on planes —
  never mix the two on one node, or moves become un-reasonable-about.

## CAM-4. Moves are phrases

A camera move obeys A1 like any element: anticipatory wind-up, thin-peak
burst, decelerated settle — **into residual drift, never a dead stop** (3–5).
Duration sits in A1's "camera phrase" band (1.6–3.6s), scaled by the pacing
dial C0.5. Exits/entrances across a cut hand momentum to the next shot
(match-motion; klik-anim A12's eye-trace law says where the eye must land).

**Motivation leads; the camera reacts.** The CAUSE of a camera move must be
on screen ~10–14f before the move begins — a line emerging, a subject
departing, a reveal starting. A camera that moves before its cause is
visible reads as unmotivated and confuses the viewer ("why is the frame
travelling?"). Anticipation is ELEMENT grammar (A2.2); **reaction delay is
camera grammar** — the operator sees, then follows. Pair it with a
front-loaded emergence on the motivating element (decisively out by the
time the camera commits, soft arrival; the landing accent supplies the
punctuation).

**The named vocabulary** — truck, pedestal, dolly, zoom, dolly-zoom, pan,
tilt, roll, crane, whip, handheld, rack focus — with exact 2.5D
implementations, the pan-vs-truck / zoom-vs-dolly distinctions, and the
dial-gated move kit lives in **`references/camera-moves.md`** (each move
render-verified in a labeled glossary demo).

## CAM-6. The camera yields to the elements (the default behavior)

The camera's authority chain is **elements > composition > music**. The music
sets the frame's TOTAL motion energy; the elements — already authored to the
music — have first claim on it; the camera is **sidechained** to their motion
and claims only the residual. This is the DEFAULT for every music-driven
piece; the user may override it (more camera, less, or off) — an override is
a recorded spec decision like any dial value, never a silent drift back.

- **Sidechain, not switch.** Element motion ducks camera *drift* with a fast
  attack (~3f) and a slow, eased release (~24–36f) — the camera parks while
  elements phrase and swells back as they settle. Never frame-instant inverse
  coupling: that stutters the camera (CAM-4 violation).
- **The C0 dial is the camera's claim multiplier on the residual** — not a
  mandate to move. Locked ≈ ×0, Anchored ≈ ×0.2, Motivated ≈ ×0.5,
  Flowing ≈ ×1, Perpetual ≈ ×1.5. The dial stays a branding decision; the
  sidechain decides moment-to-moment amount within it.
- **Accents co-fire; drift yields.** The duck governs sustained motion only.
  On rank-1 beats (bar-aligned kicks, hot sections) the camera hits WITH the
  element impact — amplifier, not competitor — mostly on depth axes.
- **Complementary axes.** The camera never rides the axis the elements are
  using: elements own the frame plane → the camera's residual lives in
  depth/roll. Same-axis stacking cancels or doubles element motion
  unpredictably.
- **Gaze-anchored, margin-capped.** Drift is defined relative to the focal
  element's home and is mean-reverting; its amplitude is capped by A11's
  margin math so the focal centroid never leaves the inner pocket (~8% of
  frame). "Center" is defined by the subject — the camera cannot walk the
  boss off its composition. **Which frame the cap is measured in follows the
  composition model** (klik-anim `references/layout.md`): normally the video
  frame, but under the **accretion artboard** it is the *reading pocket* —
  the camera travels the canvas beneath a pocket that itself stays put, so
  the boss never leaves the pocket even though the canvas leaves the frame.
  A camera that walks the active run out of the pocket is the violation;
  one that walks spent canvas out of frame is the model working.
- **Holds are the camera's turn.** During designed holds (reading time) the
  elements drop to micro idle and the camera provides the life — the slow
  push on a held line. One rank-1 mover at a time (klik-anim A10) — and the
  camera counts as a mover.

Implementations live in `references/camera-music.md` as **presets**:
**A · Hold & Glide** (the default — camera holds with breathing only, then
one composed zoom/slide per musical seam, landing on the downbeat; scenes
laid out in world space so the travel IS the scene change) · **B · Reactive
Shake** (the sidechained drift+hit rig — field-judged too twitchy as a
standing behavior; opt-in, scoped, recorded) · **C · Element-Follow**
(roadmap). Preset choice is the user's; A is what you reach for unasked.

## CAM-5. The camera hears the music too

Same music map as klik-anim §A16, camera scale — the camera moves on the
music's **big body** (bars, sections, drops), never its surface detail:

- **Energy tier maps to activity *within* the dial.** Tier 5 is the dial's
  ceiling (the one-step hero bump lives here, on the drop); tier 1–2 is its
  floor — drift only, even at dial 4.
- **Signatures change at musical seams.** CAM-1's scene-to-scene variation
  lands at section boundaries, not at arbitrary cuts — a new section sounds
  different, so the camera moves differently.
- **Bass impacts are camera hits:** a small kick/push with shutter blur,
  landing sharp on the transient. **Swells are pushes/pulls** whose ramp
  matches the swell's rise. **Breakdowns settle into drift.**
- **Never mickey-mouse the hi-hats.** Micro-percussion is element territory
  (A16's blinks and ticks); a camera that twitches on every hat reads as
  nervous, not musical.
- **Implementation recipes live in `references/camera-music.md`** (this skill
  folder) — load it when building a music-driven camera: the render-verified
  rig shape, per-section signature crossfades, the bar-kick filter, velocity
  shutter smear, and the sample-stacking-blur-flattens-3D trap.

---

## CAM CHECKLIST — run before every render with any camera movement

1. Dial value set with the user (never defaulted), recorded in the spec, applied consistently — no unmotivated non-adjacent jumps?
2. At dial 1–2: camera truly holds (≤0.5% creep) — no accidental drift? At 3–5: every move pairs zoom with a rotation axis or lateral vector — no pure scale/truck?
3. Every move resolves into residual drift or a motivated rest — never a dead stop (3–5)?
4. Shutter blur present at every velocity peak (2–5f), landing frame sharp?
5. Camera signatures differ scene to scene (direction, magnitude, drift period) — verified in rendered frames, not parameters (CAM-1)?
6. `focusZ` on the narrative target (the copy) through every move — no hero line blurred by a push (CAM-2)?
7. No CSS filter on any ancestor of the 3D space; blur applied per plane only (CAM-3)?
8. Monotone-spline interpolation at 4–5 — no camera bounce, no velocity discontinuity at pose keys?
9. Camera follows the music map (CAM-5): signature changes at section boundaries, hits on bass impacts with blur, activity tracks the energy tier — and no camera twitch on micro-percussion?
10. Camera yields to the elements (CAM-6): drift ducked during element phrases (fast attack, slow release), focal centroid inside the inner margin the whole piece, no same-axis competition, accents co-fired only on rank-1 beats — or a recorded user override says otherwise?

---

*Companion layer: `klik-anim` (element craft — its A-laws bind the camera too) · Remotion's official skills (mechanics) · the project's style bible (which dial value fits the brand).*

# The camera-move vocabulary — named moves, 2.5D implementations

The classic move names, each with: what it physically is, what it says, and
the EXACT implementation in this skill's rig convention (one perspective
wrapper → one transform on the space → planes at `translateZ`). Camera pose
convention: `transform: translate3d(−x, −y, z) rotateZ(−rz) rotateY(ry)
rotateX(rx)` on the space; `scale(s)` on the OUTER wrapper is the zoom axis
(post-projection = FOV change).

**The two distinctions that only exist once you have depth planes:**
- **Pan/tilt (rotation) vs truck/pedestal (translation):** rotation produces
  NO parallax; translation separates the planes. In 2.5D, big "pans across a
  scene" are almost always trucks.
- **Zoom (outer scale) vs dolly (camera z):** zoom magnifies everything
  equally; a dolly changes the *relationships* — near planes grow faster.
  This difference is the whole reason to build in 2.5D.

| Move | Physical | Says | 2.5D implementation | Watch out |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Truck** | camera slides left/right | follow travel, scan a scene, scene-to-scene transit | animate `x`; planes parallax automatically | the workhorse — preset A's glides are trucks |
| **Pedestal** | camera rises/falls, axis level | change of level, hands→faces reveals | animate `y` | pairs with truck for L-shaped reveals |
| **Dolly in/out** | camera moves toward/away | entering the world / leaving it; depth context | animate `z` (+ = in); planes separate | never a bare `scale()` — that's zoom, and the anti-AI-camera rule wants dollies paired with a lateral or roll component |
| **Zoom in/out** | focal length change | attention squeeze without spatial change | animate outer-wrapper `scale` 1→~1.2 | flat feel is the POINT of zoom; use when you *don't* want parallax (archival/CCTV/broadcast flavors) |
| **Dolly-zoom** (Vertigo) | dolly one way, zoom the other | unease, realization, world-shift | `z: 0→c` while outer scale compensates `s = (P − c)/P` (P = perspective, 1100): focal plane holds size, background crawls | the strongest move in the kit — one per piece, on the biggest narrative turn, tier-5 territory |
| **Pan** | camera rotates on Y | glance left/right, tension between two subjects | animate `ry`, SMALL (≤ ~6°) | flat planes go edge-on at big angles and the illusion dies; big scans = truck instead |
| **Tilt** | camera rotates on X | reveal up/down (knife → face) | animate `rx`, SMALL (≤ ~5°) | perspective distorts type — never tilt across crisp focal copy (A5 screen-flat plane) |
| **Roll** | camera rotates on Z | disorientation, energy accents | animate `rz` | already rationed by the grammar: ±0.9° poses, hit accents |
| **Crane / jib** | camera arcs up + tilts down (or reverse) | scale, arrival, finale | path: `y` down→up eased WITH compensating `rx` so the focal stays framed | the classic closer; pair with a section seam |
| **Whip (pan/truck)** | violently fast lateral | hard transition, chaos accent | truck at minimum T (~10–14f) + velocity smear per plane; landing sharp; can hide a cut at peak smear | this is a TRANSITION, not a shot; A14 ledger — twice max |
| **Handheld** | operator's body noise | authenticity, urgency, doc energy | **preset B (Reactive Shake)**, scoped | field-judged: never the standing behavior |
| **Steadicam / follow** | smoothed pursuit of a subject | intimacy with a moving subject | **preset C (Element-Follow)** — camera home tracks the focal with inertia | roadmap; needs travelling focals |
| **Rack focus** | focus shifts between depths | redirect attention without moving | animate `focusZ`: crossfade per-plane DOF blurs (far crisp→soft while near soft→crisp) over 12–20f | the "camera move" of attention; obeys CAM-2 — it must LAND on the narrative target |
| **Signature / custom** | the rope-swing | style identity | a named pose-path defined once in the style bible, reused as the piece's motif | CAM-1: vary its parameters between uses |

## Composing them

- Real moves are **pairs**: truck+pan (scan with a look), dolly+roll (the
  anti-AI pairing), pedestal+tilt (crane), truck+zoom (push-slide). Single-
  axis moves read mechanical — same law as element arcs (A2.7).
- **Dial gates the vocabulary:** 1 → cuts only · 2 → zoom/rack focus only
  (no spatial motion) · 3 → truck/pedestal/dolly as motivated phrases ·
  4 → full kit incl. crane paths · 5 → continuous pose-graph composition.
- **Music map places them:** glides/trucks land on section seams (preset A);
  dolly-zoom and crane belong to the piece's ONE biggest moment; whips are
  hot-section transitions; rack focus rides vocal/narrative handoffs.
- Every move remains a phrase (CAM-4): wind-up, travel, settle-into-breath —
  and the A14 ledger applies to moves exactly as to element devices.

*All implementations verified in the CamMoves glossary demo (fx-poc) —
rendered, viewed, each move labeled.*
