# Camera ← music recipes — implementing CAM-5 / CAM-6

## The preset family (field-judged)

| Preset | What | When |
|---|---|---|
| **A · HOLD & GLIDE — the DEFAULT** | Camera holds on each scene (Anchored-level breathing only, ≤0.5% creep + gentle level swell on depth), then ONE composed zoom/slide glide per musical seam, **starting T frames early so it lands on the incoming downbeat**. Scenes sit side by side in world space — the camera travel IS the scene change. T scales with the incoming tier (~24f hot, ~50f calm); per-section poses are quantized (3 zoom levels × 3 heights × 3 rolls) so consecutive framings differ readably. | Motion graphics, default for dials 2–4. Field verdict: continuous reactive drift "reads as camera shake, not MG" — holds + composed transitions read as design. |
| **B · REACTIVE SHAKE — opt-in** | The sidechained continuous rig (per-section drift signatures, bar-kick hits, duck envelope — the full CAM-6 sidechain math below). | Handheld/hype energy: performance montages, dial-5 sizzle, single hero sections. Never the standing behavior — scope it to a section and record the choice. |
| **C · ELEMENT-FOLLOW** | Camera pursues the focal's **phrase-level path**, never its per-frame motion — hops/bounces play inside a stable frame. Verified mechanics below. | Travelling focals: journey pieces, cursor tours, anything the eye must stay with. |

Named single moves (truck/dolly/dolly-zoom/whip/rack focus…) live in
`references/camera-moves.md` — preset A composes its glides from that
vocabulary.

**Continuity trap (render-found):** every always-on layer of the pose —
breathing, drift, swell — must be keyed to the **global frame**, never to
the section index. A section-keyed phase (`sin(f/95 + section·1.7)`)
teleports its offset the frame the index increments: a one-frame pop at
every glide landing. Verify seams numerically: frame-difference the render
across each boundary — the landing frame's diff must be in line with its
neighbors. / CAM-6

Load this when a piece's camera should follow the music. It turns the
method's analyzer output (music map + `events` + `levels`) into camera
movement. **Every recipe was render-verified in a 2.5D POC against a real
track.** Two presets, field-judged:

## PRESET A — HOLD & GLIDE (the default for motion graphics)

The camera **holds** on each section's pose — Anchored-level breathing only
(≤0.5% creep) — then executes ONE composed zoom/slide transition per musical
seam. Field verdict drove this: continuous reactive drift "reads as camera
shake, not motion graphics."

- **Scenes live side by side in world space** (one slot per music-map
  section, e.g. 2400px apart); the camera travel IS the scene change.
- **Arrive on the seam:** the glide STARTS `T` frames before the next
  section's boundary and LANDS exactly on its downbeat — the move belongs to
  the music. `T = clamp(56 − 6·tier_incoming, 24, 50)`: hot section ⇒ snappy
  arrival, calm ⇒ long glide. Monotone ease-in-out — no overshoot (C0 rule).
- **Poses are quantized per section** (zoom level ∈ {0, 80, 150} · y ∈
  {−45, 0, 45} · roll ∈ {−0.9°, 0, 0.9°}, seeded) so each transition reads as
  a deliberate zoom-in / zoom-out / rise / drop — CAM-1 variation without
  wander.
- **Holds carry only breathing + a gentle level swell on depth** — during
  element phrases the camera is still by construction (CAM-6 satisfied
  structurally: it moves BETWEEN element phrases, at the seams).

## PRESET B — REACTIVE SHAKE (opt-in accent flavor, never the default)

The sidechained continuous rig below (drift + bar-kick hits). Field-judged
too twitchy as a standing behavior — **use it scoped**: a hype section, a
performance montage, a deliberate handheld-energy moment. The user opts in;
record the scope in the spec.

## ROADMAP — ELEMENT-FOLLOW (next)

The third preset: the camera framing driven by ELEMENT positions (follow a
travelling focal with inertia, reframe on staging changes, gaze-anchored
homes per A12) with music as the timing layer. Deliberately deferred.

---

# Preset B mechanics (the original CAM-5 rig)

Element-side mappings live in `klik-anim references/music-motion.md` —
the camera takes the music's **big body** (bars, sections, drops); elements
take the syncopation and the surface detail. Do not mix the layers.

## The rig shape (CAM-3 compliant)

```
outer AbsoluteFill        perspective: 1100        ← NO filters, ever
└─ THE SPACE  div         preserve-3d; the camera is EXACTLY ONE transform here:
   │                      translate3d(−x,−y,z) rotateZ(−rz) rotateY(ry)
   ├─ far plane   div     translateZ(−380) · DOF blur 2px   (parked, soft)
   ├─ mid plane   div     translateZ(0)    · crisp          (FOCAL — CAM-2)
   └─ near plane  div     translateZ(240)  · DOF blur 1px   (biggest parallax)
```

Lateral camera translate + perspective produces true parallax (near planes
shift more on screen); pair it with a small `rotateY` (`ry = x * 0.008`) so
no move is ever a pure truck (anti-AI-camera).

## The verified mappings

| Music | Camera | Recipe |
|---|---|---|
| **Section** (map rows) | drift **signature** (CAM-1) | Per-section seeded signature: axis mix, period 110–240f, roll weight, magnitude — all differ at every musical seam. **Crossfade signatures over ~36f with smoothstep** after each boundary: the character changes at the seam, the camera never teleports. |
| **Energy tier** | activity within the dial | `tierScale = [.22, .32, .55, .85, 1.15][tier]` multiplies drift magnitude. Tier 1–2 = the dial's floor (breath only); tier 5 = its ceiling. The breakdown *exhale* is as expressive as the drop hit. |
| **Bar-aligned kicks** | the camera HIT | Filter kick events to within ±2f of a bar line (`(e − DOWN0) mod (FPB·4)`) — the POC track kept 42 of 279 kicks. Hit = `hitPulse(barKicks, f, 5)` driving `z += 34·p`, `rz += 0.55·p`, `x += 7·p` — push + paired roll + lateral, exp decay into drift (CAM-4: never a dead stop). **Never hit on every kick** — syncopation is element territory. |
| **Swells / level** | the slow push | `z += 130 · (0.6·levelAt(bass, 8) + 0.4·levelAt(full, 8))` — ramps by nature of the smoothed level; no pulse. |
| **Camera speed** | shutter smear | `camSpeed(f) = |Δpose|` between f and f−1; `smear = clamp((speed − 3) · 0.35, 0, 4.5)` px added to **each plane's own blur**. Non-zero only 2–4f around a hit; the landing is sharp by decay. |

## DISCOVERED TRAP — sample-stacking motion blur flattens 3D

`@remotion/motion-blur`'s `CameraMotionBlur` composites fractional-**opacity**
samples. Opacity is a CSS *grouping property*: it forces `transform-style:
flat`, so a `preserve-3d` camera space inside it **collapses — mid/near
planes vanish** (render-verified failure; the far plane's leftovers made it
look like a partial render). This is CAM-3's ancestor-filter law in another
costume: **no filter, no opacity < 1, no grouping property on the space or
any ancestor of it.**

- DOM 3D rig → implement the smear as the per-plane velocity blur above.
- `CameraMotionBlur` remains correct for **flat scenes** (camera faked in 2D
  transforms without preserve-3d) — that's its domain, not this one's.

## Core code (verified — `src/music-cam.ts`)

```ts
export const barKicks = kicks.filter((e) => {
  const pos = ((e - DOWN0) % BAR + BAR) % BAR;
  return pos <= 2 || pos >= BAR - 2;                 // the big body only
});

const signature = (i: number) => ({                   // CAM-1, per section
  ax: random(`sig-ax-${i}`) * 2 - 1,
  ay: (random(`sig-ay-${i}`) * 2 - 1) * 0.55,
  rz: (random(`sig-rz-${i}`) * 2 - 1) * 0.9,
  period: 110 + random(`sig-p-${i}`) * 130,
  phase: random(`sig-ph-${i}`) * Math.PI * 2,
  mag: 34 + random(`sig-m-${i}`) * 46,
});

// camPose(frame): section drift (crossfaded 36f at seams, smoothstep)
//   + swell push from smoothed levels + bar-kick hit (z/rz/x paired, decay 5)
//   + ry = x * 0.008  — full implementation in the POC, structure above.
```

## Preset C — ELEMENT-FOLLOW (render-verified)

CAM-6 doctrine applied to pursuit. Three mechanisms, all pure functions of
frame:

- **The landing track.** The follow target is where the focal will LAND, not
  where it is: the moment a hop/phrase starts, the target jumps to its end
  point. The element's arcs, squash, and bounces play out INSIDE a stable
  frame — the camera tracks phrases, the element keeps the syncopation.
- **Lookahead lead room.** Sample the landing track ~14f into the future
  (deterministic — the future is data) to counter the inertia lag: the
  subject then rides slightly *behind* center with clear space ahead — real
  follow grammar. Without it the camera *chases* (subject ahead of center —
  a render-found defect, fixed and re-verified).
- **Inertia.** Camera x = trailing exponential average of the target
  (`Σ target(f−k)·e^(−k/10)`, k ≤ 36) — steadicam glide, natural lag on
  direction changes, settle-into-breath. Breathing/swell layers key to the
  GLOBAL frame (continuity law).

**Boss handoff (A12 eye-trace made physical):** when the focal changes, the
target blends to the new boss over ~30f with smoothstep, keyed to the
musical seam — never a snap. And the outgoing boss must actually YIELD:
render-found, the traveller kept advancing on sparse breakdown kicks and
wandered past its replacement mid-handoff — a resting boss's residual event
stream is texture, not travel; freeze its phrase motion for the handoff
span.

**THE GOVERNOR — the jarring threshold.** Too much camera movement
back-to-back is jarring regardless of what demands it. Two caps, both
render-found and numerically verified:

- **Element phrases complete.** An event may only start a travel phrase if
  the previous phrase has landed (greedy min-gap = phrase duration + a
  ground beat). Without it, dense syncopation (kicks 2–5f apart vs a 12f
  hop) snaps the base position forward — the subject **teleports**. Events
  beyond phrase capacity are texture, not travel.
- **Sustained camera speed cap** (~13px/f at 1080p): a forward pass clamps
  the follow target's per-frame advance, so demand bursts become a steady
  glide toward the *trend* instead of surge-after-surge — the operator
  going steady-and-wide when the subject gets frantic. Verify numerically:
  max per-frame camera delta ≤ cap across the piece; the focal's max delta
  ≤ its own phrase cruise speed.

Music layer on top: tier can scale follow tightness; depth-only co-fire on
bar-kicks stays tiny — the travelling element owns its own impacts — and is
**gated OFF entirely while the boss is not the traveller** (render-found: a
bar-aligned kick during the handoff pushed the camera while it contemplated
a resting boss — jitter on a moment that must be still).

**Per-segment physics (element side, feeds the follow):** when travel
energy evolves with the piece, keep **gravity constant** and derive
airtime from bounce — `T = √(8h/g)`; height and stride scale with the
section tier, impact squash/ripple scale with height (A16 weight). Size
the governor cap just above the fastest segment's cruise speed
(`max(stride/T)`) so steady travel passes while bursts still cap.

## CAM-6 layer — the sidechain (v2, render-verified A/B)

v1 of this rig moved the camera off the music alone and walked the subject
off-center during busy element phrases. v2 subordinates it (the DEFAULT;
user-overridable as a recorded spec decision):

```ts
// authored element motion — the SAME music data, used a second time:
elementMotion(f) = min(1, kickPulse + 0.5·snarePulse + 0.2·hatPulse
                        + |Δ bass level|·8 + |Δ vocal level|·5)

// sidechain envelope — fast attack (current value counts fully),
// slow release (~24–30f perceptible tail):
duckEnv(f) = max over k∈0..30 of elementMotion(f − k) · exp(−k / 12)

// the camera's claim on the residual:
DIAL_GAIN = [—, 0, 0.18, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5]        // C0 dial = claim multiplier
gXY = tierScale(tier) · DIAL_GAIN[dial] · (1 − 0.85·duck)   // frame plane
gZR = tierScale(tier) · DIAL_GAIN[dial] · (1 − 0.45·duck)   // depth/roll
// → complementary axes: elements own the frame plane, camera's residual
//   lives in depth. Margin cap AFTER gains: |x| ≤ 55px, |y| ≤ 40px (A11
//   inner pocket at 1080p). Accent co-fire (bar-kicks, tier ≥ 4) is EXEMPT
//   from the duck, scaled by the dial, and rides z/rz with only ~4px x.
```

Verified A/B on the same track and frames: busy tier-5 frame — v1 subject
displaced right + tilted, v2 dead-center with camera parked; bar-kick frame —
v2 keeps the push + smear co-fire with composition held. The music is still
audible in the camera — it just speaks in the gaps the elements leave.

## Judging it (CAM checklist hooks)

- Two stills in different sections show different drift orientations (CAM-1).
- A breakdown still is crisp and near-home; a hit still is displaced AND
  smeared; 3 frames later it is sharp again (checklist 3–4).
- The focal plane stays crisp through every drift (CAM-2) — whole-frame smear
  is allowed only at the 2–4 frame velocity peak.
- Scrub any section seam: the signature changes, the camera never jumps.
- **CAM-6:** pick the busiest element frame — the focal centroid sits inside
  the inner margin and the camera is near-parked; pick a designed hold — the
  camera carries the life. If both fail, the sidechain isn't wired.

  promo/launch/brand video", "create an animated video for X", "turn this
  script into a video" — or when a project contains *_animation_SSOT.md /
  *_storyboard.html / *_execution_plan.md / PROGRESS.md artifacts (at the root
  or in a klik/ planning folder) mid-production, or the user asks to update or

  tweaks or one-off animation edits — the klik-anim skill (with klik-cam for

# Klik Motion Method

Prompt → discovery → visual storyboard → execution plan → build → QA. Keep it
lean: this file is the spine; load ONE reference file for the stage you are in.

## The gate model

**Prose gates facts. Pixels gate aesthetics.** A document can settle duration,
codec, or an asset list; it cannot settle typography, composition or footage
strategy — those are only real once seen. From the storyboard onward the user
approves **rendered frames, not descriptions**, and klik-anim §A9 binds you
first: never show the user anything you have not rendered and looked at
yourself. **A look-pass cannot catch durations** — the arithmetic checks
(reading holds, feasibility) run beside it, never instead of it.

## The three-layer contract

- **`klik-anim`** — element craft laws (Part A, incl. §A8 only-the-user's-words,
  §A9 look-before-showing, §A12 reading-hold arithmetic, §A14 device ledger,
  §A15 boundary continuity), Remotion layer (B), style hooks (C: pacing dial
  C0.5, style interview C2), pre-flight (Part D). Loaded for build/QA. Never
  overridden.
- **`klik-cam`** — camera movement: the camera dial C0, camera grammar
  (signature variation, focus discipline, 3D hygiene), CAM checklist. Loaded
  whenever the piece's camera dial is above 1.
- **This method** — the orchestration: sequence, artifacts, gates, personas.
  Never restate skill content in artifacts — cite section numbers.

## Pipeline map

| Stage | Persona | Artifact (in `klik/`) | Gate |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 Discovery — items 1–8 | Producer (1–4) · Asset Wrangler (5) · Copy Editor (6) · Music Supervisor (7) · DP (8) | `<project>_animation_SSOT.md` | **Text** — user approves the SSOT |
| 2 Storyboard — item 9 | Storyboard Artist | `<project>_storyboard.html` + `boards/` stills | **PIXELS** — user approves real stills |
| 3 Execution plan | Tech Director | `<project>_execution_plan.md` | **Text** — user approves, then FROZEN; switch to Opus |
| 4 Build | Animator | compositions | **PIXELS** — proof scene first, then per-scene |
| 5 QA | QA (fresh context) | final render | klik-anim Part D pre-flight + klik-cam checklist + board match |

Reference files: `references/discovery.md` · `references/storyboard.md` ·
`references/execution-plan.md` · `references/build-qa.md` ·
`references/reference-analysis.md` (load whenever the user supplies a
reference, any stage).
Templates: `templates/SSOT.template.md` · `templates/storyboard.template.html`
· `templates/EXECUTION_PLAN.template.md` · `templates/PROGRESS.template.md`.
Tooling: `scripts/analyze-audio.py` (dependency-free: BPM/downbeat grid +
the MUSIC MAP — sections, energy tiers, spectral lead, attack/sustain,
per-source rhythm patterns, and JSON `events`/`levels` for deterministic
reactive comps — consumed by klik-anim §A16 and klik-cam CAM-5. Optional
stem mode via demucs, if installed, isolates kick/snare/hats/vocals/bass/
guitar/piano; degrades gracefully to 3-band analysis without it) ·
`scripts/measure-motion.py` (QA side of the same loop: frame-diffs a
RENDER into its actual energy curve — event/rest contrast, floor-relative
rest ratio vs klik-anim §A6, and per-bar correlation against the recorded
arc/tier curve, klik-anim §A18 — run at the Stage-5 arithmetic pass).

## The questioning sequence is law

Discovery follows the SSOT's numbered intake in order, **always**. The user may
answer anything ahead of time (references early, script early) — record it in
its section, then **return to the sequence where they left off**. The next
question is always the SSOT's first ⬜ item. Ask in batches within a section;
confirm anything inferred. Never generate an artifact the user already has —
every section asks "do you have one?" before making one.

## Context architecture (BMAD-style)

Artifacts are the context transfer — a handoff succeeds only if the document
carries everything the next agent needs.

- **Main conversation (Fable 5):** discovery + storyboard — elicitation is
  dialogue; personas frame the questioning, one conversation.
- **Fresh context (Opus):** execution-plan synthesis and build — inherit ONLY
  the artifacts. The model/session switch IS the handoff.
- **QA is always a separate context** that did not author the code — an author
  reviewing its own work rubber-stamps (role bleed). QA reads artifacts +
  render and judges.

## Planning documents live on disk

- Everything is written to disk the moment it is drafted — an in-chat plan
  cannot gate anything. Folder: user-assigned, else auto-create **`klik/`** at
  the project root (don't ask; say you did). Rendered gate material lives in
  `klik/boards/` so a resumed session can see what was approved.
- **`PROGRESS.md`** (from template, created at discovery start) tracks pipeline
  position, per-scene status, and the change log. Update at every gate, every
  scene built, every user "update progress". It is state; the SSOT is truth;
  the plan is contract — never merge them.
- Artifact headers carry `Status: DRAFT | APPROVED`. The user's approval flips
  them — never flip one yourself. Post-approval changes are dated amendments.

## Resuming

Read `PROGRESS.md` first, then **verify it against the artifacts AND the code
and renders** — artifacts drift (a real resume found the plan saying
AT-PROOF-GATE while PROGRESS said all-built). Reconcile every artifact to
match reality before any new work. The ladder is authoritative:

1. No SSOT → Discovery, item 1.
2. SSOT with ⬜ intake items → Discovery, first ⬜.
3. SSOT approved, board missing or DRAFT → Storyboard.
4. Board approved, plan missing or DRAFT → Execution plan.
5. Plan approved, unbuilt scenes → Build (respect the proof gate).
6. All scenes built → QA.

## House rules

- **Cheap pixels early beat expensive pixels late.** Stills at `--scale=0.5`
  cost seconds; discovering the typography was wrong after a build costs the
  build. Never defer a visual decision to save a render — that economy has
  already failed once.
- **Nothing is throwaway.** Board mockups use the brand tokens; approved cards
  become posed comps; the build animates those comps.
- **One reference file in context at a time**; during build, one scene row at
  a time (plus klik-anim + SSOT).
- **Iterate cheap:** stills over clips, `--scale=0.5`, `--frames=a-b`;
  full-res only at QA.
- **Right-size.** A 15s single-scene ask doesn't need the method — say so and
  work under klik-anim (+ klik-cam) alone. Short videos compress the board, never skip it.
- **Model split:** planning phases on **Fable 5**; build on **Opus** — say so
  at the plan gate, with the plan's token estimate (band, excludes iterations).
- **Session limits:** for ~30s+ videos the user WILL hit limits a few times —
  warn at discovery start; artifacts + PROGRESS.md make resume lossless.

# Stages 4–5 — Build & QA

Two personas, two contexts, on purpose: the **Animator** builds; **QA judges
in a fresh context that did not author the code** — an author reviewing its
own work rubber-stamps.

## Stage 4 — Build (persona: Animator, on Opus)

You inherit ONLY: the execution plan + SSOT + storyboard/boards + ref library
+ klik-anim (+ klik-cam if the camera dial > 1) + PROGRESS.md. Read them in
that order. The plan's §4 build order is the law of this stage:

1. **Setup + foundations** per plan §1–2 (scaffold if needed, pinned
   versions, the plan's §1 file layout, tokens verbatim). `npm run dev` and tell the
   user Studio's URL — they can watch scenes land live. Lint gates every step.
   **The timing contract comes first:** before any scene, write `timeline.ts`
   (+ a `copyTiming.ts` mirror) with every line's legible window computed from
   klik-anim §A12's reading law, device assignments per scene (§A14 ledger),
   and a lint check that FAILS on any violated window. Scenes are then written
   to satisfy the contract — cue-level timing never lives only in scene code.
2. **PROOF GATE — hard stop.** The agreed proof scene + signature transition,
   rendered `--scale=0.5`, §A9 look-pass (render → look → list defects → fix →
   re-render until the list is empty), then show the user. **Nothing else gets
   built until they approve.** Style misses here are cheap; after mass
   production they cost the build.
3. **Scene by scene** in plan order. Per scene: build → lint → cheap render of
   its range → §A9 look-pass → check against its board card (layout, type
   scale, palette — deviations are defects) → mark the plan row ✅ → log in
   PROGRESS.md. Show the user at the agreed checkpoint cadence.
4. **Friction rules:** missing asset → placeholder-then-swap (same component
   boundary and dimensions, so the real asset drops in cleanly), logged in
   TODO.md with the exact required format — never stall. Plan wrong or vague →
   STOP, amend with the user (dated), continue. Copy is SSOT §6 verbatim
   (§A8) — a word the script lacks does not appear, however good it looks.
   Library-cited transitions (L-IDs) reproduce the catalogued mechanics, not
   your memory of them.
5. **Edits must land.** Every scripted string-replace carries a post-condition
   check scoped to the exact target — `replace` no-ops silently on a miss and
   stale code ships while PROGRESS says fixed (a real shipped failure).
6. **Rebuilds are visibly new.** "Make a new version" = a NEW composition ID,
   registered beside the old (V1/V2) until the user culls one — never an
   in-place rewrite under the same ID, and never delete a superseded sequence
   that isn't in git. Renders are not source.

## Stage 5 — QA (persona: QA, fresh context)

Open a clean window/session. Inputs: SSOT, storyboard, execution plan, ref
library, klik-anim + klik-cam, and the rendered output. You judge; you don't
rebuild.

1. **Full-timeline watch-down** at `--scale=0.5` — flow defects no per-scene
   check catches: tempo sameness, transition monotony, focal fights at
   boundaries, drift.
2. **Arithmetic pass — a watch-down cannot catch durations.** Recompute every
   line's legible window against klik-anim §A12's reading law from the actual
   frame numbers; audit the §A14 device ledger (no unvaried repeats) and every
   §A15 boundary (no exit → gap → entrance). Both checks always: only looking
   catches smudges and strobes; only arithmetic catches a 7-frame hold.
   **Then measure the arc:** run `scripts/measure-motion.py render.mp4
   [--map <music-map.json>]` — it frame-diffs the render into the piece's
   ACTUAL energy curve and reports event/rest contrast, the floor-relative
   rest ratio vs §A6's 40–60% band, and (with the map) per-bar correlation
   against SSOT §8's recorded arc with per-tier means. Non-monotonic tier
   means or a flat curve on a designed piece = the render is not following
   its arc (§A18) — a defect with a frame-number address, not a vibe.
3. **klik-anim Part D pre-flight — every item**, including 16 (every on-screen
   word traces to SSOT §6), 17 (every asset was viewed and logged clean), 18
   (the §A9 look-pass ran and its defect list is empty), 27–29 (reading holds,
   device ledger, boundary continuity). **Plus klik-cam's CAM checklist** when
   the camera dial > 1.
4. **Board match** — each scene against its approved card. Divergence is a
   defect unless a dated amendment covers it.
5. **Dial audit** — camera C0 (klik-cam) and pacing C0.5 (klik-anim) as set in
   SSOT §8, local overrides only where recorded.
6. **The distraction test.** After the watch-down, write the copy from
   memory before re-reading the SSOT. If you remember the animation but not
   the words, motion is too dominant — klik-anim's restraint law failed even
   if every mechanical check passes. Judge per scene, not just overall.
7. **Speed & robustness probes** (cheap, run on the half-res render):
   re-watch at 0.75× and 0.5× playback — pacing defects (rushed holds,
   dead spots, tempo sameness) surface at reduced speed that real-time
   watching hides. If the deliverable targets a platform honoring
   `prefers-reduced-motion`, confirm with the user what the fallback is
   (static poster / fades-only variant) — an unanswered accessibility
   question is an open TODO, not a silent skip.
8. **Deliverable render** at full res per SSOT §1 hard numbers (correct
   resolution/fps/codec/handoff — mp4 vs chroma slice vs ProRes alpha).
9. **Close out:** deliver render + pre-flight + arithmetic results + open TODO
   list. Nothing silently dropped. A run is correct only if: every legible
   window passes by computation · feasibility was computed at discovery · the
   device ledger shows no unvaried repeats · every boundary continues ·
   scripted edits carried post-condition checks · artifacts were reconciled on
   resume · superseded sequences stayed visible until the user culled them.
   Mark PROGRESS.md `DELIVERED` when the user accepts.

## Change requests (any time after delivery or mid-build)

Re-enter by scope, artifacts first, code second — they must stay truthful:
copy → SSOT §6, then the scene · style → SSOT/tokens, then code · one scene →
its plan row · timing/structure → storyboard, then plan. Check PROGRESS.md
before starting any new feature; log it after.

# Stage 1 — Discovery

Goal: one approved `<project>_animation_SSOT.md` a context-blind agent could
build from. The template (`templates/SSOT.template.md`) defines the sections
and carries inline guidance — this file is how to *run the interview*.

## Setup (before question 1)

1. Create the planning folder (user-assigned, else `klik/`), copy in the SSOT
   template named `<project>_animation_SSOT.md`, create `PROGRESS.md` from its
   template. Say you did.
2. Warn now: 30s+ videos WILL hit session limits a few times; artifacts on
   disk make resume lossless.
3. If the user's opening prompt already answered things, fill those sections
   first, mark them ✅ only if nothing needs confirming, then start at the
   first ⬜.

## Conduct

- **The sequence is law.** Ask in SSOT order 1→8. Early answers get recorded
  in their section; then return to where you left off and say so ("Logged your
  track for §7 — back to the brand guide").
- **One section per message batch.** All of a section's questions in one go,
  never one-question messages, never two sections at once.
- **Ask before generating — every section.** "Do you have X?" precedes making
  X, for every artifact class: script, refs, brand kit, assets, music, board.
- **Recommend, then defer.** Where you can infer (platform → format/length),
  present the inference as a recommendation and ALWAYS let the user overrule.
  Record who decided.
- **Confirm the fork early.** Item 1's dialogue-vs-pure-MG answer changes the
  questions in 6 and 7 — get it locked before moving past 1.
- Mark a section ✅ only when filled AND user-confirmed. Guesses stay
  `(inferred)` and go to Open Questions.

## Per-section notes (persona · the judgment the template can't carry)

**1 · Objective & spec — Producer.** Platform drives the recommendation
(IG/TikTok/FB → vertical, 20–30s cap · YouTube/web → landscape, longer), but
the user chooses. Convert duration to frames the moment fps is known. Vertical
platform → fill safe zones; don't skip the row with "n/a" unless the user
says so.

**2–3 · Style & mood — Producer.** Elicit, never propose. Push adjectives
toward named references ("premium like what — Apple keynote? Linear launch?").
Collect anti-references too; they constrain better than positives. **Every
supplied reference gets the extraction pass** — load
`references/reference-analysis.md`: analyze it into dial/motif terms, then
confirm takeaways per item before they enter the SSOT table. If the user
has no view at all, note it — the storyboard stage will render candidate
directions to react to (cheaper to pick from pixels than describe a vibe).

**4 · Brand guide — Producer.** Get hex codes, not color names. The deviation
allowances (font AND color) are the questions users never volunteer — ask
explicitly, they define your creative room. Logo: every variant they have, SVG
preferred; record the guide's forbidden treatments while you're there.

**5 · Assets — Asset Wrangler.** For software showcases this is the critical
section: live site to pull HTML from? Figma to export SVGs? Screenshots?
**View every asset before logging it** (klik-anim §A9) — resolution tier, and
clean of burned-in captions/watermarks/third-party logos. Anything needed but
absent: the fallback is HTML/CSS built with real frontend-design craft (ports
~1:1 into Remotion) — generative images only for texture, never for anything
that must re-render exactly. If the user has no asset direction, check the
ref library's asset-design entries first — decomposed recipes from their own
references seed the fallback designs (`references/reference-analysis.md`).

**6 · Copy — Copy Editor.** Recommend the user writes their own copy — say
why (their voice, their claims to stand behind). If AI-drafts, they approve
every word before it enters the SSOT; once in, §A8 makes it the only text
that can appear on screen.
- *Dialogue:* ask for the stitched a-roll; **offer auto-transcription**
  (`remotion-captions` skill) rather than asking them to hand-transcribe. No
  recording yet → take the script, mark timing provisional.
- *No dialogue:* explain the line-spacing convention once (single break =
  sequential in-scene, blank line = new scene with gap), parse their script,
  and **echo the numbered scene table back for confirmation** — pasted text is
  full of accidental breaks. Then ask which words carry emphasis; bold them
  inline, nowhere else.
- **Feasibility — run it NOW, before the gate.** Per line compute
  `max(0.70s, 0.25s + chars ÷ 17)` (klik-anim §A12) and sum against the §1
  duration. A script that needs 667f of hold against a 600f spec is knowable
  today; discovered after the build it costs full re-times. Over budget →
  cut lines or extend duration, with the user, here. Record the sum in §6.

**7 · Music — Music Supervisor.** First the timing role (set by the fork):
no dialogue → the track IS the timing authority; dialogue → background mood
only, animation follows speech. Then sourcing: who supplies it, licensed for
this use? (Real blocker for client work — flag, don't police.) Track in hand →
run `scripts/analyze-audio.py`: it emits the grid (BPM/downbeat) **and the
MUSIC MAP** — sections with energy tier, bass/mid/high lead, attack/sustain
character, and per-source rhythm patterns. **Stem mode** (`--stems auto`, the
default) uses demucs if installed to split vocals/drums/bass/guitar/piano
first — kick/snare/hats then come from the isolated drums, and vocals/guitar
stop reading as percussion. If demucs is missing the script degrades to
3-band mode and says so — mention `pip install demucs` to the user when the
piece leans on per-instrument sync. Paste both layers into §7. Sanity-check the
grid against hand-counted beats AND the map by ear (is the detected top-tier
section actually the drop? is the bar phase right — patterns can sit rotated
when the intro has no accent?). The map is what klik-anim §A16 and klik-cam
CAM-5 build motion character from — a wrong map ships wrong-feeling motion
everywhere. No track → internal pulse grid, and say plainly that landing the
track later means a re-time pass.

**8 · Dials & composition model — DP.** Two values, global-first (klik-cam C0
camera, klik-anim C0.5 pacing) — plus the **composition model** for any
copy-led passage (klik-anim `references/layout.md`: fixed anchor · accretion
artboard · growing line · world-space · annotation layer). The model is a
spec decision of the same kind as a dial, and it must be set here because it
changes the arithmetic downstream — accretion budgets holds in the reading
pocket and excludes demoted copy, world-space needs a 3D plate, annotation
needs something in frame worth annotating. Default is fixed anchor; anything
else is a deliberate, recorded choice.
Tie each recommendation to the mood answer from §3 ("premium calm → camera 2,
pacing 2"), let the user set the numbers. Local overrides exist but are not
part of discovery — note the mechanism, don't collect them yet.
Then the **energy arc** (klik-anim §A18) — the ONE intensity shape for the
whole piece. Music-driven: the §7 tier row IS the arc; confirm it reads as
the piece's dramaturgy (does the copy's climax sit on the musical peak?).
No music: offer the shapes (ramp · wave · cold open · plateau-drop), tie
the recommendation to §1's objective and §6's script structure, sketch it
per section in §8. This row is what QA later measures the render against
(`scripts/measure-motion.py`) — an unrecorded arc is unmeasurable.

## Gate — text

Present the filled SSOT compactly: the decisions, not the file. Surface every
`(inferred)` and open question in the same message. User approval flips
`Status: DRAFT → APPROVED` (you edit the line). Log the gate in PROGRESS.md.
Then → `references/storyboard.md`.

Right-size check: if this turned out to be a single-scene ask, say the method
is overkill and offer to work under klik-anim (+ klik-cam) alone.

# Stage 3 — Execution plan (persona: Tech Director)

Goal: an approved, then **frozen**, `<project>_execution_plan.md`. The
template (`templates/EXECUTION_PLAN.template.md`) defines the document; this
file is how to produce it. This stage is synthesis, not dialogue — run it in a
fresh context if practical, inheriting only the artifacts (SSOT, storyboard,
ref library, PROGRESS).

## Process

1. **Inputs must be APPROVED.** SSOT and storyboard both — a plan built on a
   DRAFT artifact is a plan built on sand; go finish the earlier gate instead.
2. **Fill the template verbatim.** Scene table from the board's `data-*`
   attributes + SSOT §6 copy (word-for-word, emphasis bold intact); transition
   specs exactly as their cards state them, with library IDs where cited;
   tokens from SSOT §4; beat grid from §7; dials + overrides from §8. The
   plan quotes the artifacts — it never paraphrases them.
3. **The context-blind test.** Before presenting: could an agent with zero
   chat history build this video from the plan + SSOT + board + craft skills alone?
   Anything that fails that test gets written in — never rely on what "we
   discussed".
4. **Propose the proof scene** — the most style-defining scene plus the
   signature transition, not the easiest one. The user confirms it at the
   gate, along with the checkpoint cadence (every N scenes / per act).
5. **Estimate tokens honestly.** Classify each scene — simple type scene
   ~15–25k · component/asset scene ~25–45k · heavy composite ~45–80k — sum,
   add ~30k setup/shared, present as a band, and say **"not including
   iterations"** in exactly those words.

## Gate — text, then frozen

Present compactly: build order, proof scene, checkpoint cadence, token band,
what happens next. Approval flips `Status: DRAFT → APPROVED` and the plan is
now **frozen** — build-time discoveries become dated amendments with the user,
never silent edits.

At approval, tell the user: **switch to Opus for the build** (planning ran on
Fable 5); quote the token band again; remind them 30s+ builds will likely hit
a session limit and that resume is lossless via the artifacts. Log the gate in
PROGRESS.md. Then → `references/build-qa.md`.

## Judgment

- Cite skill law numbers (§A.., C0, CAM-..); never restate mechanics (the builder loads the
  skills themselves).
- Assets: only SSOT §5 rows marked Clean ✅ may appear in the plan. A scene
  needing an unlogged asset → back to the user, or placeholder-then-swap
  written into the plan explicitly (exact required format in TODO.md).
- Missing information discovered here (a transition card left vague, a scene
  with no frame range) is a storyboard defect — fix it there first, don't
  compensate in the plan.

# Reference analysis — pulling insights from what the user shows you

Load this whenever the user supplies a reference — a video link, a file, a
screenshot, "make it like X" — at any stage. Output lands in two places: the
SSOT §2 profile (global direction) and the **reference library** (reusable
catalogued animations).

## Principles

- **A reference is a question, not an instruction.** You extract and itemize;
  the user confirms per item (take / adapt / skip). Never absorb a reference
  wholesale — the user usually wants two attributes of it, not twelve.
- **Extract into the system's vocabulary** — dial estimates, C1 motif names,
  A-law terms, frame counts — so every takeaway is buildable. "Feels premium"
  is not an extraction; "camera ≈2, pacing ≈2, sequential type" is.
- **Catalogue, then confirm.** The library collects everything notable; the
  user's confirmation decides what the project actually uses.
- **Vague name-drops get narrowed first.** "Kinda like Apple" → ask *which
  video*. Deep-analyze only refs the user actually points at.

## How to look

- **Local video files are the PRIMARY path** — ask the user to download and
  drop the file. Vimeo blocks all automated access (yt-dlp OAuth, player
  config 403, fetch = bot page); other hosts rot too. A URL is the fallback,
  not the default.
- **Video URL** → the `watch` skill (frames + transcript).
- **Local video** → ffmpeg: a 1fps contact sheet for structure, plus dense
  bursts (~15fps for 1–2s) around transitions and hero moves — motion shape
  lives in the bursts, not the stills.
- **Images/screenshots** → read directly (photo profile below).

## The segment pass → the reference library

Don't analyze a video as one blob. **Split it into segments at shot/section
boundaries** (visible in the contact sheet), analyze each segment, and
catalogue every notable device as a library entry in
`klik/<project>_ref_library.md`:

```
## L-07 · transition · <ref name> @ 0:14 (≈f420–432)
Type: transition | camera-move | element-move | text-placement | asset-design
What: whip-pan left→right, ~12f, background streaks, incoming scene decelerates
Curve: whip-snap (near-vertical peak, hard landing) · Direction: L→R
Notes: sells continuity between unrelated scenes; needs motion blur at peak
Status: catalogued | CONFIRMED (take/adapt) | skipped
```

- Entry types: **transition · camera-move · element-move · text-placement ·
  asset-design · depth-rig** (parallax/plane constructions; add another type
  only if none fits).
- Every entry: source + timestamp/frames · what happens in plain terms ·
  curve/speed character · direction · duration in frames · status.
- The library is cumulative across all refs in a project — later stages pull
  from it: storyboard transition cards may cite entries by ID ("T 2→3: per
  L-07, adapted to brand palette"), and the execution plan carries the ID so
  the build reproduces the *catalogued* mechanics, not a memory of them.

## Video extraction profile (global summary — fill only rows with evidence)

| Attribute | Read it as | Evidence to cite |
|---|---|---|
| Camera — movement | Per move: type (**push/pull zoom · pan L/R · tilt · orbit · tracking · handheld shake · whip**), specific direction, and magnitude; overall C0 dial estimate | the moves, frame-ranged |
| Camera — speed curve | How each move accelerates: constant · ease-in/out · thin-peak burst · whip-snap; does it resolve into drift or stop dead? | 2–3 frame-counted moves |
| Pacing — curves | The motion vocabulary: smooth bezier · spring/bounce (count the overshoots) · ripple/wave (propagating stagger) · snap · elastic · linear (flag it — A1 bans it for us) | hero entrances/exits |
| Pacing — effects | Recurring motion effects: smear/motion blur, echo/trails, glow pulses, particle garnish, masking reveals | where each appears |
| Pacing — tempo | C0.5 dial estimate: avg shot length, hold lengths, move durations in frames | shot-length sample |
| Parallax & depth | Plane count and what sits on each; relative speeds (fg:mid:bg ratio); direction (lateral/vertical/zoom); camera-driven or autonomous; DOF on parked planes (A5)? Catalogue setups as **depth-rig** entries | one camera/scroll move |
| Transitions | Motifs in C1 terms, frame-counted (also catalogued as L-entries) | 2–3 cuts |
| Typography | Face character, scale, case; sequential vs composed; placement habits (also catalogue notable text-placements) | representative frames |
| Palette | Approximate hexes — **direction only**, never token-grade (screenshot compression shifts color) | sampled frames |
| Choreography | Stagger/chain patterns in A3 terms | one plural-entry moment |
| Density | One-idea-per-beat vs layered | busiest frame |
| Beat relationship | Do cuts/hits land on the grid? | audio + cut timing |
| Signature | The 1–2 devices that make this ref recognizable | name them precisely |

## Photo reference profile (images/screenshots)

| Attribute | Read it as |
|---|---|
| Gradients | Type (linear/radial/mesh), direction, hue span, where used (bg/type/accent) |
| Subject | What it is, treatment (photo/3D/flat/outline), how it's lit |
| Background | Flat/textured/gradient/scene; how it separates from subject |
| Negative space | How much, where it sits, what it's protecting |
| Positioning | Composition: centered/thirds/edge-bleed; alignment grid; margins |
| Type placement | Where text sits relative to subject; scale contrast; overlap or clear |
| Texture & finish | Grain, noise, shadows (hard/soft/none), corner radii, line weights |
| Asset recipes | Any notable asset gets the full decomposition pass (section below) → library entry |

## Asset decomposition (the deep pass for asset-design entries)

Applies to assets seen in video segments AND photo refs — backgrounds,
elements, subjects, frame devices. Don't log "nice background"; log the
**recipe**. Decompose bottom-up:

| Layer | Note |
|---|---|
| Role | background · midground element · subject · frame device · text container |
| Base | shape language (rounded/hard/organic/torn) · fill (flat / gradient type+direction / image) |
| Texture | paper grain · film grain · halftone · noise · fabric · riso — and how applied (blend mode, opacity, scale) |
| Edges | clean vector · outlined (weight) · torn/deckled · rough brush · feathered |
| Warp | subtle wave warp · ripple · skew · perspective tilt — **static or animated (cycle period in frames)** |
| Light | shadow type (hard/soft/inner/none), light direction — consistent across assets? |
| Motion attached | idle behavior (bob, breathe, warp cycle), entrance style |
| Reproduction | how to rebuild it deterministically in Remotion: seeded-noise overlay for grain, sine-offset points / SVG turbulence for wave warps (frame-based, A0), CSS gradient stack, SVG filter — name the technique |

```
## L-12 · asset-design · <ref> @ 0:22
Role: background. Base: organic blob, radial gradient coral→cream.
Texture: paper grain, multiply ~12%, large scale. Edges: torn/deckled.
Warp: subtle wave, animated ~90f cycle. Light: soft drop, top-left.
Motion: slow breathe ±0.5%. Repro: SVG blob + seeded turbulence displacement
(frame-based), grain via seeded noise overlay.
Status: catalogued
```

**When the user has no asset ideas, the library IS the design source.** Take
inspiration heavily: decompose the strongest reference assets, then propose
2–3 asset treatments built from those recipes **recolored to brand tokens**,
and confirm per item before building. Inspiration is ingredient-level — never
trace or copy a reference asset wholesale; rebuild from the decomposed recipe
in the brand's own palette and shape language.

## The confirm step (mandatory)

Present the profile **and the new library entries** as one itemized list —
"which of these do you want?" — take / adapt / skip per item. Then:

- Confirmed profile rows → the SSOT §2 reference table, in dial/motif terms.
- Library entries get their status set (CONFIRMED / skipped) — skipped entries
  stay in the library; they may fit a later scene and can be re-offered.
- Explicit skips on a liked ref → record as constraints ("like X but NOT its
  palette") — they prevent exactly the drift that gets builds rejected.
- **Anti-references get the same pass inverted:** extract, then record
  precisely what to avoid, in the same vocabulary.

## Storyboard-stage refs

Screenshots dropped on a specific card get the photo profile, scoped to that
card — noted in the card's description, confirmed at the next board review.
A card ref never silently changes the global SSOT profile; if it should,
that's an SSOT amendment, with the user. When filling transition cards, check
the library first and offer matching entries by ID before inventing new ones.

# Stage 2 — Visual storyboard (persona: Storyboard Artist)

Goal: an approved `<project>_storyboard.html` where the user approved **real
rendered stills** — pixels, not prose. The template
(`templates/storyboard.template.html`) carries the file mechanics in its
header comment; this file is how to run the stage.

## Setup

- Copy the template → `klik/<project>_storyboard.html`; stills and previews go
  in `klik/boards/`.
- **Scaffold the Remotion project NOW, in the background**, if none exists
  (`remotion-create` skill). Drafting continues while it installs — the
  approval pass needs the real project, and the install takes minutes you
  shouldn't spend blocking.

## Process

**1 · Cards from the SSOT.** One scene card per SSOT §6 row — including
visual-only scenes — one transition card in every gap. Copy verbatim, emphasis
bold preserved. If a scene isn't in the SSOT, it doesn't get a card; if the
board needs a scene the SSOT lacks, amend the SSOT first (with the user).
**Time the cards against the music map** (SSOT §7): scene boundaries want to
land on section boundaries, the biggest scene on the highest-tier section —
and each card notes its section's character (tier · lead · attack), which the
plan later turns into motion directives (klik-anim §A16 / klik-cam CAM-5).

**2 · Draft pass — HTML mockups, cheap iteration.** Build each card's visual
as an HTML/CSS mockup with real frontend craft, using the SSOT brand tokens.
Iterate here — this is the cheapest medium the look will ever be in. Ask for
the user's reference screenshots per card (refs strip).
*If discovery logged "no style direction":* open by mocking scene 1 in 2–3
candidate directions and let the user pick — reacting to pixels beats
describing a vibe. The pick gets one confirming sentence in the SSOT (§2).

**3 · Transitions — elicit every gap.** For each boundary ask how it should
move: motif, duration (frames), speed/curve (against pacing dial C0.5),
camera involvement (against C0). **Check the reference library first** — if
`<project>_ref_library.md` holds matching transition/camera-move entries,
offer them by ID as candidates before inventing new ones. Offer real rendered
previews **only after saying they cost extra tokens**; default is the text
spec on the card. Record the agreed spec verbatim (with any L-ID) — the
execution plan carries it word-for-word.

**4 · Approval pass — real stills.** When drafts are stable: pose each card as
a real component in the project (these comps ARE the build's starting point),
render `npx remotion still` per card into `boards/`, run the §A9 loop on every
still — look, list defects, fix, re-render — then swap the stills into the
html, replacing the mockups.

**5 · Gate — PIXELS.** The user reviews the board with real stills and every
transition card filled. Approval flips the board's status; log it in
PROGRESS.md. Then → `references/execution-plan.md`.

## Judgment

- **One focal idea per card** (density per SSOT). A card that needs two focal
  elements is usually two scenes — split it and flag the SSOT amendment.
- **Iterate in the cheapest medium that can settle the question.** Layout and
  type questions die in HTML; only stable cards earn a still; only approved
  boards earn motion.
- **Right-size the board.** A 15s piece may be 3–4 cards; don't pad. Long
  pieces: board in acts, gate per act if the user prefers.
- **Refs are references.** A user screenshot on a card steers the mockup; it
  is never composited into the deliverable (Remotion output only). Card refs
  get the lighter per-card pass in `references/reference-analysis.md` — a card
  ref never silently changes the global SSOT profile.
- Camera/pacing overrides surfacing here ("this one slower") are recorded in
  SSOT §8 Local overrides — never left as verbal agreements.

FILE: skills_toolkit/klik-remotion-method/scripts/analyze-audio.py

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Klik method — dependency-free music analysis (discovery §7).

Pure stdlib + ffmpeg (bundled with Remotion / present on most systems).
No numpy, no aubio — by design: this runs anywhere the method runs.

  python3 analyze-audio.py track.mp3 [--fps 30] [--json out.json] [--stems auto|off|<dir>]

OPTIONAL stem separation (--stems auto, the default): if `demucs` is
installed (pip install demucs — needs torch), the track is split into
vocals/drums/bass/guitar/piano/other first and every source is analyzed
separately — kick/snare/hats come from the isolated drums stem, so vocals
and guitar no longer read as percussion. Without demucs the script degrades
gracefully to 3-band splitting and says so. Pre-split stems can be passed
as --stems <dir>.

Two layers of output:

1. THE GRID — BPM (autocorrelation + whole-track grid-alignment refinement),
   first beat & downbeat (seconds AND frames), frames-per-beat constants.
2. THE MUSIC MAP — what klik-anim §A16 / klik-cam CAM-5 consume: sections
   with energy tier (1–5), spectral balance (bass/mid/high), transient
   density, attack & sustain character, and per-source rhythm patterns on a
   16th-note grid (kick/snare/hats/vocals/bass/guitar/piano in stem mode;
   low/mid/high bands otherwise). The JSON adds `events` (per-source
   transient frames) and `levels` (per-frame source energy) — deterministic
   reactive data a composition can consume directly.

Paste the summary into SSOT §7, then VERIFY against a few hand-counted beats
before trusting the grid — and sanity-check the map by ear (does the detected
drop sound like the drop?).
"""
import argparse, array, json, math, os, shutil, subprocess, sys, tempfile, wave

SR = 11025          # full-band decode rate — plenty for onset timing
HOP = 128           # ~86 envelope points/sec → beat timing to ~±12 ms
SR_B = 22050        # band decode rate (high band needs Nyquist > 6 kHz)
HOP_B = 256         # 22050/256 == 11025/128 → band envelopes align 1:1

BANDS = [           # name, ffmpeg filter, what it carries (band-mode fallback)
    ("low",  "lowpass=f=150",                 "kick / bass"),
    ("mid",  "highpass=f=400,lowpass=f=4000", "snare / vocals / melody"),
    ("high", "highpass=f=6000",               "hats / cymbals / sizzle"),
]

# Within the isolated DRUMS stem, the same band trick is now clean:
KIT = [
    ("kick",  "lowpass=f=150"),
    ("snare", "highpass=f=200,lowpass=f=4000"),
    ("hats",  "highpass=f=6000"),
]
STEM_NAMES = ("vocals", "drums", "bass", "guitar", "piano", "other")
STEM_LABEL = {"kick": "kick (drums stem)", "snare": "snare (drums stem)",
              "hats": "hats (drums stem)", "vocals": "vocals", "bass": "bass",
              "guitar": "guitar", "piano": "piano", "other": "other instr."}


def scan_stem_dir(d):
    found = {}
    for root, _, files in os.walk(d):
        for f in files:
            base, ext = os.path.splitext(f)
            if base.lower() in STEM_NAMES and ext.lower() in (".wav", ".mp3", ".flac"):
                found[base.lower()] = os.path.join(root, f)
    return found


def find_stems(mode, track):
    """Resolve stems: 'off' → band mode · a directory → use its stem files ·
    'auto' → run demucs if installed, else fall back to band mode.

    Stem separation needs an ML model — it can never be stdlib-only, so it is
    an OPTIONAL stage with graceful degradation: without it, band-splitting
    conflates vocals/guitar transients with percussion (a known field defect).
    """
    if mode == "off":
        return None, "band mode (--stems off)"
    if mode != "auto":
        stems = scan_stem_dir(mode)
        if not stems:
            sys.exit(f"--stems {mode}: no vocals/drums/bass/… stem files found there")
        return stems, f"stems from {mode}"
    demucs = os.environ.get("DEMUCS_BIN") or shutil.which("demucs")
    if not demucs:
        return None, ("band mode — demucs not found. For true stems (vocals/"
                      "drums/bass/guitar/piano): pip install demucs, or pass "
                      "--stems <dir> of pre-split files.")
    outdir = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="klik-stems-")
    for model in ("htdemucs_6s", "htdemucs"):
        try:
            subprocess.run([demucs, "-n", model, "-o", outdir, track], check=True)
        except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
            continue
        stems = scan_stem_dir(outdir)
        if stems:
            return stems, f"stems via demucs {model} → {outdir}"
    return None, "band mode (demucs ran but produced no stems)"


def decode(path, sr=SR, af=None):
    tmp = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(suffix=".wav", delete=False)
    tmp.close()
    cmd = ["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-y", "-i", path, "-ac", "1", "-ar", str(sr)]
    if af:
        cmd += ["-af", af]
    cmd += ["-f", "wav", tmp.name]
    try:
        subprocess.run(cmd, check=True)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        sys.exit("ffmpeg not found on PATH — install it or use `npx remotion ffmpeg`.")
    except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
        sys.exit(f"ffmpeg could not decode {path!r}")
    with wave.open(tmp.name, "rb") as wf:
        raw = wf.readframes(wf.getnframes())
    os.unlink(tmp.name)
    samples = array.array("h")
    samples.frombytes(raw)
    return samples


def envelopes(samples, hop=HOP):
    """Per-hop mean |amplitude| (energy) and half-wave-rectified flux (onset)."""
    n = len(samples) // hop
    energy = []
    for i in range(n):
        seg = samples[i * hop:(i + 1) * hop]
        acc = 0
        for s in seg:
            acc += s if s >= 0 else -s
        energy.append(acc / (hop * 32768.0))
    onset = [0.0]
    for i in range(1, n):
        d = energy[i] - energy[i - 1]
        onset.append(d if d > 0.0 else 0.0)
    sm = [0.0] * n                                   # 3-point smooth
    for i in range(n):
        a, b = max(0, i - 1), min(n, i + 2)
        sm[i] = sum(onset[a:b]) / (b - a)
    return sm, energy


def detect_bpm(onset, hps, lo=60.0, hi=200.0):
    n = len(onset)
    mean = sum(onset) / n
    x = [v - mean for v in onset]
    lmin, lmax = int(hps * 60.0 / hi), int(hps * 60.0 / lo) + 2
    scores = {}
    for lag in range(lmin, lmax):
        s = 0.0
        for i in range(n - lag):
            s += x[i] * x[i + lag]
        scores[lag] = s / (n - lag)
    best = max(scores, key=scores.get)

    def refined(lag):                                # parabolic sub-hop peak
        if lag - 1 in scores and lag + 1 in scores:
            y0, y1, y2 = scores[lag - 1], scores[lag], scores[lag + 1]
            den = y0 - 2 * y1 + y2
            if den:
                return lag + 0.5 * (y0 - y2) / den
        return float(lag)

    lag_f = refined(best)
    bpm = 60.0 * hps / lag_f
    folded = bpm
    while folded < 90.0:
        folded *= 2.0
    while folded >= 180.0:
        folded /= 2.0
    conf = scores[best] / (sum(abs(v) for v in scores.values()) / len(scores) + 1e-12)
    return folded, conf


def refine_bpm(onset, hps, bpm0, span=1.5, step=0.01):
    """Full-track grid-alignment refinement around the autocorrelation BPM.

    Tempo error is cumulative — a 0.5% error drifts a full beat by the tail —
    so scoring onset alignment across the WHOLE track disambiguates candidates
    the (windowed, sub-hop-limited) autocorrelation peak cannot. Field case:
    autocorrelation reported 139.36 where truth was 140.000; whole-track
    alignment separates them decisively.
    """
    n = len(onset)
    best_bpm, best_s = bpm0, -1.0
    cand = bpm0 - span
    while cand <= bpm0 + span + 1e-9:
        period = 60.0 * hps / cand
        s_best = -1.0
        off = 0.0
        while off < period:                      # coarse best phase per candidate
            s, t, k = 0.0, off, 0
            while t < n:
                i = int(t + 0.5)
                if i < n:
                    s += onset[i]
                    k += 1
                t += period
            if k:
                s /= k
            if s > s_best:
                s_best = s
            off += period / 8.0
        if s_best > best_s:
            best_s, best_bpm = s_best, cand
        cand += step
    return best_bpm


def align(onset, energy, period):
    """Best beat phase, then best of 4 bar phases → first downbeat."""
    n = len(onset)

    def grid_score(seq, offset, step):
        s, t = 0.0, offset
        while t < n:
            i = int(t + 0.5)
            if i < n:
                s += seq[i]
            t += step
        return s

    best_off, best_s = 0.0, -1.0
    off = 0.0
    while off < period:
        s = grid_score(onset, off, period)
        if s > best_s:
            best_off, best_s = off, s
        off += 0.25
    beat0 = best_off
    best_db, best_e = 0, -1.0
    for db in range(4):
        e = grid_score(energy, beat0 + db * period, period * 4)
        if e > best_e:
            best_db, best_e = db, e
    return beat0, beat0 + best_db * period


# ───────────────────────────── the music map ─────────────────────────────

def pct(sorted_vals, p):
    if not sorted_vals:
        return 0.0
    return sorted_vals[min(len(sorted_vals) - 1, int(p * len(sorted_vals)))]


def find_peaks(onset, energy, min_gap=4, prominence=2.2):
    """Local onset maxima that are real transients → hop indices.

    Three gates, all verified against phantom-pattern failures:
    - relative threshold (0.30 × p95 of flux) — scales to the band's loudness;
    - absolute floor tied to the band's ENERGY (a steady pad has near-zero
      flux; without a floor, quantization ripple becomes an all-16ths pattern);
    - PROMINENCE over the local ±110ms neighborhood — a transient is a flux
      spike sparse in time; a beating/chorused pad produces *continuous* flux
      that clears any level threshold but never stands clear of its own
      surroundings.
    """
    n = len(onset)
    th = max(0.30 * pct(sorted(onset), 0.95),
             0.04 * pct(sorted(energy), 0.95))
    pre = [0.0]                                       # prefix sums → local mean
    for v in onset:
        pre.append(pre[-1] + v)
    out, last = [], -min_gap
    W = 9
    for i in range(2, n - 2):
        v = onset[i]
        if v <= th or v != max(onset[i - 2:i + 3]) or i - last < min_gap:
            continue
        a, b = max(0, i - W), min(n, i + W + 1)
        local_mean = (pre[b] - pre[a]) / (b - a)
        if v > prominence * local_mean:
            out.append(i)
            last = i
    return out


def bar_starts(downbeat, period, n):
    out, t = [], downbeat
    while t + 4 * period <= n:
        out.append(t)
        t += 4 * period
    return out


def attack_ms(onset, peak, hop_ms):
    """Rise time: hops from 20% of peak value up to the peak."""
    v = onset[peak]
    j = peak
    while j > 0 and onset[j - 1] < onset[j] and onset[j - 1] > 0.2 * v:
        j -= 1
    return (peak - j + 1) * hop_ms


def sustain_ms(energy, peak, hop_ms):
    """Time until energy falls below half its value at the peak."""
    v = energy[min(peak, len(energy) - 1)]
    j = peak
    lim = min(len(energy), peak + int(1200 / hop_ms))
    while j < lim and energy[j] > 0.5 * v:
        j += 1
    return (j - peak) * hop_ms


def slot16(h, bar_start, period):
    """Hop index → 16th-note slot 0–15 within its bar."""
    pos = (h - bar_start) / (period / 4.0)
    return int(pos + 0.5) % 16


def pattern_string(band_peaks, bars, period, bar_lo, bar_hi):
    """Presence-per-slot over a bar range → 'X x . .' 16-char pattern."""
    nbars = bar_hi - bar_lo
    if nbars <= 0:
        return "." * 16
    hist = [0] * 16
    lo_h, hi_h = bars[bar_lo], bars[bar_hi - 1] + 4 * period
    for h in band_peaks:
        if lo_h <= h < hi_h:
            b = int((h - bars[bar_lo]) / (4 * period))
            hist[slot16(h, bars[bar_lo] + b * 4 * period, period)] += 1
    out = []
    for c in hist:
        f = c / nbars
        out.append("X" if f >= 0.5 else ("x" if f >= 0.25 else "."))
    return "".join(out)


def build_map(full_onset, full_energy, bands_env, bars, period, hps, fps, down0,
              pattern_env=None):
    """pattern_env: {name: (onset, energy)} used for the per-section rhythm
    patterns. Defaults to the mix bands; in stem mode it's the per-source
    envelopes (kick/snare/hats from the drums stem, vocals, bass, …)."""
    hop_ms = 1000.0 / hps
    nb = len(bars)
    if nb < 2:
        return [], []

    # per-bar features
    def bar_sum(seq, b):
        a, z = int(bars[b]), int(min(len(seq), bars[b] + 4 * period))
        seg = seq[a:z]
        return sum(seg) / max(1, len(seg))

    e_bars = [bar_sum(full_energy, b) for b in range(nb)]
    ranked = sorted(e_bars)
    tiers = []
    for e in e_bars:                                  # energy tier 1–5 by percentile
        t = 1 + sum(1 for q in (0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8) if e > pct(ranked, q))
        tiers.append(t)

    bal = []                                          # low/mid/high fractions per bar
    for b in range(nb):
        vals = [bar_sum(bands_env[name][1], b) for name, _, _ in BANDS]
        tot = sum(vals) + 1e-12
        bal.append([v / tot for v in vals])

    full_peaks = find_peaks(full_onset, full_energy)
    dens = [0.0] * nb                                 # transients/sec per bar
    bar_sec = 4 * period / hps
    for h in full_peaks:
        b = int((h - bars[0]) / (4 * period))
        if 0 <= b < nb:
            dens[b] += 1
    dens = [d / bar_sec for d in dens]

    # section boundaries: sustained change in tier or bass balance
    sections, start = [], 0
    for b in range(2, nb - 1):
        if b - start < 4:
            continue
        t_prev = sum(tiers[max(0, b - 2):b]) / 2.0
        t_next = sum(tiers[b:b + 2]) / 2.0
        l_prev = sum(x[0] for x in bal[max(0, b - 2):b]) / 2.0
        l_next = sum(x[0] for x in bal[b:b + 2]) / 2.0
        if abs(t_next - t_prev) >= 1.5 or abs(l_next - l_prev) >= 0.22:
            sections.append((start, b))
            start = b
    sections.append((start, nb))

    if pattern_env is None:
        pattern_env = {name: bands_env[name] for name, _, _ in BANDS}
    pat_peaks = {name: find_peaks(o, e) for name, (o, e) in pattern_env.items()}

    rows = []
    for lo, hi in sections:
        seg_peaks = [h for h in full_peaks if bars[lo] <= h < bars[hi - 1] + 4 * period]
        if seg_peaks:
            atk = sorted(attack_ms(full_onset, h, hop_ms) for h in seg_peaks)
            sus = sorted(sustain_ms(full_energy, h, hop_ms) for h in seg_peaks)
            a_med, s_med = pct(atk, 0.5), pct(sus, 0.5)
            a_char = "sharp" if a_med < 35 else ("medium" if a_med < 90 else "soft")
            s_char = "staccato" if s_med < 150 else ("held" if s_med < 400 else "sustained")
            attack_str = f"{a_char} (~{int(a_med)}ms)"
            sustain_str = f"{s_char} (~{int(s_med)}ms)"
        else:
            attack_str = sustain_str = "— (no transients: swell/pad territory)"
        t_avg = sum(tiers[lo:hi]) / (hi - lo)
        b_avg = [sum(x[i] for x in bal[lo:hi]) / (hi - lo) for i in range(3)]
        lead = ("bass", "mid", "high")[b_avg.index(max(b_avg))]
        rows.append({
            "bars": [lo, hi],
            "start_s": round(bars[lo] / hps, 3),
            "start_frame": round(bars[lo] / hps * fps),
            "tier": round(t_avg, 1),
            "balance": {"low": round(b_avg[0], 2), "mid": round(b_avg[1], 2), "high": round(b_avg[2], 2)},
            "lead": lead,
            "transients_per_s": round(sum(dens[lo:hi]) / (hi - lo), 2),
            "attack": attack_str,
            "sustain": sustain_str,
            "pattern": {name: pattern_string(pat_peaks[name], bars, period, lo, hi)
                        for name in pattern_env},
        })
    tier_strip = "".join(str(t) for t in tiers)
    return rows, tier_strip


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    ap.add_argument("track")
    ap.add_argument("--fps", type=float, default=30.0)
    ap.add_argument("--json", help="also write full results to this path")
    ap.add_argument("--stems", default="auto",
                    help="'auto' (run demucs if installed) · 'off' (band mode) "
                         "· or a directory of pre-split stem files "
                         "(vocals/drums/bass/guitar/piano/other .wav)")
    a = ap.parse_args()

    samples = decode(a.track)
    dur = len(samples) / SR
    onset, energy = envelopes(samples)
    hps = SR / HOP
    bpm, conf = detect_bpm(onset, hps)
    bpm = refine_bpm(onset, hps, bpm)                # whole-track grid alignment
    period = 60.0 * hps / bpm
    alt = bpm / 2.0 if bpm / 2.0 >= 45.0 else bpm * 2.0
    beat0_h, down0_h = align(onset, energy, period)
    beat0, down0 = beat0_h / hps, down0_h / hps
    fpb = 60.0 / bpm * a.fps

    bands_env = {}
    for name, af, _ in BANDS:                        # mix bands: balance + fallback
        bands_env[name] = envelopes(decode(a.track, SR_B, af), HOP_B)

    stems, stem_note = find_stems(a.stems, a.track)
    sources = None                                   # {name: (onset, energy)}
    if stems:
        sources = {}
        if "drums" in stems:                         # clean K/S/H from the kit
            for name, af in KIT:
                sources[name] = envelopes(decode(stems["drums"], SR_B, af), HOP_B)
        for name in ("bass", "vocals", "guitar", "piano", "other"):
            if name in stems:
                sources[name] = envelopes(decode(stems[name], SR_B), HOP_B)

    bars = bar_starts(down0_h, period, len(onset))
    e_bars = []
    t = down0_h
    while t + 4 * period <= len(energy):
        seg = energy[int(t):int(t + 4 * period)]
        e_bars.append(sum(seg) / max(1, len(seg)))
        t += 4 * period
    drops = sorted(
        ({"bar": i, "time_s": round(down0 + i * 4 * 60.0 / bpm, 2),
          "delta": round(e_bars[i] - e_bars[i - 1], 4)}
         for i in range(1, len(e_bars))),
        key=lambda d: -d["delta"])[:3]

    map_rows, tier_strip = build_map(onset, energy, bands_env, bars, period,
                                     hps, a.fps, down0, pattern_env=sources)

    # Deterministic reactive data for builds (JSON only): transient frames per
    # source + per-video-frame normalized levels. Lets a comp light up on the
    # SAME detections the map was built from — pure function of frame (A0).
    react_env = sources if sources else {name: bands_env[name] for name, _, _ in BANDS}
    react_peaks = {name: find_peaks(o, e) for name, (o, e) in react_env.items()}
    nframes = int(dur * a.fps)

    def levels(seq):
        peak = max(seq) or 1.0
        return [round(seq[min(len(seq) - 1, int(f / a.fps * hps))] / peak, 3)
                for f in range(nframes)]

    events = {name: [round(h / hps * a.fps) for h in react_peaks[name]]
              for name in react_env}
    events["full"] = [round(h / hps * a.fps) for h in
                      find_peaks(onset, energy)]
    levels_out = {name: levels(react_env[name][1]) for name in react_env}
    levels_out["full"] = levels(energy)

    out = {
        "track": os.path.basename(a.track), "duration_s": round(dur, 2),
        "bpm": round(bpm, 2), "alt_bpm": round(alt, 2),
        "confidence": round(conf, 2), "fps": a.fps,
        "first_beat_s": round(beat0, 3), "first_downbeat_s": round(down0, 3),
        "first_beat_frame": round(beat0 * a.fps),
        "first_downbeat_frame": round(down0 * a.fps),
        "frames_per_beat": round(fpb, 4),
        "drops": [dict(d, frame=round(d["time_s"] * a.fps)) for d in drops],
        "energy_tier_per_bar": tier_strip,
        "mode": "stems" if sources else "bands",
        "stem_note": stem_note,
        "music_map": map_rows,
        "events": events,
        "levels": levels_out,
    }
    if a.json:
        with open(a.json, "w") as f:
            json.dump(out, f, indent=2)

    print(f"track          {out['track']}  ({out['duration_s']}s)")
    print(f"BPM            {out['bpm']}  (alternate: {out['alt_bpm']}, confidence {out['confidence']})")
    print(f"first beat     {out['first_beat_s']}s  → f{out['first_beat_frame']} @ {a.fps:g}fps")
    print(f"first downbeat {out['first_downbeat_s']}s  → f{out['first_downbeat_frame']}")
    print(f"motion.ts      FRAMES_PER_BEAT = {out['frames_per_beat']}; "
          f"beat(n) = round({out['first_downbeat_frame']} + n * FRAMES_PER_BEAT)")
    for d in out["drops"]:
        print(f"energy jump    bar {d['bar']}  @ {d['time_s']}s (f{d['frame']})  ΔE {d['delta']}")

    print(f"\nSOURCES        {stem_note}")
    print(f"MUSIC MAP      (energy tier per bar: {tier_strip})")
    band_carries = {name: carries for name, _, carries in BANDS}
    for r in map_rows:
        b = r["balance"]
        print(f"  bars {r['bars'][0]:>2}–{r['bars'][1]:<2} @ {r['start_s']:>7.2f}s f{r['start_frame']:<6}"
              f" tier {r['tier']}  lead {r['lead']:<4} (L{b['low']:.2f}/M{b['mid']:.2f}/H{b['high']:.2f})"
              f"  {r['transients_per_s']}/s  attack {r['attack']}  sustain {r['sustain']}")
        for name, pat in r["pattern"].items():
            label = STEM_LABEL.get(name, band_carries.get(name, name))
            print(f"      {name:<6} |{pat}|  ({label})")
    print("\n16th-grid legend: X ≥50% of bars · x ≥25% · slots 1–16, downbeat first.")
    print("Feed the map to klik-anim §A16 (motion character) and klik-cam CAM-5")
    print("(camera). VERIFY: hand-count 4 beats at two points; check the loudest")
    print("detected section IS the drop by ear before building to it. Bar phase")
    print("(which slot is beat 1) is a guess when the intro lacks accents — the")
    print("patterns may be rotated by a constant offset; confirm against the kick.")
    if out["confidence"] < 1.5:
        print("NOTE: low confidence — ambient/sparse track; confirm BPM by ear.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""measure-motion.py — arithmetic QA for the energy arc (A18) and the
rest ratio (A6), measured from RENDERED FRAMES, not from code.

  python3 measure-motion.py render.mp4 [--map music-map.json]
      [--rest-k 0.35] [--json out.json]

What it does
  1. Frame-diffs the video (ffmpeg tblend=difference, downscaled) into a
     per-frame motion-energy series — the piece's ACTUAL energy curve.
  2. Rest ratio: fraction of the timeline whose smoothed energy sits
     below a FLOOR-RELATIVE threshold `p10 + rest_k × (p90 − p10)` —
     checked against A6's 40–60% band. (Floor-relative because textural
     grounds elevate the baseline — see the in-code note.)
  3. With --map (the analyzer's music-map JSON): per-bar energy means vs
     `energy_tier_per_bar` — Pearson correlation + per-tier mean table.
     A piece that follows its arc shows rising means tier 1 → 5.
  4. ASCII sparkline of the smoothed curve (valleys and peaks at a
     glance — the arc SHAPE, for eyes; the numbers are the contract).

Scope note: camera-vs-element motion separation (klik-cam CAM-6 balance)
is a planned second stage; this tool measures TOTAL motion energy.
Requires ffmpeg on PATH. stdlib only.
"""
import argparse
import json
import math
import re
import subprocess
import sys

BLOCKS = " ▁▂▃▄▅▆▇█"


def frame_energy(path: str) -> list[float]:
    cmd = [
        "ffmpeg", "-i", path, "-vf",
        "tblend=all_mode=difference,scale=320:180,signalstats,"
        "metadata=mode=print:key=lavfi.signalstats.YAVG:file=-",
        "-f", "null", "-",
    ]
    proc = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
    vals = [float(m) for m in re.findall(r"lavfi\.signalstats\.YAVG=([\d.]+)", proc.stdout)]
    if not vals:
        sys.exit("no frames measured — is ffmpeg on PATH and the file a video?")
    return vals


def smooth(xs: list[float], w: int) -> list[float]:
    out = []
    for i in range(len(xs)):
        a, b = max(0, i - w // 2), min(len(xs), i + w // 2 + 1)
        out.append(sum(xs[a:b]) / (b - a))
    return out


def pearson(a: list[float], b: list[float]) -> float:
    n = min(len(a), len(b))
    a, b = a[:n], b[:n]
    ma, mb = sum(a) / n, sum(b) / n
    cov = sum((x - ma) * (y - mb) for x, y in zip(a, b))
    va = math.sqrt(sum((x - ma) ** 2 for x in a))
    vb = math.sqrt(sum((y - mb) ** 2 for y in b))
    return cov / (va * vb) if va and vb else 0.0


def sparkline(xs: list[float], width: int = 66) -> str:
    if not xs:
        return ""
    step = max(1, len(xs) // width)
    pts = [sum(xs[i:i + step]) / len(xs[i:i + step]) for i in range(0, len(xs), step)]
    hi = max(pts) or 1
    return "".join(BLOCKS[min(8, int(p / hi * 8.999))] for p in pts)


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("video")
    ap.add_argument("--map", dest="map_path")
    ap.add_argument("--rest-k", type=float, default=0.35,
                    help="rest threshold as a fraction of p90 energy")
    ap.add_argument("--json", dest="json_out")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    raw = frame_energy(args.video)
    fps = 30.0
    bars_meta = None
    if args.map_path:
        m = json.load(open(args.map_path))
        fps = float(m.get("fps", 30.0))
        bars_meta = m

    sm = smooth(raw, int(fps))  # ~1s window
    n = len(sm)
    srt = sorted(sm)
    p10 = srt[int(0.1 * (n - 1))]
    p50 = srt[int(0.5 * (n - 1))]
    p90 = srt[int(0.9 * (n - 1))]
    # Textural treatments (grain/boil grounds) elevate the energy FLOOR —
    # rest is measured against that baseline (p10), never against zero:
    # A6's own distinction between idle life and motion events.
    rest_thr = p10 + args.rest_k * (p90 - p10)
    rest = sum(1 for v in sm if v < rest_thr) / n
    contrast = (p90 - p10) / p50 if p50 else 0.0

    print(f"frames: {n}  duration: {n / fps:.1f}s @ {fps:g}fps")
    print(f"energy curve  |{sparkline(sm)}|")
    print(f"floor p10 {p10:.2f} · median {p50:.2f} · p90 {p90:.2f} · "
          f"event/rest contrast {contrast:.2f}")
    if contrast < 0.15:
        print("verdict: FLAT piece — no event/rest contrast (catalogue/glossary "
              "territory; a designed piece wants a shaped curve, A18)")
    else:
        band = "OK (A6 40-60%)" if 0.40 <= rest <= 0.60 else "OUT OF BAND (A6 wants 40-60%)"
        print(f"rest ratio: {rest * 100:.1f}%  (floor-relative, k={args.rest_k})  -> {band}")

    result = {"frames": n, "fps": fps, "rest_ratio": round(rest, 4),
              "contrast": round(contrast, 3), "p10": round(p10, 3),
              "p50": round(p50, 3), "p90": round(p90, 3),
              "energy_smoothed": [round(v, 3) for v in sm]}

    if bars_meta is not None:
        fpb = float(bars_meta["frames_per_beat"])
        f0 = int(bars_meta["first_downbeat_frame"])
        tiers = [int(c) for c in str(bars_meta["energy_tier_per_bar"])]
        bar_len = fpb * 4
        bar_means, bar_tiers = [], []
        for bi, tier in enumerate(tiers):
            a = int(f0 + bi * bar_len)
            b = int(f0 + (bi + 1) * bar_len)
            if a >= n:
                break
            seg = sm[a:min(b, n)]
            if seg:
                bar_means.append(sum(seg) / len(seg))
                bar_tiers.append(tier)
        r = pearson(bar_means, [float(t) for t in bar_tiers])
        print(f"arc correlation (per-bar energy vs designed tier): r = {r:.2f}  "
              f"[{len(bar_means)} bars]")
        per_tier: dict[int, list[float]] = {}
        for t, e in zip(bar_tiers, bar_means):
            per_tier.setdefault(t, []).append(e)
        mono_prev, mono = -1.0, True
        for t in sorted(per_tier):
            mean = sum(per_tier[t]) / len(per_tier[t])
            flag = "" if mean >= mono_prev else "  <-- non-monotonic"
            mono = mono and mean >= mono_prev
            print(f"  tier {t}: mean energy {mean:6.2f}  ({len(per_tier[t])} bars){flag}")
            mono_prev = mean
        print(f"tier means monotonic: {'YES' if mono else 'NO'} — "
              f"{'motion climbs with the designed arc' if mono else 'the piece is not following its arc'}")
        result.update({"arc_r": round(r, 3),
                       "bar_means": [round(v, 3) for v in bar_means],
                       "bar_tiers": bar_tiers})

    if args.json_out:
        json.dump(result, open(args.json_out, "w"))
        print(f"wrote {args.json_out}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

      fights, drift).

      ACTUAL frame numbers; audit the §A14 device ledger and every §A15
      boundary. A watch-down cannot catch durations — both checks, always.

      klik-cam's CAM checklist when the camera dial > 1.

      result + open TODO list.

  style → SSOT/style tokens first, then code · single scene → §3 row ·
  timing → storyboard, then plan. Artifacts stay truthful; never patch code
  against what the documents say.
